title: Joshua 1:1
content:
Section 1:1–9 Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua)

In this section Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into the land that he had promised them. He told Yehoshua that no enemy would be able to oppose him, and that he must obey the law which Yahweh gave to Mosheh (Moses). Yehoshua told the Israelis to prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Yahweh told Yehoshua to be strong and courageous

Yahweh told Yehoshua to lead the people across the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:1–5

Mosheh led the Israeli (Israelite) people through the wilderness for forty years. At the end of the book of Deuteronomy the people were almost ready to enter the land of Kena’an (Canaan), and Mosheh died. Here at the beginning of the book of Yehoshua, Yahweh put Yehoshua in command of the Israelis, and told him to lead them into Kena’an. Yahweh promised to be with Yehoshua and to help him.

1:1a

Now after the death of His servant Mosheh,

  • ¶ After Mosheh the servant of Yahweh died,

  • ¶ Mosheh (Moses) had recently died. He was a person who served Yahweh.

after the death of His servant Mosheh: The death of…Mosheh is described in Deuteronomy 34. The book of Yehoshua (Joshua) follows that story. This sentence is the opening words of a new book. Think about the natural way to begin a new book in your language. In some languages it may be better to begin with a main clause, for example:

Mosheh had recently died

His servant Mosheh: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as servant can also be translated as “slave.” It refers to someone who must obey the commands of a master. It is recommended that you use a term that indicates the lowly position of a slave or a servant.

In some languages it may be more natural to place Mosheh’s title His servant after his name, for example:

Mosheh, Yahweh’s servant

In some languages it may be more natural to use the verb “serve” instead of the noun servant, for example:

Mosheh, a man who served Yahweh

General Comment on 1:1a

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

After Mosheh (Moses), Yahweh’s servant, died

Mosheh had recently died. He was a man who served Yahweh.

1:1b

Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun, Mosheh’s assistant, saying,

  • Yahweh spoke to Nun’s son, Yehoshua, who had assisted Mosheh.

  • Then Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua. Yehoshua’s father was Nun, and he was the person who helped Mosheh.

Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua son of Nun: This is the first event of the book. If you used a main clause to translate 1:1a you may want to use a temporal phrase here, such as “at that time.”

Here is another way to translate this clause:

At that time Yahweh said to Yehoshua the son of Nun

Yahweh: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates Yahweh is “Yahweh,” the personal name of God. See the notes in the Introduction on how to translate this term.

Yehoshua son of Nun: In some languages it may be more natural to say:

Yehoshua (Joshua) whose father was called Nun

Mosheh’s (Moses’) assistant: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as assistant comes from a verb that means “to be an attendant on” or “to wait on.” It is different from the Hebrew word translated as “servant” in 1:1a. This word was used when Yehoshua accompanied Mosheh up Mount Sinay (Sinai) (Exodus 24:13) where the BSB translated it as “attendant.” Yehoshua’s task was not that of a servant but of an assistant.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

the person who helped Mosheh

Mosheh’s aide (NIV)

Mosheh’s helper (GNT)

Here are some ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yahweh said to Yehoshua (Joshua), Nun’s son, who had been Mosheh’s assistant

Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua. Yehoshua was the son of Nun, and he was the person who had helped Mosheh (Moses)

title: Joshua 1:2
content:
Section 1:1–9 Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua)

In this section Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into the land that he had promised them. He told Yehoshua that no enemy would be able to oppose him, and that he must obey the law which Yahweh gave to Mosheh (Moses). Yehoshua told the Israelis to prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Yahweh told Yehoshua to be strong and courageous

Yahweh told Yehoshua to lead the people across the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:1–5

Mosheh led the Israeli (Israelite) people through the wilderness for forty years. At the end of the book of Deuteronomy the people were almost ready to enter the land of Kena’an (Canaan), and Mosheh died. Here at the beginning of the book of Yehoshua, Yahweh put Yehoshua in command of the Israelis, and told him to lead them into Kena’an. Yahweh promised to be with Yehoshua and to help him.

1:2a

“Mosheh My servant is dead.

  • Yahweh said: “Mosheh my servant is dead.

  • Yahweh said: “Mosheh (Moses) served me, but he has died.

Mosheh My servant is dead: You should translate the word servant the same way you did in 1:1a.

My: The word My refers to Yahweh. It was Yahweh who was speaking.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

My servant Mosheh is dead

Mosheh served me, and now he has died

1:2b

Now therefore arise, you and all these people, and cross over the Yarden (Jordan)

  • Now, prepare to cross the Yarden River, you(sing) and all these people.

  • So now, get ready. You must lead all these Israelis (Israelites) across the Yarden River.

Now therefore arise: The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as arise is more literally “get up.” It is an idiom that indicates the beginning of an action. For example:

get ready to cross the Yarden River (NIV)

you and all these people: The phrase you and all these people refers to Yehoshua (Joshua) and all the Israelis.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Get ready to cross the Yarden River, you and all the people of Yisrael (Israel)

You and all the Israelis must prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

Now get ready to lead all the Yisrael people across the Yarden River

cross over the Yarden: The clause cross over the Yarden is a command to cross the Yarden River. The Israelis (Israelites) were on the east side of the Yarden River, and the land of Kena’an (Canaan) was on the west side. The river is referred to as the Yarden because it was close to the place where Yehoshua was.

1:2c

into the land that I am giving to the children of Yisrael.

  • Enter the land which I am giving to them, the people of Yisrael.

  • Go into the land I am giving to all of you.

into the land that I am giving to the children of Yisrael (Israel): In some languages it may be clearer to start a new sentence here. For example:

Go into the land

to the children of Yisrael: The phrase to the children of Yisrael is used for emphasis. It emphasizes that Yahweh was giving the land of Kena’an to the children of Yisrael to live in. Yehoshua (Joshua) was a part of the people of Yisrael. In some languages it may be clearer to include Yehoshua in this phrase.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

to you(plur) the people of Yisrael

to you(sing) and the people of Yisrael

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Enter the land that I am giving to you and to all the Israelis (Israelites)

Go into the land which I am giving to all of you

You must go into the land that I am giving to all the Yisrael (Israel) people

title: Joshua 1:3
content:
Section 1:1–9 Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua)

In this section Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into the land that he had promised them. He told Yehoshua that no enemy would be able to oppose him, and that he must obey the law which Yahweh gave to Mosheh (Moses). Yehoshua told the Israelis to prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Yahweh told Yehoshua to be strong and courageous

Yahweh told Yehoshua to lead the people across the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:1–5

Mosheh led the Israeli (Israelite) people through the wilderness for forty years. At the end of the book of Deuteronomy the people were almost ready to enter the land of Kena’an (Canaan), and Mosheh died. Here at the beginning of the book of Yehoshua, Yahweh put Yehoshua in command of the Israelis, and told him to lead them into Kena’an. Yahweh promised to be with Yehoshua and to help him.

1:3a

I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread,

  • I have given you(plur) everywhere that you place your feet,

  • Everywhere that you walk/tread I have given to you.

I have given you: There are two ways to interpret the Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as I have given you.

  1. Some English versions translate with the past tense. For example:

    I have given to you (ESV) (BSB, ESV, RSV, NASB, KJV, REB, GNT, NLT)

  2. Some English versions translate with the future tense. For example:

    I will give you (NIV) (NIV, NJB, NCV, GW, CEV)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1). The Israelis (Israelites) had not yet entered Kena’an (Canaan), but because Yahweh promised it, it was as certain as if they were already there.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

I have given you(plur) everywhere that you(plur) place your feet

Every place where you walk I have given to you

every place where the sole of your foot will tread: The phrase every place where the sole of your foot will tread indicates that Yahweh will give the Israelis every part of the land that they walk on.

your: The Hebrew pronouns in this verse are plural: “your(plur) feet,” and “given to you(plur).” Yahweh spoke to all the people of Yisrael (Israel).

1:3b

just as I promised to Mosheh (Moses).

  • as I promised Mosheh.

  • This was the promise I made to Mosheh.

I promised to Mosheh: Yahweh promised Mosheh that he would give the land of Kena’an (Canaan) to the Israelis (Israelites) in Exodus 3:8. He repeated this promise in Deuteronomy 11:24

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

just as I promised Mosheh

I promise you what I promised to Mosheh (NLT)

title: Joshua 1:4
content:
Section 1:1–9 Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua)

In this section Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into the land that he had promised them. He told Yehoshua that no enemy would be able to oppose him, and that he must obey the law which Yahweh gave to Mosheh (Moses). Yehoshua told the Israelis to prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Yahweh told Yehoshua to be strong and courageous

Yahweh told Yehoshua to lead the people across the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:1–5

Mosheh led the Israeli (Israelite) people through the wilderness for forty years. At the end of the book of Deuteronomy the people were almost ready to enter the land of Kena’an (Canaan), and Mosheh died. Here at the beginning of the book of Yehoshua, Yahweh put Yehoshua in command of the Israelis, and told him to lead them into Kena’an. Yahweh promised to be with Yehoshua and to help him.

1:4a

Your territory shall extend from the wilderness and Levanon (Lebanon)

  • Your land will extend from the desert in the south to the Levanon mountains in the north.

  • Your borders will reach from the wilderness in the south to the mountains of Levanon in the north.

In verse 1:4 Yahweh described the four sides of the land that he was giving to the Israeli people: the south and the north, the east and the west.

from the wilderness: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as wilderness refers to the dry area in the south of the land of Kena’an. Because it was dry, few people lived there, and it was difficult to grow crops there.

Here are some other ways to translate the word wilderness:

desert

deserted place

dry land

and Levanon (Lebanon): The word Levanon refers to a range of mountains at the north end of the land that Yahweh gave to the Israelis (Israelites). These mountains had snow on them all year long, and the word Levanon means “white” in Semitic languages. The country of Levanon did not yet exist at this time.

Here are some ways to translate this term:

Levanon Mountains (GNT)

Levanon mountain range

Levanon: The Hebrew is literally “the Levanon,” which is difficult to understand. The mountains of Levanon were a long way from where the Israelis were. Possibly it means “over there”, but no English version translates it that way. Many versions omit it, and you may do the same.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse.

Your land will extend from the wilderness in the south to the mountains of Levanon in the north.

Your borders will reach from the desert in the south to the Levanon Mountains in the north (GNT)

1:4b

to the great River Perat (Euphrates)—all the land of the Hitim (Hittites)—

  • It will extend from the great river Perat in the east, and across all the land that belongs to the Het (Heth) people.

  • Your borders will extend to the great Perat River in the east and include all the land of the people of Het.

to the great River Perat: The River Perat was on the east side of the land that God gave to the Israelis (Israelites). The phrase the great River describes the Perat River. The Perat River was very wide.

all the land of the Hitim: The term Hitim refers to one of groups of people who lived in the land of Kena’an (Canaan). The phrase all the land of the Hitim is another way to refer to the land of Kena’an.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It will extend from the great Perat River in the east, across the land that belongs to the Hitim

Your borders will reach from the great river Perat in the east and include all the land of the Hitti people

1:4c

and west as far as the Great Sea.

  • It will go to the Mediterranean Sea in the west.

  • Your borders will extend to the Mediterranean Sea on the west where the sun sets.

and west: The phrase and west refers to the west. The Mediterranean Sea was the western boundary of the land that Yisrael (Israel) received.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Your land will reach to the Mediterranean Sea in the west

to the Mediterranean Sea where the sun sets

as far as the Great Sea: The term the Great Sea refers to the Mediterranean Sea.

General Comment on 1:4

In some languages it may be clearer to reorder the parts of this verse. For example:

Your land will reach from the Negev (Negeb) wilderness in the south to the Levanon (Lebanon) mountains in the north. It will reach from the great Perat (Euphrates) River in the east to the Mediterranean Sea in the west. It will include all the land of the Hitim (Hittites).

title: Joshua 1:5
content:
Section 1:1–9 Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua)

In this section Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into the land that he had promised them. He told Yehoshua that no enemy would be able to oppose him, and that he must obey the law which Yahweh gave to Mosheh (Moses). Yehoshua told the Israelis to prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Yahweh told Yehoshua to be strong and courageous

Yahweh told Yehoshua to lead the people across the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:1–5

Mosheh led the Israeli (Israelite) people through the wilderness for forty years. At the end of the book of Deuteronomy the people were almost ready to enter the land of Kena’an (Canaan), and Mosheh died. Here at the beginning of the book of Yehoshua, Yahweh put Yehoshua in command of the Israelis, and told him to lead them into Kena’an. Yahweh promised to be with Yehoshua and to help him.

1:5a

No one shall stand against you all the days of your life.

  • No enemy will be able to defeat you(sing) as long as you live.

  • Nobody will be able to stand against you all your life.

No one shall stand against you: The expression stand against means “resist” or “oppose.” Yahweh told Yehoshua (Joshua) that no enemy would be able to defeat him.

you: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as you is singular, and refers to Yehoshua.

all the days of your life: The phrase all the days of your life indicates for as long as Yehoshua lived.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

No one will succeed in fighting with you(sing) all your life

No one will be able to defeat you as long as you live (GNT)

1:5b

As I was with Mosheh (Moses), so will I be with you;

  • I will be with you(sing) as I was with Mosheh.

  • I helped Mosheh, and I will help you.

As I was with Mosheh, so will I be with you: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

I will be with you in the same way that I was with Mosheh

I will help you as I helped Mosheh

1:5c

I will never leave you nor forsake you.

  • I will not leave you or abandon you.

  • I will always be with you. I will never leave you.

I will never leave you nor forsake you: The Hebrew verbs that the BSB translates as leave and forsake are close in meaning. The use of two verbs shows emphasis in Hebrew. In some languages the use of two synonymous verbs may not show emphasis. It might be unnatural or confusing to use two words that mean the same thing. If this is true in your language, you could use only one word but add an intensifier, for example:

I will never fail you

I will definitely not abandon you

You could also use two expressions with the same meaning, one positive and one negative. For example:

I will always be with you; I will never abandon you (GNT)

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse.

I will not leave you or forget you (NCV)

title: Joshua 1:6
content:
Section 1:1–9 Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua)

In this section Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into the land that he had promised them. He told Yehoshua that no enemy would be able to oppose him, and that he must obey the law which Yahweh gave to Mosheh (Moses). Yehoshua told the Israelis to prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Yahweh told Yehoshua to be strong and courageous

Yahweh told Yehoshua to lead the people across the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:6–9

God encouraged Yehoshua to be brave and to be faithful to the law.

1:6a

Be strong and courageous,

  • ¶ Be strong and do not be afraid.

  • ¶ Be determined and confident.

Be strong and courageous: The phrases Be strong and [be] courageous have a similar meaning. The use of these two synonyms shows emphasis in Hebrew. In some languages it may be unnatural or confusing to use two words that mean the same thing. If this is true in your language, you could use one word and add an intensifier, for example:

be very brave

You could also use two words with the same meaning, one positive and one negative. For example:

be strong and do not be afraid

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Be determined and confident (GNT)

Be very courageous

1:6b

for you shall give these people the inheritance of the land

  • You will lead these people so that they inherit the land

  • You must lead these people so they can take the land.

for: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as for introduces the reason why Yehoshua (Joshua) must be brave. He must be brave because he was going to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into Kena’an (Canaan).

you shall give these people the inheritance of the land: The clause you shall give these people the inheritance of the land means that Yehoshua will lead the Israelis to take the land that Yahweh will give them. Usually, a person does not inherit something until someone has died. In the book of Yehoshua, Yahweh gave the land of Kena’an as an inheritance to the Israelis. The word inheritance means that the Israelis took possession of the land. Some languages may not use the word inheritance in this way.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

because you will lead them so that they inherit the land

You must lead these people so they can take the land (NCV)

because you will help these people take possession of the land (GW)

you: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as you is emphatic. In English we might express this as:

it is you who will cause this people to inherit the land

If you have emphatic pronouns in your language, you may be able to use one here.

1:6c

that I swore to their fathers I would give them.

  • that I promised their/your fathers that I will give them.

  • This is the land which I vowed to give to their/your ancestors.

that I swore: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as swore can also be translated as:

vowed

promised

to their fathers I would give them: The word fathers refers to the ancestors of the Israelis (Israelites), that is, Avraham (Abraham), Yitshak (Isaac) and Ya’akov (Jacob). Yahweh promised Avraham, Yitshak and Ya’akov that he would give them the land of Kena’an (Canaan). See, for example, Genesis 13:14–15. These people were also the ancestors of Yehoshua (Joshua). In some languages it may be more natural to translate the phrase to their fathers as “to your fathers.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

that I promised their/your fathers that I would give them

which I vowed to give to their/your ancestors

I promised their fathers that I would give them this land (ERV)

title: Joshua 1:7
content:
Section 1:1–9 Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua)

In this section Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into the land that he had promised them. He told Yehoshua that no enemy would be able to oppose him, and that he must obey the law which Yahweh gave to Mosheh (Moses). Yehoshua told the Israelis to prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Yahweh told Yehoshua to be strong and courageous

Yahweh told Yehoshua to lead the people across the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:6–9

God encouraged Yehoshua to be brave and to be faithful to the law.

1:7a

Above all, be strong and very courageous.

  • Be strong and do not be afraid.

  • Be determined and very confident.

Above all, be strong and very courageous: The Hebrew words that the BSB translates as be strong and [be] very courageous are the same as those translated “be strong” and “[be] courageous” in 1:6a. You should translate them the same way in both places.

Above all: The phrase Above all makes the command stronger.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

you must be strong and very courageous

very: There is a textual issue with this part of the verse.

  1. The Hebrew text includes the word very (BSB, RSV, NIV, NET, REB, GW, NJPS, NASB, NLT, KJV)

  2. The Septuagint, the early Greek translation, does not have the word very (GNT, NCV, CEV)

It is recommended that you follow the Hebrew text and include a word that means very.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

You must be strong and very courageous

Be determined and very brave

1:7b

Be careful to observe all the law that My servant Mosheh (Moses) commanded you.

  • You must carefully keep all the commandments which my servant Mosheh commanded you.

  • Be careful to obey all the instructions that Mosheh who served me gave you.

Be careful to observe all the law: The clause Be careful to observe indicates that Yehoshua (Joshua) must follow all the law.

all the law: The phrase all the law refers to the laws and commandments that Yahweh gave to Mosheh to pass on to the Israelis (Israelites).

that My servant Mosheh commanded you: Yahweh referred to Mosheh as My servant in verse 1:2a, and you should translate it the same way in both places.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

You must carefully keep all the commandments that my servant Mosheh commanded you

Be sure to follow all the laws that Mosheh (Moses), my servant, told you to do

1:7c

Do not turn from it to the right or to the left,

  • Do not stop obeying any of them,

  • Follow them exactly.

Do not turn from it to the right or to the left: The phrase Do not turn from it means that Yehoshua (Joshua) must not disobey the law.

The phrase to the right or to the left is an idiom. It indicates that Yehoshua must not disobey the law in any way. He must carefully follow every part of the law.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Do not stop obeying any of the law

follow them exactly (NCV)

Do not walk away from any of these laws

1:7d

so that you may prosper wherever you go.

  • in order that you will be successful wherever you go.

  • Then it will go well with you in everything you do.

so that you may prosper wherever you go: This clause indicates that if Yehoshua (Joshua) obeyed all the laws, he would prosper wherever he went. However, this means more than “wherever he traveled.” It also means that he would be successful in everything he did.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

so that you will succeed wherever you go

Then you will be successful in everything you do (NCV)

then everything will go well with you wherever you go

title: Joshua 1:8
content:
Section 1:1–9 Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua)

In this section Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into the land that he had promised them. He told Yehoshua that no enemy would be able to oppose him, and that he must obey the law which Yahweh gave to Mosheh (Moses). Yehoshua told the Israelis to prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Yahweh told Yehoshua to be strong and courageous

Yahweh told Yehoshua to lead the people across the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:6–9

God encouraged Yehoshua to be brave and to be faithful to the law.

1:8a

This Book of the Law must not depart from your mouth;

  • Never stop reading this book of the law.

  • Always remember what is written in this law book.

This Book of the Law: The phrase This Book of the Law refers to “all the law” in 1:7b.

must not depart from your mouth: The clause must not depart from your mouth means that Yehoshua (Joshua) should always think about the law of Yahweh. He could do this by reading it and speaking it out loud.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Never stop reading this Book of the Law. (NIRV)

Always remember what is written in this law book

Do not stop reciting these laws

1:8b

meditate on it day and night,

  • Think about what it says all day and all night.

  • Say it over to yourself in the day and in the night.

meditate on it: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as meditate can also be translated as “mutter,” or “read in a low voice.” This was a way to keep thinking about something.

day and night: The phrase day and night means always or all the time.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Day and night you must think about what it says (NIRV)

Never stop reciting these teachings (GW)

Study it day and night (NCV)

1:8c

so that you may be careful to do everything written in it.

  • Then you will be able to do everything written in it.

  • Obey everything that it says.

so that you may be careful to do everything written in it: The clause be careful to do everything written in it indicates that Yehoshua (Joshua) must obey all the laws that Mosheh (Moses) wrote down.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Make sure you do everything written in it (NIRV)

Carefully follow every law that Mosheh wrote

1:8d

For then you will prosper and succeed in all you do.

  • Then you will be prosperous, and you will have great success.

  • If you do that then it will go well with you and you will succeed.

For then you will prosper and succeed in all you do: The Hebrew verbs that the BSB translates as will prosper and succeed are similar in meaning. In some languages there may not be two words with such similar meanings. In that case it may be more natural to translate this as “very successful”, or “very prosperous.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then things will go well with you. And you will have great success. (NIRV)

Only then will you prosper and succeed (GW)

If you do that, you will be successful in everything that you do (T4T)

title: Joshua 1:9
content:
Section 1:1–9 Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua)

In this section Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to lead the Israelis (Israelites) into the land that he had promised them. He told Yehoshua that no enemy would be able to oppose him, and that he must obey the law which Yahweh gave to Mosheh (Moses). Yehoshua told the Israelis to prepare to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Yahweh told Yehoshua to be strong and courageous

Yahweh told Yehoshua to lead the people across the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:6–9

God encouraged Yehoshua to be brave and to be faithful to the law.

1:9a

Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous?

  • I have commanded you to be strong and not to be afraid.

  • Remember that I told you to be determined and confident.

Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous?: This is a rhetorical question. It functions as a strong statement and emphasizes a fact that is true.

There are two ways to translate this statement:

  • Use a question, as the BSB does.

  • Use a strong statement. For example:

    I have commanded you, be strong and courageous (GW)

    I repeat, be strong and brave (NET)

    Remember that I have commanded you to be determined and confident (GNT)

Translate this in a way that is natural in your language to express a strong statement.

be strong and courageous: The Hebrew words that the BSB translates as be strong and courageous are the same as in verse 1:6a. You should translate them the same way in both places. Yahweh commanded Yehoshua (Joshua) “be strong and courageous” in 1:6a and 1:7a, and he repeated the command here.

1:9b

Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged,

  • Do not be afraid, but be brave.

  • Do not be at all afraid.

Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged: These two negative commands have the same meaning as the positive commands in 1:9a. This is a way to emphasize those commands. The command Do not be afraid has the same meaning as the command do not be discouraged. In some languages it may not be natural to use two verbs that have the same meaning.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Do not be at all frightened

Do not be frightened, but be brave

1:9c

for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”

  • Yahweh your(sing) God, will be with you wherever you go.”

  • I, Yahweh the God whom you worship, will go with you in everything you do.”

for Yahweh your God is with you: The phrase Yahweh your God is another way to refer to Yahweh. The word for God is added to the personal name of Yahweh. This title for Yahweh indicates that Yahweh is the God whom Yehoshua (Joshua) worships.

As it is Yahweh who is speaking, another way to translate this isː

I, Yahweh your God, am with you(sing)

is with you: This refers to the time when Yahweh was talking to Yehoshua. It is also a promise for the future. You could translate this “will be with you” if that would be more natural in your language.

you: The Hebrew word that the BSB translate as you is singular. It refers to Yehoshua.

wherever you go: The phrase wherever you go is the same phrase as is used at the end of verse 7d.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

I, Yahweh your God, am with you in all you do (NET)

I am Yahweh your God. I will be with you everywhere you go

title: Joshua 1:10
content:
Section 1:10–18 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) to get ready to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section Yehoshua told the Israelis to get ready and prepare food to cross the Yarden River. He reminded the men of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) that they would cross the Yarden River with the rest of the Israelis.

Here are some other possible sections headings:

Preparing to cross the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:10–11

Yehoshua told the Israelis that they will soon cross the Yarden River. They must get food ready to take with them.

1:10

Then Yehoshua commanded the officers of the people:

  • ¶ Then Yehoshua ordered the leaders of the people of Yisrael (Israel):

  • ¶ So Yehoshua (Joshua) summoned the leaders of the Israelis (Israelites) and told them

Then: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as Then is used to show that the next action in the story will take place. Use a connection that is appropriate in your language for the beginning of a new section.

Here are some other ways to translate this wordː

And

So

Yehoshua commanded the officers of the people: In some languages it may be necessary to say that Yehoshua summoned the officers before he spoke to them.

officers of the people: The phrase officers of the people refers to the leaders of each Israeli (Israelite) tribe. Choose a word that indicates a position of responsibility and leadership but not of command over all the Israelis.

Here is another way to translate this phraseː

the leaders of the tribes of Yisrael (Israel)

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

Then Yehoshua (Joshua) commanded the leaders of the people of Yisrael (T4T)

Yehoshua ordered the tribal leaders (CEV)

Then Yehoshua called the leaders of the Israelis (Israelites) together and told them

title: Joshua 1:11
content:
Section 1:10–18 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) to get ready to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section Yehoshua told the Israelis to get ready and prepare food to cross the Yarden River. He reminded the men of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) that they would cross the Yarden River with the rest of the Israelis.

Here are some other possible sections headings:

Preparing to cross the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:10–11

Yehoshua told the Israelis that they will soon cross the Yarden River. They must get food ready to take with them.

1:11a

“Go through the camp and tell the people,

  • “Walk through the camp and give this order to the people.

  • to go through the place where the tents were set up. They should order the people

Go through the camp and tell the people: This verse gives the content of the command that Yehoshua (Joshua) gave to the officers. It is in direct speech. In some languages it may be more natural to use indirect speech. For example:

10Yehoshua commanded the officers of the people 11to pass through the camp and command the people

the camp: The Israelis (Israelites) lived in tents. The word camp refers to the area where they set up their tents.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verseː

walk all through the camping place and tell the people

walk by all the tents and order the people

go through the tent area and command the people

1:11b

‘Prepare your provisions,

  • Say, ‘Make food ready for a journey.

  • to prepare food to take with them.

Prepare your provisions: This clause is a speech within a speech. It continues to the end of the verse. Consider whether direct or indirect speech is more appropriate in your language.

provisions: The term provisions refers to food that the Israelis (Israelites) took with them.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Get your food supplies ready

Prepare food to take with you

1:11c

for within three days you will cross the Yarden (Jordan)

  • The day after tomorrow you will cross the Yarden River,

  • In three days they were going to cross the Yarden River

for: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as for introduces the reason why the Israelis (Israelites) had to get food ready. They were going to cross the Yarden River and conquer the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

within three days: The Israelis counted days inclusively. They began with the day from which they were counting.

Here is another way to translate the phrase within three daysː

the day after tomorrow

you will cross the Yarden: The clause that the BSB translates as you will cross the Yarden indicates that the Israelis will cross the Yarden River. Yehoshua (Joshua) will cross the river with the people. In some languages it may be more natural to use “we(incl)” instead of you.

the Yarden (Jordan): See the note on 1:2b.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Three days from now you will cross the Yarden River (NCV)

the day after tomorrow we(incl) are going to cross the Yarden River

1:11d

to go in and take possession of the land that Yahweh your God is giving you to possess.’”

  • to enter and conquer the land which Yahweh your(plur) God is giving you as your own.’”

  • to enter and take over the land which Yahweh their God was giving them.

to go in and take possession: The clause go in and take possession states the reason why the Israelis (Israelites) were about to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River. The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as take possession indicates that they would take the land to be their own.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

to occupy the land

to conquer the land

the land that Yahweh your God is giving you to possess: The clause the land that Yahweh your God is giving you to possess indicates that Yahweh is giving them the land to be their own. It will belong to them.

your: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as your is plural. Yehoshua (Joshua) and the leaders were included in those who worshiped God. In some languages it may be more natural to say “our(incl) God” instead of “your God.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

in order to occupy the land that Yahweh your God is giving to you as your own

and take the land that Yahweh our(incl) God is giving us to live in

General Comment on 1:11b-d

In some languages it is more natural to put the reason for an action (1:11c-d) before the action itself (1:11b). For example:

11cThe day after tomorrow you will cross the Yarden (Jordan) River 11dto conquer the land which Yahweh your God is giving you. 11bSo get ready food to take with you.

title: Joshua 1:12
content:
Section 1:10–18 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) to get ready to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section Yehoshua told the Israelis to get ready and prepare food to cross the Yarden River. He reminded the men of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) that they would cross the Yarden River with the rest of the Israelis.

Here are some other possible sections headings:

Preparing to cross the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:12–15

The tribes of Re’uven, Gad and half the tribe of Menasheh already chose land on the east side of the Yarden River. In this paragraph Yehoshua reminded the men of these tribes about what they promised Mosheh (Moses). They promised to help the other Israelis conquer the land on the west of the Yarden River. When they had done this, they could return to their own territory.

1:12

But to the Re’uvenim (Reubenites), the Gadim (Gadites), and the half-tribe of Menasheh, Yehoshua said,

  • ¶ Then Yehoshua spoke to the people of the clans of Re’uven and Gad and half the clan of Menasheh and said:

  • ¶ But Yehoshua (Joshua) said this to the clan of Re’uven, the clan of Gad and the half-clan of Menasheh:

But to the Re’uvenim, the Gadim, and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh), Yehoshua said: In verses 1ː10–11 Yehoshua spoke to the leaders of the people of Yisrael (Israel). In verses 1:12–15 he spoke to just two and a half of the tribes. The Hebrew text shows this contrast by putting to the Re’uvenim, the Gadim, and the half-tribe of Menasheh at the beginning of the sentence. Use the connection and sentence order that is most natural in your language.

the Re’uvenim, the Gadim, and the half-tribe of Menasheh: This refers to the people of the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and half the tribe of Menasheh. They already received their territory on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan). See Numbers 32.

tribe: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as tribe can also be translated “branch” or “clan.” The Israelis (Israelites) were divided into twelve tribes. Each tribe was named after one of the sons of Ya’akov (Jacob). The people in the tribe were descendants of that ancestor. Choose a word for a group of people who are descended from a common ancestor. See also the note at Joshua 7:14 where “tribe” and “clan” are used in the same verse.

Here are some other ways to translate the word tribe:

clan

branch

division

descendants

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

Then Yehoshua (Joshua) spoke to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben) and Gad and half the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh)

Yehoshua said to the descendants of Re’uven, the descendants of Gad, and half of the descendants of Menasheh

title: Joshua 1:13
content:
Section 1:10–18 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) to get ready to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section Yehoshua told the Israelis to get ready and prepare food to cross the Yarden River. He reminded the men of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) that they would cross the Yarden River with the rest of the Israelis.

Here are some other possible sections headings:

Preparing to cross the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:12–15

The tribes of Re’uven, Gad and half the tribe of Menasheh already chose land on the east side of the Yarden River. In this paragraph Yehoshua reminded the men of these tribes about what they promised Mosheh (Moses). They promised to help the other Israelis conquer the land on the west of the Yarden River. When they had done this, they could return to their own territory.

1:13a

“Remember what Mosheh the servant of Yahweh commanded you when he said,

  • “Do not forget(plur) what Mosheh, Yahweh’s servant, commanded you.

  • “You know the command that Mosheh, the servant of Yahweh, gave you.

Remember: The verb Remember does not imply that the Israelis (Israelites) had forgotten Mosheh’s command. Yehoshua (Joshua) reminded them of something they already knew.

Here are some ways to translate this wordː

You know

Do not forget

what Mosheh (Moses) the servant of Yahweh commanded you: The term what does not refer to a single word. It refers to all that Mosheh said to the Re’uvenim (Reubenites), the Gadim (Gadites) and half of the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) when they asked for land to settle on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan).

Mosheh the servant of Yahweh: See the note on 1:1a for other ways to translate a similar phrase. Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Remember the command which Mosheh, Yahweh’s servant, gave you

Do not forget what Mosheh, Yahweh’s servant, told you

Remember how the Lord’s servant Mosheh told you (GNT)

when he said: The phrase when he said introduces what Mosheh said. This is direct speech. In some languages it may be more natural to report what Mosheh said using indirect speech.

1:13b

‘Yahweh your God will give you rest, and He will give you this land.’

  • He said, ‘Yahweh your(plur) God will make you secure by giving you this land to settle in.’

  • He told you that Yahweh your God will give you this land where you may live in safety.

Yahweh your God will give you rest: The sentence Yahweh your God will give you rest indicates that Yahweh will give them a permanent place to live. It will be a place where they can live safely.

and He will give you this land: The clause give you this land further explains the clause “give you rest.” The “rest” that Yahweh will give them is the land they are about to enter. It may be more natural to combine the two expressions, for example:

Yahweh your God will provide this land for you, where you may live in safety

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Mosheh (Moses) said, ‘Yahweh your God is giving you this land. It will be a place where you can make your homes and find rest.’

Mosheh said, ‘Yahweh your God will provide this land for you, a place where you may live in safety.’

Mosheh told you that the Lord your God would give you this land on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) as your home. (GNT)

title: Joshua 1:14
content:
Section 1:10–18 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) to get ready to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section Yehoshua told the Israelis to get ready and prepare food to cross the Yarden River. He reminded the men of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) that they would cross the Yarden River with the rest of the Israelis.

Here are some other possible sections headings:

Preparing to cross the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:12–15

The tribes of Re’uven, Gad and half the tribe of Menasheh already chose land on the east side of the Yarden River. In this paragraph Yehoshua reminded the men of these tribes about what they promised Mosheh (Moses). They promised to help the other Israelis conquer the land on the west of the Yarden River. When they had done this, they could return to their own territory.

1:14a

Your wives, your young children, and your livestock may remain in the land that Mosheh gave you on this side of the Yarden.

  • Your(plur) wives, children and livestock may stay here in the land which Mosheh gave you on this side of the Yarden River.

  • Mosheh gave you this land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River. Your wives, children and animals may stay here.

and your livestock: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as livestock refers to cows and also to sheep and goats. Use a general word for domestic animals.

may remain in the land that Mosheh gave you: Yehoshua (Joshua) gave permission to the men of the two and a half tribes to let their families stay in the land east of the Yarden River. The men must cross the Yarden River to help the other Israelis (Israelites).

on this side of the Yarden: The phrase on this side of the Yarden refers to the east side of the Yarden River. Yehoshua spoke as if he were already on the west side of the Yarden.

Here are some ways to translate this part of the verse:

Your wives, your children and your livestock may stay in the land that Mosheh (Moses) gave you here on the east side of the Yarden River

Your wives and children and animals can stay here in the land Mosheh gave you (CEV)

Mosheh gave you this land east of the Yarden River. Your wives, children and animals may stay here

1:14b

But all your mighty men of valor must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers

  • But all your(plur) fighting men must lead your brothers across the Yarden (Jordan), ready for fighting.

  • But all the men who are able to fight should cross the Yarden River first, before the other Israelis (Israelites). You should take your weapons with you.

But: This word marks a contrast between the men and their families. The fighting men went with the other tribes across the Yarden River to fight alongside them. Their families remained where they had settled on the east side of the Yarden.

all your mighty men of valor must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as all your mighty men of valor must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers is more literally “but you shall cross over armed before your brothers, all the mighty men of strength.”

all your mighty men of valor: The phrase all your mighty men of valor refers to every Israeli (Israelite) man who was able to fight. The Israelis did not have a professional army. Every Israeli man who was over twenty years old and was fit to fight was considered a soldier. Avoid a term which will make your readers think that this refers to paid soldiers.

Here are some other ways to translate this phraseː

all the men who can fight

all the soldiers

all the fighting men

must be armed for battle to cross over: The phrase must be armed for battle to cross over indicates that the fighting men must cross the Yarden (Jordan) River carrying their weapons. They must be ready to fight.

ahead of your brothers: The phrase ahead of your brothers indicates that the fighting men of the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben) and Gad and of half the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) must cross the Yarden River in front of the other Israelis (Israelites). All the Israelis were considered to be brothers, or relatives.

your fellow Israelis

your relatives

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But all your men who are able to fight must carry their weapons and cross the Yarden River in front of their fellow Israelis

but all your fighting men, ready for battle, must cross over ahead of your fellow Israelis (NIV)

But your strong warriors, fully armed, must lead the other tribes across the Yarden (Jordan) (NLT)

1:14c

and help them,

  • You(plur) will help them conquer the land.

  • You will fight with them,

and help them: The clause help them indicates that the two and a half tribes must help the other Israelis (Israelites) to fight and conquer the land on the west side of the Yarden River.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

You must continue to help them fight

to help them conquer their territory. Stay with them (NLT)

title: Joshua 1:15
content:
Section 1:10–18 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) to get ready to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section Yehoshua told the Israelis to get ready and prepare food to cross the Yarden River. He reminded the men of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) that they would cross the Yarden River with the rest of the Israelis.

Here are some other possible sections headings:

Preparing to cross the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:12–15

The tribes of Re’uven, Gad and half the tribe of Menasheh already chose land on the east side of the Yarden River. In this paragraph Yehoshua reminded the men of these tribes about what they promised Mosheh (Moses). They promised to help the other Israelis conquer the land on the west of the Yarden River. When they had done this, they could return to their own territory.

1:15a

until Yahweh gives them rest as He has done for you,

  • Yahweh will make the peoples of Yisrael (Israel) secure, as he made you(plur) secure.

  • until Yahweh gives your relatives a place to live as he has given one to you.

until Yahweh gives them rest: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as gives them rest is the same verb as the BSB translated “give you rest” in 1:13b. You may be able to translate it the same way in both places.

as He has done for you: The phrase as He has done for you indicates that Yahweh will give a place of safety to the other Israeli (Israelite) tribes as he did for the two and a half tribes.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

until Yahweh gives all the tribes of Yisrael a secure place to rest just as he did for you

until Yahweh gives your relatives a place to live as he gave one to you

1:15b

and your brothers also possess the land that Yahweh your God is giving them.

  • When they have settled in the land which Yahweh your(plur) God is giving them,

  • After you have conquered the land that Yahweh your God is giving you,

and your brothers also possess the land: The clause and your brothers also possess the land indicates that the Israeli (Israelite) tribes will own the land. The phrase your brothers also is in an emphatic position in the Hebrew sentence. It emphasizes that the other Israeli tribes will receive land just as surely as Gad, Re’uven (Reuben), and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) received it.

that Yahweh your God is giving them: The phrase Yahweh your God occurred in verse 1:9c. You should translate it the same way in both places.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

When they also have settled in the land that Yahweh your God is giving them

After they have conquered the land that Yahweh your God is giving them, just as you did

1:15c

Then you may return to the land of your inheritance and take possession of

  • then you(plur) may come back to your land here and settle in it.

  • you may come back to the land that you have settled in and live here.

Then you may return to the land of your inheritance: The phrase the land of your inheritance means their own land. It was the land that Mosheh (Moses) gave them on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

and take possession of: The noun possession and the verb “possess” come from the same root in Hebrew. The Hebrew text uses both the noun and the verb to show emphasis. Some languages may not be able to show emphasis in this way.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

then you shall return to the land which you have settled and occupy it

then you can come back to your own land and live in it

1:15d

that which Mosheh the servant of Yahweh gave you on the east side of the Yarden.”

  • This is the land which Mosheh, Yahweh’s servant, gave you(plur) on the east side of the Yarden River.”

  • Mosheh (Moses), the one who served Yahweh, gave you this land on the east bank of the Yarden (Jordan) River.”

that which Mosheh the servant of Yahweh gave you: In Hebrew, the phrase used here for the servant of Yahweh is the same as the phrase used in 1:1a. You should translate it the same way in both places.

on the east side of the Yarden: The phrase on the east side of the Yarden indicates that the land which Mosheh gave them was on the east side of the Yarden River.

Some other ways to translate this part of the verse are:

It is the land here on the east side of the Yarden River, which Mosheh, Yahweh’s servant, gave to you

Mosheh gave you this land on the east bank of the Yarden River

General Comment on 1:12–15

Verses 12–15 are similar to Deuteronomy 3:18–20. If you have already translated Deuteronomy, you should compare the similarities and differences so that similar words and phrases are translated in the same way.

title: Joshua 1:16
content:
Section 1:10–18 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) to get ready to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section Yehoshua told the Israelis to get ready and prepare food to cross the Yarden River. He reminded the men of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) that they would cross the Yarden River with the rest of the Israelis.

Here are some other possible sections headings:

Preparing to cross the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:16–18

The tribes who lived on the east side of the Yarden River said that they will obey Yehoshua.

1:16a

So they answered Yehoshua,

  • ¶ The people answered Yehoshua:

  • ¶ Then the clans of Re’uven and Gad and half the clan of Menasheh said to Yehoshua (Joshua):

So: The Hebrew connector that the BSB has translated as So introduces the next event in time. Another way to translate it is:

Then

Translate this connector in a way that is natural to introduce a consecutive event.

they answered Yehoshua: The word they refers to the people of Re’uven (Reuben) and Gad and half the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). This list of names was last given in 1:12. It may be necessary in some languages to specify these names clearly. If you need to do this, you could either repeat the list or use an expression like “those people.” Use whatever is most natural in your language.

Yehoshua: In Hebrew, the name of a main character is repeated often. In some languages it will be more natural to use a pronoun after the first occurrence.

Here is another way to translate this name:

him

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The people answered him

Then the men of the tribes of Re’uven and Gad and half the tribe of Menasheh answered Yehoshua (Joshua). They said

1:16b

“Everything you have commanded us we will do,

  • “Whatever you(sing) command us to do, we will do,

  • “We will do everything that you have told us to do,

Everything you have commanded us we will do: The BSB translated this sentence following the Hebrew order. In Hebrew, the object is placed first for emphasis. Use whatever order is most natural in your language.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Anything you command us to do, we will do (NCV)

We will do everything you have told us (GNT)

1:16c

and everywhere you send us we will go.

  • and wherever you send us, we will go.

  • and we will go anywhere you tell us to go.

and everywhere you send us we will go: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Any place you send us, we will go (NCV)

and will go anywhere you send us (GNT)

title: Joshua 1:17
content:
Section 1:10–18 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) to get ready to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section Yehoshua told the Israelis to get ready and prepare food to cross the Yarden River. He reminded the men of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) that they would cross the Yarden River with the rest of the Israelis.

Here are some other possible sections headings:

Preparing to cross the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:16–18

The tribes who lived on the east side of the Yarden River said that they will obey Yehoshua.

1:17a

Just as we obeyed Mosheh (Moses) in all things, so we will obey you.

  • We(excl) will obey you(sing) in everything as we obeyed Mosheh.

  • We obeyed everything Mosheh told us to do, and we will obey you too.

Just as we obeyed Mosheh in all things, so we will obey you: In some languages it may be more natural to reorder this part of the verse, for example:

We will obey you in everything, just as we used to obey Mosheh

Another way to translate this part of the verse is:

We did everything that Mosheh told us to do, and we will do everything you tell us to do

1:17b

And may Yahweh your God be with you, as He was with Mosheh (Moses).

  • May Yahweh your God be with you, as he was with Mosheh.

  • We pray that Yahweh your God may help you, as he helped Mosheh.

And may Yahweh your God be with you, as He was with Mosheh: These words have the form of a wish or a blessing.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

We pray/ask that Yahweh your God may help you, just as he helped Mosheh

Yahweh your God was always with Mosheh. May he always be with you too.

title: Joshua 1:18
content:
Section 1:10–18 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) to get ready to cross the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section Yehoshua told the Israelis to get ready and prepare food to cross the Yarden River. He reminded the men of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) that they would cross the Yarden River with the rest of the Israelis.

Here are some other possible sections headings:

Preparing to cross the Yarden River

Paragraph 1:16–18

The tribes who lived on the east side of the Yarden River said that they will obey Yehoshua.

1:18a

Anyone who rebels against your order and does not obey your words, all that you command him,

  • If anyone opposes you(sing) and does not obey your orders, no matter what you tell him to do,

  • If anybody refuses to obey a single one of your commands,

Anyone who rebels against your order and does not obey your words: The clauses rebels against your order and does not obey your words use different words to express the same meaning. In some languages it will not be possible to find two expressions with similar meanings to use.

Anyone who rebels against your order: In some languages it may be more natural to translate this as:

if anyone rebels against your commandment

rebels against: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as rebels can also be translated as:

disobeys

opposes

all that you command him: The relative clause all that you command him gives extra emphasis. Find a way that is natural to give emphasis to the people’s promise to obey Yehoshua (Joshua).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

whoever refuses to obey your commands in any way

if anybody opposes your commands and disobeys what you tell them to do

1:18b

will be put to death.

  • he must die.

  • some of us(excl) shall kill him.

will be put to death: This phrase is in the passive voice. Here are some other ways to translate it:

must die

some of us (excl) will kill him

will be killed (ERV)

1:18c

Above all, be strong and courageous!”

  • Be strong and do not be afraid.”

  • Be determined and confident.”

Above all, be strong and courageous: The people encouraged Yehoshua (Joshua) to be strong. The words they used in Hebrew are identical to Yahweh’s word in 1:7a, except that the “very” in 1:7a (“very courageous”) is absent here. See the notes on 1:7a and 1:6a. You should use the same words for strong and courageous as you did in those verses.

title: Joshua 2:1
content:
Section 2:1–24 Yehoshua (Joshua) sent men to explore Yeriho (Jericho) secretly

Yehoshua sent two men to look at Yeriho, a town in the land of Kena’an (Canaan). A woman of Yeriho called Rahav (Rahab) hid the two men so that the king’s soldiers could not find them. She did this because she believed that Yahweh would help the Israelis (Israelites) conquer their land. The men promised Rahav that if she did not betray them, they would rescue her and her family when the Israelis conquered the town. Rahav helped the men escape from Yeriho and they hid in the hills for three days. When the soldiers of Yeriho stopped looking for them, they returned to Yehoshua.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The spies went to Yeriho

The spies and Rahav

Rahav helped the spies

Paragraph: 2:1–7

Yehoshua sent two spies to Yeriho and they entered the house of Rahav. The king of Yeriho sent soldiers to arrest them, but Rahav protected the two men. She hid the spies and told the soldiers that they had already left.

2:1a

Then Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shitim (Shittim), saying,

  • ¶ Then Yehoshua son of Nun sent two men from Shitim where the Israelis (Israelites) were staying to go and explore the land secretly. He said to them:

  • ¶ The Israelis were staying at Shitim Campground. Yehoshua, the son of Nun, sent two men from there to go in secret and learn about the land. He told them:

Then: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Then introduces the next event in the narrative. This is the start of a new section, and some English versions start this section with the word “then.” Translate this in a way that is natural to introduce a new section in your language.

Yehoshua son of Nun: You should translate this the same way you did in 1:1b.

secretly sent two spies from Shitim, saying: In some languages, a literal translation would suggest that Yehoshua spoke to the two men after he sent them away. If this is true in your language, you need to make it clear that Yehoshua gave the orders to the men before they left.

Here is another way to translate this sentence:

Yehoshua sent two men secretly from Shitim as spies. Before he sent them, he said

secretly: The term secretly means that the two men explored the land secretly. They did not want the Kena’anim (Canaanites) to know where they came from or what they were doing.

two spies: These two men were Israelis (Israelites).

spies: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as spies comes from a verb that means “go as an explorer” or “go as a spy.”

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

to explore secretly

to learn about the land of Kena’an (Canaan)

to see where the land is weak

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then Yehoshua (Joshua), the son of Nun, chose two men from the camp at Shitim (Shittim) to go in secret and explore the land. Before he sent them, he said,

The Israelis (Israelites) were staying at Shitim Campground. Yehoshua, the son of Nun, sent two men from there to go secretly and learn about the land. He told them,

from Shitim: Shitim was the place where the Israelis set up their tents on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) River. This place is referred to in Numbers 25:1. It was northeast of the Dead Sea, opposite Yeriho (Jericho).

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

while the Israelis were camping at Shitim

The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Shitim means “acacia.” It is possible that there were several acacia trees in this area.2:1 Dallaire, p. 864. Some English versions use the name “Acacia” instead of the name Shitim. If you are familiar with acacia trees, you may choose to use that term instead of Shitim.

Shitim was the name of this area, but it was not a town or a village. If you must identify it you could call it “Shitim campground” or “Shitim region.”

Here are some other ways to translate this Hebrew word:

Acacia Grove (NLT)

Shitim (Shittim) campground/region

Acacia campground/region

2:1b

“Go, inspect the land, especially Yeriho (Jericho).”

  • “Go(dual) and look at the land and especially the city of Yeriho.”

  • “Go to the land of Kena’an (Canaan) and learn about it. Look particularly at Yeriho.”

Go, inspect the land: The clause Go, inspect the land indicates that the men must go to the land of Kena’an and gather information about how to conquer it.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

Go through the land and find out about it

especially Yeriho: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as especially Yeriho is more literally “and Yeriho.” Yeriho was a town in Kena’an that was across the river from the Israeli (Israelite) camp. It was the most important town in that region. There were many towns in Kena’an. Yehoshua (Joshua) told the men to find out especially about this town because they would attack it first.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Go through the land and find out about it, especially the town of Yeriho (Jericho).

Go and look around the land, particularly Yeriho.

2:1c

So they went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahav (Rahab) and stayed there.

  • Then they(dual) left the camp at Shitim (Shittim). When they arrived at the city of Yeriho, they entered the house of a prostitute to stay there. Her name was Rahav.

  • So, the men went to Yeriho. They stayed for the night at the house of a prostitute named Rahav.

Then: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as Then introduces the next event in time.

Here is another way to translate this conjunction:

and

Translate this conjunction in a way that is natural to introduce the next event in the narrative.

they went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahav: Rahav’s house was in Yeriho (Jericho). It may be clearer to make explicit that they arrived in Yeriho.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

They went to Yeriho and entered the house of a prostitute whose name was Rahav (Rahab)

a prostitute named Rahav: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates literally as prostitute refers to someone who has sex with other people for money.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

a prostitute. Her name was Rahav.

and stayed there: The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as stayed there means “to lie down (to sleep).” The men intended to spend the night there, but they had to flee, and they left during the night.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

they intended to stay there that night

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the men went to the town of Yeriho (Jericho). They entered the house of a prostitute whose name was Rahav (Rahab). They planned to spend the night there.

So the men arrived at Yeriho, and stayed at the house of a prostitute named Rahav

title: Joshua 2:2
content:
Section 2:1–24 Yehoshua (Joshua) sent men to explore Yeriho (Jericho) secretly

Yehoshua sent two men to look at Yeriho, a town in the land of Kena’an (Canaan). A woman of Yeriho called Rahav (Rahab) hid the two men so that the king’s soldiers could not find them. She did this because she believed that Yahweh would help the Israelis (Israelites) conquer their land. The men promised Rahav that if she did not betray them, they would rescue her and her family when the Israelis conquered the town. Rahav helped the men escape from Yeriho and they hid in the hills for three days. When the soldiers of Yeriho stopped looking for them, they returned to Yehoshua.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The spies went to Yeriho

The spies and Rahav

Rahav helped the spies

Paragraph: 2:1–7

Yehoshua sent two spies to Yeriho and they entered the house of Rahav. The king of Yeriho sent soldiers to arrest them, but Rahav protected the two men. She hid the spies and told the soldiers that they had already left.

2:2a

And it was reported to the king of Yeriho (Jericho):

  • The king of Yeriho received a report:

  • While they were there, someone told the king of Yeriho:

And: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as And introduces the next event in the story.

Here is another way to translate this conjunction:

then

Translate this conjunction in a way that is natural to introduce the next event in the narrative.

it was reported to the king of Yeriho: We do not know who told the king of Yeriho.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

somebody told the king of Yeriho (Jericho)

people told the king of Yeriho

the king of Yeriho: There were many towns in the land of Kena’an (Canaan) at that time, and each town had its own king.

2:2b

“Behold, some men of Yisrael (Israel) have come here tonight to spy out the land.”

  • “Listen, some Israeli (Israelite) men came here tonight to spy on this land.”

  • “Tonight, men from Yisrael have come into Yeriho. They have come to find out things about our land.”

Behold: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Behold introduces something that is surprising or unexpected. Some English versions do not translate this word. Some languages may have a grammatical marker which shows this information.

Here are some other ways to translate this word:

look

listen

take note

some men of Yisrael (Israel) have come here tonight: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as some men of Yisrael is more literally “men of the sons of Yisrael.”

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

some Israeli (Israelite) men have come to our town tonight

men from Yisrael are in our town tonight

to spy out the land: The clause to spy out the land means that the men planned to explore the land to find out information about it.

the land: As in 2:1b, the men were spying on the land of Kena’an (Canaan). It may be helpful to say “our land” or “this land” to make it clear that Yeriho (Jericho) was part of the land they referred to.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

to spy on our land

They want to find out things about this land.

title: Joshua 2:3
content:
Section 2:1–24 Yehoshua (Joshua) sent men to explore Yeriho (Jericho) secretly

Yehoshua sent two men to look at Yeriho, a town in the land of Kena’an (Canaan). A woman of Yeriho called Rahav (Rahab) hid the two men so that the king’s soldiers could not find them. She did this because she believed that Yahweh would help the Israelis (Israelites) conquer their land. The men promised Rahav that if she did not betray them, they would rescue her and her family when the Israelis conquered the town. Rahav helped the men escape from Yeriho and they hid in the hills for three days. When the soldiers of Yeriho stopped looking for them, they returned to Yehoshua.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The spies went to Yeriho

The spies and Rahav

Rahav helped the spies

Paragraph: 2:1–7

Yehoshua sent two spies to Yeriho and they entered the house of Rahav. The king of Yeriho sent soldiers to arrest them, but Rahav protected the two men. She hid the spies and told the soldiers that they had already left.

2:3a

So the king of Yeriho (Jericho) sent to Rahav (Rahab) and said,

  • Then the king of Yeriho sent some of his soldiers to Rahav.

  • The king of Yeriho sent men to Rahav,

So: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as So introduces the next event in the story line. Use a connection that is natural in your language.

the king of Yeriho: In some languages it is not natural to repeat the phrase the king of Yeriho as it has just been used in 2:2a. If this is true in your language, you could say “the king” or “he.”

sent to Rahav: In some languages it is clearer to make it explicit that the king sent some of his people. These are the same people who later searched for the spies along the road to the Yarden (Jordan) river. See 2:7a.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So the king of Yeriho sent soldiers/messengers to Rahav.

Then the king sent some people to Rahav (Rahab)

and said: The words and said introduce the direct quotation that follows.

2:3b

“Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house,

  • They said to her: “Bring out the men who entered your house,

  • saying: “Make the people who went into your house come out.

Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house: The clause Bring out the men who came to you indicates that Rahav must make the men come out of her house.

Here are some other ways to translate this direct quotation:

Bring out the men who have come to you and gone into your house.

Make the men who went into your house come out.

In some languages it may be more natural to use an indirect quotation.

They told her to bring out the men who had entered her house.

2:3c

for they have come to spy out the whole land.”

  • because they have come to spy on all this land.”

  • They have come here and intend to learn about all our land.”

for: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as for introduces the reason why Rahav (Rahab) should bring out the two men. She should hand them over because they had come to spy out the country.

they have come to spy out the whole land: The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as spy out was also used in 2:2b. You should translate it in the same way in both places.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

because they have come to spy on our land

because they have come to find out things about the land

General Comment on verse 3b-c

In some languages it may be more natural to reorder parts 3b and 3c so that the reason for the command comes before the command itself. For example:

The men in your house have come to spy out the whole country! Bring them out!” (GNT)

title: Joshua 2:4
content:
Section 2:1–24 Yehoshua (Joshua) sent men to explore Yeriho (Jericho) secretly

Yehoshua sent two men to look at Yeriho, a town in the land of Kena’an (Canaan). A woman of Yeriho called Rahav (Rahab) hid the two men so that the king’s soldiers could not find them. She did this because she believed that Yahweh would help the Israelis (Israelites) conquer their land. The men promised Rahav that if she did not betray them, they would rescue her and her family when the Israelis conquered the town. Rahav helped the men escape from Yeriho and they hid in the hills for three days. When the soldiers of Yeriho stopped looking for them, they returned to Yehoshua.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The spies went to Yeriho

The spies and Rahav

Rahav helped the spies

Paragraph: 2:1–7

Yehoshua sent two spies to Yeriho and they entered the house of Rahav. The king of Yeriho sent soldiers to arrest them, but Rahav protected the two men. She hid the spies and told the soldiers that they had already left.

2:4a

But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them.

  • But Rahav (Rahab) already took the two men and hid them.

  • Before the soldiers got there, Rahav helped the two men to hide.

But: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as But is usually used to indicate the next event in a narrative. However, Rahav hid the two men before the soldiers came to her.2:4 Boling and Wright, p 145–146; Woudstra, p. 70. The BSB translates this conjunction as But to show that something unexpected happened. Choose a connecting word which sounds natural for this situation.

the woman had taken the two men and hidden them: The context of the story shows that Rahav hid the men before she spoke to the soldiers. English versions indicate this by using the pluperfect tense had taken them. Languages have various ways to indicate events that are not reported in order. Translate this clause in a way that is natural for events that are not reported in order.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

Before the soldiers arrived, the woman hid the two men

The woman had already hidden the two men before she spoke to the king’s messengers

2:4b

So she said,

  • Then she said to the soldiers:

  • So she answered them:

So she said: Rahav (Rahab) replied to the people that the king had sent.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

So she answered them,

2:4c

“Yes, the men did come to me, but I did not know where they had come from.

  • “It is true, some men came to me. I did not know where they came from.

  • “You are right that some people came to my house. I don’t know where they were from.

Yes, the men did come to me: Here is another way to translate this phrase:

It is true that the men came to me

That’s right. The men did come to my house.

but I did not know where they had come from: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as where they had come from is more literally “but I did not know from where they were.”

Here is another way to translate this part of the phrase:

but I didn’t know where they were from (NLT)

title: Joshua 2:5
content:
Section 2:1–24 Yehoshua (Joshua) sent men to explore Yeriho (Jericho) secretly

Yehoshua sent two men to look at Yeriho, a town in the land of Kena’an (Canaan). A woman of Yeriho called Rahav (Rahab) hid the two men so that the king’s soldiers could not find them. She did this because she believed that Yahweh would help the Israelis (Israelites) conquer their land. The men promised Rahav that if she did not betray them, they would rescue her and her family when the Israelis conquered the town. Rahav helped the men escape from Yeriho and they hid in the hills for three days. When the soldiers of Yeriho stopped looking for them, they returned to Yehoshua.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The spies went to Yeriho

The spies and Rahav

Rahav helped the spies

Paragraph: 2:1–7

Yehoshua sent two spies to Yeriho and they entered the house of Rahav. The king of Yeriho sent soldiers to arrest them, but Rahav protected the two men. She hid the spies and told the soldiers that they had already left.

2:5a

At dusk, when the gate was about to close, the men went out,

  • Before the city gate was closed this evening, the men went out of the city.

  • At sunset, at the time when the gatekeeper was about to shut the gate, they left Yeriho (Jericho).

At dusk: The phrase At dusk refers to the time when the sun had just set and the sky was becoming dark.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

at sundown (GNT)

at dark (RSV)

when the gate was about to close: Yeriho was a town surrounded by a wall. The word gate refers to the door in the wall through which people entered and left the town. It was closed at night to make the town more secure. The clause when the gate was about to close indicates that the gate was not yet closed.
