the slopes: The phrase the slopes refers to the steep slopes that go down from the hill country eastward to the Dead Sea. This word was used in 10:40 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

the wilderness: The term wilderness indicates the wilderness of Yehudah (Judah). This is a deserted area that lies between the Yehudi hill country and the Dead Sea.12:8 Aharoni, p. 41.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

the Yehudi wilderness (NLT)

and the Negev: The word Negev indicates the southern wilderness area. This word was used in 10:40 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

General Comment on 12:7b-8c

Verse 12:7b described the land of Yisrael (Israel) by naming its northern and southern points. In 12:8a-b the same land is described again by naming its geographical regions. 12:8c describes this land a third time by naming the Kena’ani (Canaanite) peoples who lived there.

12:8c

the lands of the Hitim (Hittites), Amorim (Amorites), Kena’anim (Canaanites), Perizim (Perizzites), Hivim (Hivites), and Yevusim (Jebusites)):

  • This is the land that belonged to the Het (Heth) people, the Amor people, the Kena’an (Canaan) people, the Periz people, the Hiv people, and the Yevus (Jebus) people.

  • This was the land where the Hitti people, the Amor people, the Kena’an people, the Periz people, the Hiw people, and the Yabus people used to live.

the lands of the Hitim, Amorim, Kena’anim, Perizim, Hivim, and Yevusim: These are names of peoples who lived in the land of Yisrael before the Israelis (Israelites) conquered the land. These names occurred in 3:10, but in a different order.

Here is another way to translate this list of peoples:

The people who lived in this region were the Hitim, the Amorim, the Kena’anim, the Perizim, the Hivim, and the Yevusim. These are the kings Yisrael defeated: (NLT)

General Comment on 12:9–24

Verses 12:9–24 is a list of the kings that the Israelis defeated. The BSB translates the words literally according to the Hebrew text. In some languages this may not be natural.

You should translate this list in a way that your language naturally arranges a list. It may be clearer to begin the list with an introduction stating that these are the kings the Israelis defeated. This information was in verse 12:7a and the readers may not make the connection. You can include this introduction at the end of verse 8, as NLT and NCV have done, or at the beginning of verse 9, as GNT has done.

These notes on verses 9–24 include only issues which need explanation.

title: Joshua 12:9
content:
Section 12:1–24 The kings that Yehoshua (Joshua) and the Israelis (Israelites) defeated

In this section there is a list of the kings that the Israelis defeated on the east side and the west side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The kings that the Israelis defeated on both sides of the Yarden River

Paragraph 12:7–24

The kings that the Israelis defeated on the west side of the Yarden River.

12:9

the king of Yeriho (Jericho), one; the king of Ay (Ai), which is near Beyt-El (Bethel), one;

  • These are the kings they defeated: the king of Yeriho, the king of Ay near Beyt-El,

  • The people of Yisrael (Israel) defeated the kings of the following cities: Yeriho City, Ay City (near Beyt-El City),

the king of Yeriho, one: The word one indicates that there was one king of Yeriho. This is a literal translation of the Hebrew word. Most English versions do not include the word one. You should translate this list in a way that your language naturally arranges a list.

the king of Ay, which is near Beyt-El, one: The phrase near Beyt-El indicates that the town of Ay was near the town of Beyt-El.

Here are two different ways to translate verses 9–24:

9 The people of Yisrael defeated the kings of the following cities: Yeriho, Ay (near Beyt-El), 10 Yerushalem (Jerusalem), Hevron (Hebron), 11 Yarmut (Jarmuth), Lakish (Lachish), 12 Eglon, Gezer, 13 Devir (Debir), Geder, 14 Hormah, Arad, 15 Livnah (Libnah), Adulam (Adullam), 16 Makedah (Makkedah), Beyt-El, 17 Tapuah (Tappuah), Hefer (Hepher), 18 Afek (Aphek), Lasharon, 19 Madon, Hatsor (Hazor), 20 Shimron Meron, Akshaf (Achshaph), 21 Ta’anak (Taanach), Megidon (Megiddo), 22 Kedesh, Yakeneam (Jokneam) (in Karmel (Carmel)), 23 Dor (on the coast), Goiim (in Galil (Galilee)), 24 and Tirtsah (Tirzah)—thirty-one kings in all. (GNT)

9 The king of Yeriho

The king of Ay (Ai), near Beyt-El (Bethel)

10 The king of Yerushalem

The king of Hevron

11 The king of Yarmut

The king of Lakish (Lachish)

12 The king of Eglon

The king of Gezer

13 The king of Devir (Debir)

The king of Geder

14 The king of Hormah

The king of Arad

15 The king of Livnah (Libnah)

The king of Adulam (Adullam)

16 The king of Makedah (Makkedah)

The king of Beyt-El (Bethel)

17 The king of Tapuah (Tappuah)

The king of Hefer (Hepher)

18 The king of Afek (Aphek)

The king of Lasharon

19 The king of Madon

The king of Hatsor (Hazor)

20 The king of Shimron-Mer’on (Shimron-meron)

The king of Akshaf (Achshaph)

21 The king of Ta’anak (Taanach)

The king of Megidon (Megiddo)

22 The king of Kedesh

The king of Yakeneam (Jokneam) in Karmel (Carmel)

23 The king of Dor in the town of Naphoth-dor

The king of Goyim in Gilgal

24 The king of Tirtsah (Tirzah).

In all, thirty-one kings were defeated. (NLT)

title: Joshua 12:22
content:
Section 12:1–24 The kings that Yehoshua (Joshua) and the Israelis (Israelites) defeated

In this section there is a list of the kings that the Israelis defeated on the east side and the west side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The kings that the Israelis defeated on both sides of the Yarden River

Paragraph 12:7–24

The kings that the Israelis defeated on the west side of the Yarden River.

12:22

the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Yakeneam (Jokneam) in Karmel (Carmel), one;

  • the king of Kedesh, the king of Yakeneam in Karmel,

  • Kedesh City, Yakeneam City near Karmel Mountain,

Yakeneam in Karmel: The phrase in Karmel indicates that the town of Yakeneam mentioned here was at the northern border of the territory of the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh), near Mount Karmel. There was another town named Yakeneam that was in the territory of the tribe of Efrayim (Ephraim).12:22 Boling and Wright, p. 329.

Here is another way to translate this name:

Yakeneam on Mount Karmel (CEV)

title: Joshua 12:23
content:
Section 12:1–24 The kings that Yehoshua (Joshua) and the Israelis (Israelites) defeated

In this section there is a list of the kings that the Israelis defeated on the east side and the west side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The kings that the Israelis defeated on both sides of the Yarden River

Paragraph 12:7–24

The kings that the Israelis defeated on the west side of the Yarden River.

12:23

the king of Dor in Nafat-Dor (Naphath-dor), one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;

  • the king of Dor City in Nafat-Dor, the king of Goiim in Galil (Galilee),

  • Dor City in Nafat-Dor, Goiim City (in the Galil Region),

Dor in Nafat-Dor: The town of Dor was a seaport on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea south of Karmel (Carmel). It is not clear what the Hebrew word “Nefet (Naphath)” refers to. This word appeared in 11:2 in a similar context. It is recommended that you translate this place name in agreement with the major language version in your area.

English versions differ in how they translate the word Nafat-Dor. Here are some other ways to translate the name of this town:

Dor – near Nefet Dor (NET)

Dor (in Nefet Dor) (NIV)

Dor in the heights of Dor (NASB)

Dor in the district of Dor (NJPS)

Dor (on the coast) (GNT)

Dor in the coast of Dor (KJV)

the king of Goiim: The Hebrew word that the BSB transliterates as Goiim means “nations.” For example:

the king of the nations in Galil (Galilee) (NJB)

Most English versions transliterate this word, as the BSB does. It is recommended that you transliterate it as the BSB does.

in Gilgal: There is a textual issue with the term Gilgal.

  1. The ancient Greek translation, the Septuagint, has the name Galil. (RSV, ESV, NJB, REB, GNT, CEV)

  2. The Hebrew text has the name Gilgal. (BSB, NIV, NET, NCV, NJPS, NLT, GW, KJV)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) and translate this word as “Galil” or “Galil Region.” There is no evidence that there was a place called Gilgal in this area.12:23 Hess, p. 228; Woudstra, p. 206.

title: Joshua 12:24
content:
Section 12:1–24 The kings that Yehoshua (Joshua) and the Israelis (Israelites) defeated

In this section there is a list of the kings that the Israelis defeated on the east side and the west side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The kings that the Israelis defeated on both sides of the Yarden River

Paragraph 12:7–24

The kings that the Israelis defeated on the west side of the Yarden River.

12:24a

and the king of Tirtsah (Tirzah), one.

  • and the king of Tirtsah.

  • and Tirtsah City.

12:24b

So there were thirty-one kings in all.

  • In total they defeated thirty-one kings.

  • They defeated the kings of thirty-one (31) cities.

12:24

So there were thirty-one kings in all: The kings listed in verses 9–24a come to a total of thirty-one kings.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

In total they defeated thirty-one kings

They defeated the kings of thirty-one (31) towns

title: Joshua 13:1
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:1a

Now Yehoshua was old and well along in years,

  • ¶ Yehoshua was very old,

  • ¶ Yehoshua was old and had lived for many years.

Now: The word Now indicates that a new section of the narrative is beginning in this verse. It does not refer to a specific time.

Here are some other ways to translate this connection:

When Yehoshua (Joshua) was very old (NCV)

Many years later (CEV)

There may be a particle or grammatical marker in your language to indicate that a significant time had passed between the events of the previous chapter and chapter 13.

Yehoshua was old and well along in years: The Hebrew idiom that the BSB translates as well along in years is more literally “he had come in days.” This idiom means that Yehoshua was very old. If there is an idiom for great age in your language, you can use it. Or you can say:

Yehoshua was very old

13:1b

and Yahweh said to him,

  • and Yahweh said to him:

  • Then Yahweh told him:

and Yahweh said to him: The clause Yahweh said to him may be restructured according to how you have translated the first part of verse one. For example:

When Yehoshua (Joshua) was very old, the Lord said to him (NCV)

Yehoshua was old, near the end of his life. So the Lord said to him (GW)

13:1c

“You are old and well along in years,

  • “You are very old,

  • “You are old and have lived for many years.

You are old and well along in years: The clause You are old and well along in years contains the same words as 13:1a. It indicates that Yehoshua was very old. If it is not natural to restate this information, it maybe left implicit in the first part of the verse, for example,

Many years later, the Lord told Yehoshua (Joshua), “Now you are very old,” (CEV)

13:1d

but very much of the land remains to be possessed.

  • and there is still much land left to be conquered.

  • There is a lot of land left for you to take.

but: In some languages it may be more natural to begin a new sentence rather than use the conjunction but.

very much of the land remains to be possessed: The clause very much of the land remains to be possessed indicates that there was still a lot of land that the Israelis (Israelites) had not conquered. In some languages it may be more natural to translate this clause in an active voice, for example:

There is still much land for you to take (NCV)

There is still a lot of land that the Israelis must conquer

title: Joshua 13:2
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:2–6

These verses are a list of all the towns and regions that the Israelis (Israelites) had not yet conquered. Use a format that is appropriate to list place names in your language. Verse 2a introduces the list.

13:2a

This is the land that remains:

  • These are the places that you still must conquer:

  • This is the territory that remains for you to take:

This is the land that remains: The phrase the land that remains indicates the places in Kena’an (Canaan) that Yisrael (Israel) has not yet conquered. It may be helpful to include some implicit information. For example:

This is the land that has not yet been conquered

13:2b

All the territory of the Pelishtim (Philistines) and the Geshurim (Geshurites),

  • all the land where the Pelishtim and the Geshurim live.

  • all the districts that belong to the Filisti people and the Geshur people.

All the territory of the Pelishtim: The territory of the Pelishtim were on the coastal plain of the Mediterranean Sea in the southwestern part of Kena’an.

Pelishtim: The Pelishtim indicates a group of people who lived in several large towns near the Mediterranean Sea.

Here is another way to translate this word:

Filisti people

The Pelishtim are mentioned several times in Genesis. If you have already translated Genesis, you should translate this name the same way you did there. See, for example, Genesis 10:14.

and the Geshurim (Geshurites): The phrase the Geshurim indicates the land where the Geshur people lived. The Geshur people were mentioned in Joshua 12:5 and you should translate the term the same way in both places.

title: Joshua 13:3
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:3a-d

The BSB adds parentheses around part of this section to make it clear that this is a description of the “territory of the Pelishtim (Philistines) and the Geshurim (Geshurites).” These parentheses are not in the Hebrew text. You may find that parentheses are helpful, or there may be some other way to connect verses 3a-d to verse 2.

13:3a

from the Shihor east of Mitsrayim (Egypt) to the territory of Ekron on the north

  • Their land extends from the Shihor Canal which is east of Mitsrayim, and north as far as the border of Ekron,

  • That area goes south to the Shihor Canal at the east border of Mitsrayim, and it goes north to Ekron City.

from the Shihor east of Mitsrayim: The term Shihor indicates a canal of the Nile River in the eastern delta of Mitsrayim, near the present-day Suez Canal. The Shihor Canal was on the east side of Mitsrayim, and it was the south boundary of the Pelishti (Philistine) and Geshuri (Geshurite) region.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

The Pelishti and Geshuri region goes south to the Shihor Canal which is east of Mitsrayim

to the territory of Ekron on the north: The phrase to the territory of Ekron on the north indicates that Ekron was the north boundary of the Pelishti and Geshuri region. Ekron was a town of the Pelishti people and is mentioned in 13:3d.

13:3b

(considered to be Kena’ani (Canaanite) territory)—

  • which is considered to be Kena’ani territory.

  • All that area formerly belonged to the Kena’an (Canaan) people.

considered to be Kena’ani territory: The clause considered to be Kena’ani territory indicates that Ekron was considered to be part of Kena’an because the Pelishtim (Philistines) took it from the original Kena’ani settlers.13:3 Woudstra, p. 210.

13:3c

that of the five Pelishti (Philistine) rulers

  • There are five Pelishti rulers,

  • There are five kings of Filisti people who rule in these five cities:

that of the five Pelishti rulers: The clause that of the five Pelishti rulers indicates that each Pelishti town had its own ruler. The towns are listed in the next part of the verse.

13:3d

of Azah (Gaza), Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gat (Gath), and Ekron,

  • of Azah, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gat, and Ekron.

  • Azah City, Ashdod City, Ashkelon City, Gat City, and Ekron City.

of Azah: The name Azah refers to a Pelishti (Philistine) town in southwest Kena’an (Canaan), near the Mediterranean Sea.

Ashdod: The name Ashdod indicates a Pelishti town 22 miles south of Yafo (Joppa) on the Mediterranean Sea.

Ashkelon: The name Ashkelon indicates a Pelishti town on the Mediterranean Sea 32 miles south of Yafo.

Gat: The name Gat indicates a Pelishti town 25 miles southeast of the town of Yafo. In later times King David fought against Galyat (Goliath), who came from Gat.

and Ekron: The name Ekron indicates a Pelishti town 20 miles southeast of Yafo.

13:3e

as well as that of the Avim (Avvites);

  • There is also the land where the Avim people live

  • The district of the Avim people

as well as that of the Avim: The phrase that of the Avim indicates that the Israelis (Israelites) must also conquer the region where the Avim people lived. This is a third region that is mentioned, and it is parallel to the “territory of the Pelishtim (Philistines)” and the “territory of the Geshurim (Geshurites)” (13:2b). In some languages it may be clearer to start a new sentence here.

Avim: The Avim are mentioned in Deuteronomy 2:23. They lived in villages near Azah (Gaza).13:3 Boling and Wright, p. 338.

Here are some other ways to translate the word Avim:

Avim (NRSV)

Avim people

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

There is also the region of the Avim (Avvim) people in the south that has not been conquered

title: Joshua 13:4
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:4a

to the south,

  • in the south.

  • in the south has not been conquered.

to the south: The Avim (Avvim) lived in the south of the Pelishti (Philistine) territory. This prepositional phrase describes the Avim people and is a continuation of verse 3e. You should translate it as a single phrase.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

The region of the Avim people in the south has also not been conquered

13:4b

all the land of the Kena’anim (Canaanites),

  • There is also all the land of the Kena’anim,

  • There are also the districts of all the Kena’an (Canaan) people,

all the land of the Kena’anim: The phrase the land of the Kena’anim introduces a second group of towns. These are places in the north that are named in verses 4–6.13:4 Woudstra, p. 211.

For example:

In the north, the following area has not yet been conquered: all the land of the Kena’anim, including Me’arah (Mearah) (which belongs to the Tsidonim (Sidonians)) stretching northward to Afek (Aphek) on the border of the Amorim (Amorites). (NLT)

The term “Kena’ani (Canaanite)” is used here as a term for the inhabitants of Kena’an. This is different from how it is used in verse 13:3b, where it refers to a specific group of Kena’an people.

13:4c

from Me’arah of the Tsidonim

  • from Me’arah City which belongs to the Tsidonim,

  • including Me’arah City which belongs to the Tsidoni (Sidonian) people

from Me’arah: There is a textual issue in this verse.

  1. The Hebrew text says Me’arah. We do not know where the town of Me’arah was. (BSB, RSV, ESV, NJB, NABRE, NJPS, GW, NLT, GNT, KJV)

  2. Some scholars suggest that we should divide the word Me’arah (Mearah) and modify the vowels so that it becomes two Hebrew words “from Arah.” The town of Arah is also unknown. (NIV, NET, CEV)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) along with the Hebrew text.

of the Tsidonim (Sidonians): The clause of the Tsidonim indicates that town of Me’arah was ruled by the people of Tsidon (Sidon). Tsidon was on the Mediterranean coast in the north.

13:4d

to Afek (Aphek), as far as the border of the Amorim (Amorites);

  • and on to Afek, on the Amori (Amorite) border.

  • and going north to Afek City on the border of the Amor people.

to Afek: The term Afek indicates a town that was probably southeast of Byblos in Levanon (Lebanon).13:4 Rasmussen p. 226.

as far as the border of the Amorim: The phrase as far as the border of the Amorim indicates that “Afek” was on the northern border of the land that was ruled by the Amori people. The next people further north from there were the Amori people.

title: Joshua 13:5
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:5a

the land of the Givlim (Gebalites);

  • There is also the land of the Givlim,

  • There are also the districts of the Geval (Gebal) people,

the land of the Givlim: It may be more natural to begin a new sentence at the beginning of verse 5, for example:

It also includes the land of the Geval people

the Givlim: The term Givlim indicates the people who lived in Geval, a town on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, eighteen miles northeast of modern Beirut.13:5 Rasmussen, p. 235. The ancient Greek name of this town was Byblos, and some English versions (NIV11, NET) refer to it by this name. The modern Arabic name for this town is Jubayl.

13:5b

and all Levanon (Lebanon) to the east,

  • and all of Levanon eastward

  • all of Levanon to the east,

and all Levanon to the east: The phrase all Levanon to the east indicates that the rest of Levanon east of Geval (Gebal) must still be conquered.

The places named in 13:5c describe the southern and northern limits of all Levanon.

13:5c

from Ba’al-Gad (Baal-gad) below Mount Hermon to Levo-Hamat (Lebo-hamath).

  • from Ba’al-Gad at the foot of Mount Hermon to the entrance into Hamat (Hamath) City,

  • from Ba’al-Gad at the base of Mount Hermon in the south, to Hamat Mountain Pass in the north.

from Ba’al-Gad below Mount Hermon: The town of Ba’al-Gad was mentioned in Joshua 11:17. It was in the Levanon (Lebanon) Valley at the western foot of Hermon Mountain. Ba’al-Gad was at the southern point Levanon Valley.

Here is another way to spell the word Ba’al-Gad:

Ba’al (Baal) Gad (NIV, NET)

below Mount Hermon: The phrase below Mount Hermon indicates that the town of Ba’al-Gad was at the base of Hermon Mountain.

to Levo-Hamat: There are two ways to interpret the phrase Levo-Hamat.

  1. The Hebrew text reads lebo hamath. The Hebrew word lebo means “entrance.” Some English versions translate this as the entrance of Hamat or the Hamat Mountain Pass. For example:

    the border of Hamat (Hamath) (GW) (GW, RSV, NJB, GNT, CEV, KJV)

  2. Some English versions translate this as a proper name, Lebo Hamat. For example:

    Lebo Hamat (NIV) (BSB, NIV, ESV, NCV, NLT, NET, NJPS, REB)

It is difficult to know which is the proper interpretation. It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1) unless the national version used in your area uses interpretation (2).

Levo-Hamat (Lebo-hamath): The town of Levo-Hamat and its mountain pass occurs several times in the Bible in boundary lists. See, for example, Numbers 13:21 and Judges 3:3. Hamat town was the northern point of the Levanon (Lebanon) Valley.

title: Joshua 13:6
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:6a

All the inhabitants of the hill country from Levanon (Lebanon) to Misrefot-Mayim (Misrephoth-maim)—

  • and all the inhabitants of the mountain region from Levanon to Misrefot-Mayim,

  • There are also all the people who live in the mountain range that runs from Levanon to Misrefot-Mayim,

All the inhabitants of the hill country: The phrase the inhabitants of the hill country indicates the people who lived in the mountain range that runs from north to south in Levanon, away from the coastal plain.

from Levanon to Misrefot-Mayim: The phrase from Levanon to Misrefot-Mayim indicates that the mountain range extended from the north part of the country of Levanon south to the town of Misrefot-Mayim.

Misrefot-Mayim: The location of the town of Misrefot-Mayim is uncertain. It was probably north of Galil (Galilee) and not far from Tsidon (Sidon), near the Litani River.13:6 Rasmussen, p. 245.

Here is another way to spell Misrefot-Mayim:

Misrephoth Maim (NIV, NET)

13:6b

all the Tsidonim (Sidonians)—

  • that is, all the Tsidonim.

  • who are under the rule of Tsidon City.

all the Tsidonim: The phrase the Tsidonim indicates that the people who lived in the mountain range of Levanon (Lebanon) were Tsidonim. This region was governed by Tsidon. The town of Tsidon was twenty-four miles southwest of Beirut on the Lebanese coast.

In some languages it may be more natural to reorder verses 6a and 6b. For example:

This includes all the territory of the Tsidonim, who live in the hill country between the Levanon Mountains and Misrephoth Maim (GNT)

13:6c

I Myself will drive out before the Israelis (Israelites).

  • I am the one who will drive them out before the Israelis.

  • It is I who will drive the people mentioned above out of the land ahead of the Israelis.

I Myself will drive out: The Hebrew pronoun that the BSB translates as Myself emphasizes that Yahweh is the one who will give the Israelis victory. Use the most natural way in your language to show this emphasis.

before the Israelis: The phrase before the Israelis indicates that God will give the Israelis victory as they move forward to conquer the land.

13:6d

Be sure to divide it by lot as an inheritance to Yisrael (Israel),

  • Be sure to give this land to Yisrael as an inheritance,

  • However, Yehoshua (Joshua), you must distribute the land to Yisrael for them to own,

Be sure to: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Be sure to introduces a command. It contrasts what is Yehoshua’s responsibility with what Yahweh would do for the Israelis (Israelites).

Here are some other ways that English versions emphasize this command:

So be sure to give this land to Yisrael as a special possession (NLT)

All you have to do is to distribute the territory as a heritage for the Israelis as I have commanded you (NJB)

divide it by lot as an inheritance to Yisrael (Israel): The clause divide it by lot as an inheritance to Yisrael indicates that Yehoshua must divide the land among the tribes of Yisrael who would live on the west side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

as an inheritance: The phrase as an inheritance indicates that the Israelis received the land of Kena’an (Canaan) as a gift from Yahweh to them. It would then belong to them and their descendants forever if they obeyed Yahweh. The word “inheritance” was used in 11:23, and you should translate it the same way in both places.

13:6e

as I have commanded you.

  • as I have told you.

  • as I commanded you.

as I have commanded you: Yahweh gave this command to Mosheh (Moses) in Numbers 33:54. Mosheh told Yehoshua (Joshua) to carry out this command in Deuteronomy 31:7.

title: Joshua 13:7
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:7a

Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance

  • Now, divide up this land as an inheritance

  • So, divide this land

Now therefore: The Hebrew words that the BSB translates as Now therefore are literally “and now.” The word Now indicates that the time has arrived for Yehoshua to divide the land between the Israeli (Israelite) tribes. Use a joining word that is natural to connect this clause with the preceding clause.

divide this land as an inheritance: The clause divide this land as an inheritance has the same meaning as the command in 13:6d. It is repeated for emphasis, using different words.

13:7b

to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh).”

  • for the nine clans and the half-clan of Menasheh.”

  • for the nine clans and half the clan of Menasheh to own.”

to the nine tribes: The phrase to the nine tribes indicates the nine tribes of Yisrael (Israel) that had not yet received land. These nine tribes are Yehudah (Judah), Efrayim (Ephraim), Benyamin (Benjamin), Shim’on (Simeon), Zevulun (Zebulun), Yisakar (Issachar), Asher, Naftali (Naphtali), and Dan.

and the half-tribe of Menasheh: The phrase the half-tribe of Menasheh indicates those people of the tribe of the Menasheh who chose to live west of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

There is a textual issue in this verse. The Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation, includes another clause at the end of verse 13:7 which is not in the Hebrew text. Most English versions do not include this clause, but it is found in the NJB:

from the Yarden as far as the Great Sea in the west, you must give it them; the Great Sea will be their limit (NJB)

It is recommended that you do not include this clause unless it is included in the majority language version in your area.

title: Joshua 13:8
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:8a

The other half of Menasheh,

  • ¶ Half the clan of Menasheh

  • ¶ The other half of the clan of Menasheh

The other half of Menasheh: The phrase The other half of Menasheh indicates those people from the tribe of Menasheh who chose to live on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) River. This story is first told in Numbers 32.

In some languages it may be more natural to reverse the order of 8a and 8b, for example:

The tribes of Re’uven (Reuben) and Gad and the other half of the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) had already received their land on the east side of the Yarden River

13:8b

along with the Re’uvenim (Reubenites) and Gadim (Gadites), had received the inheritance

  • and the clans of Re’uven and Gad received their inheritance

  • and the clans of Re’uven and Gad had already received their land

along with the Re’uvenim and Gadim, had received the inheritance: The terms the Re’uvenim and Gadim indicate the tribe of Re’uven and the tribe of Gad.

Here is another way to translate these names:

the tribe of Re’uven and the tribe of Gad

13:8c

Mosheh (Moses) had given them beyond the Yarden (Jordan) to the east,

  • which Mosheh gave them on the east side of the Yarden.

  • on the east side of the Yarden River.

Mosheh had given them beyond the Yarden to the east: The phrase beyond the Yarden to the east indicates that the land Mosheh gave these tribes was on the east side of the Yarden River.

13:8d

just as Mosheh the servant of Yahweh had assigned to them:

  • Mosheh, the servant of Yahweh, gave this land to them.

  • Mosheh, Yahweh’s servant, gave them this land.

just as Mosheh (Moses) the servant of Yahweh had assigned to them: The phrase Mosheh the servant of Yahweh was used in Joshua 1:1 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

Verse 8d repeats information from 8c, and some English versions combine these two phrases together. Here is another way to translate this verse:

The tribes of Re’uven (Reuben) and Gad and the other half of the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) had already received the land that Mosheh, the Lord’s servant, had given them; it was on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) River. (GNT)

title: Joshua 13:9
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:9a

The area from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley,

  • Their territory extended from Aroer on the edge of the valley of the Arnon River,

  • Their land started at Aroer City at the Arnon River gorge.

The area from Aroer: In some languages it may be more natural to add implicit information, for example:

Their land started at Aroer (NCV)

Aroer: The term Aroer indicates a town that was along the Arnon River.

on the rim of the Arnon Valley: The clause on the rim of the Arnon Valley indicates that the town of Aroer was on the bank of the Arnon River, in the Arnon River Valley.

Here is another way to translate this clause:

Aroer was on the bank of the Arnon River, in the valley.

Arnon Valley: The term Arnon Valley appeared in 12:1 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

13:9b

along with the city in the middle of the valley,

  • including the town that is halfway along the valley,

  • It included the city that is halfway along the Arnon River gorge,

along with the city in the middle of the valley: The phrase in the middle of the valley indicates that the town was halfway along the valley. The town is not named.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

including the town that is halfway along the Arnon River Valley

13:9c

the whole plateau of Meydeva (Medeba) as far as Divon (Dibon),

  • to the plain beyond Meydeva, as far as Divon City.

  • and the whole of the Meydeva Plateau to Divon City.

the whole plateau of Meydeva: The word plateau indicates a plain. The plateau of Meydeva was a high, flat area between the Arnon River in the south and Heshbon in the north. It was 600–700 meters high.13:9 Woudstra, p. 216.

Meydeva: The town of Meydeva was a Moavi (Moabite) town that the Israelis (Israelites) captured from King Sihon (see Numbers 21:21–32). Today it is the town of Madaba in Yarden (Jordan), twenty miles south of Amman.13:9 Rasmussen, p. 244.

as far as Divon: The phrase as far as Divon indicates that the tableland of Meydeva stretched from Meydeva in the north to Divon in the south. Divon was one of the Moavi towns that the Israelis captured. Its name today is Dhiban and it is thirteen miles east of the Dead Sea and three miles north of the Arnon Gorge.13:9 Rasmussen, p. 244.

title: Joshua 13:10
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:10a

and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorim (Amorites) who reigned in Heshbon,

  • It extended to all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorim, who reigned in Heshbon,

  • It included all the cities ruled by King Sihon of the Amorim, who ruled from Heshbon City,

and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorim: The phrase all the cities refers to all the towns in the territory that King Sihon ruled.

the Amorim: The word Amorim can be used in two senses. It can refer to a group of people who lived in the mountainous region of Kena’an (Canaan). This is the way it is used here. It can also be a synonym for “Kena’ani (Canaanite),” and refer to the whole population of Kena’an.

The word Amorim occurred in Joshua 2:10 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

who reigned in Heshbon: The clause who reigned in Heshbon indicates that Heshbon was the capital town of King Sihon. Heshbon was about 25 kilometers northeast of the Dead Sea, and southwest of present-day Amman, the capital city of Yarden (Jordan).13:10 Bratcher and Newman, p. 171.

It may be helpful to start a new sentence here. Here is another way to translate this clause:

Their territory extended as far as the towns of King Sihon of the Amorim, who reigned in Heshbon

13:10b

as far as the border of the Amonim (Ammonites);

  • and extended to the border of the Amonim.

  • and as far as the area where the Amon (Ammon) people lived.

as far as the border of the Amonim: The phrase as far as the border of the Amonim indicates that the territory Mosheh (Moses) assigned to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and half the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) extended to the border of the Amon people.

Amonim: The term Amonim indicates a group of people who lived in the country of Amon and whose capital city was Rabbah-ammon. This term was used in Joshua 12:2 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

title: Joshua 13:11
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:11a

also Gilead and the territory of the Geshurim (Geshurites) and Ma’akatim (Maacathites),

  • It extended to Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurim and the Ma’akatim,

  • It included Gilead Region, and the place where the Geshur people and the Ma’akah (Maacath) people lived.

also Gilead: The term Gilead indicates the mountainous region north of the Dead Sea. The Gilead Region stretched from the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) River to the desert.

The term Gilead occurred in 12:2 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

and the territory of the Geshurim: The term Geshurim indicates the people of the kingdom of Geshur. They were a small group who lived northeast of the Sea of Galil (Galilee).

The term Geshurim occurred in 12:5 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

and Ma’akatim: The term Ma’akatim indicates the people of Ma’akah. This was a small kingdom in modern Aram (Syria) whose people continued to live in their land.

The term Ma’akatim occurred in 12:5 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

It may be more natural to begin a new sentence at the beginning of verse 11. Here is another way to translate it:

It also included Gilead Region, and the region where the Geshur people lived and the Ma’akah people lived

13:11b

all of Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salkah (Salecah)—

  • and all of Mount Hermon and all of Bashan as far as Salkah.

  • It included all of Mount Hermon and Bashan Region as far as Salkah City.

all of Mount Hermon: The phrase all of Mount Hermon indicates Mount Hermon and its surrounding foothills. Mount Hermon was a high mountain that was the northern limit of Yehoshua’s (Joshua’s) conquests. It was in the northeast part of Yisrael (Israel). It formed the northwest limit of King Og’s kingdom.

The term Mount Hermon occurred in Joshua 11:3 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

and all Bashan: The territory of Bashan stretched south to the hills of northern Gilead, where Sihon’s territory began, and west to the Sea of Galil (Galilee). The east boundary of the Bashan territory was the desert.

The term Bashan occurred in Joshua 9:10| and you should translate it the same way in both places.

as far as Salkah: The name Salkah indicates a town on the east boundary of the territory of Bashan. Salkah was southeast of the Sea of Galil.

The term Salkah occurred in 12:5 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

title: Joshua 13:12
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:12a

the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan,

  • Those places were all the kingdom of Og in Bashan,

  • All these places named above were the kingdom of King Og in Bashan Territory,

the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan: The phrase the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan indicates all the places that were named in the previous verse. It may be helpful to make this explicit. For example:

that is, the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan (NIV)

These previously mentioned places were all included in the land of King Og, who ruled in Bashan Territory

The story of how Mosheh (Moses) and the Israelis (Israelites) defeated the kingdom of Og in Bashan is found in Numbers 21:33–35.

13:12b

who had reigned in Ashtarot (Ashtaroth) and Edre’i (Edrei)

  • who reigned in Ashtarot and Edre’i,

  • who ruled in Ashtarot City and Edre’i City.

who had reigned in Ashtarot: The town of Ashtarot was the capital city of King Og. It was twenty-two miles east of the Sea of Galil (Galilee).13:12 Rasmussen. p. 227.

and Edre’i: King Og also had a residence in the town of Edre’i. Edre’i was mentioned in Joshua 12:4, and you should translate it the same way in both places.

13:12c

and had remained as a remnant of the Refaim (Rephaim).

  • and who was the last of the Rephaite people.

  • King Og was the last of the Repha people,

and had remained as a remnant of the Refaim: The clause and had remained as a remnant of the Refaim is placed in parentheses in some English versions to indicate that the translators consider this to be background information. There are no parentheses in the Hebrew text or the BSB.

remnant: The word remnant indicates that only a few of the Refaim were still alive.

Refaim: The word Refaim occurred in Joshua 12:4 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

13:12d

Mosheh (Moses) had struck them down and dispossessed them,

  • Mosheh defeated them and drove them out of their land.

  • but Mosheh defeated him and took their land.

Mosheh had struck them down and dispossessed them: The pronoun them indicates the two kings, King Sihon and King Og. It may be more natural to make this information explicit, for example:

Mosheh had conquered and dispossessed these two kings (NJB)

Mosheh had defeated Sihon and Og and their people and had forced them to leave their land (CEV)

title: Joshua 13:13
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:13a

but the Israelis (Israelites) did not drive out the Geshurim (Geshurites) or the Ma’akatim (Maacathites).

  • But the Israelis did not drive out the Geshurim and the Ma-acathites,

  • However, the Israelis did not make the Geshur people and the Ma’akah (Maacah) people leave,

but: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as but contrasts what follows with the information in 13:11a. Yahweh told the Israelis to conquer the land of the Geshurim and Ma’akatim, but they did not.

Here are some other ways to translate this word:

but (NIV, NET)

however (GNT, NJB)

the Israelis (Israelites) did not drive out the Geshurim (Geshurites) or the Ma’akatim (Maacathites): The clause did not drive out indicates that the Israeli (Israelite) army did not defeat the Geshur people and the Ma’akah people and did not drive them out of their land.

13:13b

So Geshur and Ma’akah dwell among the Israelis to this day.

  • and so they still live among the Israelis to this day.

  • and today they still live among the Yisrael (Israel) people.

Geshur and Ma’akah (Maacath): The terms Geshur and Ma’akah are another way to refer to the Geshurim and Ma’akatim.

dwell among the Israelis to this day: The clause dwell among the Israelis to this day indicates that the Geshur people and the Ma’akah people still lived among the Israelis.

to this day: The phrase this day indicates the time that the author was writing the book of Yehoshua (Joshua).

title: Joshua 13:14
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:14a

To the tribe of Levi, however, Mosheh had given no inheritance.

  • The clan of Levi was the only one to whom Mosheh did not give any land as their inheritance.

  • But Mosheh did not give any land to the clan of Levi.

To the tribe of Levi: In the Hebrew text the phrase that the BSB translates as To the tribe of Levi is at the beginning of the sentence to show emphasis. The tribe of Levi was the only tribe that did not receive land as their gift from Yahweh.

In some languages it may not be natural to begin a sentence with this phrase. Use a natural way in your language to emphasize that the tribe of Levi was different from the other tribes.

Mosheh (Moses) had given no inheritance: The clause Mosheh had given no inheritance indicates that Mosheh did not assign any land to the tribe of Levi.

13:14b

The offerings made by fire to Yahweh, the God of Yisrael (Israel), are their inheritance,

  • The sacrifices burned on the altar to Yahweh God of Yisrael are what the Levites inherited,

  • Instead, he gave them the burned sacrifices that were offered to Yahweh, the God of Yisrael,

The offerings made by fire to Yahweh, the God of Yisrael, are their inheritance: The phrase offerings made by fire refers to sacrifices that were partially burned. In Numbers 18:21–32| Yahweh told Aharon (Aaron) that the Levites could eat some of these offerings.

There is a textual issue in this verse:

  1. The Hebrew text includes the words offerings made by fire. For example:

    To the tribe of Levi alone Mosheh gave no inheritance. The offerings by fire to the Lord God of Yisrael are their inheritance (ESV) (BSB, ESV, RSV, NIV84, NET, GW, NJPS, NLT, GNT, CEV, KJV)

  2. The Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation, does not include the words offerings made by fire. For example:

    To the tribe of Levi alone no heritage was given; Yahweh, God of Yisrael (Israel), was his heritage (NJB) (NJB, NEB, REB, NABRE)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) and the Hebrew text.

offerings made by fire: There are two ways to interpret the phrase offerings made by fire:

  1. It means offerings that are burned. For example:

    the sacrifices burned on the altar to the Lord God of Yisrael (GNT) (BSB, GNT, RSV, NET, ESV, NIV84, GW, NJPS, NLT, KJV)

  2. It means food offerings. For example:

    the food offerings presented to the Lord, the God of Yisrael (NIV11) (NIV11)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1). This agrees with most English versions and the Hebrew lexicons.

Here is another way to translate the phrase offerings made by fire:

offerings burned on the altar (NLT)

are their inheritance: The phrase their inheritance indicates that God gave the tribe of Levi the offerings of the Israelis (Israelites) instead of land.

13:14c

just as He had promised them.

  • as Yahweh said to Mosheh (Moses).

  • as Yahweh told Mosheh and the Israelis.

just as He had promised them: The clause just as He had promised them indicates that Yahweh told this to Mosheh. This is recorded in Deuteronomy 18:1–2.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

as the Lord had told Mosheh (GNT)

them: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as them is singular. Some English versions, such as the BSB, NIV, and KJV, observe that God spoke to all the Israelis (Israelites) as well as to Mosheh, and so they translate this word as them.

title: Joshua 13:15
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:15

This is what Mosheh had given to the clans of the tribe of Re’uven:

  • ¶ Mosheh gave land to the clan of Re’uven for each sub-clan.

  • ¶ Mosheh assigned the following land to the sub-clans of the clan of Re’uven.

This verse begins with a Hebrew word that is often translated as “and.” This word introduces the next event in the story. Many English versions do not translate this word.

This is what Mosheh (Moses) had given to the clans of the tribe of Re’uven (Reuben): The Hebrew text is more literally “Mosheh gave to the tribe of the sons of Re’uven.” The phrase This is what is not in the Hebrew text. The BSB has supplied this phrase to make clear what Mosheh gave to the tribe of Re’uven. Mosheh assigned land to the tribe of Re’uven in Numbers 32.

to the clans: The phrase to the clans indicates that each clan or group of families within the tribe of Re’uven received their own portion of land. See how you translated the words “clan” and “family” in Joshua 7:14.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

Mosheh had given each family group from the tribe of Re’uven some land. (NCV)

Mosheh had assigned the following area to the clans of the tribe of Re’uven. (NLT)

the tribe of Re’uven: The phrase the tribe of Re’uven indicates the people who were descended from Re’uven, one of the sons of Ya’akov (Jacob).

title: Joshua 13:16
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:16a

The territory from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley,

  • Their territory extended from Aroer on the edge of the valley of the Arnon River,

  • Their land started at Aroer City at the Arnon River gorge.

The Hebrew word that the BSB that other versions translate as “and” or “so” leaves untranslated introduces the details about the land that was given to Re’uven. Use whatever connecting word or particle is appropriate in your language.

The territory from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley: The Hebrew words of this clause are almost identical to the words in 13:9a, and you should translate it in the same way.

13:16b

along with the city in the middle of the valley, to the whole plateau beyond Meydeva (Medeba),

  • including the town that is halfway along the valley, to the plain beyond Meydeva.

  • It included the city that is halfway along the Arnon River gorge, and the whole of the Meydeva Plateau.

along with the city in the middle of the valley, to the whole plateau beyond Meydeva: The Hebrew words of this clause are almost identical to the words in 13:9b-c, and you should translate it in the same way.

title: Joshua 13:17
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:17a

to Heshbon

  • It included Heshbon

  • It included Heshbon City

to Heshbon: In some languages it may be more natural to begin a new sentence. For example:

It included Heshbon

Heshbon: Heshbon was the capital city of King Sihon. You should translate the name of this town the same way you did in 13:10a.

13:17b

and all its cities on the plateau,

  • and all the cities on the plain near Heshbon:

  • and the other cities in the Meydeva (Medeba) Plateau.

and all its cities on the plateau: The phrase and all its cities on the plateau indicates all the towns that Sihon king of the Amorim (Amorites) ruled. They were in the plateau or tableland that was near Meydeva. These towns are listed in the following verses.

13:17c

including Divon (Dibon), Bamot-Ba’al (Bamoth-baal), Beyt-Ba’al-Me’on (Beth-baal-meon),

  • Divon, and Bamot-Ba’al, and Beyt-Ba’al-Me’on,

  • These are Divon City, Bamot-Ba’al Region, Beyt-Ba’al-Me’on City,

including Divon: Divon was a large town that was captured by Yisrael (Israel) (Numbers 21:30). Its name today is Dhiban and it is thirteen miles east of the Dead Sea and three and a half miles north of the Arnon Gorge.13:17 Bratcher and Newman, p. 232.

Bamot-Ba’al: The term Bamot-Ba’al indicates the area northeast of the Dead Sea to which Balak took Bil’am (Balaam) to curse Yisrael (Numbers 22:41). Bamot-Ba’al is not a town, but an area or a region.13:17 Rasmussen p. 228.

Here is another way to spell this name:

Bamot (Bamoth) Ba’al (Baal) (NIV, NET)

Beyt-Ba’al-Me’on: The term Beyt-Ba’al-Me’on indicates a town that was twenty-three miles southwest of Amman, Yarden (Jordan), and ten miles east of the Dead Sea. Its name today is Ma’in.13:17 Rasmussen, p. 228, 229.

Here is another way to spell the name of this town:

Beth Ba’al Meon (NIV, NET)

title: Joshua 13:18
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:18

Yahats (Jahaz), Kedemot (Kedemoth), Mofa’at (Mephaath),

  • and Yahats, and Kedemot, and Mepha-ath,

  • Yahats City, Kedemot City, Mepha-ath City,

Yahats: The term Yahats indicates a town that was part of the kingdom of Sihon. The story of how Mosheh (Moses) defeated King Sihon at Yahats is told in Numbers 21:23–24. The location of Yahats is uncertain.

Kedemot: The term Kedemot indicates another town that was part of the kingdom of King Sihon. Its location is uncertain.

Mofa’at: The term Mofa’at indicates another town east of the Yarden (Jordan) River. It was a part of the kingdom of King Sihon. Its location is uncertain.

Here is another way to spell the name of this town:

Mepha-ath (RSV)

title: Joshua 13:19
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:19a

Kiryatayim (Kiriathaim), Sivmah (Sibmah),

  • and Kiryatayim, and Sivmah,

  • Kiryatayim City, Sivmah City,

Kiryatayim: The term Kiryatayim indicates a town that was part of the kingdom of King Sihon. Its location is uncertain.

Sivmah: The term Sivmah indicates a town that was part of the kingdom of King Sihon. It was famous for its vineyards and is mentioned in Isaiah 16:8–9 and Jeremiah 48:32. Its location is unknown.

13:19b

Tseret-Hashahar (Zereth-shahar) on the hill in the valley,

  • and Tseret-Hashahar on the hill in the valley,

  • Tseret-Hashahar City on the hill in the middle of the valley,

Tseret-Hashahar on the hill in the valley: The term Tseret-Hashahar indicates a town that was part of the kingdom of King Sihon. The location of this town is uncertain.

the hill in the valley: The word valley probably refers to the Yarden (Jordan) River Valley. It is not known what hill this refers to.

Here is another way to spell the name of this town:

Tseret (Zereth) Shahar (NIV, NET)

title: Joshua 13:20
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:20

Beyt-Pe’or (Beth-peor), the slopes of Pisgah, and Beyt-Hayeshimot (Beth-jeshimoth)—

  • and Beyt-Pe’or, and the slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beyt-Hayeshimot.

  • Beyt-Pe’or City, the area around Pisgah Mountain, and Beyt-Hayeshimot City.

Beyt-Pe’or: The term Beyt-Pe’or indicates a town east of the Yarden (Jordan) River, where the Israelis (Israelites) stayed while Mosheh (Moses) gave them the law (Deuteronomy 4:46). It was also the place where Bil’am (Balaam) gave one of his prophecies about the Israelis (Numbers 23:28). Its location is uncertain.

Here is another way to spell the name of this town:

Beth Pe’or (Peor) (NIV, NET)

the slopes of Pisgah: The slopes of Pisgah indicates the area around Mount Pisgah. It formed the south boundary of King Sihon’s territory. The location of Mount Pisgah is uncertain.

and Beyt-Hayeshimot: The town of Beyt-Hayeshimot is referred to in Joshua 12:3 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

Here is another way to spell the name of this town:

Beth Jeshimoth (NIV, NET)

title: Joshua 13:21
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:21a

all the cities of the plateau

  • Re’uven inherited all these cities on the plain

  • The clan of Re’uven inherited all these cities on the Meydeva (Medeba) Plateau

all the cities of the plateau: The clause all the cities of the plateau summarizes the list of towns that appear in verses 17–21. This clause is almost identical to the clause in verse 13:17b and you should translate it the same way. In verse 17 this phrase was at the beginning of the list, and here it comes at the end of the list.

13:21b

and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorim (Amorites),

  • and the whole kingdom of King Sihon of the Amorim,

  • and all the area that King Sihon of the Amorim ruled

and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorim: The phrase the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorim indicates that Mosheh (Moses) gave the land that King Sihon ruled on the plateau to the tribe of Re’uven (Reuben).

13:21c

who reigned in Heshbon until Mosheh killed him and the chiefs of Midyan (Midian)

  • who ruled in Heshbon. Mosheh defeated him and Midyan’s leaders

  • from Heshbon City. Mosheh defeated him along with the leaders of the Midyanites (Midianites),

who reigned in Heshbon: The clause who reigned in Heshbon indicates that Heshbon was the capital city of King Sihon. Heshbon was mentioned in 13:10 and 13:17, and you should translate it the same way every time.

until Mosheh killed him and the chiefs of Midyan: Mosheh defeated King Sihon along with all the other leaders of Midyan. It may be helpful to begin a new sentence here. For example:

Mosheh had defeated him along with the Midyanites including Evi, Rekem, Tsur (Zur), Hur and Reva (Reba) (NCV)

chiefs of Midyan: Midyan was one of the sons of Avraham (Abraham) and Keturah (Genesis 25:1–2). Midyan’s descendants became a group called Midyan. They were a nomadic people who lived in northwest Arav (Arabia), east of the Gulf of Aqaba.13:21 Rasmussen p. 245.

13:21d

(Evi, Rekem, Tsur, Hur, and Reva), the princes of Sihon who lived in the land.

  • Evi, Rekem, Tsur, Hur, and Reva. They were rulers under King Sihon who lived in that country.

  • including Evi, Rekem, Tsur, Hur, and Reva. These leaders lived in that land and ruled with King Sihon.

(Evi, Rekem, Tsur, Hur, and Reva), the princes of Sihon: These five names are the leaders of the Midyan (Midian) people. The story of how Mosheh (Moses) and the Israelis (Israelites) fought and killed these leaders is found in Numbers 31:7–8.

princes of Sihon: The phrase princes of Sihon indicates that these leaders of Midyan were under the authority of King Sihon.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

all of them had ruled the land for King Sihon (GNT)

who lived in the land: The clause who lived in the land indicates that these five Midyanite (Midianite) leaders and their people lived in the land that King Sihon ruled.

title: Joshua 13:22
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:22a

The Israelis (Israelites) also killed the diviner Bil’am (Balaam) son of Be’or (Beor)

  • The Israelis killed Bil’am, son of Be’or, who cast lots to predict the future,

  • The Israeli (Israelite) soldiers also killed Bil’am, the son of Be’or, who used magic to tell the future,

The Israelis also killed: In some languages it is more natural to restructure verse 22 so that it begins with the subject, The Israelis. The term The Israelis indicates the Israeli soldiers. The Israelis soldiers killed Bil’am.

also: The word also is not in the Hebrew text. It is added in the BSB to show that Bil’am is a new topic. Choose the word order or lexical means that is most natural in your language to do this.

the diviner Bil’am son of Be’or: In this verse the diviner Bil’am son of Be’or is the object of the verb. In Hebrew the object is sometimes put at the beginning of the sentence to show emphasis.

the diviner: The word diviner indicates a person who predicted the future by casting lots. The lots were probably small stones. The word diviner refers to Bil’am, not to Be’or his father.

Here are some other ways to translate this word:

the one who practiced divination (ESV

who used black magic (GW)

fortune teller (GNT)

who used magic to tell the future (NLT)

13:22b

along with the others they put to the sword.

  • along with other people.

  • and some other people.

along with the others: The phrase along with the others indicates that the Israelis (Israelites) killed other people at the same time that they killed Bil’am (Balaam).

Here is another way to translate this verse:

The Israelis killed many people during the fighting, including Bil’am, son of Be’or (Beor), who tried to use magic to tell the future (NCV)

they put to the sword: The phrase that the BSB translates as they put to the sword is a Hebrew idiom. It indicates that they killed these people.

Here is another way to translate this Hebrew idiom:

they killed

title: Joshua 13:23
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:23a

And the border of the Re’uvenim (Reubenites) was the bank of the Yarden.

  • The west boundary of the clan of Re’uven was the Yarden River.

  • The Yarden River marked the west side of the land that the clan of Re’uven inherited.

And the border of the Re’uvenim was the bank of the Yarden (Jordan): This clause indicates that the Yarden River was the western boundary of the land that belonged to the tribe of Re’uven.

13:23b

This was the inheritance of the clans of the Re’uvenim,

  • These were the places that the clan of Re’uven (Reuben) inherited,

  • The places listed above were given to the clan of Re’uven,

This was the inheritance of the clans of the Re’uvenim (Reubenites): The clause This was the inheritance indicates that God gave this land to belong to the tribe of Re’uven. This summarizes the explanation of the area that the tribe of Re’uven inherited, which began in 13:15.

of the clans of the Re’uvenim: The phrase of the clans of the Re’uvenim indicates that each clan of families within the tribe of Re’uven received their own portion of the land. See how you translated the words “clan” and “family” in Joshua 7:14.

13:23c

including the cities and villages.

  • for each of their sub-clans, including cities and villages.

  • with some cities and villages for each sub-clan.

including the cities and villages: Each family in the tribe of Re’uven (Reuben) received certain cities and villages as their own. The term cities indicates settled areas with a wall around them to protect them. The term villages indicates small settled areas without walls.

title: Joshua 13:24
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:24

This is what Mosheh had given to the clans of the tribe of Gad:

  • ¶ Mosheh gave land to the clan of Gad for their people to inherit.

  • ¶ Mosheh assigned the following land to the clan of Gad.

The Hebrew word that the BSB leaves untranslated is often translated as “and.” It indicates a transition to the next topic. Many English versions do not translate this connecting word.

Mosheh (Moses) had given to the clans of the tribe of Gad: This indicates that Mosheh assigned land to the tribe of Gad for them to live on and pass on to their descendants.

to the clans of the tribe of Gad: The phrase the clans of the tribe of Gad indicates the people who had Gad as their ancestor.

to the clans: The phrase to the clans indicates that each clan or group of families in the tribe of Gad received their own portion of the land. See how you translated the words “clan” and “family” in Joshua 7:14.

title: Joshua 13:25
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:25a

The territory of Yazer (Jazer), all the cities of Gilead,

  • Their territory included Yazer City, all the cities of Gilead Region,

  • Their land included Yazer City, all the cities in the southern part of Gilead Region,

The territory of Yazer: The term Yazer indicates a town east of the Yarden (Jordan) River. Yazer was part of the kingdom of King Sihon. Its location is uncertain.

all the cities of Gilead: The phrase cities of Gilead indicates the towns in the region of Gilead that were near to Yazer. This was the southern part of Gilead. In verse 13:31 it says that the northern part of Gilead was assigned to the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh).

The name Gilead appeared in Joshua 12:2 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

13:25b

and half the land of the Amonim (Ammonites)

  • and half the region of the Amoni (Ammonite) people

  • and half the land of the Amon (Ammon) people

and half the land of the Amonim: The phrase half the land of the Amonim indicates the western half of the land controlled by the Amon people. This area was between the Arnon River and Yabok (Jabbok) River.13:25 Woudstra, p. 221.

the Amonim: The term Amonim refers to the Amon people. It was used in Joshua 12:2 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

13:25c

as far as Aroer, near Rabah (Rabbah);

  • to Aroer City, which is near Rabah City.

  • as far as Aroer City close to Rabah City.

as far as Aroer, near Rabah: The term Aroer indicates a town that was part of the kingdom of King Sihon. The town named Aroer in this verse is not the same as the Aroer mentioned in verse 16 which was assigned to Re’uven (Reuben). The location of the Aroer in this verse is not known.

near: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as near is more literally “on the face of.” There are three ways to interpret this word.

  1. It means near. For example:

    near Rabah (BSB) (BSB, NIV, NCV, NET, NJPS, GW, NJB)

  2. It means east. For example:

    east of Rabah (Rabbah) (GNT) (GNT, RSV, ESV, REB)

  3. It means west. For example:

    west of Rabah (CEV) (CEV, NLT)

It is recommended that you choose interpretation (1). We do not know for certain which direction Aroer town was in relation to Rabah town. It is best to translate it using a word that means “near” or “close to.”

Here are some other ways that English versions translate this word:

by (GW)

facing (NJB)

Rabah (Rabbah): The term Rabah indicates the capital city of the Amon (Ammon) people. Today it is the city of Amman, Yarden (Jordan) and it is 22 miles east of the Yarden River.

General Comment on 13:25

It may be more natural in some languages to translate this list of cites using more than one sentence. For example:

Their territory included the town of Yazer (Jazer) and all the towns of the southern Gilead Region. It also included half the land of the Amonim (Ammonites). It extended as far as Aroer, which was close to Rabah.

title: Joshua 13:26
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:26a

the territory from Heshbon to Ramat-Hamitspeh (Ramath-mizpeh) and Betonim,

  • Their territory went from Heshbon to Ramat-Hamitspeh and Betonim,

  • The land given to the clan of Gad went from Heshbon City in the south to Ramat-Hamitspeh City and Betonim City

the territory from Heshbon to Ramat-Hamitspeh and Betonim: It is recommended that you begin a new sentence here.

Heshbon: The town of Heshbon was about 25 kilometers northeast of the Dead Sea, and southwest of Amman, Yarden (Jordan).13:26 Bratcher and Newman, p. 238. It formed the south boundary of the land of the tribe of Gad.

Ramat-Hamitspeh: The town of Ramat-Hamitspeh was one of the towns that the tribe of Gad inherited. The location of Ramat-Hamitspeh is uncertain.

Here is another way to spell the name of this town:

Ramath Mitspah (Mizpah) (NIV, NET)

Betonim: The town of Betonim was sixteen miles northeast of Yeriho (Jericho). Its name today is Khirbet Batneh.13:26 Rasmussen, p. 230.

13:26b

and from Mahanayim (Mahanaim) to the border of Devir (Debir);

  • and from Mahanayim to Devir.

  • and further north to Mahanayim City and Devir City.

and from Mahanayim: The phrase from Mahanayim indicates that the land of the tribe of Gad included the town of Mahanayim. Mahanayim was to the north, at the border between the tribes of Gad and Menasheh (Manasseh). Its location is uncertain.

to the border of Devir: There is a textual issue with the word Devir.

  1. In the Hebrew text this word is spelled lidber. In 2 Samuel 9:4 there is a town called Lo-Devar (Lo-debar). Some scholars think that the town mentioned here in Yehoshua (Joshua) is Lo-Devar. However, they have to amend the Hebrew spelling slightly to make it fit.

The town of Lo-Devar in 2 Samuel 9:4 was in the Yarden (Jordan) River Valley, ten miles south of the Sea of Galil (Galilee).13:26 Rasmussen, p. 232.

Here are some ways that English versions spell this name:

Lo-Devar (NLT, NABRE)

Lodebar (GNT)

Lidbir (GW, NJPS)

Lidebor (CEV)

  1. Some ancient versions of Yehoshua (Joshua) omit the letter “l” when they spell this name. They spell it idber. From this we get the English name Devir (Debir) as in the BSB. However, there is no town known by the name of Devir east of the Yarden River.13:26 Woudstra, p. 222. For example:

    Devir (NIV) (BSB, NIV, RSV, ESV, NET, NASB, KJV)

The commentaries do not agree on this issue. It is recommended that you follow the majority language version of your area in translating this word.

title: Joshua 13:27
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:27a

and in the valley, Beyt-Haram (Beth-haram), Beyt-Nimrah (Beth-nimrah), Sukot (Succoth), and Tsafon (Zaphon),

  • In the valley were Beyt-Haram, Beyt-Nimrah, Sukot, and Tsafon,

  • In the Yarden River Valley it included Beyt-Haram City, Beyt-Nimrah City, Sukkoth City, and Tsafon City,

and in the valley: The word valley indicates the Yarden (Jordan) River Valley.

Beyt-Haram: The term Beyt-Haram indicates a town in the Yarden River Valley that was eighteen miles southwest of present-day Amman. Today it is identified with Tel Iktanu.13:27 Rasmussen, p. 229.

Here is another way to spell the name of this town:

Beth Haram (NIV, NET)

Beyt-Nimrah: The term Beyt-Nimrah indicates a town that was eighteen miles east of present-day Amman. Today it is identified with Tel el-Bleibil.13:27 Rasmussen, p. 229.

Here is another way to spell the name of this town:

Beth Nimrah (NIV, NET)

Sukot (Succoth): The term Sukot indicates a town in the Yarden River Valley that was north of the Yabok (Jabbok) River.

and Tsafon (Zaphon): The term Tsafon indicates a town in the Yarden River Valley that was north of the Yabok River.

13:27b

with the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon

  • the rest of the kingdom of King Sihon of Heshbon.

  • which were the rest of the kingdom of King Sihon, king of Heshbon City.

with the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon: The phrase the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon describes the towns in verse 13:27a. These towns and the area surrounding them were the second half of King Sihon’s kingdom. The tribe of Re’uven (Reuben) had received the first half.

Here is another way to translate 27a-b:

Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Gad the towns of Beyt-Haram (Beth-haram), Beyt-Nimrah (Beth-nimrah), Sukot, and Tsafon which were in the Yarden (Jordan) River Valley. These towns were the other half of the kingdom of King Sihon of Heshbon.

13:27c

(the territory on the east side of the Yarden

  • The Yarden River was the western boundary,

  • The west border of Gad’s territory was the Yarden River

the territory on the east side of the Yarden: The clause the territory on the east side of the Yarden indicates that the Yarden River was the western boundary of the land that the tribe of Gad received.

13:27d
