up to the edge of the Sea of Kineret (Chinnereth)).

  • and it went north to the edge of the Sea of Galil (Galilee).

  • and the north border was the bottom of the Sea of Galil.

up to the edge of the Sea of Kineret: The phrase up to the edge of the Sea of Kineret indicates that the territory of the tribe of Gad extended north to the southern end of the Sea of Kineret.

Sea of Kineret: The term Sea of Kineret is another name for the Sea of Galil. It is recommended that you use the term “Lake Galil” if it is more familiar to your readers. Translate this name the same way as in Joshua 11:2.

Here is another way to translate Sea of Kineret:

Sea of Galil (NCV, CEV, NLT, GNT, GW)

The RSV spells this name “Kineret”. As with many of these names, you may wish to use a spelling/pronunciation that is used in a nearby or well-known translation from your region.

title: Joshua 13:28
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:28a

This was the inheritance of the clans of the Gadim (Gadites),

  • These were the places that the clan of Gad inherited,

  • The places listed above were given to the clan of Gad,

This was the inheritance of the clans of the Gadim: The clause This was the inheritance of the clans of the Gadim indicates that God gave the land described in the previous verses to the tribe of Gad.

of the clans: The phrase of the clans indicates that each clan or group of families in the tribe of Gad received their own portion of the land. See how you translated the words “clan” and “family” in Joshua 7:14.

13:28b

including the cities and villages.

  • for each of their sub-clans, including cities and villages.

  • with some cities and villages for each sub-clan.

including the cities and villages: Each family or clan in the tribe of Gad received certain cities and villages as their own. This is the same wording as used in 13:23c and you should translate it the same way in both places.

title: Joshua 13:29
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:29a

This is what Mosheh had given to the clans of the half-tribe of Menasheh,

  • ¶ Mosheh gave land to half the clan of Menasheh for their people to inherit.

  • ¶ Mosheh assigned the following land to half the clan of Menasheh.

The Hebrew word that the BSB leaves untranslated but some English versions translate as “and" indicates a transition to the next topic. Many English versions do not translate this connecting word.

Mosheh (Moses) had given to the clans of the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh): The clause Mosheh had given to the clans of the half-tribe of Menasheh indicates that Mosheh assigned land to half of the tribe of Menasheh for them to live on and pass on to their descendants. Mosheh mentioned this in Deuteronomy 3:13.

the half-tribe of Menasheh: The half-tribe of Menasheh indicates the people who had Menasheh as their ancestor. Menasheh was the oldest son of Yosef (Joseph), son of Ya’akov (Jacob). The tribe of Menasheh received land on both the east and the west sides of the Yarden (Jordan) River, and so there were two “half-tribes.” Some English versions refer to these two groups as East Menasheh and West Menasheh.

13:29b

that is, to half the tribe of the descendants of Menasheh:

  • It was given to them with some for each sub-clan.

  • He gave some to each of their sub-clans.

to half the tribe of the descendants of Menasheh: The clause to half the tribe of the descendants of Menasheh repeats the information in 29a using different words. In some languages it may be more natural to leave this part of the clause as implicit information.

the descendants of Menasheh: The phrase the descendants indicates that each family or clan within half of the tribe of Menasheh received their own portion of the land on the east side of the Yarden River. See how you translated the word “family” in Joshua 7:14.

title: Joshua 13:30
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:30a

The territory from Mahanayim (Mahanaim)

  • Their territory started at Mahanayim,

  • Their land went north from Mahanayim City

The territory from Mahanayim: The town of Mahanayim was on the south border of the tribes of Gad and Menasheh. Its exact location is uncertain. The town of Mahanayim was mentioned in 13:26 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

their land extended north from the town of Mahanayim

13:30b

through all Bashan—all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan,

  • and included all of Bashan, the country of King Og,

  • through all of the country of Bashan, which was ruled by King Og.

through all Bashan—all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: The phrase through all Bashan contains the same information as the next phrase, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan.

Here is another way to translate this clause:

it included the country of Bashan, which was ruled by King Og

Bashan: The term Bashan indicates a country or a region that was on a high and fertile plateau north of Gilead. The country of Bashan was mentioned in Joshua 9:10 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

13:30c

including all the towns of Yair (Jair) that are in Bashan, sixty cities;

  • and all sixty of the cities which Yair of the clan of Menasheh (Manasseh) captured in Bashan.

  • It included all sixty cities in the country of Bashan which Yair, a descendant of Menasheh, captured.

including all the towns of Yair that are in Bashan: The phrase all the towns of Yair that are in Bashan indicates that the towns that Yair captured were included in the territory of Menasheh. Yair was a descendant of Menasheh. The story of how he captured these towns is found in Numbers 32:41.

sixty cities: In some languages it may be more natural to include the words sixty cities as part of the preceding phrase. For example:

It included all the sixty cities which Yair, a descendant of Menasheh, captured in Bashan

title: Joshua 13:31
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:31a

half of Gilead; and Ashtarot (Ashtaroth) and Edre’i (Edrei), the royal cities of Og in Bashan.

  • It included half of Gilead, and Ashtarot and Edre-i in Bashan, the country of King Og.

  • It included the northern half of the region of Gilead, as well as Ashtarot City and Edre-i City, the capital cities of King Og who ruled the country of Bashan.

half of Gilead: The phrase half of Gilead indicates half of the region of Gilead. The other half of the Gilead region was captured from King Sihon and was mentioned in 12:2. You should translate the term Gilead the same way in both places.

and Ashtarot and Edre’i, the royal cities of Og in Bashan: Ashtarot and Edre’i were two important towns in the kingdom of King Og.

In some languages it may be more natural to begin a new sentence here. Here is another way to translate this verse:

It included half of Gilead, as well as Ashtarot and Edre’i (GNT)

Ashtarot: The town of Ashtarot was the capital town of King Og of Bashan. Ashtarot was mentioned in Joshua 9:10 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

Edre’i (Edrei): King Og also had a residence where he sometimes lived in the town of Edre’i. Edre’i was mentioned in Joshua 12:4, and you should translate it the same way in both places.

13:31b

All this was for the clans of the descendants of Makir (Machir) son of Menasheh (Manasseh),

  • These cities were given to the descendants of Makir, who was Menasheh’s son,

  • Mosheh (Moses) gave this land to the people descended from Makir the son of Menasheh.

All this was for the clans of the descendants of Makir son of Menasheh: The word All this indicates the towns that were listed in verses 13:30–31.

was for: The verb phrase was for is not in the Hebrew text. The Hebrew text has no verb, but in English a verb must be supplied.

the clans of the descendants: The phrase the clans of the descendants indicates that each clan or group of families within half of the tribe of Menasheh that was descended from Makir received their own portion of the land on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

Mosheh gave these towns to the people of Makir the son of Menasheh

Makir (Machir) son of Menasheh (Manasseh): Makir was the first-born son of Menasheh.

Here is another way to spell Makir:

Makir (NET, NIV)

13:31c

that is, half of the descendants of Makir.

  • for the Makir side of the clan of Menasheh, with some land for each family.

  • He gave it to each family descended from Makir. These families made up this half-clan of Menasheh.

that is, half of the descendants of Makir: The phrase half of the descendants of Makir contains similar information to the phrase in verse 13:31b “the people of Makir the son of Menasheh.” In some languages it is more natural to leave one of these phrases as implicit information.

Here is another way to translate verse 13:31b-c:

Mosheh (Moses) gave these towns to the families in this half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). These families were the descendants of Makir (Machir) the son of Menasheh.

title: Joshua 13:32
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:32a

These were the portions Mosheh had given them

  • ¶ These are the land assignments that Mosheh made

  • ¶ The lands described above are the places that Mosheh gave to the people

These were the portions Mosheh (Moses) had given them: The word These refers back to 13:15–31. It indicates the regions and towns that Mosheh gave to the tribes of Re’uven, Gad, and half the tribe of Menasheh.

13:32b

on the plains of Moav (Moab) beyond the Yarden (Jordan), east of Yeriho (Jericho).

  • when the Israelis (Israelites) were in the plains of Moav, east of the Yarden River, opposite Yeriho.

  • while they were camped on the plains of Moav, across the Yarden River, east of Yeriho.

on the plains of Moav: The phrase the plains of Moav indicates a flat land on the east side of the Yarden River. Moav was one of the kingdoms on the east side of the Yarden. Mosheh made the distribution of land while the Israelis were camped on this plain.

beyond the Yarden, east of Yeriho: The phrase beyond the Yarden, east of Yeriho is written from the perspective of the author, who wrote this book in the land west of the Yarden River. It indicates that the plains of Moav were on the east side of the Yarden River. They were to the east of the town of Yeriho, which was on the west side of the Yarden River.

title: Joshua 13:33
content:
Section 13:1–33 Mosheh (Moses) had distributed the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River

Before Mosheh died he had given land to the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). In this section Yahweh reminded Yehoshua (Joshua) of the land that they still had not conquered. Then there is a detailed listing of the boundaries of the lands on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here is another possible section heading:

The land east of the Yarden River

13:33a

To the tribe of Levi, however, Mosheh had given no inheritance.

  • But Mosheh did not give an allotment to the clan of Levi,

  • But Mosheh did not give any land to the clan of Levi.

To the tribe of Levi, however, Mosheh (Moses) had given no inheritance: The tribe of Levi was the only tribe that did not receive land of their own.

The Hebrew text places the phrase To the tribe of Levi at the beginning of the sentence. In Hebrew this shows emphasis. In some languages it may not be natural to begin a sentence with this phrase. Use a way that is natural to emphasize that the tribe of Levi was different from the other tribes.

This verse is similar to verse 13:14.

13:33b

Yahweh, the God of Yisrael (Israel), is their inheritance, just as He had promised them.

  • because Yahweh, the God of Yisrael, promised that he himself will be their allotment.

  • Instead, the Levi clan received Yahweh, the God of Yisrael himself, as he promised to them.

Yahweh, the God of Yisrael, is their inheritance: The phrase their inheritance indicates that the tribe of Levi had a special relationship with Yahweh, the God of Yisrael. They were the only tribe that served Yahweh at his altar in the Tent of Meeting. The words here are similar to Numbers 18:20.

just as He had promised them: The clause just as He had promised them indicates that Yahweh had previously promised this privilege to the tribe of Levi. See, for example, Deuteronomy 18:1–2.

title: Joshua 14:1
content:
Section 14:1–5 The Israelis (Israelites) divided the land west of the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section the nine and a half tribes who were to live on the west side of the Yarden River received their allotment of land. The tribe of Levi received only towns to live in.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land west of the Yarden River

Dividing up the land

14:1a

Now these are the portions that the Israelis inherited in the land of Kena’an (Canaan),

  • ¶ This is the land that the Israelis received in the land of Kena’an.

  • ¶ This description that follows is about how the land of Kena’an west of the Yarden (Jordan) was divided among the people of Yisrael (Israel).

Now these are the portions that the Israelis (Israelites) inherited in the land of Kena’an: This sentence introduces a new topic. The topic is the areas of land which each tribe received on the west side of the Yarden River. Begin this sentence in a way that is natural in your language.

these are the portions: This phrase refers to the detailed description of land areas in chapters 14–19.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

forWhat follows is an account of how the land…was divided (GNT)

Here are the pieces of land that the people of Yisrael received

portions: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as portions is more literally “gave them as a possession.” God gave some land to each tribe of Yisrael. He intended that their children and grandchildren would inherit those lands forever.

Here are some other ways to translate this word:

the land that God gave them

the lands they received as a possession

the land of Kena’an (Canaan): The phrase the land of Kena’an refers to the land on the west side of the Yarden (Jordan) River, and also to some of the other nearby lands. God first promised this land to Avraham (Abraham) in Genesis 15:17–21.

14:1b

as distributed by Eleazar the priest, Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun,

  • Eleazar the priest, and Yehoshua the son of Nun,

  • Eleazar the priest, and Yehoshua whose father was Nun,

as distributed by Eleazar the priest: Eleazar was the son of Aharon (Aaron) and he became the high priest after Aharon died. The word priest was used in 3:3 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

as distributed: The phrase that the BSB translates as as distributed can also be translated “divided” or “gave.”

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

they divided it among the people

they decided what land to give to each group

Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun: This phrase was used in Joshua 1:1 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

14:1c

and the heads of the families of the tribes of Yisrael (Israel).

  • and the leaders of the clans gave a piece of land to each Israeli (Israelite) family.

  • and the leaders of the families of the Israeli clans divided it among the people.

and the heads of the families of the tribes of Yisrael: This phrase refers to the leaders of the Israeli tribes. In Numbers 34:16–29 Yahweh commanded Mosheh (Moses) to appoint one leader from each of the tribes of Yisrael to help assign the land along with Yehoshua and Eleazar the priest. Mosheh decided who each of these leaders would be.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

the leaders of the families of the Israeli tribes (GNT)

the leaders of all the tribes of Yisrael (NCV)

General Comment on 14:1a-c

In some languages it may be more natural to change the order of the clauses in this verse. For example:

1bEleazar the priest, Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun, 1cand the leaders of all the tribes of Yisrael (Israel) 1adecided what land to give to the people in the land of Kena’an (Canaan). (NCV)

title: Joshua 14:2
content:
Section 14:1–5 The Israelis (Israelites) divided the land west of the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section the nine and a half tribes who were to live on the west side of the Yarden River received their allotment of land. The tribe of Levi received only towns to live in.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land west of the Yarden River

Dividing up the land

14:2a

Their inheritance was assigned by lot

  • These leaders used lots to decide which land the people would receive

  • The priests rolled stones to decide which piece of land each family will receive

Their inheritance was assigned by lot: It was the role of the priest to throw the lots. God used the lots to show which piece of land he would give to each family.

Here is another way to translate this clause:

Eleazar threw stones to decide which piece of land each family would receive.

inheritance: This word was used in 11:23 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

lot: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as lot refers to small objects that the Israeli (Israelite) people threw to determine God’s will. It is possible that the lots were stones with a different color on each side.14:2 Bean, Albert: Lots, Holman Bible Dictionary p. 896. Holman Bible Publishers, Nashville, TN 1991. If you have a tradition of choosing or throwing small objects to make a decision, you can use that term here. Or you can use some other term that is familiar in your language for choosing by chance.

Here are some ways to translate this term:

throw dice

draw straws

14:2b

for the nine and a half tribes,

  • for the remaining nine and one-half clans.

  • for the nine and a half clans that hadn’t yet received any land.

for the nine and a half tribes: The nine and a half tribes included all the tribes except for Re’uven (Reuben), Gad, and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh). They received land on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

for the remaining nine and one-half tribes

for the nine and a half tribes that hadn’t yet received their inheritance

14:2c

as Yahweh had commanded through Mosheh (Moses).

  • Yahweh told Mosheh to do this.

  • This is what Yahweh told Mosheh to do.

as Yahweh had commanded through Mosheh: Numbers 33:50–54 tells the story of how Yahweh commanded Mosheh to distribute the land on the west side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

title: Joshua 14:3
content:
Section 14:1–5 The Israelis (Israelites) divided the land west of the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section the nine and a half tribes who were to live on the west side of the Yarden River received their allotment of land. The tribe of Levi received only towns to live in.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land west of the Yarden River

Dividing up the land

14:3a

For Mosheh (Moses) had given the inheritance

  • Mosheh already gave an inheritance

  • Mosheh already assigned land

For: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB has translated as For can also mean “because.” It states the reason for something. Many English versions do not translate this conjunction. For example:

Mosheh had already given a grant of land to the two and a half tribes on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) River. (NLT)

Mosheh had given the inheritance: This verse explains the reason why the land on the west side of the Yarden River was divided between nine and a half tribes, rather than all twelve tribes.

14:3b

east of the Yarden to the other two and a half tribes.

  • to the two and one-half clans on the other side of the Yarden River.

  • to the other two and a half clans on the east side of the Yarden River.

east of the Yarden to the other two and a half tribes: Theother two and a half tribes refers to the tribes of Gad, Re’uven (Reuben) and one half of the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh).

east of the Yarden: The phrase east of the Yarden indicates the east side of the Yarden River. It may be helpful to make this clear. For example

Mosheh (Moses) had given the two-and-a-half tribes their inheritance east of the Yarden (Jordan) River. (GW)

Mosheh had given the other two and a half tribes their own land on the east side of the Yarden River.

14:3c

But he granted no inheritance among them to the Levites.

  • But he did not give any inheritance of land to the clan of Levi.

  • Mosheh did not assign any land to the Levi clan.

But he granted no inheritance among them to the Levites: Although the BSB puts the phrase to the Levites at the end of the clause, it comes first in the Hebrew clause to emphasize that the Levites were different from the other tribes. Many languages will have another way to show this emphasis.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

He did not give any land as an inheritance to Levi’s tribe. (GW)

The tribe of Levi did not receive any land like the other tribes. (ERV)

he granted no inheritance among them: This indicates that the Levites did not receive any land. If you have translated the word inheritance as “land” in previous verses then you should translate it the same way here.

title: Joshua 14:4
content:
Section 14:1–5 The Israelis (Israelites) divided the land west of the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section the nine and a half tribes who were to live on the west side of the Yarden River received their allotment of land. The tribe of Levi received only towns to live in.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land west of the Yarden River

Dividing up the land

14:4a

The descendants of Yosef (Joseph) became two tribes, Menasheh (Manasseh) and Efrayim (Ephraim).

  • This happened because the clan of Yosef divided into two clans, Menasheh and Efrayim.

  • There were still twelve clans even if Levi is not counted because the descendants of Yosef divided into two clans, Menasheh and Efrayim.

The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB leaves untranslated but many English versions translates as “For” is the same as the word in verse 3. It means “because.” It introduces the reason why the tribe of Levi did not receive land of their own.

The descendants of Yosef became two tribes, Menasheh and Efrayim: This verse explains why there were twelve tribes who inherited land, even though the Levite tribe did not receive any land. The descendants of Yosef had split into two tribes.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

The descendants of Yosef had divided into two tribes—Menasheh and Efrayim. (ERV)

Menasheh and Efrayim were the sons of Yosef. They had become two tribes. (NIRV)

14:4b

And no portion of the land was given to the Levites,

  • The clan of Levi did not receive a share of the land,

  • The Levi clan did not receive any land.

And no portion of the land was given to the Levites: The clause no portion of the land was given to the Levites indicates that the Levites did not receive any land area of their own.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

The Levites received no share of the land (NIV)

The Levite tribe did not receive any land.

General Comment on 14:3–4b

The information about the Levites is repeated in 4b for emphasis. If it is not natural to repeat this information, verses three and four may be combined, as in the GNT:

Mosheh (Moses) had already assigned the land east of the Yarden (Jordan) to the other two and one-half tribes. (The descendants of Yosef (Joseph) were divided into two tribes: Menasheh (Manasseh) and Efrayim (Ephraim).) However, Mosheh gave the Levites no portion of the territory. (GNT)

14:4c

except for cities in which to live,

  • but only towns to live in,

  • They only received cities to live in,

except for cities in which to live: The phrase except for cities in which to live, indicates that the Levite tribe did not receive a region of land as the other tribes did. Instead, they received towns to live in.

14:4d

along with pasturelands for their flocks and herds.

  • along with the surrounding lands for their cattle and sheep and goats to graze in.

  • and the nearby land for their animals to live on.

along with pasturelands for their flocks and herds: The word pasturelands indicates fields in which cattle or other domestic animals could eat the grass.

their flocks and herds: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates their flocks and herds is more literally “their acquired possessions.” It can also refer to animals. In this context it refers to other domesticated animals that the Levites owned, such as sheep and goats.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

nearby pastures for their sheep, goats, and cattle (CEV)

fields for all their animals to live on

title: Joshua 14:5
content:
Section 14:1–5 The Israelis (Israelites) divided the land west of the Yarden (Jordan) River

In this section the nine and a half tribes who were to live on the west side of the Yarden River received their allotment of land. The tribe of Levi received only towns to live in.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land west of the Yarden River

Dividing up the land

14:5a

So the Israelis did as Yahweh had commanded Mosheh (Moses),

  • The Israelis did what Yahweh commanded Mosheh.

  • The Israelis (Israelites) followed Yahweh’s commands to Mosheh

So the Israelis did as Yahweh had commanded Mosheh: This is a summary of verses 1–5. Yahweh told Mosheh how to divide up the land when they were on the plains of Moav (Moab), before they entered the land of Kena’an (Canaan) (Numbers 33:50–54).

Here is another way to translate this clause:

The Israelis followed the Lord’s instructions to Mosheh. (NET)

14:5b

and they divided the land.

  • They divided the land in the way he told them to do.

  • and divided up the land among the twelve clans.

and they divided the land: Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

they allotted the land (RSV)

they assigned the land to the people

title: Joshua 14:6
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:6a

Then the sons of Yehudah (Judah) approached Yehoshua at Gilgal,

  • ¶ Then people from the clan of Yehudah approached Yehoshua at Gilgal.

  • ¶ One day the Yehudah clan came to Yehoshua (Joshua) while they were camped at Gilgal camp.

Then the sons of Yehudah approached Yehoshua at Gilgal: While the Israelis (Israelites) were camped at Gilgal, the people of the tribe of Yehudah went to talk to Yehoshua.

Here is another way to translate this clause:

While the Israelis were camped at Gilgal, the people of Yehudah came to Yehoshua

Gilgal: Gilgal is the name of a place east of Yeriho (Jericho) and west of the Yarden (Jordan) River. It is the place where the Israelis set up their camp after they crossed the Yarden River. It is first mentioned in Joshua 4:19| and you should translate it the same way in both places.

14:6b

and Kalev (Caleb) son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh) the Kenizi (Kenizzite) said to him,

  • Kalev, who was the son of Yefuneh and grandson of Kenaz, said to Yehoshua:

  • Kalev was the son of Yefuneh, and the grandson of Kenaz. He said to Yehoshua (Joshua):

and Kalev son of Yefuneh the Kenizi said to him: The story of Kalev is told in 13. He was one of the twelve spies who explored the land of Kena’an (Canaan). Kalev and Yehoshua were the only two of the twelve spies who trusted God.

the Kenizi: There are two ways to interpret the Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Kenizi.

  1. It indicates that Kalev is a grandson of Kenaz. For example:

    Kalev…the grandson of Kenaz (GW) (GW)

  2. It indicates that Kalev (Caleb) belongs to the family or clan of Kenaz. For example:

    Kalev belonged to the Kenaz clan (CEV) (BSB, CEV)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1). This is based on Judges 3:9 and I Chronicles 4:13–15.

14:6c

“You know what Yahweh said to Mosheh (Moses) the man of God

  • “You know what Yahweh told Mosheh the man of God

  • “You remember what Yahweh said to Mosheh the prophet of God

You know what Yahweh said to Mosheh the man of God: The phrase Mosheh the man of God is a title for Mosheh. He is called this several times, for example in Deuteronomy 33:1. This is a term that is often used for a prophet who speaks for God, for example 1 Samuel 2:27.

Here are some other ways to translate the phrase Mosheh the man of God:

Mosheh the man who belongs to God

the prophet Mosheh (NCV, CEV)

14:6d

at Kadesh-Barnea (Kadesh-barnea) about you and me.

  • about you and me in Kadesh-Barnea.

  • about us two while we were in Kadesh-Barnea.

at Kadesh-Barnea: The term Kadesh-Barnea refers to a town on the south boundary of Kena’an (Canaan). The twelve spies returned here to make their report about Kena’an (Numbers 13:26). This town was mentioned in Joshua 10:41 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

about you and me: Kalev (Caleb) said this to Yehoshua (Joshua). Yahweh promised that Kalev and Yehoshua would receive land which their descendants would inherit (Numbers 14:24–30).

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

concerning you and me (RSV)

about the two of us

title: Joshua 14:7
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:7a

I was forty years old

  • At that time I was forty years old.

  • When I was forty years of age,

I was forty years old: In some languages it may be more natural to put this phrase at the end of the verse rather than at the beginning.

Here is another way to translate this clause:

When Mosheh (Moses) the servant of Yahweh sent me from Kadesh-Barnea (Kadesh-barnea), I was forty years old.

14:7b

when Mosheh the servant of Yahweh sent me from Kadesh-Barnea

  • Mosheh the servant of Yahweh sent me from Kadesh-Barnea

  • Mosheh, Yahweh’s servant, told me to go from Kadesh-Barnea

when Mosheh the servant of Yahweh: This phrase was used in Joshua 1:1 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

sent me from Kadesh-Barnea: The account of what happened when Mosheh sent the twelve spies to explore the land of Kena’an (Canaan) occurs in Numbers 13.

Here is another way to translate this clause:

when Mosheh (Moses), Yahweh’s servant, commanded me to go from Kadesh-Barnea (Kadesh-barnea)

Both Kalev (Caleb) and Yehoshua (Joshua) were among the twelve spies. It is also possible to translate this clause as:

when Mosheh, Yahweh’s servant, commanded us to go from Kadesh-Barnea

14:7c

to spy out the land,

  • to explore the land of Kena’an.

  • to look around the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

to spy out the land: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as spy out is more literally “explore.”

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

to explore the land

to look all around the land

14:7d

and I brought back to him an honest report.

  • I brought him back an honest report.

  • I came back and told him what I thought.

and I brought back to him: This means that Kalev (Caleb) returned to Mosheh (Moses) and gave him a report about what had happened while he explored the land. In some languages it may be clearer to start a new sentence here.

an honest report: The clause an honest report indicates that Kalev spoke honestly about what he had seen in Kena’an (Canaan). (The only other person who was not afraid of the Kena’an people was Yehoshua (Joshua), but he is not directly mentioned in this narrative.) The other ten spies said that they were afraid of the Kena’an people, but Kalev said that God would help the Israelis (Israelites) to fight them.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

I returned and gave him an honest report (NLT)

I brought him back a report according to my convictions (NIV)

I came back and gave him a faithful account about the land.

title: Joshua 14:8
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:8a

Although my brothers who went with me

  • But the people who went up with me

  • However, my companions who went with me

Although my brothers who went with me: The phrase my brothers refers to ten of the twelve spies. They were also Israelis (Israelites) and Kalev (Caleb) thought of them as brothers.

who went with me: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as went indicates that the men were going up to a higher place. They started in the wilderness of Kadesh-Barnea (Kadesh-barnea). which was on the edge of the coastal plain. From there they went up into the hill country. In languages that do not keep track of elevation, it may be more natural to say went, as the BSB does.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

But the other Israelis who went with me

But my companions who went with me

14:8b

made the hearts of the people melt with fear,

  • made the other Israelis afraid.

  • said things that terrified the rest of the people.

made the hearts of the people melt with fear: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as made the hearts of the people melt with fear is an idiom. It indicates that the people were very afraid. The words the people refer to the Israeli (Israelite) people. A similar expression was used in verse 2:9d. If possible, you should translate this clause in the same way as you did there.

Here are some other ways to translate this idiom:

my companions made the Israelis (Israelites) afraid

the brothers who went with me said things that terrified the rest of the people

14:8c

I remained loyal to Yahweh my God.

  • But I followed Yahweh my God with all my heart.

  • However, I was completely loyal to Yahweh my God.

I remained loyal to Yahweh my God: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as I remained loyal to Yahweh my God is more literally “I fulfilled after Yahweh my God.” This is a Hebrew idiom. It means that Kalev (Caleb) was completely loyal to Yahweh.14:8 This idiom also occurs in Numbers 14:24, Numbers 32:12 and Deuteronomy 1:36. If you have already translated those books, it is recommended that you translate it the same way here.

Here are some other ways to translate this Hebrew idiom:

I was completely loyal to Yahweh my God.

I followed Yahweh my God with all my heart.

I completely trusted the Lord God (CEV)

title: Joshua 14:9
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:9a

On that day Mosheh swore to me, saying,

  • That day Mosheh made a promise to me, saying:

  • The day that I came back from Kena’an, Mosheh promised me:

On that day Mosheh (Moses) swore to me, saying: The clause Mosheh swore means that Mosheh made a promise to Kalev (Caleb).

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

On the day I returned, Mosheh promised me

The same day I came back, Mosheh told me (CEV)

14:9b

‘Surely the land on which you have set foot

  • 'The land on which your feet have walked

  • 'The land you have walked on

Surely the land on which you have set foot: The phrase the land on which you have set foot indicates the land on which Kalev (Caleb) walked. This was a part of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

The land which your feet walked on

The land in Kena’an where you walked

14:9c

will be an inheritance to you and your children forever,

  • will become your land and that of your children and grandchildren forever,

  • will certainly belong to you and to your descendants always,

will be an inheritance to you and your children forever: This clause indicates that Kalev (Caleb) would receive the land he walked on as a gift from God. He could pass it on to his children and his grandchildren.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

it will be your land and that of your descendants always

it will belong to you and to your children and grandchildren for ever

14:9d

because you have wholly followed Yahweh my God.’

  • because you followed Yahweh my God with all your heart.’

  • because you were completely loyal to Yahweh my God.’

because you have wholly followed Yahweh my God: The clause you have wholly followed Yahweh my God is the same Hebrew idiom that was used in verse 14:8c and you should consider translating it the same way.

title: Joshua 14:10
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:10a

Now behold, as Yahweh promised, He has kept me alive

  • ¶ Now, look. Yahweh has let me live, as he said he would.

  • ¶ Now see. Yahweh has caused me to live, as he promised.

Now behold: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as Now behold, is a literary device to call attention to what comes next. Use a natural expression in your language to call attention to what comes next. In some languages this expression may best be left implicit.

as Yahweh promised, He has kept me alive: In Numbers 14:24–30 Yahweh promised that Kalev (Caleb) would live to inherit land in Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

Yahweh has let me live as he promised

Yahweh has caused me to live, as he said he would

14:10b

these forty-five years since He spoke this word to Mosheh (Moses),

  • It has been forty-five years since Yahweh said this to Mosheh.

  • Yahweh gave Mosheh this promise about me forty-five years ago,

these forty-five years since He spoke this word to Mosheh: Kalev (Caleb) said that it had been forty-five years since Yahweh promised to give him the land that he had walked on in Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

It has been forty-five years since Yahweh said this to Mosheh

Yahweh said this to Mosheh forty-five years ago

14:10c

while Yisrael (Israel) wandered in the wilderness.

  • At that time the Israelis (Israelites) were walking through the wilderness.

  • while the people of Yisrael were wandering through the wilderness.

while Yisrael wandered in the wilderness: The name Yisrael refers to the descendants of Yisrael (who was also called Ya’akov (Jacob)). This is another way to say “Israelis.”

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

at that time the Israelis were walking through the wilderness

while the people of Yisrael were going through the wilderness

14:10d

So here I am today, eighty-five years old,

  • Now look at me. I am eighty-five years old today.

  • Here I am, eighty-five years old now.

So here I am: In the BSB, the phrase So here I am translates the same Hebrew words as occurred in verse 14:10a. This is a literary device to call attention to what comes next. You should translate this phrase in whatever way is natural to call attention to what comes next.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

Look at me! (GNT)

Now here I am (NCV)

today, eighty-five years old: Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

Today I am eighty-five years old.

Now here I am, eighty-five years old today

General Comment on 14:10a-d

Some English versions translate this verse as one long sentence. In some languages it may be more natural to divide the verse into several sentences. For example:

But now, look. It has been forty-five years since the Lord said that to Mosheh (Moses). That was when Yisrael (Israel) was going through the desert, and the Lord, as he promised, has kept me alive ever since. Look at me! I am eighty-five years old. (GNT)

title: Joshua 14:11
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:11a

still as strong today as I was the day Mosheh sent me out.

  • I am as strong today as I was when Mosheh told me to go explore the land.

  • I am still as strong now as I was on the day Mosheh sent me out.

still as strong today as I was the day Mosheh (Moses) sent me out: Here are some other ways to translate this sentence:

I am as strong today as I was when Mosheh told me to go to spy on the land

I am as strong today as I was then

14:11b

As my strength was then, so it is now

  • I am as strong now as I was then.

  • I am strong enough

As my strength was then, so it is now: The clause As my strength was then, so it is now has the same meaning as the previous clause. It is repeated in slightly different words in Hebrew to emphasize the statement.

14:11c

for war, for going out, and for coming in.

  • I can go fight battles and I can do anything else.

  • to go fight in battle, and do my daily work.

for war: The phrase for war indicates the ability to be a soldier and fight in a battle.

for going out, and for coming in: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as for going out, and for coming in is more literally “to go out and to come in.” This is a Hebrew idiom that refers to the ability to do one’s daily activities.

Here are some other ways to translate these phrases:

to fight battles and to do all my daily work

to go out to war as well as do any other thing

I am still strong enough to fight in war, and to do anything else.

title: Joshua 14:12
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:12a

Now therefore give me this hill country that Yahweh promised me on that day,

  • So please give me the hill country that Yahweh promised me then.

  • Now please give me the mountain region that Yahweh told me I will receive.

Now therefore give me this hill country: The phrase hill country refers to a region that had mountains in it. In verses 13–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gives the town of Hevron (Hebron) to Kalev (Caleb). Hevron was in this mountainous area.

that Yahweh promised me on that day: Numbers 14:24 tells how Yahweh promised to give Kalev the land that he had explored.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

So I’m asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day (CEV)

Now give me the mountain region which Yahweh told me then I will receive

14:12b

for you yourself heard then that the Anakim were there,

  • You heard then that the descendants of Anak lived there,

  • At that time you heard that the Anak people lived there.

for you yourself heard then that the Anakim were there: When the twelve spies came back, they told Mosheh (Moses) about people called Anakim who lived in that land. Yehoshua (Joshua) was there and heard the report.

Anakim: The term Anakim refers to people who were descended from Anak. They are mentioned in Joshua 11:21, and you should translate this word the same way in both places.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

You heard then that the descendants of Anak lived there

At that time you heard that the Anak people lived there

14:12c

with great and fortified cities.

  • in large cities surrounded by walls.

  • They lived in large walled cities.

with great and fortified cities: The phrase with great and fortified cities indicates that the Anak people lived in towns with strong walls and gates.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

they lived in large towns surrounded by walls

they have large walled towns

14:12d

Perhaps with Yahweh’s help I will drive them out,

  • If Yahweh is with me, I will take their land from them,

  • With Yahweh helping me, I will force them to leave their land,

Perhaps with Yahweh’s help: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB has translated as Perhaps is more literally “perhaps, maybe.” This word in Hebrew expresses hope, not doubt.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

if Yahweh is with me

I know that Yahweh will help me

I will drive them out: The clause I will drive them out means that Kalev (Caleb) will force the Anak people to leave the land and he will be able to live there himself.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

I will force them to leave their land

I will take their land from them

14:12e

as Yahweh has spoken.”

  • as Yahweh said I will.”

  • as Yahweh promised.”

as Yahweh has spoken: Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

as Yahweh promised

as Yahweh promised that I would do.

title: Joshua 14:13
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:13a

Then Yehoshua blessed Kalev son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh)

  • ¶ Then Yehoshua blessed Kalev.

  • ¶ Then Yehoshua (Joshua) prayed that Yahweh would be with Kalev (Caleb),

Then Yehoshua blessed Kalev son of Yefuneh: The phrase Yehoshua blessed Kalev indicates that Yehoshua prayed that God would help Kalev and give him success. In 8:33 it said that Mosheh (Moses) blessed the people. You should translate this verb the same way you did there.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

Then Yehoshua gave a blessing to Kalev

Then Yehoshua prayed that God would help Kalev (CEV)

Kalev son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh): This phrase was used in 14:6 and you should translate it the same way in both places.

14:13b

and gave him Hevron (Hebron) as his inheritance.

  • Yehoshua (Joshua) gave the city of Hevron to Kalev (Caleb) the son of Yefuneh as his own possession.

  • and he gave Hevron City to Kalev and to his descendants.

and gave him Hevron as his inheritance: The town of Hevron was in the mountainous area that Yehoshua gave to Kalev. Hevron was mentioned in 10:3, and you should translate it the same way in both places.

as his inheritance: The phrase as his inheritance indicates that Kalev will receive the town of Hevron for his own.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

Yehoshua gave the town of Hevron to Kalev the son of Yefuneh and to his descendants

Yehoshua gave Kalev the son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh) the town of Hevron as his own possession

title: Joshua 14:14
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:14a

Therefore Hevron belongs to Kalev son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh) the Kenizi (Kenizzite) as an inheritance to this day,

  • So the city of Hevron became the possession of Kalev the son of Yefuneh, the grandson of Kenaz, up to this day,

  • So Kalev (Caleb) the son of Yefuneh the son of Kenaz conquered the city of Hevron (Hebron), and it still belongs to his descendants to this day.

Therefore Hevron belongs to Kalev son of Yefuneh the Kenizi as an inheritance to this day: There is some implied information here. Kalev conquered the town of Hevron.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

The town of Hevron became the possession of Kalev the son of Yefuneh the son of Kenaz up to today

So Kalev conquered the town of Hevron, and it still belongs to his descendants

14:14b

because he wholly followed Yahweh, the God of Yisrael (Israel).

  • because he was completely loyal to Yahweh the God of Yisrael.

  • This happened because he followed Yahweh the God of Yisrael with all his heart.

because he wholly followed Yahweh, the God of Yisrael: The expression wholly followed translates the same Hebrew words as were found in verses 14:8c (“remained loyal” in the BSB) and 14:9d (“wholly followed” in the BSB). Translate this expression the same way as you did in those verses.

Yahweh, the God of Yisrael: The phrase Yahweh, the God of Yisrael is slightly different from the way that God was referred to in verses 8c and 9d. There the phrase “Yahweh, my God” was used.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

because he was completely loyal to Yahweh the God of Yisrael

because Kalev (Caleb) followed Yahweh the God of Yisrael with all his heart

title: Joshua 14:15
content:
Section 14:6–15 Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron)

In this section Kalev reminded Yehoshua of a promise that Mosheh (Moses) had made to him. After Kalev helped to spy out the land of Kena’an (Canaan), Mosheh promised that he would inherit the land he had walked on. So Yehoshua granted the town of Hevron to Kalev.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Kalev’s inheritance

Kalev claimed his inheritance

14:15a-b

(Hevron used to be called Kiryat-Arba (Kiriath-arba), after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakim.): The Hebrew word that begins this verse is often translated as “Now” and introduces an explanation about the name of Hevron. The BSB indicates this by putting it in parentheses. Introduce this explanation in a way that is natural in your language.

14:15a

(Hevron used to be called Kiryat-Arba,

  • The city of Hevron (Hebron) used to be called Kiryat-Arba,

  • Before that time, the city of Hevron was called the City of Arba.

Hevron used to be called Kiryat-Arba: The town of Kiryat-Arba is mentioned in Genesis 23:2. The word “Kiryat (Kiriath)” means “town” in Hebrew. Arba is the name of one of the Anak people.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

The town of Hevron used to be called Kiryat-Arba

In the past times, the name of Hevron was Kiryat-Arba (Kiriath-arba)

Before that time, the town of Hevron was called Arba

14:15b

after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakim.)

  • because Arba was the most important man of the Anak people.

  • It was named after Arba, the greatest man among the people of Anak.

after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakim: Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

because Arba was the most important man of the Anak people

It was named after Arba, the greatest man among the people of Anak

14:15c

Then the land had rest from war.

  • Then there was no war in the land.

  • Then there was peace in the land.

Then the land had rest from war: The clause the land had rest from war translates the same Hebrew words as are found in verse 11:23. You should translate this sentence in the same way that you translated verse 11:23.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

Then there was peace in the land.

Then there was no war in the land

title: Joshua 15:1
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:1–4

The next four paragraphs describe the boundaries of the land that Yehoshua (Joshua) assigned to the tribe of Yehudah. The south boundary is described in verses 1–4. The east boundary is in verse 5a. The north boundary is in verses 5b through verse 11. The west boundary is in verse 12.

The south boundary starts at the south end of the Dead Sea. From there it swings south and then west to encompass a large area of the Negev Desert. Finally it ends at the Mediterranean Sea.

15:1a

Now the allotment for the clans of the tribe of Yehudah (Judah)

  • ¶ The land that the people of Yehudah received by lot according to their sub-clans

  • ¶ When Yehoshua threw lots for the clan of Yehudah, this was the land that they received. Each sub-clan received their own piece of land.

Now the allotment for the clans of the tribe of Yehudah: The phrase the allotment refers to the land that the tribe of Yehudah received when Eleazar and Yehoshua cast lots for them. This was first mentioned in Joshua 14:2 where it was translated as “inheritance…assigned by lot.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The land that was assigned by lot to the tribe of Yehudah

When Yehoshua (Joshua) threw the lots, this was the land that the people of Yehudah received

Yehoshua assigned this land to the tribe of Yehudah (Judah)

for the clans: The nation of Yisrael (Israel) was divided into tribes, named after the twelve sons of Ya’akov (Jacob). Each tribe was divided into clans or groups of families named after the sons of the leader of the tribe. See how you translated “tribe,” “clan,” and “family” in Joshua 7:14.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

Each family/clan received their own portion of land.

15:1b

extended to the border of Edom,

  • extended south to the border of Edom in the southeast.

  • Their land went south to the border of the land of Edom.

extended to the border of Edom: The clause extended to the border of Edom indicates that the southern border of the land that Yehudah (Judah) received was next to the land of Edom.

Edom: Edom was a kingdom that was south of the Dead Sea and southeast of the territory of Yehudah. The kingdom of Edom is mentioned throughout the Old Testament. See for example, Genesis 32:3. You should translate it the same way every time.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

their land extended south to the land of Edom

their land went south to the border of the Edom Kingdom in the southeast

15:1c

to the Wilderness of Tsin (Zin) at the extreme southern boundary:

  • It went south to the wilderness of Tsin in the southwest.

  • The southernmost point was the Wilderness of Tsin.

to the Wilderness of Tsin at the extreme southern boundary: The Wilderness of Tsin was south of the land that Yehudah (Judah) received, and west of the land of Edom.

at the extreme southern boundary: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as at the extreme southern boundary is more literally “from the end of the south.” It indicates the southernmost point of the southern border of Yehudah’s land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

as far south as the wilderness of Tsin (NLT)

The southernmost point was the wilderness of Tsin in the southwest

title: Joshua 15:2
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:1–4

The next four paragraphs describe the boundaries of the land that Yehoshua (Joshua) assigned to the tribe of Yehudah. The south boundary is described in verses 1–4. The east boundary is in verse 5a. The north boundary is in verses 5b through verse 11. The west boundary is in verse 12.

The south boundary starts at the south end of the Dead Sea. From there it swings south and then west to encompass a large area of the Negev Desert. Finally it ends at the Mediterranean Sea.

15:2a

Their southern border started at the bay on the southern tip of the Salt Sea,

  • ¶ The southern border started at the south end of the Salt Sea where the end of the sea points to the south.

  • ¶ That boundary began at the southern tip of the Dead Sea

Their southern border started at the bay on the southern tip of the Salt Sea: Verses 2–4 describe the southern boundary of Yehudah’s (Judah’s) land in more detail. The clause Their southern border started at the bay on the southern tip of the Salt Sea indicates that the Salt Sea was the eastern point of the south boundary of Yehudah. the Salt Sea is also known as the Dead Sea.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yehudah’s southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea (CEV)

That boundary began at the south tip of the Salt Sea

at the bay on the southern tip of the Salt Sea: The phrase at the bay on the southern tip of the Salt Sea further describes the beginning point of the southern border of Yehudah.

Some English versions combine verse 15:2a-b. For example:

Their southern boundary started from the bay at the southern end of the Dead Sea (NIV)

title: Joshua 15:3
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:1–4

The next four paragraphs describe the boundaries of the land that Yehoshua (Joshua) assigned to the tribe of Yehudah. The south boundary is described in verses 1–4. The east boundary is in verse 5a. The north boundary is in verses 5b through verse 11. The west boundary is in verse 12.

The south boundary starts at the south end of the Dead Sea. From there it swings south and then west to encompass a large area of the Negev Desert. Finally it ends at the Mediterranean Sea.

15:3a

proceeded south of the Ascent of Akrabim (Akrabbim),

  • The border goes south of Akrabim Pass,

  • The boundary line continued to the south of Scorpion Pass,

proceeded south of the Ascent of Akrabim: This indicates that the border passed to the south of the Ascent of Akrabim as it continued going on toward the west.

proceeded: The Hebrew verbs in verses 3–12 are not in the same tense as the verbs in verses 1 and 2. The RSV uses a present tense to reflect this change in the Hebrew tense, but some English versions like the BSB do not.

It is recommended that you translate these verses using the same tense or aspect throughout. Choose a tense or aspect that is natural for a description of land boundaries.

Ascent of Akrabim: The phrase Ascent of Akrabim refers to a mountain pass or a road through the mountains. The Hebrew word Akrabim means scorpion. Some English versions translate this phrase as “Scorpion Pass.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass (CEV)

The boundary line continued south of Scorpion Pass

The border went south of Akrabim (Akrabbim) Pass as it continued westward

15:3b

continued on to Tsin (Zin), went over to the south of Kadesh-Barnea (Kadesh-barnea),

  • continues to the Wilderness of Tsin, and ascends south of Kadesh-Barnea.

  • went to the Wilderness of Tsin and went uphill as it passed south of Kadesh-Barnea Town.

continued on to Tsin, went over to the south of Kadesh-Barnea: The town of Kadesh-Barnea was mentioned in Joshua 10:41. You should translate it the same way in both places.

Tsin: This refers to the “Wilderness of Tsin” that was mentioned in verse 15:1.

went over: The phrase went over indicates that the boundary went uphill as it went past the town of Kadesh-Barnea.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

then continued to the Wilderness of Tsin, and up south of the town of Kadesh-Barnea

the boundary line went to the Wilderness of Tsin (Zin) and went uphill as it passed south of Kadesh-Barnea (Kadesh-barnea)

15:3c

ran past Hetsron (Hezron) up to Adar (Addar), and curved toward Karka.

  • It continues past Hetsron, up to Adar, and turns toward Karka.

  • The boundary line went to the town of Hetsron, then ascended to the town of Adar, and turned toward the town of Karka.

ran past Hetsron up to Adar, and curved toward Karka: The phrase up to Adar indicates that the boundary ascended in elevation as it went from Hetsron to Adar.

Hetsron…Adar…Karka: These are the names of small towns. It may be helpful in some languages to include the term “town” in the translation.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It continued past Hetsron up to Adar, turned toward Karka (CEV)

Then it ran past Hetsron up to Adar and curved around to Karka (NIV)

The boundary line went on to the town of Hetsron (Hezron), then went uphill to the town of Adar (Addar), and turned toward the town of Karka

title: Joshua 15:4
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:1–4

The next four paragraphs describe the boundaries of the land that Yehoshua (Joshua) assigned to the tribe of Yehudah. The south boundary is described in verses 1–4. The east boundary is in verse 5a. The north boundary is in verses 5b through verse 11. The west boundary is in verse 12.

The south boundary starts at the south end of the Dead Sea. From there it swings south and then west to encompass a large area of the Negev Desert. Finally it ends at the Mediterranean Sea.

15:4a

It proceeded to Atsmon (Azmon),

  • The border then continues to Atsmon,

  • The boundary line went past the town of Atsmon,

It proceeded to Atsmon: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border then continued to Atsmon

The boundary line went past the town of Atsmon

15:4b

joined the Egyptian Brook (Brook of Egypt),

  • follows the river on the border with Mitsrayim (Egypt),

  • and continued along the Mitsrayim River

joined the Egyptian Brook: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Brook refers to a river. This river had water only in the rainy season. See Joshua 12:1 where this Hebrew word was translated “Valley.”

Egyptian Brook: The phrase Egyptian Brook refers to a river that drains rainwater from the Sinay (Sinai) Peninsula into the Mediterranean Sea. This river is usually dry but becomes a large river when it rains. It formed the boundary between Yisrael (Israel) and Mitsrayim. Today this river is called the Wadi el Arish.

Here are some ways to translate this phrase:

Stream of Mitsrayim (NET)

River of Mitsrayim (GW, KJV)

Wadi of Mitsrayim (Egypt) (NIV, NJPS)

the stream on the border of Mitsrayim (GNT)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The boundary line followed the river valley on the border of Mitsrayim

and continued along the Egyptian Brook (Brook of Egypt)

15:4c

and ended at the Sea.

  • and ends at the Mediterranean Sea.

  • until it reached the Mediterranean Sea.

and ended at the Sea: The term the Sea refers to the Mediterranean Sea. It may be helpful to make this clear.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and ended at the Mediterranean Sea

until it reached the Mediterranean Sea

15:4d

This was their southern border.

  • That is your southern border.

  • This is the southern boundary line of the clan of Yehudah (Judah).

This was their southern border: Here the author speaks directly to the people of Yehudah. The BSB translates this as their southern border, while some English versions chose to translate this with a second person plural reference. For example:

All this describes your boundary on the south

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

their south boundary (NIV, NET)

That was the south border of the tribe of Yehudah

title: Joshua 15:5
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:5a

The east boundary of Yehudah is marked by the Dead Sea.

15:5a

The eastern border was the Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Yarden (Jordan).

  • ¶ Yehudah’s (Judah’s) eastern border is along the Salt Sea, to where the Yarden River flowed into it.

  • ¶ The eastern boundary is the Dead Sea, going north to the mouth of the Yarden River.

The eastern border was the Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Yarden: The Salt Sea is another name for the Dead Sea. The phrase as the mouth of the Yarden indicates that the east border of Yehudah’s land extended the length of the Dead Sea, from its southern point to where the Dead Sea reached the Yarden River in the north.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yehudah’s east boundary was along the Dead Sea, from its south end to where the Yarden River flows into it

The border on the east was the Dead Sea, going north to the mouth of the Yarden River

Paragraph 15:5b-11

The north boundary of Yehudah (Judah) started from the north end of the Dead Sea and went west from there to the Mediterranean Sea. This boundary did not go in a straight line. It swung south to avoid Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which was part of the territory of Benyamin (Benjamin).

15:5b

The northern border started

  • ¶ The northern border starts

  • ¶ The boundary on the north begins at

The northern border started: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The north border ran

The boundary on the north began at

15:5c

from the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Yarden (Jordan),

  • at the end of the Dead Sea, where it meets the Yarden River.

  • the north end of the Dead Sea, where the Yarden River flows into it.

from the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Yarden: The phrase the bay of the sea indicates the north end of the Dead Sea.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

from the end of the Dead Sea where it meets the Yarden River

the north end of the Dead Sea where the Yarden River flows into it

title: Joshua 15:6
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:5b-11

The north boundary of Yehudah started from the north end of the Dead Sea and went west from there to the Mediterranean Sea. This boundary did not go in a straight line. It swung south to avoid Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which was part of the territory of Benyamin (Benjamin).

15:6a

went up to Beyt-Hoglah (Beth-hoglah),

  • From there the boundary ascends to the town of Beyt-Hoglah

  • Then the border goes uphill to Beyt-Hoglah Town

went up to Beyt-Hoglah: The location of the town of Beyt-Hoglah is uncertain.

went up: The Dead Sea is at a low point, so the path from the Dead Sea to Beyt-Hoglah went uphill.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border went uphill to the town of Beyt-Hoglah

From there the border ascended to Beyt-Hoglah

15:6b

proceeded north of Beyt-Ha’aravah (Beth-arabah),

  • and continues north of the town of Beyt-Ha’aravah.

  • and goes north of Beyt-Ha’aravah Town.

proceeded north of Beyt-Ha’aravah: The location of the town of Beyt-Ha’aravah is uncertain.15:6 Rasmussen, p. 229.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and continued north of the town of Beyt-Ha’aravah

and went on north of Beyt-Ha’aravah

15:6c

and went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Re’uven (Reuben).

  • Then the boundary ascends to the large stone of Bohan, the son of Re’uven.

  • The border continues westward, uphill to the stone of Bohan who was Re’uven’s son.

and went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Re’uven: The location of the Stone of Bohan is not known. Probably it was a large rock set up to remember an important event. In some languages it may be helpful to add a qualifier such as “big stone” or “large stone.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border ascended to the large stone of Bohan the son of Re’uven

The boundary continued west, uphill to the stone of Bohan who was the son of Re’uven

title: Joshua 15:7
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:5b-11

The north boundary of Yehudah started from the north end of the Dead Sea and went west from there to the Mediterranean Sea. This boundary did not go in a straight line. It swung south to avoid Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which was part of the territory of Benyamin (Benjamin).

15:7a

Then the border went up to Devir (Debir) from the Valley of Akor (Achor),

  • The border ascends to Devir from the Valley of Akor.

  • Then it continues along Trouble Valley, going up to Devir Town.

Then the border went up to Devir from the Valley of Akor: The location of the town of Devir is uncertain.

the Valley of Akor: the Valley of Akor was mentioned in Joshua 7:24. You should translate it the same way in both places. If you translated it as “Valley of Trouble” in chapter 7 you should also do so here.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The boundary ascended from the Valley of Akor to the town of Devir

The border went up to the town of Devir from Trouble Valley

15:7b

turning north to Gilgal, which faces the Ascent of Adumim (Adummim)

  • It turns north to Gilgal, which is across from the Pass of Adumim

  • It goes north toward Gilgal Town, which faces the road going through the Adumim Pass

turning north: The phrase turning north indicates that the border turned north after reaching the town of Devir (Debir).

to Gilgal: The phrase to Gilgal indicates that when the border turned north it went toward the town of Gilgal.

Gilgal: This town of Gilgal is not the same as the Gilgal mentioned in Joshua 5:9.

which faces the Ascent of Adumim: The phrase the Ascent of Adumim refers to a pass that goes from east to west through the mountains. The road along this pass was the major road from the Dead Sea up to Yerushalem (Jerusalem). The road was on the south side of this pass. The town of “Gilgal” was on the north side of the pass.15:7 Rasmussen, p. 225.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

it turned north to Gilgal, which faced the Pass of Adumim

it turned north toward Gilgal, which was on the north side of Adumim (Adummim) Pass, opposite the road that goes through the pass

15:7c

south of the ravine.

  • on the south side of the valley.

  • which is across the valley, on its southern side.

south of the ravine: The clause south of the ravine indicates that the road through mountains was on the south side of the pass.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

south of the valley

which was across the valley on its southern side

15:7d

It continued along the waters of Eyn-Shemesh (En-shemesh)

  • The boundary continues west to the spring of Eyn-Shemesh,

  • Then the border goes to Eyn-Shemesh Spring

Verses 7d through verse 8 describe the boundary as it swings south around Yerushalem (Jerusalem), going from east to west.

It continued along the waters of Eyn-Shemesh: The phrase waters of Eyn-Shemesh refers to a spring called Eyn-Shemesh. Eyn-Shemesh Spring was near Yerushalem. This spring still exists today and is called Ayin (Ain) el-Hod.15:7 Rasmussen, p. 234.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The boundary continued west to the spring of Eyn-Shemesh

Then the border went to Eyn-Shemesh Spring

15:7e

and came out at Eyn-Rogel (En-rogel).

  • and southwest to Eyn-Rogel.

  • and goes southwest to Eyn-Rogel Spring, which ends its southward direction.

and came out at Eyn-Rogel: The clause and came out at Eyn-Rogel means that this was the southernmost point of the border as it went south around Yerushalem (Jerusalem).15:7 Boling and Wright, p 368. It does not mean that the border ended here.

Eyn-Rogel: The name Eyn-Rogel refers to a spring in the Kidron Valley south of Yerushalem.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and went on to Eyn-Rogel Spring

and it went southwest to the spring of Eyn-Rogel, which ends its southward direction

title: Joshua 15:8
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:5b-11

The north boundary of Yehudah started from the north end of the Dead Sea and went west from there to the Mediterranean Sea. This boundary did not go in a straight line. It swung south to avoid Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which was part of the territory of Benyamin (Benjamin).

15:8a

From there the border went up the Valley of Hinom (Hinnom)

  • The boundary then ascends through the valley of the son of Hinom

  • The border goes up the valley of the son of Hinom

From there the border went up the Valley of Hinom: The clause the border went up indicates that the boundary line climbed in elevation from the spring of Eyn-Rogel (En-rogel) through the Valley of Hinom.

the Valley of Hinom: The phrase Valley of Hinom refers to a valley that is southwest of Yerushalem.

Hinom: Hinom is the name of a person. The Hebrew word ben hinnom means “son of Hinom.” Some English versions keep the Hebrew word and say “valley of Ben Hinom.” It is recommended that you follow the tradition of the major language version in your area when you translate this name.

Here are some ways that English versions translate this name:

valley of the son of Hinom (RSV, ESV, KJV)

valley of Ben Hinom (Hinnom) (NET, NIV, NABRE, NASB, NJPS, GW, NLT)

Hinom Valley (Hinnom Valley) (GNT, CEV)

15:8b

along the southern slope of the Yevusim (Jebusites) (that is, Yerushalem (Jerusalem))

  • and along the southern slope of Yerushalem, where the Yevus (Jebus) people live.

  • beside the hill to the south of the town of Yerushalem, which was then called Yevus.

along the southern slope of the Yevusim (that is, Yerushalem): The phrase southern slope refers to the slope of the hill that is south of Yerushalem.15:8 Aharoni, p. 255.

of the Yevusim: The term Yevusim refers to the Yevus people. Yevus was also the name of their town at the time of Yehoshua (Joshua). Later King David conquered this town and renamed it Yerushalem.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

along the south slope of Yerushalem, where the Yevus people live

beside the hill to the south of Yerushalem, which was then called Yevus

15:8c

and ascended to the top of the hill

  • The border then climbs up to the top of the mountain

  • From there the border goes up to the peak of the mountain

and ascended to the top of the hill: The clause ascended to the top of the hill indicates that the border continued to climb up until it reached the top of a mountain.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

the border climbed up to the top of the mountain

15:8d

that faces the Valley of Hinom (Hinnom) on the west,

  • which is on the west side of the valley of Hinom.

  • on the west edge of Hinom Valley (Hinnom Valley)
