that faces the Valley of Hinom on the west: The clause faces the Valley of Hinom on the west indicates that the mountain is on the west side of the Valley of Hinom.

the Valley of Hinom: The Valley of Hinom is the same place as the “Valley of Hinom” in verse 15:8a.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

which is on the west side of the valley of Hinom

on the west side of the Hinom Valley

15:8e

at the northern end of the Valley of Refaim (Rephaim).

  • It is on the northern side of the valley of Refaim.

  • and on the north edge of Refaim Valley (Rephaim Valley).

at the northern end of the Valley of Refaim: The Refaim people were mentioned in Joshua 12:4 and you should translate the term the same way in both places.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

That mountain is on the northern side of the valley of Refaim

It is on the northern edge of the Refaim Valley

title: Joshua 15:9
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:5b-11

The north boundary of Yehudah started from the north end of the Dead Sea and went west from there to the Mediterranean Sea. This boundary did not go in a straight line. It swung south to avoid Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which was part of the territory of Benyamin (Benjamin).

15:9a

From the hilltop the border curved

  • From the peak of that mountain the border goes downhill northwest

  • Then the border turns from the mountain top to go down

From the hilltop the border curved: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From the peak of that mountain the border went downward northwest

Then the border turned from the mountain top to go down

15:9b

to the spring of the Waters of Neftoah (Nephtoah),

  • to the spring of Neftoah.

  • to Neftoah Spring.

to the spring of the Waters of Neftoah: The phrase the spring of the Waters of Neftoah refers to a spring northwest of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

to the spring of Neftoah

to the Neftoah Spring

15:9c

proceeded to the cities of Mount Efron (Ephron),

  • The border continues up to the towns around Mount Efron.

  • The border goes from there to the towns near Efron Mountain.

proceeded to the cities of Mount Efron: Mount Efron was west of Yerushalem (Jerusalem), but its exact location is uncertain.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border continued to the towns around Mount Efron

The border went from there to the towns near Efron Mountain

15:9d

and then bent around toward Ba’alah (Baalah) (that is, Kiryat-Yearim (Kiriath-jearim)).

  • Then it turns west toward the town of Ba’alah. That town is called Kiryat-Yearim today.

  • Then the border continues down to Ba’alah Town, which is now called Kiryat-Yearim Town.

and then bent around toward Ba’alah (that is, Kiryat-Yearim): The town of Kiryat-Yearim is mentioned in Joshua 9:17. It is at a lower elevation than the towns around Mount Efron (Ephron).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then it turned west toward the town of Ba’alah. That town is called Kiryat-Yearim today

Then the border continued down to Ba’alah, which is now called Kiryat-Yearim

title: Joshua 15:10
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:5b-11

The north boundary of Yehudah started from the north end of the Dead Sea and went west from there to the Mediterranean Sea. This boundary did not go in a straight line. It swung south to avoid Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which was part of the territory of Benyamin (Benjamin).

15:10a

The border curled westward from Ba’alah (Baalah) to Mount Se’ir (Seir),

  • The border then curves to the west of Ba’alah on to Mount Se’ir.

  • The border goes in a curve west from Ba’alah Town and arrives at Mount Se’ir.

The border curled westward from Ba’alah to Mount Se’ir: The clause curled westward from Ba’alah to Mount Se’ir indicates that the border line was not straight. It went on a curve as it went westward to Mount Se’ir.

Mount Se’ir: The location of this mountain is uncertain. It may be a mountain ridge west of Kiryat-Yearim (Kiriath-jearim) and north of Kesalon (Chesalon), about eleven miles west of Yerushalem.15:10 Rasmussen, p. 250.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border then curved to the west of the town of Ba’alah to Mount Se’ir

The border went in a curve west from Ba’alah to Se’ir Mountain

15:10b

ran along the northern slope of Mount Jearim (that is, Kesalon),

  • It descends on to the northern side of Mount Jearim (also called Kesalon).

  • Then the border goes down along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim (which is also called Mount Kesalon).

ran along the northern slope of Mount Jearim (that is, Kesalon (Chesalon)): The phrase the northern slope of Mount Jearim refers to the northern ridge of Mount Jearim.

Mount Jearim (that is, Kesalon): Mount Jearim was one of the low hills west of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).

There is an interpretation issue here. There are two ways to understand the relationship between Kesalon and Mount Jearim.

  1. Kesalon is another name for Mount Jearim. For example, the ESV says:

    Mount Jearim (that is Kesalon) (BSB, ESV, RSV, NET, NIV, GW, NJPS, GNT, KJV)

  2. Kesalon is the name of a town. For example:

    the town of Kesalon on the northern slope of Mount Jearim (NLT) (NLT, CEV)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1). This is followed by most English versions.15:10 In modern times there is a town in this area called Kesla. Thus, it is possible that there was an ancient town called Kesalon (Chesalon). See Woudstra, p. 255–256.

Kesalon: Here are some ways that the English versions spell this word:

Kesalon (BSB, ESV, RSV, GW, GNT, CEV, NABRE, NJPS, KJV)

Kesalon (NIV, NET, NLT)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border continued to the northern side of Mount Jearim (also called Mount Kesalon)

Then the border went down along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim (which is also called Mount Kesalon)

15:10c

went down to Beyt-Shemesh (Beth-shemesh), and crossed to Timnah.

  • It continues going down southwest to Beyt-Shemesh and then northwest to Timnah.

  • The border descends to Beyt-Shemesh Town and goes to Timnah Town.

went down to Beyt-Shemesh, and crossed to Timnah: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border descended to the town of Beyt-Shemesh and went on to the town of Timnah

It continued going down southwest to Beyt-Shemesh and then northwest to Timnah

crossed to Timnah: There is an interpretation issue here:

  1. The border goes to the town of Timnah. For example:

    and on to Timnah (GW) (BSB, GW, NIV, NET, NABRE, NJPS, CEV, NLT, KJV)

  2. The border passes by the town of Timnah. For example:

    passes along by Timnah (ESV) (ESV, RSV, GNT)

It is recommended that you follow option (1). This is the option taken by most English versions. However, the Hebrew grammar can be understood either way, and probably both are true.

title: Joshua 15:11
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:5b-11

The north boundary of Yehudah started from the north end of the Dead Sea and went west from there to the Mediterranean Sea. This boundary did not go in a straight line. It swung south to avoid Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which was part of the territory of Benyamin (Benjamin).

15:11a

Then it went out to the northern slope of Ekron,

  • The border then goes along the slope of the hill to the north of Ekron.

  • It continues along the hillside north of Ekron Town.

Then it went out to the northern slope of Ekron: The phrase the northern slope indicates a mountain slope.

Ekron: The town of Ekron was one of the five most important towns of the Pelishtim (Philistines). It was southwest of Timnah.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It continued along the hillside north of the town of Ekron

The border then went on along the slope of the hill to the north of Ekron

15:11b

curved toward Shikeron (Shikkeron),

  • Then it curves westward toward Shikeron.

  • There the border turns to go west to Shikeron Town.

curved toward Shikeron: The town of Shikeron lies between the town of Ekron and the town of Yavne’el (Jabneel).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then it curved westward toward the town of Shikeron

Then the border turned to go west to Shikeron

15:11c

proceeded to Mount Ba’alah (Baalah), went on to Yavne’el,

  • It goes on west to Mount Ba’alah and down to Yavne’el.

  • It goes along to Ba’alah Mountain and down to Yavne’el Town.

proceeded to Mount Ba’alah: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It went on west to Mount Ba’alah

The border went along to Ba’alah Mountain

went on to Yavne’el (Jabneel): The town of Yavne’el is northwest of the town of Shikeron (Shikkeron). In later times Yavne’el was referred to as Yavneh (Jamnia). The GNT uses the name Yavneh.

15:11d

and ended at the Sea.

  • There it ends at the Mediterranean Sea.

  • Then it goes on to its end at the Mediterranean Sea.

and ended at the Sea:. The term the Sea refers to the Mediterranean Sea.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border continued down to the town of Yavne’el and then went on to end at the Mediterranean Sea

The border went to Yavne’el (Jabneel) and ended at the Mediterranean Sea

title: Joshua 15:12
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:12

The west boundary of Yehudah is the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.

15:12a

And the western border was the coastline of the Great Sea.

  • ¶ The western border runs along the shore of the Mediterranean Sea.

  • ¶ The coast of the Mediterranean Sea forms the western border.

And the western border was the coastline of the Great Sea: The phrase the coastline of the Great Sea indicates that the western border of Yehudah’s (Judah’s) land was the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The western border ran along the shore of the Mediterranean Sea

The Mediterranean Sea was the western border

15:12b

These are the boundaries around the clans of the descendants of Yehudah.

  • The sub-clans of the clan of Yehudah lived within these boundaries.

  • The boundary described above was the boundary of the land that belonged to the sub-clans of the clan of Yehudah.

Verse 15:12b is a conclusion to verses 1–12.

These are the boundaries around the clans of the descendants of Yehudah (Judah): The phrase the clans of the descendants of Yehudah refers to all the families or clans within the tribe of Yehudah.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The clans of the tribe of Yehudah lived within these borders

The boundary described above was the boundary of the land that belonged to the families of the tribe of Yehudah

title: Joshua 15:13
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:13–19

This paragraph tells about Kalev (Caleb) and his daughter Acsah (also spelled Aksah or Aksah (Achsah) in other English versions). The story of Kalev starts in Numbers 13. In Joshua 14:6–15 Kalev received land from Yehoshua (Joshua). In this paragraph Kalev gave Acsah a gift of land when she married Othni-el.

15:13a

According to Yahweh’s command to him,

  • ¶ As Yahweh commanded Yehoshua to do,

  • ¶ Yahweh had commanded Yehoshua

According to Yahweh’s command to him: In this paragraph more information is given about Kalev.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yahweh had commanded Yehoshua

As Yahweh had instructed Yehoshua (Joshua)

15:13b

Yehoshua gave Kalev (Caleb) son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh) a portion among the sons of Yehudah (Judah)—

  • he gave a part of the land that belonged to Yehudah to Kalev the son of Yefuneh.

  • to give Kalev some land within the borders of Yehudah, and Yehoshua did so.

Yehoshua gave Kalev son of Yefuneh a portion among the sons of Yehudah: The phrase a portion among the sons of Yehudah indicates that Yehoshua gave Kalev some land within the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah.

Here are some other ways to translate verse 13a-b:

Yahweh had commanded Yehoshua to give Kalev the son of Yefuneh some land within the borders of Yehudah. So he gave it to him

As Yahweh instructed Yehoshua (Joshua) to do, he gave some land in Yehudah to Kalev, the son of Yefuneh

In some languages it may be more natural to reverse the order of 13a and 13b. For example:

Yehoshua gave Kalev (Caleb) the son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh) a piece of land within the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah (Judah), as Yahweh had told him to do

15:13c

Kiryat-Arba (Kiriath-arba), that is, Hevron (Hebron).

  • He gave him the town of Kiryat-Arba, which is now called Hevron.

  • He received the town of Hevron which was formerly called Kiryat-Arba

Kiryat-Arba, that is, Hevron: The term Kiryat-Arba refers to the town that Yehoshua (Joshua) gave to Kalev. In Hebrew the word Kiryat-Arba means “town of Arba.” Some English versions translate it this way. For example:

Kalev’s share was Hevron, which at that time was known as Arba’s Town (CEV)

Hevron: Hevron was the name of the town of Kiryat-Arba at the time the book of Yehoshua was written.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The town Yehoshua gave him was Kiryat-Arba, but it is now called Hevron

He gave Kalev (Caleb) the town of Hevron (Hebron), which in former times was called Kiryat-Arba (Kiriath-arba)

15:13d

(Arba was the forefather of Anak.)

  • Arba was the ancestor of the Anak people.

  • because Arba was the ancestor of the people of Anak.

Arba was the forefather of Anak: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as the forefather of Anak is more literally “the father of the Anak.” The word “father” in Hebrew is often used to mean ancestor. For example:

Arba was the ancestor of the Anak people-group (T4T)

Anak: There is an interpretation issue concerning the word Anak.

  1. The word Anak refers to a group of people, the descendants of a man called Anak. For example:

    because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim (CEV) (CEV, NIV)

  2. The word Anak refers to a person, the son of a man named Arba. For example:

    Arba was the father of Anak (RSV) (BSB, RSV, NET, ESV, GW, GNT, NJPS, KJV)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1) which is supported by Hebrew grammars and is implied by the information in verse 14:15.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Arba was the ancestor of the Anak people

Arba was the ancestor of the people of Anak

15:13b-c

(reordered) Yehoshua (Joshua) gave Kalev (Caleb) the son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh) a piece of land within the boundaries of the clan of Yehudah (Judah), as Yahweh had told him to.

title: Joshua 15:14
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:13–19

This paragraph tells about Kalev (Caleb) and his daughter Acsah (also spelled Aksah or Aksah (Achsah) in other English versions). The story of Kalev starts in Numbers 13. In Joshua 14:6–15 Kalev received land from Yehoshua (Joshua). In this paragraph Kalev gave Acsah a gift of land when she married Othni-el.

15:14a

And Kalev drove out from there the three sons of Anak—

  • Kalev forced the three clans of Anak people to leave there.

  • Kalev attacked the three clans of Anak who lived in Hevron (Hebron) and made them leave.

And Kalev drove out from there the three sons of Anak: The clause Kalev drove out from there indicates that Kalev attacked the three sons of Anak and made them leave Hevron.

the three sons of Anak: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as sons can refer to a group of descendants. In this verse it is likely that the three sons of Anak refers to three tribes of the descendants of Anak.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Kalev forced three tribes of Anak people to leave there

Kalev (Caleb) attacked the three tribes of Anak people who lived in Hevron and made them leave

15:14b

the descendants of Sheshay (Sheshai), Ahiman, and Talmay (Talmai), the children of Anak.

  • Those were the clans of Sheshay, Ahiman, and Talmay, descended from Anak.

  • They were the descendants of Sheshay, Ahiman, and Talmay. Anak was their ancestor.

the descendants of Sheshay, Ahiman, and Talmay, the children of Anak: The names Sheshay, Ahiman, and Talmay refer to three tribes. Anak was their forefather. These tribes are also mentioned in Numbers 13:22 and Judges 1:10.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Those were the tribes of Sheshay, Ahiman and Talmay, all descended from Anak

These were the descendants of Sheshay, Ahiman and Talmay, who were descended from Anak

title: Joshua 15:15
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:13–19

This paragraph tells about Kalev (Caleb) and his daughter Acsah (also spelled Aksah or Aksah (Achsah) in other English versions). The story of Kalev starts in Numbers 13. In Joshua 14:6–15 Kalev received land from Yehoshua (Joshua). In this paragraph Kalev gave Acsah a gift of land when she married Othni-el.

15:15a

From there he marched against the inhabitants of Devir (Debir)

  • Then he went on from Hevron (Hebron) to fight the people of Devir.

  • After that Kalev attacked the town of Devir

From there he marched against the inhabitants of Devir: The town called Devir in this verse is not the same as the place mentioned in 15:7. The location of this town is not clear.

he marched: Kalev marched uphill to fight against the people of Devir. Hebrew verbs keep track of elevation, and thus it says “went up.” If your language does not keep track of elevation, it may be more natural to say “went.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then he went from Hevron to fight the people of Devir

Kalev (Caleb) next went to attack the town of Devir

15:15b

(formerly known as Kiryat-Sefer (Kiriath-sepher)).

  • In past times Devir (Debir) was called Kiryat-Sefer.

  • which used to be called Kiryat-Sefer.

Devir (formerly known as Kiryat-Sefer): Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

in past times the name of Devir was Kiryat-Sefer

Paragraph 15:13–19

This paragraph tells about Kalev (Caleb) and his daughter Acsah (also spelled Aksah or Aksah (Achsah) in other English versions). The story of Kalev starts in Numbers 13. In Joshua 14:6–15 Kalev received land from Yehoshua (Joshua). In this paragraph Kalev gave Acsah a gift of land when she married Othni-el.

15:16a

And Kalev said, “To the man who strikes down Kiryat-Sefer (Kiriath-sepher) and captures it,

  • Kalev said, “Whoever attacks Kiryat-Sefer and captures it,

  • Then Kalev said, “The man who fights and defeats the town of Kiryat-Sefer

And Kalev said, “To the man who strikes down Kiryat-Sefer and captures it: The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as strikes means “to hit.” This is a Hebrew idiom which means that somebody would attack Kiryat-Sefer and capture it.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

whoever defeats the town of Kiryat-Sefer

the man who attacks the town of Kiryat-Sefer and captures it

15:16b

I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.”

  • I will give my daughter Aksah (Achsah) to him to be his wife.”

  • can marry my daughter Aksah.”

I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

I will give my daughter Acsah to him to be his wife

I will let him marry my daughter Acsah

In some languages it may be more natural to reverse the order of 16a and 16b. For example:

I will let my daughter Acsah marry the man who defeats the town of Kiryat-Sefer (Kiriath-sepher)

title: Joshua 15:18
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:13–19

This paragraph tells about Kalev (Caleb) and his daughter Acsah (also spelled Aksah or Aksah (Achsah) in other English versions). The story of Kalev starts in Numbers 13. In Joshua 14:6–15 Kalev received land from Yehoshua (Joshua). In this paragraph Kalev gave Acsah a gift of land when she married Othni-el.

15:18a

One day Acsah came to Otniel (Othniel) and urged him to ask her father for a field.

  • When she arrived to marry him, she urged Othni-el to ask her father for a field.

  • When she became his wife, Aksah told Othni-el to ask her father to give her a field.

One day Acsah came to Otniel and urged him to ask her father for a field: There is an interpretation issue with the Hebrew word that the BSB translates as One day Acsah came to Otniel.

  1. It refers to the time of Acsah’s marriage to Otniel. For example:

    On the wedding day (GNT) (GNT, NLT, CEV)

  2. It refers to an unspecified day. For example:

    One day when she came to Otniel (Othniel) (NIV) (BSB, NIV, NET)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1), which is supported by commentaries15:18 See for example, Woudstra, p. 241. and by several English versions.

urged him: There is a textual issue with this Hebrew word.

  1. The Hebrew text and most Greek translations read “she urged him.” For example:

    she urged him (NIV) (BSB, NIV, ESV, RSV, NABRE, NJPS, NLT, CEV, GW, NCV, KJV)

  2. One Greek translation reads “he urged her.” For example:

    Otniel urged her (GNT) (GNT, NET, NEB)

It is recommended that you follow option (1). These are the words of the Hebrew text and of most Greek manuscripts and the reading followed by most English versions.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

When Acsah came to marry Othni-el, she urged Othni-el to ask her father for a field

When she became his wife, Acsah told Othni-el to ask her father to give her a field

15:18b

When she got off her donkey,

  • So Aksah (Achsah) got down from her donkey

  • Then Aksah went to see her father, Kalev (Caleb). As she got off her donkey

When she got off her donkey: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Acsah got down from her donkey

as she got off her donkey

To make a smoother transition between 18a and 18b, some English versions add implied information. The implied information is underlined below. For example:

Right after the wedding, Aksah started telling Otniel (Othniel) that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey (CEV)

When Kalev’s daughter married Otniel, she told him to ask her father to give her a field. Then Acsah went to talk with her father Kalev. As she got down from her donkey (T4T)

It is recommended that you add implied information if it will help readers to understand the meaning clearly.

15:18c

Kalev (Caleb) asked her, “What do you desire?”

  • And Kalev asked her, “What do you want?”

  • Kalev asked her, “What shall I do for you?”

Kalev asked her, “What do you desire?”: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and Kalev asked her “What do you want?”

Kalev asked her, “What can I do for you?”

title: Joshua 15:19
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph 15:13–19

This paragraph tells about Kalev (Caleb) and his daughter Acsah (also spelled Aksah or Aksah (Achsah) in other English versions). The story of Kalev starts in Numbers 13. In Joshua 14:6–15 Kalev received land from Yehoshua (Joshua). In this paragraph Kalev gave Acsah a gift of land when she married Othni-el.

15:19a

“Give me a blessing,” she answered.

  • She said, “Give me a gift as a sign of your blessing.”

  • Aksah answered, “Do something to show that you have blessed me.”

“Give me a blessing,” she answered: In this context, the blessing that Acsah asks for is a gift. She asks her father to give her a source of water for her land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Give me a gift as a sign of your blessing

Do something to show that you have blessed me

15:19b

“Since you have given me land in the Negev,

  • You have given me land in the dry southern region,

  • You gave me dry land in the south,

Since you have given me land in the Negev: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as you have given me is more literally “You gave me.” The word Negev often refers to the dry desert land in the south of Yehudah (Judah). In this context it probably refers to dry land south of the town of Devir (Debir). Kalev (Caleb) gave Devir to Othni-el. The town had no natural water source, so Acsah asked to be given a source of water that was nearby.15:19 Coleson, p. 132–134.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

because you have given me land in the dry south region

since you have given me dry land in the south

15:19c

give me springs of water as well.”

  • please give me pools of water as well.”

  • so give me some springs of water also.”

give me springs of water as well:

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

please give me springs of water as well

give me water holes also

15:19d

So Kalev (Caleb) gave her both the upper and lower springs.

  • So Kalev gave her both the higher and the lower springs.

  • Then Kalev gave Aksah (Achsah) the upper and the lower pools of water near Hevron (Hebron).

So Kalev gave her both the upper and lower springs: It is most likely that these water sources were near Hevron.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then Kalev gave Acsah the upper and lower pools of water

Paragraph 15:20–32

This paragraph is a list of the towns that the tribe of Yehudah received in the southern part of their land. After the paragraph there are several other paragraphs that list towns throughout the territory of Yehudah.

15:20a

This is the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Yehudah.

  • ¶ This is the land that God gave to the people of the clan of Yehudah (Judah). Each sub-clan received their own share of the land.

  • ¶ The following list shows the towns that the Yehudah clan received. Every sub-clan received its own land.

This is the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Yehudah: The word inheritance refers to the land which God gave to the people of the tribe of Yehudah.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This is the land that God promised to the people who belonged to the tribe of Yehudah

The following list shows the towns that the Yehudah tribe received

the clans: The phrase that the BSB translates as clans means that each clan or group of families received their own share of the land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Each clan received their own share of the land

Every family got their own land

twenty-nine cities in all, along with their villages.

twenty-nine cities in all, along with their villages: Most towns in the time of Yehoshua (Joshua) were very small. They had a wall for protection and a ruler of their own. Outside the walls of the town, there were villages that depended on that town for protection.

The list of town names in verses 15:21–32 adds up to thirty-six towns. It is not clear why the author says twenty-nine. It is possible that seven of the towns were small settlements that did not have villages attached to them. It is recommended that you translate this as twenty-nine.

15:36a

Sha’arayim (Shaaraim), Aditayim (Adithaim), and Gederah (or Gederotayim (Gederothaim))—

  • Sha’arayim, Aditayim. Gederah, and Gederotayim.

  • Sha’arayim Town and Aditayim Town and Gederah Town and Gederotayim Town.

Sha’arayim, Aditayim, and Gederah (or Gederotayim): There are two ways to interpret the names Gederah and Gederotayim.

  1. These names refer to two different places. For example:

    Gederah and Gederotayim (GW) (GW, ESV, NASB, RSV, NABRE, NJPS, GNT, NLT, CEV, KJV)

  2. These names refer to one place that has two different names. For example, the NIV says:

    Gederah (or Gederotayim (Gederothaim)) (BSB, NIV, NET, NCV)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1). This agrees with the Hebrew text and is followed by most English versions.15:36 If Gederah and Gederotayim are two names for the same place, then the list in this paragraph comes to a total of fourteen towns.

15:36b

fourteen cities, along with their villages.

  • In all there were fourteen towns, and there were villages that surrounded them.

  • The number of these towns was fourteen (14), with the villages that were near them.

fourteen cities, along with their villages: The list of town names in verses 15:33–36 adds up to fifteen towns. It is not clear why the author says fourteen. It is possible that one of the towns was a small settlement that did not have villages attached to it. It is recommended that you translate this as fourteen.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

In all there were fourteen towns together with the villages that surrounded them

The number of towns was fourteen, and there were villages that were near them

from Ekron to the sea, all the cities near Ashdod: The phrase from Ekron to the sea refers to the area between the town of Ekron and the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.

Ashdod: The town of Ashdod was one of the five most important towns of the Pelishtim (Philistines). Ashdod was on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. It was the largest town between Ekron and the Mediterranean Sea.

along with their villages: The phrase their villages refers to the villages that were near these towns.

  • ¶ The people of Yehudah (Judah) also received towns in the wilderness near the Dead Sea. These were Beyt-Ha’aravah Town and Midin Town and Sekakah Town,

These were in the wilderness: Beyt-Ha’aravah, Midin, Sekakah: The phrase the wilderness refers to the area near the Dead Sea, on its west side. This was a desert area.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The towns in the wilderness were Beyt-Ha’aravah, Midin, Sekakah,

The people of Yehudah also received towns in the wilderness near the Dead Sea. These were Beyt-Ha’aravah, Midin, Sekakah,

title: Joshua 15:62
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph: 15:61–62

This paragraph is a list of towns in the wilderness that were given to the tribe of Yehudah.

15:62a

Nivshan (Nibshan), the Ir-Hamelah (City of Salt), and Eyn-Gedi (En-gedi)—

  • Nivshan and the Town of Salt and Eyn-Gedi.

  • Nivshan Town and Ir Hamelah Town and Eyn-Gedi Town.

Nivshan, the Ir-Hamelah, and Eyn-Gedi: The phrase Ir-Hamelah is a translation of the Hebrew words Ir Hamelah. Some English versions transliterate this phrase instead of translating it.

Here are some ways that English versions translate this name:

Ir-Hamelah (BSB, RSV, NET, ESV, NIV, NLT, KJV)

Salt City (GNT)

Salt Town (CEV)

Ir Hamelah (GW, NABRE)

15:62b

six cities, along with their villages.

  • In all there were six towns, and there were villages that surrounded them.

  • The number of these towns was six (6), with the villages that surrounded them.

six cities, along with their villages: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

In all there were six towns, and there were villages that surrounded them

The number of these towns was six, with the villages that were near them.

title: Joshua 15:63
content:
Section 15:1–63 The tribe of Yehudah (Judah) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the tribe of Yehudah and lists the towns that are within those boundaries.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The boundaries of Yehudah

The land of the tribe of Yehudah

Paragraph: 15:63

This paragraph talks about the Yevus (Jebus) people, whom the people of Yehudah could not drive out.

15:63a

But the descendants of Yehudah could not drive out

  • The people of Yehudah (Judah) were not able to rid themselves of

  • But the clan of Yehudah could not force out.

But the descendants of Yehudah could not drive out: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the people of Yehudah were not able to make them leave

The tribe of Yehudah could not force them to leave Yerushalem (Jerusalem).

15:63b

the Yevusim (Jebusites) living in Yerushalem.

  • the Yevus (Jebus) people who lived in the town of Yerushalem,

  • the people of Yevus who lived in Yerushalem.

the Yevusim living in Yerushalem: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But as for the Yevus people who lived in the town of Yerushalem

The people of Yevus lived in Yerushalem (Jerusalem)

15:63c

So to this day the Yevusim (Jebusites) live there among the descendants of Yehudah (Judah).

  • Therefore, the Yevus (Jebus) people live with the Yehudah people in Yerushalem up to today.

  • Because of this, the people of Yevus still live with the people of Yehudah in Yerushalem till this present day.

So to this day the Yevusim live there among the descendants of Yehudah: The phrase this day refers to the time when the book of Yehoshua (Joshua) was written.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Because of this, the Yevus people still live with the Yehudah people in the town of Yerushalem up to today

Therefore, the people of Yevus live with the people of Yehudah in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) till this present day

title: Joshua 16:1
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:1a

The allotment for the descendants of Yosef (Joseph) extended from the Yarden (Jordan) at Yeriho (Jericho)

  • ¶ The land that the descendants of Yosef received began at the Yarden River near Yeriho,

  • ¶ The southern border of the land given to the descendants of Yosef started at the Yarden River near the town of Yeriho.

The allotment for the descendants of Yosef: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as The allotment is more literally “the lot went out.” There is a similar phrase in Joshua 15:1. It is recommended that you translate this phrase in a similar way in both places.

the descendants of Yosef: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as the descendants of Yosef is more literally “the sons of Yosef.” Yosef had two sons: Efrayim and Menasheh. Their descendants became the clans of Efrayim and Menasheh.

Here are some ways to translate this phrase:

the descendants of Yosef (BSB, RSV, GNT, NLT, NET)

the people of Yosef (ESV)

Yosef (Joseph) (NIV, GW)

the children of Yosef (KJV)

extended from the Yarden (Jordan) at Yeriho (Jericho): The clause extended from the Yarden at Yeriho describes the starting point of the southern border of the land given to Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh). The eastern point of the border was at the Yarden River near the town of Yeriho.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

The land that the descendants of Yosef received began at the Yarden River, near Yeriho

The south border of the land given to the descendants of Yosef started at the Yarden River, near the town of Yeriho

16:1b

to the waters of Yeriho on the east, through the wilderness

  • to the east of the springs of Yeriho. It went west into the wilderness.

  • It began to the east of the springs at the town of Yeriho and then went west into the wilderness.

to the waters of Yeriho (Jericho) on the east: The phrase waters of Yeriho refers to springs that were north of the town of Yeriho.

through the wilderness: The phrase through the wilderness indicates that the border then continued west into the wilderness.

wilderness: A wilderness is an uncultivated and uninhabited area. In this verse it refers to the Yehudi (Judean) wilderness. The Yehudi wilderness is between the Yehudi mountains and the valley of the Dead Sea. This wilderness is a rocky place that descends steeply from the mountains into the valley. It consists of flat plateaus, rounded hills, deep canyons, and cliffs.Rasmussen p. 42. It receives little rainfall and no crops can grow there. It is not a typical desert with large areas of sand. Many languages may have a term for an uncultivated area or an uninhabited place.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

It then went to the east of the springs of Yeriho and continued west into the wilderness

The border began to the east of the springs at the town of Yeriho and went west into the wilderness

16:1c

that goes up from Yeriho into the hill country of Beyt-El (Bethel).

  • It ascended from Yeriho up into the hill country to Beyt-El.

  • From Yeriho (Jericho) it went up into the mountain country as far as the town of Beyt-El.

that goes up from Yeriho into the hill country of Beyt-El: The clause goes up from Yeriho indicates that the border ascended in elevation as it went through the wilderness, into the hill country to the town of Beyt-El.

hill country: The term hill country refers to the central mountain range which runs from the north to the south of Yisrael (Israel). This area receives a lot of rain and farmers plant crops in terraces along the hillsides. See how you translated this phrase in Joshua 9:1.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border went from Yeriho up into the hill country to the town of Beyt-El

From Yeriho it went up into the mountains as far as Beyt-El

title: Joshua 16:2
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:2a

It went on from Beyt-El (Bethel) (that is, Luz)

  • It then continued west from Beyt-El, which used to be called Luz.

  • The border went to the west from the town of Beyt-El. In the past Beyt-El was called Luz.

It went on from Beyt-El (that is, Luz): There is a textual issue in this verse.

  1. The Septuagint reads from Beyt-El (that is Luz). (BSB, NIV, NLT, NCV)

  2. The Masoretic Text reads from Beyt-El to Luz. (RSV, ESV, NJPS, NABRE, GNT, KJV)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) since this agrees with four other biblical references. In Genesis 28:19, 35:6, Joshua 18:13 and Judges 1:23 Beyt-El is identified with Luz.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

it then continued westward from Beyt-El (Bethel), which used to be called Luz

The border went on from the town of Beyt-El. In the past Beyt-El was called Luz

16:2b

and proceeded to the border of the Arkim (Archites) in Atarot (Ataroth).

  • It continued to Atarot in the area of the Arkim.

  • It went to the town of Atarot in the land of the Arch people.

and proceeded to the border of the Arkim in Atarot: The Arkim were a group of people who are mentioned in only one other place in the Bible. In 2 Samuel 15:32 Hushay (Hushai) the Arki (Archite) is named as a counselor of David.This is not the same as the group mentioned in Genesis 10:17, where the Hebrew name is spelled differently.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border continued to the town of Atarot in the territory of the Arkim

It continued to the town of Atarot in the land of the Arch people

in Atarot (Ataroth): There is an interpretation issue with the term Atarot.

  1. It refers to a town called Atarot whose location is unknown. This town is also mentioned in verse 16:7. (BSB, RSV, ESV, NIV, NJPS, NLT, NCV, NET, GW)

  2. It refers to the town of Atarot Adar (Addar), which is mentioned in Joshua 16:5 and 18:13. The GNT adds the word Adar in verse 2 to show that these both refer to the same place. (GNT)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1) and translate this term Atarot. Biblical scholars do not agree on whether the town referred to in this verse is Atarot Adar or is a different town called Atarot.

title: Joshua 16:3
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:3a

Then it descended westward to the border of the Japhletites

  • It then went westward downhill to the area of the Yaflet (Japhlet) people,

  • Then the border descended west to the land of the Yaflet people,

Then it descended westward to the border of the Japhletites: Yaflet was the son of Hever (Heber) from the clan of Asher. He is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 7:32–33. The Japhletites are descendants of Yaflet.

In verse 2 the border ascended into the hill country. Now it has passed over the hills and is going downhill on its way toward the Mediterranean Sea.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It then went downhill in a westward direction to the area where the Yaflet people lived

Then the border descended west to the land of the descendants of Yaflet

16:3b

as far as the border of Lower Beyt-Horon (Lower Beth-horon)

  • continuing west as far as Lower Beyt-Horon.

  • and went on to the area of Lower Beyt-Horon town.

as far as the border of Lower Beyt-Horon: The border continued to the west until it reached the town of Lower Beyt-Horon. Lower Beyt-Horon is first mentioned in Joshua 10:10.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border continued west as far as the town of Lower Beyt-Horon

and went on as far as the area of Lower Beyt-Horon

16:3c

and on to Gezer, and it ended at the Sea.

  • Then it went to Gezer and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

  • It continued west to the town of Gezer and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

and on to Gezer, and it ended at the Sea: Gezer is a town that was seventeen miles southeast of the town of Yafo (Joppa). Yehoshua (Joshua) and the Israelis (Israelites) had defeated this town. The account of the battle is in Joshua 10:33.

the Sea: The term the Sea refers to the Mediterranean Sea.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and went to the town of Gezer and ended at the Mediterranean Sea

It then continued west to Gezer and on to the Mediterranean Sea

title: Joshua 16:4
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:4

So Efrayim and Menasheh, the sons of Yosef (Joseph), received their inheritance.

  • So the descendants of Yosef, that is the clans of Efrayim and Menasheh, received this land as their inheritance.

  • The sons of Yosef, which were the clans of Efrayim and Menasheh, received their land according to the boundary lines given above.

So Efrayim and Menasheh, the sons of Yosef, received their inheritance: This verse is the conclusion to the paragraph. It may be helpful to add a conjunction or a phrase which shows that this is a conclusion, like the BSB does with So. For another example:

The people of Yosef, namely Menasheh and Efrayim, received their land according to the boundary lines given above

Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh): It may be helpful to state that the clans of Efrayim and Menasheh are the descendants of Yosef. For example:

the descendants of Yosef, that is, the clans of Efrayim and Menasheh

Menasheh: Menasheh was the first son of Yosef (Joseph) so he is listed first in the Hebrew. In the paragraph that follows, the land that Efrayim received is described before that of Menasheh. This reflects the story in Genesis 48, in which Yosef blessed Efrayim before he blessed Menasheh.Woudstra p.256.

title: Joshua 16:5
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:5a

This was the territory of the descendants of Efrayim by their clans:

  • ¶ The land that the clan of Efrayim received, according to their sub-clans, was like this:

  • ¶ Each sub-clan in the clan of Efrayim received their own portion of land. That land had the following boundary.

This was the territory of the descendants of Efrayim by their clans: The phrase the territory of the descendants of Efrayim refers to the land that the clan of Efrayim received.

clans: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as clans actually refers to families or groups of people within a clan. This word is translated in the display as “sub-clans.” See the note at Joshua 7:14.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

according to their sub-clans

each sub-clan in the clan of Efrayim (Ephraim) received their own portion of land

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the land that the clan of Efrayim received, according to their sub-clans, was like this

each family in the clan of Efrayim received their own portion of land. That land had the following boundaries.

16:5b

The border of their inheritance went from Atrot-Adar (Ataroth-addar) in the east

  • The border of their land began at Atrot-Adar in the east

  • On the east their southern boundary started at the town of Atrot-Adar,

The border of their inheritance went from Atrot-Adar in the east: The boundary points in this verse define the southern boundary of the clan of Efrayim (Ephraim).

Atrot-Adar: This town may be the same town as the town of “Atarot (Ataroth)” in Joshua 16:2, but this is not certain.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border of their land began at Atrot-Adar in the east

Their southern boundary started at the town of Atrot-Adar in the east

16:5c

to Upper Beyt-Horon (Upper Beth-horon)

  • and continued west to Upper Beyt-Horon.

  • and went to the town of Upper Beyt-Horon.

to Upper Beyt-Horon: The town of Upper Beyt-Horon was to the west of Atrot-Adar (Ataroth-addar).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and continued west to Upper Beyt-Horon

and went on to the town of Upper Beyt-Horon

title: Joshua 16:6
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:6a

and out toward the Sea.

  • The border then continued to the Mediterranean Sea.

  • It then went down to the Mediterranean Sea.

and out toward the Sea: There is an interpretation issue in this verse.

  1. The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as toward the Sea refers to the Mediterranean Sea. (BSB, RSV, NRSV, NET, ESV, NIV, NJPS, NABRE, GNT, KJV)

  2. The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as toward the Sea means to the west.

    Then the border went westward (NASB) (NASB, GW)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) which is followed by most English versions.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The boundary then continued to the Mediterranean Sea

From there it went downhill to the Mediterranean Sea

16:6b

From Mikmetat (Michmethath) on the north

  • The town of Mich-methath was on their northern border.

  • The town of Mich-methath was the northern boundary of Efrayim’s (Ephraim’s) territory.

From Mikmetat on the north: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as From Mikmetat on the north is more literally “Mikmetat from north.” Most commentaries agree that this part of the verse describes the northern border of Efrayim.

Mikmetat: The town of Mikmetat was on the north border of Efrayim, near the town of Shekem (Shechem). The exact location of Mikmetat is unknown.

The English versions spell Mikmetat in several ways:

Mich-methath (RSV)

Mikmetat (BSB, ESV, GW, NABRE, GNT, CEV)

Michmethah (KJV)

Micmethath (NET, NIV84, NLT)

Mikmethath (NIV11)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The town of Mikmetat (Michmethath) was on their northern border

The town of Mikmetat was in the north of Efrayim’s (Ephraim’s) territory

16:6c

it turned eastward toward Ta’anat-Shiloh (Taanath-shiloh)

  • The border turned east toward Ta’anat-Shiloh.

  • The northern boundary line curved around to the east to the town of Ta’anat-Shiloh

it turned eastward toward Ta’anat-Shiloh: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as eastward toward Ta’anat-Shiloh is more literally “the boundary turns east, Ta’anat-Shiloh.”

Ta’anat-Shiloh: Ta’anat-Shiloh refers to a town to the east of Mikmetat (Michmethath).

The English versions spell Ta’anat-Shiloh in several ways:

Ta’anat-Shiloh (BSB, RSV, ESV, NLT, NABRE, KJV)

Taanath Shiloh (NIV, NET, GW, GNT)

Ta’anat-Shiloh (Taanath-shiloh) (CEV)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border then turned east toward the town of Ta’anat-Shiloh

The boundary then curved around to the east to the town of Ta’anat-Shiloh

16:6d

and passed by it to Yanoah (Janoah) on the east.

  • It went past that town and continued east to Jan-oah.

  • and continued past it, and east to the town of Jan-oah.

and passed by it to Yanoah on the east: The clause passed by it to Yanoah on the east indicates that the border went past the town of Ta’anat-Shiloh (Taanath-shiloh) and continued east to the town of Yanoah.

The English versions spell Yanoah in several ways:

Jan-oah (RSV)

Yanoah (BSB, NIV, NET, ESV, GW, NABRE, GNT, CEV, NLT)

Yanoah (Janohah) (KJV)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border then went past that town and continued east to the town of Yanoah

The border continued east from the town of Ta’anat-Shiloh (Taanath-shiloh) to the town of Yanoah

title: Joshua 16:7
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:7a

From Yanoah (Janoah) it went down to Atarot (Ataroth) and Na’arah (Naarah),

  • Then the border went down from Jan-oah to Atarot, and on to Na’arah.

  • From Jan-oah it went southeast and down to the town of Atarot, and on to the town of Na’arah.

From Yanoah it went down to Atarot and Na’arah: The phrase From Yanoah it went down to indicates that the town of Yanoah is at a higher elevation than the other two towns.

Atarot and Na’arah: These towns are southeast of the town of Yanoah. The town of Atarot listed here is not the same town as that mentioned in verses 2 or 5.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border went down from Yanoah to Atarot, and on to Na’arah

Then the border went southeast to the town of Atarot and on to the town of Na’arah

16:7b

and then reached Yeriho (Jericho) and came out at the Yarden (Jordan).

  • It then went on to Yeriho and ended at the Yarden River.

  • The border reached the town of Yeriho and then ended at the Yarden River.

and then reached Yeriho and came out at the Yarden: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It then went on to Yeriho, and ended at the Yarden River

The border reached the town of Yeriho and then went on to end at the Yarden River

title: Joshua 16:8
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:8a

From Tapuah (Tappuah) the border went westward to the Brook of Kanah and ended at the Sea.

  • From the town of Tapuah the border went west to the Kanah River, and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

  • The border went west from the town of Tapuah as far as the Kanah streambed and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

From Tapuah the border went westward to the Brook of Kanah: The town of Tapuah was about ten miles southwest of Shekem (Shechem).

the Brook of Kanah: The Brook of Kanah is a deep ravine with a river that runs only when it rains. Today it is called Wadi Qana in Arabic, and Nahal Ha Yarkon in Hebrew. It flows west to join the Yarkon River, which then flows into the Mediterranean Sea.Coleson p.137–138.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From the town of Tapuah the border went west to the Kanah River

The border went west from Tapuah to the Kanah streambed

From Tapuah (Tappuah) the boundary line went west to the Kanah ravine

and ended at the Sea: Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

and ended at the Mediterranean Sea

the end of the border was the Mediterranean Sea

16:8b

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Efrayim (Ephraim),

  • This was the land that the families of the Efrayim clan received.

  • The land described above was the land that the clan of Efrayim received. Each family received a part of that land.

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Efrayim: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This is the land that the sub-clans of the clan of Efrayim received

This is the land that the Efrayim clan received. Each family in Efrayim received a part of the land

title: Joshua 16:9
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:9

along with all the cities and villages set apart for the descendants of Efrayim within the inheritance of Menasheh.

  • The clan of Efrayim also received other towns within the land of the clan of Menasheh. The villages surrounding these towns also belonged to the clan of Efrayim.

  • Their land also included some towns in areas belonging to the clan of Menasheh. They also received the villages that were near those towns.

  • (reordered) The clan of Efrayim also received other towns and the villages which surrounded them. These towns and villages were in the land that belonged to the clan of Menasheh.

along with all the cities and villages set apart for the descendants of Efrayim: The clause the cities and villages set apart for the descendants of Efrayim indicates that there were other towns that the clan of Efrayim received. These towns were in the land belonging to the clan of Menasheh.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The clan of Efrayim (Ephraim) also received other towns

Their land also included towns

all the cities and villages: The phrase and villages indicates that there were villages that surrounded the cities. These villages also belonged to the clan of Efrayim.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The villages surrounding these cities also belonged to the clan of Efrayim

The Efrayim clan also received the villages that were near these cities

within the inheritance of Menasheh (Manasseh): Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

which were within the land that the clan of Menasheh received

which were in the land that belonged to the clan of Menasheh

General Comment on 16:9

It may be more natural to reorder the parts of this verse so that the last clause follows the first. For example:

The clan of Efrayim (Ephraim) also received other cities and the villages that surrounded them. These towns and villages were in the land that belonged to the clan of Menasheh.

title: Joshua 16:10
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

16:10a

But they did not drive out the Kena’anim (Canaanites) who lived in Gezer.

  • But the people of Efrayim could not force the Kena’ani (Canaanite) people to leave Gezer.

  • But the Efrayim clan could not make the Kena’an (Canaan) people leave the town of Gezer.

But they did not drive out the Kena’anim who lived in Gezer: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

but they did not conquer the Kena’ani people who lived in the town of Gezer

but the Efrayim (Ephraim) people did not force the Kena’an people to leave Gezer

16:10b

So the Kena’anim (Canaanites) dwell among the Efrayimim (Ephraimites) to this day,

  • So the Kena’ani (Canaanite) people still live among the Efrayim people up to this time.

  • That is why the Kena’an (Canaan) people still live there along with the Efrayim people.

So the Kena’anim dwell among the Efrayimim to this day: This clause indicates that the people of Kena’an still lived alongside the people of the clan of Efrayim.

to this day: The phrase to this day indicates that they still lived there when the book of Yehoshua (Joshua) was written.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

so the Kena’an people still live among the Efrayim (Ephraim) people up to this time

that is why the people of Kena’an still live along with the clan of Efrayim

16:10c

but they are forced laborers.

  • However, they work as slaves to the Efrayim people.

  • But they are slaves to the clan of Efrayim and have to work hard for them.

but they are forced laborers: Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

but they work as slaves to the Efrayim (Ephraim) people

but they are slaves to the clan of Efrayim and have to work hard for them

title: Joshua 17:1
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:1a

Now this was the allotment for the tribe of Menasheh

  • ¶ Then the clan of Menasheh received land according to the lot.

  • ¶ This is the land that Yehoshua (Joshua) gave to the clan of Menasheh

Now this was the allotment for the tribe of Menasheh: The clause allotment for the tribe of Menasheh translates the same Hebrew words as in Joshua 15:1, except that here it refers to the clans of the tribe of Menasheh rather than the clans of the tribe of Yehudah (Judah). It refers to the land that the clan of Menasheh received when Yehoshua and Eleazar cast lots for them. It is recommended that you translate this the same way as you did in 15:1.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the clan of Menasheh received land according to the lot

Then the descendants of Menasheh (Manasseh) were assigned land by lot

Yehoshua gave land to the descendants of Menasheh according to the lot

17:1b

as Yosef’s (Joseph’s) firstborn son,

  • Menasheh was the first-born son of Yosef.

  • who was the elder son of Yosef.

as Yosef’s firstborn son: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

He was Yosef’s first son

Menasheh (Manasseh) was the oldest son of Yosef

as: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as as shows that the phrase “Yosef’s firstborn son” is additional information.

Here are some other ways to translate this clause:

The tribe of Menasheh, Yosef’s (Joseph’s) firstborn son, was also allotted land (NET)

This was the allotment for the tribe of Menasheh as Yosef’s firstborn (NIV)

A part of the land west of the Yarden (Jordan) was assigned to some of the families descended from Yosef’s older son Menasheh (GNT)

17:1c

namely for Makir (Machir) the firstborn of Menasheh (Manasseh) and father of the Giladim (Gileadites),

  • Makir, the firstborn son of Menasheh and the father of Gilead,

  • Makir was Menasheh’s oldest son. The name of Makir’s son was Gilead.

for Makir the firstborn of Menasheh and father of the Giladim: There is an interpretation issue concerning the name Giladim.

  1. Giladim is the name of a person, Gilead. For example:

    To Makir…the father of Gilead (ESV) (ESV, RSV, NET, NLT, NABRE, NJPS, GNT, CEV, KJV)

  2. Giladim is the name of a group of people who descended from a person name Gilead. For example:

    Makir was the ancestor of the Giladim (Gileadites) (NIV) (BSB, NIV)

  3. Giladim is the name of a region. For example:

    Makir (Machir)…the ancestor of the people living in Gilead (GW) (GW)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1). In this phrase the word “Gilead” refers to a person, not to the region of Gilead. This is the interpretation taken by the majority of English versions and by some commentaries.Woudstra, p. 263. The person named Gilead is also mentioned in Numbers 26:29–30 and 1 Chronicles 7:14|. The region of Gilead is mentioned in Joshua 17:1d.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

Makir was the firstborn son of Menasheh (Manasseh) and the father of Gilead

Makir was Menasheh’s oldest son. The name of his son was Gilead

17:1d

who had received Gilead and Bashan

  • received the territories of Gilead and Bashan,

  • Makir (Machir) was assigned the lands of Gilead and Bashan east of the Yarden (Jordan) River,

who had received Gilead and Bashan: Gilead and Bashan were regions. They were areas of land that were east of the Yarden River.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

he received the regions of Gilead and Bashan east of the Yarden River

Makir received the lands of Gilead and Bashan which were east of the Yarden River

they gave Makir land in the regions of Gilead and Bashan which were east of the Yarden River

17:1e

because Makir (Machir) was a man of war.

  • because he was a skilled fighter.

  • because he fought well in battle.

because Makir was a man of war: The phrase man of war indicates that Makir was a skilled fighter. Numbers 32:39.tells how Makir and his descendants went to Gilead and defeated the people who were living there. Because of this he received Gilead as his inheritance.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

because he was a skilled fighter

because he fought well in battle. He had fought the people of Gilead and Bashan and captured their land.

General Comment on 17:1d–e

In some languages it may be more natural to translate 1e before 1d. For example:

Makir (Machir) was a skilled fighter, so he received the territories of Gilead and Bashan on the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

title: Joshua 17:2
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:2a

So this allotment was for the rest of the descendants of Menasheh—

  • The rest of the clan of Menasheh also received land by lot

  • The other descendants of Menasheh were also assigned land.

So this allotment was for the rest of the descendants of Menasheh: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as allotment was for is more literally “was to.” Both the subject and the object of this clause are missing. In some languages it will be necessary to make them clear. For example:

Yehoshua (Joshua) gave land to the other descendants of Menasheh according to the lot

the rest of the descendants of Menasheh (Manasseh): The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as the rest of the descendants of Menasheh is more literally “the remaining sons of Menasheh.” This phrase refers to the descendants of Menasheh who did not receive land east of the Yarden (Jordan) River. These people were descendants of Makir (Machir) and his son Gilead.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the rest of the clan of Menasheh also received land by lot

the other descendants of Menasheh were also assigned land

they gave land also to other descendants of Menasheh

17:2b

the clans of Aviezer (Abiezer), Helek, Asriel, Shekem (Shechem), Hefer (Hepher), and Shemida.

  • according to their sub-clans. These are the names of the sub-clans: Abi-ezer, Helek, Asri-el, Hefer, and Shemida.

  • The names of the families were Abi-ezer and Helek and Asri-el and Shekem and Hefer and Shemida.

the clans: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as the clans was used in Joshua 16:5a. It is recommended that you translate it in the same way as you did in that verse. The Hebrew word is translated in the display as “sub-clans.” See the note at Joshua 7:14.

Aviezer, Helek, Asriel, Shekem, Hefer, and Shemida: These are the names of the sub-clans that received land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

according to their sub-clans. These are the names of the sub-clans: Aviezer, Helek, Asriel, Shekem, Hefer, and Shemida

The names of the sub-clans that received land were Aviezer and Helek and Asriel and Shekem and Hefer and Shemida

17:2c

These are the other male descendants of the clans of Menasheh (Manasseh) son of Yosef (Joseph).

  • They were the male descendants of Menasheh, who was the son of Yosef.

  • They were the males who inherited land in the family of Menasheh, who was one of the sons of Yosef.

These are the other male descendants of the clans of Menasheh son of Yosef: The writer wanted to make clear that these were male descendants of Menasheh, because in the next verse he talked about the female descendants of Menasheh.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The people named above were the male descendants of Menasheh

Those people were the other sons of Menasheh, and the heads of their sub-clans

title: Joshua 17:3
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:3a

But Tselofehad (Zelophehad) son of Hefer (Hepher) (the son of Gilead, the son of Makir (Machir), the son of Menasheh)

  • ¶ Tselofehad was the son of Hefer, and the grandson of Gilead, whose father was Makir and whose grandfather was Menasheh.

  • ¶ But Tselofehad, son of Hefer, son of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Menasheh,

But: The Hebrew particle that the BSB translates as But shows a contrast. Unlike the fathers of the sub-clans listed in the previous verse, Tselofehad had only daughters. He did not have any sons. Use a word or particle that is natural in your language to mark a contrast.

Tselofehad son of Hefer (the son of Gilead, the son of Makir, the son of Menasheh) had no sons but only daughters: Many languages have their own way of stating this kind of genealogy. Use whatever is the most natural way in your language.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Tselofehad, the son of Hefer, the grandson of Gilead, and the great-grandson of Makir, whose father was Menasheh (Manasseh) had no sons. He only had daughters

Tselofehad was the son of Hefer and the grandson of Gilead, whose father was Makir. Gilead’s grandfather was Menasheh. Tselofehad had only daughters and no sons

17:3b

had no sons but only daughters. These are the names of his daughters:

  • He had no sons, but he had daughters. His daughters were

  • had only daughters. He did not have any sons. The names of his daughters were

17:3c

Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milkah (Milcah), and Tirtsah (Tirzah).

  • Mahlah and Noah and Hoglah and Milkah and Tirtsah.

17:3b-c

These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milkah, and Tirtsah: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The daughters were named as follows: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milkah, and Tirtsah

The names of his daughters were Mahlah and Noah and Hoglah and Milkah and Tirtsah

title: Joshua 17:4
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:4a

They approached Eleazar the priest, Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun, and the leaders, and said,

  • These daughters went to Eleazar the priest and Yehoshua son of Nun and the tribal leaders, and said:

  • These women went to Eleazar the priest and Yehoshua son of Nun and the heads of the clans. They said to them,

They approached Eleazar the priest, Yehoshua son of Nun, and the leaders, and said: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates leaders is more literally “one who is lifted up.” It refers to the heads of the clans. This Hebrew word was used in Joshua 14:1 (see “heads of the families”). It is recommended that you translate it the same way as you did there.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

All the daughters went to Eleazar the priest and Yehoshua son of Nun and the clan leaders, and said to them

Those women went to Eleazar the priest and Yehoshua and the heads of the clans and said

17:4b

“Yahweh commanded Mosheh (Moses) to give us an inheritance among our brothers.”

  • “Yahweh told Mosheh to give us(excl) some land for our own, just as he did for our male relatives.”

  • “Yahweh commanded Mosheh to give us land to possess like he also gave to our male relatives.”

Yahweh commanded Mosheh to give us an inheritance among our brothers: The phrase among our brothers indicates that the daughters would receive land as their male relatives did. The word brothers cannot refer to literal brothers, because Tselofehad (Zelophehad) had no sons.

The story of how Yahweh commanded Mosheh to give land to Tselofehad’s daughters is told in Numbers 27:1–11.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yahweh told Mosheh to give us(excl) some land for our own, as he did for our male relatives

Yahweh commanded Mosheh to give land to us as well as our male relatives

17:4c

So Yehoshua (Joshua) gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers,

  • He gave them land along with the male relatives of their father.

  • He assigned them some land among the land of their father’s male relatives.

So Yehoshua gave them an inheritance among their father’s brothers: The Hebrew does not specify who gave them an inheritance and some versions use “he” here since it is not certain whether this refers to Yehoshua or to Eleazar the priest. If it is necessary to make this explicit then it is recommended that you choose Yehoshua, as in the BSB.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

he gave them land along with the male relatives of their father

Yehoshua assigned them some land just as he had assigned some land to the male relatives of their father

So Yehoshua (Joshua) assigned them land among their uncles (NET)

17:4d

in keeping with the command of Yahweh.

  • Then Yehoshua did what Yahweh had commanded.

  • So Yehoshua obeyed Yahweh’s command.

in keeping with the command of Yahweh: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So Yehoshua did what Yahweh commanded

So he obeyed Yahweh’s command

title: Joshua 17:5
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:5a

Thus ten shares fell to Menasheh,

  • So the clan of Menasheh received ten portions of land west of the Yarden (Jordan) River

  • That is why the clan of Menasheh had ten sections of land west of the Yarden River.

Thus ten shares fell to Menasheh: The clause ten shares fell to Menasheh indicates that the clan of Menasheh received ten pieces of land on the west side of the Yarden River. The sub-clans of Aviezer (Abiezer), Helek, Asriel, Shekem (Shechem) and Shemida each received one piece of land. The sub-clan of Hefer (Hepher) received five pieces of land. It received one piece for each of Tselofehad’s (Zelophehad’s) daughters.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So the clan of Menasheh (Manasseh) received ten portions of land on the west side of the Yarden River

That is why the descendants of Menasheh had ten sections of land west of the Yarden River

17:5b

in addition to the land of Gilead and Bashan

  • in addition to the regions of Gilead and Bashan

  • They also had the lands of Gilead and Bashan

in addition to the land of Gilead and Bashan: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

as well as the regions of Gilead and Bashan

They also had the lands of Gilead and Bashan

17:5c

beyond the Yarden (Jordan),

  • east of the Yarden River.

  • on the east side of the Yarden River.

beyond the Yarden: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

which were east of the Yarden River

These regions were on the east side of the Yarden River

title: Joshua 17:6
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:6a

because the daughters of Menasheh received an inheritance among his sons.

  • This was because the female descendants of Menasheh received land just like the male descendants.

  • The daughters of Tselofehad (Zelophehad), Menasheh’s descendant, were assigned land along with their male relatives.

because the daughters of Menasheh received an inheritance among his sons: The clause the daughters of Menasheh received an inheritance among his sons states the reason that the clan of Menasheh received ten areas of land. In some languages it may be helpful to reorder the information in verses 5 and 6 to make this clear. See the General Comment on 17:5–6a.

the daughters of Menasheh: The phrase the daughters of Menasheh refers to the five daughters of Tselofehad. These women were fifth-generation descendants of Menasheh. They were not literally his daughters. The Hebrew language uses “daughters” to refer to female descendants.

his sons: The phrase his sons refers to five of the sons of Gilead. These men were third-generation descendants of Menasheh. They were not literally his sons. The Hebrew language uses “sons” to refer to male descendants.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This happened because the female descendants of Menasheh (Manasseh) received portions of land like the male descendants

This was because the daughters of Tselofehad, who were descended from Menasheh, were assigned land along with their male relatives

General Comment on 17:5–6a

In some languages it may be more natural to reorder these verses and put the reason first. For example:

6aBecause the female descendants of Menasheh received portions of land like their male relatives, 5athe clan of Menasheh received ten portions of land on the west side of the Yarden (Jordan) River. 5bThe other descendants of Menasheh received the lands of Gilead and Bashan 5con the east side of the Yarden River.

17:6b

And the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Menasheh.

  • The land of Gilead had been assigned to the other descendants of Menasheh.

  • Other descendants of Menasheh (Manasseh) had received the land of Gilead.

And the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Menasheh: The phrase the rest of the sons of Menasheh refers to the other descendants of Menasheh who were mentioned in Joshua 17:1. They received the land of Gilead on the east side of the Yarden River.

It is not clear from scripture exactly how these descendants of Menasheh were related to the six sons of Gilead. Possibly Makir (Machir) had other sons who were brothers of Gilead.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The land of Gilead was assigned to the other descendants of Menasheh

Other descendants of Menasheh had received the land of Gilead

title: Joshua 17:7
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:7a

Now the border of Menasheh went from Asher to Mikmetat (Michmethath) near Shekem (Shechem),

  • ¶ The territory of Menasheh went from the border of Asher’s land to the town of Michmethah east of Shekem town.

  • ¶ Menasheh’s land bordered on the clan of Asher’s land in the northwest and reached to the town of Mikmetat in the south to the east of Shekem town.

Now the border of Menasheh went from Asher to Mikmetat near Shekem: The term Asher refers to the clan of Asher. Their land was northwest of the land belonging to the clan of Menasheh.

Mikmetat: The town of Mikmetat was on the northern border of Efrayim, near the town of Shekem. The exact location is unknown. This town was mentioned in Joshua 16:6b.

Shekem: The town of Shekem was in the territory assigned to Efrayim.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Menasheh’s (Manasseh’s) land bordered on the clan of Asher’s land in the northwest, and reached to the town of Mikmetat in the south. Mikmetat was east of Shekem town

The territory of the clan of Menasheh went from the border of Asher’s land in the northwest to the town of Mikmetat (Michmethath) which was east of Shekem (Shechem)

17:7b

then southward to include the inhabitants of Eyn-Tapuah (En-tappuah).

  • Then the border went south to the people who lived near Eyn-Tapuah.

  • The border then continued southward. The people who lived near the spring of Tapuah (Tappuah) were within the border.

then southward to include the inhabitants of Eyn-Tapuah: The town of Tapuah was mentioned in Joshua 16:8.
