The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as Eyn-Tapuah can also be translated as “the spring of Tapuah.” The inhabitants of Eyn-Tapuah lived in the area near Tapuah spring, which was outside the town of Tapuah.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border went south to the people who lived near the spring of Tapuah

The border then continued south. It went past the people who lived near the spring of Tapuah

title: Joshua 17:8
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:8a

The region of Tapuah (Tappuah) belonged to Menasheh,

  • The land near the town of Tapuah belonged to the clan of Menasheh,

  • The land that surrounded Tapuah Town belonged to the clan of Menasheh.

The region of Tapuah belonged to Menasheh: The phrase The region of Tapuah refers to the land near the town of Tapuah.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The land around the town of Tapuah belonged to the clan of Menasheh

The land near Tapuah belonged to the descendants of Menasheh (Manasseh)

17:8b

but Tapuah (Tappuah) itself, on the border of Menasheh, belonged to Efrayim (Ephraim).

  • but the town of Tapuah itself did not. It was on the border and belonged to the clan of Efrayim.

  • The town of Tapuah was on the border between the clans of Menasheh and Efrayim and it belonged to Efrayim.

but Tapuah itself, on the border of Menasheh, belonged to Efrayim: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

but the town of Tapuah itself did not belong to Menasheh. It was on the border of Menasheh and belonged to the clan of Efrayim

the town of Tapuah was on the border between the clans of Menasheh (Manasseh) and Efrayim, and it belonged to Efrayim

title: Joshua 17:9
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:9b

There were cities belonging to Efrayim among the cities of Menasheh,

  • Some towns that belonged to the clan of Efrayim were south of the river among the towns that belonged to the clan of Menasheh.

  • Some towns of the clan of Efrayim were south of the streambed in land that belonged to the clan of Menasheh.

17:9a-b

From there the border continued southward to the Brook of Kanah. There were cities belonging to Efrayim among the cities of Menasheh: There is an interpretation issue in this verse. Scholars do not agree on how the word southward relates to the parts of this verse.

  1. It relates to the phrase the cities in verse 9b. For example:

    These cities, to the south of the brook… (ESV) (ESV, RSV, NABRE, NJPS, NLT, GNT, CEV, KJV)

  2. It relates to the term border in verse 9a. For example:

    Then the boundary continued south to the Kanah Ravine (NIV) (BSB, NIV, NET, GW)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1) along with the majority of English versions and some commentaries.Woudstra, p. 266. The border of Menasheh (Manasseh) went south of the Kanah River for some distance. However, there were some towns belonging to the clan of Efrayim (Ephraim) that were within the borders of the land assigned to Menasheh.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

Some towns that belonged to the clan of Efrayim were south of the river, among the towns that belonged to the clan of Menasheh

17:9a

From there the border continued southward to the Brook of Kanah.

  • Then the border descended to the southwest to the Kanah River.

  • The border then continued downhill to the Kanah streambed.

From there the border continued southward to the Brook of Kanah: You should translate the phrase the Brook of Kanah the same way as you translated it in Joshua 16:8.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border descended to the southwest to the Kanah River

The border then continued south downhill to the Kanah streambed

17:9c

but the border of Menasheh (Manasseh) was on the north side of the brook and ended at the Sea.

  • The border of the clan of Menasheh’s land continued west on the north side of the river as far as the Mediterranean Sea.

  • The boundary line of Menasheh’s land was on the north side of the streambed, and it ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

but the border of Menasheh was on the north side of the brook and ended at the Sea: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border of Menasheh’s land continued westward on the north side of the river and ended at the Mediterranean Sea

Then the boundary line of Menasheh’s land went along the northern side of the river, and it ended at the Mediterranean Sea

title: Joshua 17:10
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:10a

Efrayim’s territory was to the south,

  • The land on the south side of the river belonged to the clan of Efrayim.

  • The land south of the streambed belonged to the descendants of Efrayim.

Efrayim’s territory was to the south: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The land on the south side of the river belonged to the clan of Efrayim

The land that was south of the riverbed belonged to the descendants of Efrayim (Ephraim)

17:10b

and Menasheh’s (Manasseh’s) was to the north,

  • The land on the north side of the river belonged to the clan of Menasheh.

  • The land north of the streambed belonged to the descendants of Menasheh

and Menasheh’s was to the north: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and the land on the north side of the river belonged to the clan of Menasheh

and the land that was north of the riverbed belonged to the descendants of Menasheh

17:10c

having the Sea as its border

  • The Mediterranean Sea formed the western boundary of Menasheh’s (Manasseh’s) land.

  • and the western border was the Mediterranean Sea.

having the Sea as its border: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The Mediterranean Sea formed the west boundary of Menasheh’s land

The clan of Menasheh had the Mediterranean Sea as the western border of its land

17:10d

and adjoining Asher on the north and Yisakar (Issachar) on the east.

  • Their border reached to the clan of Asher in the north, and to the clan of Yisakar in the east.

  • To the north- west was land that belonged to the descendants of Asher. To the north- east was land that belonged to the descendants of Yisakar.

and adjoining Asher on the north: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as adjoining Asher on the north is more literally “they touched Asher on the north.” The clan of Menasheh (Manasseh) shared a border with the clan of Asher in the north and northwest.

and Yisakar on the east: The phrase that the BSB translates as Yisakar on the east indicates that the clan of Menasheh shared a border with the clan of Yisakar in the east and northeast.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the clan of Menasheh had a border with the clan of Asher on the north, and with the clan of Yisakar on the east

to the north-west was land that belonged to the people of Asher. To the north-east was land that belonged to the people of Yisakar

title: Joshua 17:11
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:11a

Within Yisakar (Issachar) and Asher, Menasheh was assigned Beyt-Shean (Beth-shean),

  • The clan of Menasheh also had towns in the land of the clans of Yisakar and Asher. These were Beyt-Shean town and its surrounding villages,

  • Some towns that belonged to the Menasheh clan were in land that belonged to the Asher clan and the Yisakar clan. These towns were Beyt-Shean and the villages that surrounded it,

Within Yisakar and Asher, Menasheh was assigned Beyt-Shean: The town of Beyt-Shean was fifteen miles southwest of the Sea of Galil (Galilee).Rasmussen p. 230.

Here are some ways that English versions have spelled the name of this town:

Beth Shean (NET, GW)

Beyt-Shean (BSB, RSV, ESV, NABRE, KJV)

Beth Shan (NIV, GNT)

Beth-shan (NLT, CEV)

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

The clan of Menasheh (Manasseh) also had towns in the lands of the clan of Yisakar (Issachar) and the clan of Asher. These were Beyt-Shean (Beth-shean) town and its surrounding villages

17:11b

Yivleam (Ibleam), Dor (that is, Nefet (Naphath)),

  • and Yivleam and its surrounding villages, and the people of Dor and its surrounding villages,

  • Yivleam town and the villages that surrounded it, and the people who lived in Dor town and the villages that surrounded it,

Yivleam, Dor (that is, Nefet): Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the town of Yivleam and its surrounding villages, and the people of the town of Dor and its surrounding villages

Yivleam and the villages that surrounded it, and the people who lived in Dor and the villages that surrounded it

Dor (that is, Nefet): The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as that is, Nefet is more literally, “three is Nefet.” Most scholars understand the term Nefet to refer to the town of Dor. Dor is the third town in this list. The town of Nefet Dor is also mentioned in Joshua 11:2 and 12:23.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The third town in the list was also called Nefet (Naphath)

The town of Dor also had the name Nefet

17:11c

Endor,

  • and the people of Eyn-Dor (En-dor) and its surrounding villages,

  • the people who lived in Eyn-Dor town and the villages that surrounded it,

Endor:

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the people of the town of Eyn-Dor and its surrounding villages

the people who lived in Eyn-Dor and the villages that were around it

17:11d

Ta’anak (Taanach),

  • and the people of Ta’anak and its surrounding villages,

  • the people who lived in Ta’anak town and the villages that surrounded it,

Ta’anak: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the people of the town of Ta’anak and its surrounding villages

the people who lived in Ta’anak and the villages that surrounded it

17:11e

and Megidon (Megiddo), each with their surrounding settlements.

  • and the people of Megidon and its surrounding villages. The third town in the list was also called Nefet (Naphath).

  • and the people who lived in Megidon town and the villages that surrounded it. The town of Dor also had the name Nefet.

and Megidon, each with their surrounding settlements: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the people of the town of Megidon and its surrounding villages

the people who lived in Megidon and the villages that surrounded it

General Comment on verse 17:11

It may be more natural in your language to reorder and combine the parts of verse 11. For example:

The clan of Menasheh (Manasseh) also had towns in the lands of the Yisakar (Issachar) and Asher clans. These towns were Beyt-Shean (Beth-shean), Yivleam (Ibleam), Dor which is also called Nefet (Naphath) Dor, Endor, Ta’anak (Taanach), and Megidon (Megiddo). The villages that surrounded these towns also belonged to the clan of Menasheh

17:11a-e

(reordered) The clan of Menasheh also had towns in the land of the Yisakar and Asher clans. These towns were Beyt-Shean, Yivleam, Dor which is also called Nefet, Eyn-Dor (En-dor), Ta’anak, and Megidon. The villages that surrounded these towns also belonged to the clan of Menasheh.

title: Joshua 17:12
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:12a

But the descendants of Menasheh were unable to occupy these cities,

  • But the clan of Menasheh was not able to conquer those towns.

  • But the descendants of Menasheh could not make the Kena’an (Canaan) people leave those towns.

But the descendants of Menasheh were unable to occupy these cities: The phrase the descendants of Menasheh refers to the clan of Menasheh.

But the clan of Menasheh was not able to conquer those towns

But the descendants of Menasheh (Manasseh) clan could not make the Kena’ani (Canaanite) people leave those towns

17:12b

because the Kena’anim (Canaanites) were determined to stay in this land.

  • The people of Kena’an were determined to live in that territory.

  • The Kena’an (Canaan) people continued to live there.

because the Kena’anim were determined to stay in this land: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The people of Kena’an were determined to live in the land

The Kena’an people continued to live there

title: Joshua 17:13
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:13a

However, when the Israelis (Israelites) grew stronger,

  • But when the people of Yisrael (Israel) became stronger

  • But later, when the Yisrael people became strong enough,

However, when the Israelis grew stronger: The clause when the Israelis grew stronger indicates that the Yisrael people became strong enough to force the Kena’ani (Canaanite) people to do what they wanted.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But when the people of Yisrael became stronger

But later when the Yisrael men became strong enough

17:13b

they put the Kena’anim (Canaanites) to forced labor;

  • they made the Kena’an (Canaan) people work as slaves.

  • the Kena’an people became their slaves and had to work hard for them.

they put the Kena’anim to forced labor: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

they made the Kena’an people work as their slaves

the people of Kena’an became their slaves and had to work hard for them

17:13c

but they failed to drive them out completely.

  • But still the Yisrael (Israel) people did not completely force the Kena’an (Canaan) people to leave.

  • However, the Yisrael people did not succeed in making the Kena’an people leave the land.

but they failed to drive them out completely: The clause that the BSB translates as failed to drive them out has a form in Hebrew to show that it is emphasized. The BSB translates this emphasis with the word completely. Use a word or grammatical form in your language that shows emphasis.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But still the Yisrael people did not completely force the Kena’an people to leave

However, the people of Yisrael failed to make all of the people of Kena’an leave the land

title: Joshua 17:14
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:14a

Then the sons of Yosef (Joseph) said to Yehoshua (Joshua),

  • ¶ The people of the clan of Yosef went to Yehoshua and asked him:

  • ¶ One day the descendants of Yosef said to Yehoshua:

Then the sons of Yosef said to Yehoshua: The clan of Yosef includes both the clans of Efrayim and Menasheh. Efrayim and Menasheh were the two sons of Yosef.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The people of the clan of Yosef went to Yehoshua and asked him

One day the descendants of Yosef said to Yehoshua

17:14b

“Why have you given us only one portion as an inheritance?

  • “Why did you give us only one share of land to be our own?

  • “Why have you given just one area of land to our clan?

Why have you given us only one portion as an inheritance: The Hebrew text considers the clan of Yosef (Joseph) as a single entity. Because the clan of Yosef included many people, it is more natural to translate the Hebrew pronoun “me" with a plural pronoun us.

only one portion: In the phrase one portion refers to the area of land that Yehoshua (Joshua) had assigned to the clan of Yosef. In some languages it may be clearer to translate this phrase as:

one piece of land

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Why did you(sing) give us(excl) only one share of land to be our own?

Why have you given just one area of land for our clan to own?

17:14c

We have many people, because Yahweh has blessed us abundantly.”

  • We have many people in our clan, because Yahweh has blessed us.”

  • Yahweh has blessed our clan with many descendants, and now we are a large group of people.”

We have many people: The clause We have many people indicates that the clan of Yosef (Joseph) had many people in it.

Here is another way to translate this phrase:

even though there are many of us

because Yahweh has blessed us abundantly: The clause Yahweh has blessed us indicates that Yahweh gave the clan of Yosef many descendants.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

We(excl) have many people in our clan because Yahweh has blessed us

Yahweh has blessed our clan with many descendants. So now we are a large group of people

title: Joshua 17:15
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:15a

Yehoshua (Joshua) answered them,

  • Then Yehoshua said to them,

  • Yehoshua answered,

Yehoshua answered them: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then Yehoshua said to them

Yehoshua answered

17:15b

“If you have so many people that the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim) is too small for you, go to the forest

  • “If you have so many people, go up into the forests.

  • “You have many people, so go up into the wooded country.

If you have so many people that the hill country of Efrayim is too small for you, go to the forest: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

If you(plur) have so many people, go up into the forest

You have many people, so go up into the wooded country

that the hill country of Efrayim is too small for you: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

because you think that the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim) is not wide enough for you

because the mountain country of Efrayim is too small for all of you to live in

17:15c

and clear for yourself an area in the land of the Perizim (Perizzites) and the Refaim (Rephaim).”

  • Clear land for yourselves there, in the country of the Periz people and the Repha people. The mountain country of Efrayim is too small for you to live in.”

  • Cut down the trees to make room where the Periz and the Repha peoples live, because you think the hill country of Efrayim is not big enough for you.”

and clear for yourself an area in the land of the Perizim and the Refaim: The Hebrew that the BSB translates as clear refers specifically to the act of cutting down trees and removing shrubs in a forest to create a place to live.

the Perizim: The term Perizim refers to the Periz people. The Periz people had lived in the land of Kena’an (Canaan) for a long time. The Perizim were mentioned in Joshua 3:10 and 12:8. It is recommended that you translate the name of these people in the same way here.

the Refaim: The term Refaim refers to the Repha people. The Repha people had lived in the land of Kena’an for a long time. The Refaim were mentioned in Joshua 12:4 and 13:12. It is recommended that you translate the name of these people in the same way here.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and clear land for yourselves there, in the country of the Periz people and the Repha people

Cut down the trees to make room for yourselves where the Periz people and the Repha people live

General Comment on verse 17:15

In some languages it may be more natural to reorder the parts of this verse. For example:

15aYehoshua (Joshua) answered them, 15b-c“Go up to the forests, take the land that belongs to the Periz people and the Repha people, and make a place to live there 15bif you have so many people that the mountain country of Efrayim (Ephraim) is not wide enough for you.

title: Joshua 17:16
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:16a

“The hill country is not enough for us,” they replied,

  • The people of the Yosef (Joseph) clan said, “The hill country is not large enough for us.

  • The descendants of Yosef said, “The mountain area is still not wide enough for all of us.

“The hill country is not enough for us,” they replied: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The people of the Yosef clan answered him, “The hill country is not large enough for us.”(excl)

The mountain area is still not wide enough for all of us

17:16b

“and all the Kena’anim (Canaanites) who live in the valley have iron chariots,

  • But all the Kena’an (Canaan) people who live in the valleys have chariots made with iron.

  • But the Kena’an people who live in the lowlands have iron war carts. We cannot defeat them.

and all the Kena’anim who live in the valley have iron chariots: The clan of Yosef (Joseph) considered the mountain country to be too small for them, but they could not expand into the valley because the Kena’ani (Canaanite) people already lived there.

iron chariots: A “chariot” is a war cart with two wheels which was pulled by horses. The wheels were reinforced with iron. The Israelis (Israelites) did not have war vehicles. The chariots gave the Kena’anim an advantage over the Israelis when they fought each other.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But all the Kena’an people who live in the valleys have war carts made of iron to use when we fight

But the Kena’ani people who live in the flat area have iron war vehicles. We(excl) cannot defeat them

17:16c

both in Beyt-Shean (Beth-shean) with its towns and in the Valley of Yizre’el (Jezreel).”

  • Those in Beyt-Shean town and the villages around it, and also those in the Valley of Yizre’el have iron chariots.

  • This includes those who live in the town of Beyt-Shean and its surrounding villages, and those who live in Yizre’el Valley (Jezreel Valley).

both in Beyt-Shean with its towns and in the Valley of Yizre’el: The town of Beyt-Shean was mentioned in Joshua 17:11. You should translate it the same way here.

Valley of Yizre’el: The Valley of Yizre’el was a large valley shaped like a triangle. It separated the hill country of the clan of Menasheh (Manasseh) from the Galil (Galilee) region.Rasmussen p. 240.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

not only the people who live in Beyt-Shean and the villages around it, but also those who live in the Valley of Yizre’el

This includes those who live in the town of Beyt-Shean and its surrounding villages, and those who live in Yizre’el Valley

General Comment on verse 17:16

It may be clearer to reorder the parts of this verse. For example,

16aThe people of the Yosef (Joseph) clan said, “It is true that there is not enough space for us in the hill country. 16bBut all the Kena’an (Canaan) people who live in the plain 16cincluding those who live in town of Beyt-Shean (Beth-shean) and the villages around it, and those who live in the Valley of Yizre’el (Jezreel) 16bhave chariots made of iron.

title: Joshua 17:17
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:17a

So Yehoshua (Joshua) said to the house of Yosef (Joseph)—to Efrayim and Menasheh—

  • Then Yehoshua answered the descendants of Yosef, that is, the clans of Efrayim and Menasheh:

  • Yehoshua said to the clans of Efrayim and Menasheh, who were descendants of Yosef:

So Yehoshua said to the house of Yosef: The term the house of Yosef refers to the descendants of Yosef.

to Efrayim and Menasheh: The phrase Efrayim and Menasheh refers to the clans of Efrayim and Menasheh. It is another way of referring to the descendants of Yosef.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then Yehoshua said to the clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh), who were the descendants of Yosef

Yehoshua answered the descendants of Yosef, that is, the clan of Efrayim and the clan of Menasheh

17:17b

“You have many people and great strength.

  • “You have many people and are very strong.

  • “You have a lot of people in your clans. You are very powerful.

You have many people and great strength: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Your clans have many people and are strong

You have a lot of people in your clans. You are very powerful

17:17c

You shall not have just one allotment,

  • So you will not have only one share of land.

  • You will not have just one area of land.

You shall not have just one allotment: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So you will not have only one piece of land

You will not have just one area of land

title: Joshua 17:18
content:
Section 16:1–17:18 The clans of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land given to Efrayim and to Menasheh, and the towns within each of their lands.

17:18a

because the hill country will be yours as well.

  • The hill country will be yours.

  • The mountain country will belong to you as well.

because the hill country will be yours as well: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

You will be able to conquer the whole hill country

The mountain country will belong to you as well

17:18b

It is a forest; clear it, and its farthest limits will be yours.

  • It is a forest, but you will cut down the trees and live in all of it.

  • Even though it is a forest area, you can clear it out and make all of it your own.

It is a forest; clear it, and its farthest limits will be yours: The Hebrew that the BSB translates as clear refers specifically to the act of cutting down trees and removing shrubs in a forest to create a place to live. Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It is a forest, but you will cut down the trees and conquer all of it

Even though it is a forest area, you can clear it out and make all of it your own

17:18c

Although the Kena’anim (Canaanites) have iron chariots and although they are strong, you can drive them out.”

  • You will make the Kena’an (Canaan) people leave, though they are strong and have chariots made of iron.”

  • You will defeat the Kena’an people, even though they are powerful and have iron war carts.”

Although the Kena’anim have iron chariots and although they are strong: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

though they are strong and have chariots made of iron

even though they are powerful and have iron war carts

you can drive them out: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

You will make the Kena’anim (Canaanites) leave

You will defeat the Kena’an (Canaan) people

title: Joshua 18:1
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:1a

Then the whole congregation of Yisrael (Israel) assembled at Shiloh

  • ¶ Then all the community of Yisrael gathered at the town of Shiloh

  • ¶ All the Yisrael people met together at Shiloh town.

Then the whole congregation of Yisrael assembled at Shiloh: The phrase the whole congregation refers to all the Israeli (Israelite) people.

Shiloh: Shiloh is a town in the territory of the Efrayim (Ephraim) clan. It was in the center of Yisrael, west of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then all the community of Yisrael gathered at Shiloh

All the Israeli people met together at the town of Shiloh

18:1b

and set up the Tent of Meeting there.

  • and put up the meeting tent there.

  • They set up the holy tent there.

and set up the Tent of Meeting there: The tent of meeting was the tent that God told the Israelis (Israelites) to make. God gave detailed instructions to Mosheh (Moses) on how to set up this tent and the things that were inside it. These instructions are found in Exodus 25–27. The fabric of the tent had outer layers made of goat hair. The inner layers were made of linen which were skillfully embroidered to make the inside beautiful.

The term Tent of Meeting emphasizes that this tent is where God met with his people.

A tent is a portable shelter made of cloth. The Israelis took the tent down and carried it when they moved through the wilderness. Some languages may not have a word for “tent.” In some languages, the closest equivalent may be “hut.”

Here are some other ways to translate this term:

holy tent

meeting tent

tent of the Lord’s presence (GNT)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and put up the meeting tent there

they set up the holy tent there

18:1c

And though the land was subdued before them,

  • The Israelis (Israelites) had conquered the land.

  • They had defeated the people of the land.

And though the land was subdued before them: The clause the land was subdued before them indicates that the Israelis had conquered the people who lived in the land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The Israelis had conquered the land

They had defeated the people of the land

General Comment on verse 18:1

In some languages it may be more natural to reorder the parts of this verse so that they occur in chronological sequence. For example:

After the Israelis (Israelites) had defeated the people of the land they set up the tent of meeting at Shiloh

title: Joshua 18:2
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:2

there were still seven tribes of Yisrael (Israel) who had not yet received their inheritance.

  • There were still seven clans in Yisrael to whom Yehoshua had not assigned a share of land as their inheritance.

  • Seven of the Yisrael clans were left that had not yet received their part of the land.

there were still seven tribes of Yisrael who had not yet received their inheritance: The clause who had not yet received their inheritance indicates that Yehoshua (Joshua) and Eleazar the priest had not yet divided land for the seven clans who remained.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

There were still seven clans of Israeli (Israelite) people to whom Yehoshua had not assigned a share of land as their inheritance

Seven of the Israeli clans had not yet received their part of the land

title: Joshua 18:3
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:3a

So Yehoshua said to the Israelis (Israelites),

  • Yehoshua asked the Yisrael (Israel) people,

  • So Yehoshua (Joshua) said to the people of Yisrael,

So Yehoshua said to the Israelis: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yehoshua asked the people of Yisrael

So Yehoshua spoke to the Israelis. He said, (NIRV)

18:3b

“How long will you put off entering and possessing the land that Yahweh, the God of your fathers, has given you?

  • “Why are you waiting so long to claim the land that Yahweh the God of your ancestors has given you?

  • “Do not delay any longer. Go and settle in the land that Yahweh has given you. He is the God whom your ancestors worshiped.

How long will you put off entering and possessing the land that Yahweh, the God of your fathers, has given you?: This is a rhetorical question. It functions as a rebuke. Yehoshua (Joshua) rebuked the Israelis (Israelites) because they had not taken the land that God gave them.

Here are two ways to translate this rebuke:

  • As a rhetorical question. For example:

    How long will you wait before you begin to take possession of the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, has given you? (NIV)

  • As a rebuke. For example:

    You should not have waited so long to take possession of the land that Yahweh the God of your ancestors has given you

    Do not delay any longer. Go and settle in the land that Yahweh has given you. He is the God whom your ancestors worshiped.

Translate this as a natural rebuke in your language.

How long will you put off: The Hebrew participle that the BSB translates as put off indicates that the Israeli (Israelite) people were lazy, or slow to act.

you: This is a plural you. Yehoshua (Joshua) spoke to the people of Yisrael (Israel).

entering and possessing the land: The clause entering and possessing the land indicates that the Israelis (Israelites) should enter the land to live in it. They had conquered the land but they had not yet settled down in it.Expositor’s Bible Commentary volume 2.

the God of your fathers: The term the God of your fathers indicates that Yahweh was the God whom their ancestors had worshiped.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Why are you(plur) waiting so long to claim the land that Yahweh, the God of your ancestors, has given to you?

Do not delay any longer to go in and settle in the land that Yahweh has given you. He is the God whom your ancestors worshiped.

title: Joshua 18:4
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:4a

Appoint three men from each tribe, and I will send them out

  • Choose three men from each clan, and I will send them out.

  • Appoint three men from each of the seven remaining clans. I will send them

Appoint three men from each tribe: The phrase each tribe probably refers to the seven clans that had not yet received their share of land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Choose three men from each of the seven clans

Appoint three men per clan

18:4b

to survey the land and map it out,

  • They will go and walk around the land.

  • to go throughout the land.

There is a Hebrew verb at the beginning of this clause that the BSB leaves untranslated. This verb means “and they will arise.” This is a Hebrew idiom which is used to indicate the beginning of an action. Translate this in a way that is natural in your language to indicate the beginning of an action.

to survey the land and map it out: The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as survey the land and map it out is more literally “they will walk back and forth in the land.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

they will walk all around the land

they will go through the land

18:4c

according to the inheritance of each.

  • They can make a map of the area that they would like to receive as their inheritance.

  • They will write a report. It will show the boundaries of the land that each clan wants to receive.

according to the inheritance of each: This indicates that the men wrote a description of the land that they wanted to receive for their own clan. The description may have been in the form of a map.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

so that they can make a map of the area they want to receive as their inheritance

They will write a report. The report will show the boundaries of the land that their clan wishes to receive

18:4d

Then they will return to me

  • Then they will come back to me.

  • Then they will return to me with their report.

Then they will return to me: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then they must come back to me

Then they must return to me with the report

title: Joshua 18:5
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:5a

and divide the land into seven portions.

  • They must divide the land into seven parts among themselves.

  • They will divide the remaining land into seven areas.

and divide the land into seven portions: This indicates that the men should divide the remaining land into seven parts, one for each of the clans that had still not received a share of land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They must divide the remaining land into seven parts among themselves

They will divide it into seven areas of land

18:5b

Yehudah (Judah) shall remain in their territory in the south,

  • The clan of Yehudah will remain in the land they received in the south.

  • The clan of Yehudah will stay in their land to the south.

Yehudah shall remain in their territory in the south: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The clan of Yehudah will remain in the land they have received in the south

The clan of Yehudah will stay in their land to the south

18:5c

and the house of Yosef (Joseph) shall remain in their territory in the north.

  • The descendants of Yosef will remain in the land they received in the north.

  • The family of Yosef will stay in their land to the north.

and the house of Yosef shall remain in their territory in the north: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The descendants of Yosef will remain in the land they have received in the north

The family of Yosef will stay in their land to the north

title: Joshua 18:6
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:6a

When you have mapped out the seven portions of land

  • You(plur) must describe the land and divide it into seven parts

  • These men will divide the land into seven areas and write down what each area is like.

When you have mapped out the seven portions of land: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as you have mapped out the seven portions of land is more literally “you will write the land seven portions.”

you: In verse 4 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the people of Yisrael (Israel) that they must choose three men from each clan. He referred to them in the third person. In this verse Yehoshua addresses the chosen men in the second person. It may be more natural in some languages to keep referring to the men in the third person. For example:

In their report, the men from the seven tribes should describe the seven parts of the remaining land that they wish to receive (T4T)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But you should describe the land and divide it into seven parts (ERV)

They will divide the land into seven areas and write down what each area is like

The first two parts of this verse are similar to Joshua 18:4c–d.

18:6b

and brought it to me,

  • and bring the description back to me.

  • Then they will bring the report back to me.

and brought it to me: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Bring the map to me (ERV)

Then they will bring the report back to me

18:6c

I will cast lots for you here in the presence of Yahweh our God.

  • I will throw lots for you(plur) here in the presence of Yahweh our God.

  • I will throw marked stones to let Yahweh our God decide how to divide the land among the clans.

I will cast lots for you: The word lots refers to small objects of unknown shape and material that the Israeli (Israelite) people threw to determine God’s will.Holman Bible Dictionary p. 896. Use a term that is familiar in your language for choosing by chance.

Here are some other ways to translate this term:

throw dice/stones

draw straws

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

Yehoshua (Joshua) threw stones to decide which share of land each clan would receive

here in the presence of Yahweh our God: In 18:1 the people of Yisrael (Israel) set up the tent of meeting in Shiloh. Inside the tent of meeting was the ark of the covenant that was a symbol of God’s presence. The phrase here in the presence of Yahweh our God indicates that Yehoshua threw the lots in front of the tent of meeting, the place where God met with his people. The Israelis (Israelites) believed that Yahweh had control over the way the lot would fall.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

I will throw lots for you(plur) here in the presence of Yahweh our(incl) God

I will throw lots here before the tent of Yahweh our God. He will decide how to divide the land among the clans.

While Yahweh is watching, I will throw marked stones to decide which land should be allotted to each tribe (T4T)

title: Joshua 18:7
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:7a

The Levites, however, have no portion among you,

  • The clan of Levi will not receive any part of the land as their own

  • But the Levi clan will not have a share of land

The Levites, however, have no portion among you: The clause The Levites…have no portion among you indicates that the clan of Levi did not receive any land of their own.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The clan of Levi will not receive any land as their own

But the Levi clan will not have any share of the land

18:7b

because their inheritance is the priesthood of Yahweh.

  • because their inheritance is to serve Yahweh as his priests.

  • because their share is to be priests of Yahweh.

because their inheritance is the priesthood of Yahweh: The phrase priesthood of Yahweh indicates that the clan of Levi were to serve Yahweh as priests.

inheritance: Instead of receiving land from Yahweh, the clan of Levi received the privilege of serving Yahweh as his priests.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

their inheritance is to serve Yahweh as his priests

their gift/reward is the duty to be priests of Yahweh

their role as priests of the Lord is their allotment (NLT)

instead, they will serve the Lord as priests (CEV)

18:7c

And Gad, Re’uven (Reuben), and half the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh)

  • The clan of Gad and the clan of Re’uven and half of the clan of Menasheh

  • The Gad clan, the Re’uven clan and half of the Menasheh clan

And Gad, Re’uven, and half the tribe of Menasheh: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The clan of Gad and the clan of Re’uven and half the clan of Menasheh

The clans of Gad and Re’uven and half of the Menasheh clan

18:7d

have already received the inheritance that Mosheh (Moses) the servant of Yahweh gave them beyond the Yarden (Jordan) to the east.”

  • have land on the east side of the Yarden River as their inheritance. Mosheh the servant of Yahweh gave that land to them.”

  • have already received their share of land on the east bank of the Yarden River, as Mosheh the man who served Yahweh decided.”

have already received the inheritance that Mosheh the servant of Yahweh gave them beyond the Yarden to the east: This indicates that the clans of Gad, Re’uven (Reuben) and half the clan of Menasheh (Manasseh) had already received their land on the east side of the Yarden River.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

they have land on the east side of the Yarden River as their inheritance

they already have their share of land on the east side of the Yarden River

that Mosheh (Moses) the servant of Yahweh gave them: The phrase Mosheh the servant of Yahweh occurs in Joshua 1:1. You should translate it the same way as you did there.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

Mosheh the man who served God well (T4T)

Mosheh the man who served Yahweh

General Comment on verse 7:c-e

The words in verse 7c–d are similar to Joshua 13:8. You should translate it in a similar way.

title: Joshua 18:8
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:8a

As the men got up to go out,

  • So the men got ready and went.

  • The men went on their journey.

As the men got up to go out: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as got up to go out is more literally “the men arose and they went.” This is a Hebrew idiom that is used to indicate the beginning of an action. Translate this in a way that is natural in your language to indicate the beginning of an action.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So the men started to go

The men went on their journey

18:8b

Yehoshua (Joshua) commanded them to map out the land, saying,

  • Yehoshua had commanded the ones who were going to survey the land. He said,

  • Yehoshua had told them,

Yehoshua commanded them to map out the land, saying: The English word commanded can also be translated as “charged” or “told.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yehoshua instructed them (NIV)

Yehoshua repeated their orders (CEV)

18:8c

“Go and survey the land, map it out,

  • “Walk(plur) around the land and write a description of it.

  • “Go through the land and write a report. It will show the boundaries of the land.

Go and survey the land, map it out: The words in 18:8c are similar to 18:4b–c. You should translate these verses in a similar way.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Walk all around the land and write a report about it

Go through the land and draw a map of it. The map will show the boundaries of the land.

18:8d

and return to me.

  • Then bring the description to me.

  • When you return to me,

and return to me: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then come back to me

Then return to me

18:8e

Then I will cast lots for you here in Shiloh in the presence of Yahweh.”

  • Here in Shiloh town I will throw lots for you(plur) in the presence of Yahweh.”

  • I will throw marked stones here in Shiloh to let Yahweh decide how to divide the land among you.”

Then I will cast lots for you here in Shiloh in the presence of Yahweh: This verse is like verse 18:6c except that the words in Shiloh are added.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Here in Shiloh town I will throw lots for you in the presence of Yahweh

I will throw marked stones here in Shiloh town to let Yahweh decide how to divide the land among you

title: Joshua 18:9
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:9a

So the men departed and went throughout the land,

  • So the men left and went all through the land.

  • So the men set out and went all over the land.

So the men departed and went throughout the land: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as throughout the land is more literally “they passed through in the land.” The Hebrew verb is different from the verb used in verse 18:4b but the meaning is the same.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So the men left and went through the land (NIV)

So the men went all over the land. (GNT)

18:9b

mapping it city by city into seven portions.

  • They wrote a description of the land in seven parts on a scroll. They listed the towns that were in each part.

  • They wrote a report about it. The report showed how to divide the land into seven shares, and listed the towns in each share.

mapping it city by city into seven portions: The clause which the BSB translates as mapping it is more literally “they wrote it on a book.” This indicates that the men wrote down a description on writing material, perhaps on a scroll. They did not have books in the modern sense of the word.

city by city into seven portions: This indicates that the men described the land according to the towns that were in seven parts of the land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and wrote down a description of the land in seven parts, according to the towns that were in each part

they described in a scroll each town that was in the seven parts into which they had divided the land (T4T)

they wrote a report about it on a scroll. The report showed how they divided up the land into seven parts and listed the towns in each part

18:9c

Then they returned with the document to Yehoshua (Joshua) at the camp in Shiloh.

  • Then they returned to Yehoshua, to the camp in Shiloh town.

  • Then they went back to Yehoshua. He was at the tenting place in Shiloh.

Then they returned with the document to Yehoshua at the camp in Shiloh: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then they returned to Yehoshua, to the camp in the town of Shiloh

Then they went back to Yehoshua. He was at the tenting place in Shiloh

title: Joshua 18:10
content:
Section 18:1–10 Yehoshua (Joshua) divided land among the remaining seven clans

In this section Yehoshua instructed the remaining seven clans to make a plan for dividing up the rest of the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other possible section headings:

Dividing the rest of the land

The rest of the land is distributed

18:10a

And Yehoshua cast lots for them in the presence of Yahweh at Shiloh,

  • There in Shiloh town Yehoshua threw lots for them in the presence of Yahweh.

  • Yehoshua (Joshua) threw marked stones in the town of Shiloh to let Yahweh decide how to divide the land among the clans.

And Yehoshua cast lots for them in the presence of Yahweh at Shiloh: The words here are similar to Joshua 18:6c and 18:8e.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So there in the town of Shiloh Yehoshua threw lots for them in the presence of Yahweh

Yehoshua threw marked stones in Shiloh town to let Yahweh decide how to divide the land among the clans

18:10b

where he distributed the land to the Israelis (Israelites) according to their divisions.

  • Yehoshua divided the land among the remaining clans of Yisrael (Israel). Each clan received its own piece of land.

  • He gave a share of land to each of the remaining clans of Yisrael.

where he distributed the land to the Israelis according to their divisions: The clause he distributed the land indicates that Yehoshua (Joshua) divided up the remaining land.

The word Israelis refers to the seven clans who had not yet received any land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and Yehoshua divided out the land to the remaining clans of Yisrael. Each clan received its own piece of land.

There he gave out a share of land to each of the remaining tribes in Yisrael (NIRV)

title: Joshua 18:11
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:11a

The first lot came up for the clans of the tribe of Benyamin.

  • ¶ The first lot went to the clan of Benyamin by its families.

  • ¶ The first clan to be given land was the Benyamin (Benjamin) clan and its families.

The first lot came up for the clans of the tribe of Benyamin: This sentence indicates that the first clan chosen by lot was the clan of Benyamin. Each family of Benyamin received some land. This verse is similar to Joshua 15:1.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The first lot belonged to the tribe of Benyamin by its clans (NET)

The first clan to receive land was the Benyamin clan and its families

18:11b

Their allotted territory lay between the tribes of Yehudah (Judah) and Yosef (Joseph):

  • The land they received was between the lands of the Yehudah clan and the Yosef clan.

  • The land given to them was between the land that the clans of Yehudah and Yosef had received.

Their allotted territory lay between the tribes of Yehudah and Yosef: This indicates that the land that the clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received was between the lands of the clans of Yehudah and Yosef. Yehudah’s land was to the south of Benyamin’s land. Yosef’s land was to the north of Benyamin’s land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The land they received by lot was between the land of the Yehudah clan and the Yosef clan

The land assigned to them was between the land that the clans of Yehudah and Yosef had received

title: Joshua 18:12
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:12a

On the north side their border began at the Yarden (Jordan),

  • Their northern border began at the Yarden River in the east.

  • These are the boundaries of Benyamin’s (Benjamin’s) land. On the north the boundary began at the Yarden River.

On the north side their border began at the Yarden: The description of Benyamin’s boundary began at the Yarden River in the east and continued to the west.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Their northern border began at the Yarden River

Benyamin’s boundary on the north began at the Yarden River

18:12b

went up past the northern slope of Yeriho (Jericho),

  • Then it ascended the mountain ridge north of the town of Yeriho.

  • It went up from there to the mountain slope north of Yeriho town

went up past the northern slope of Yeriho: The phrase went up indicates that the boundary ascends in elevation.

the northern slope of Yeriho: The northern slope of Yeriho refers to a mountain ridge that is north of Yeriho.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then it ascended the mountain ridge north of Yeriho

It went up from there to the mountain slope to the north of Yeriho

18:12c

headed west through the hill country,

  • It continued west up through the mountain country

  • and westward into the mountains.

headed west through the hill country: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and continued west up through the mountain country

and westward into the mountains

18:12d

and came out at the wilderness of Beyt-Aven (Beth-aven).

  • until it reached the wilderness near Beyt-Aven.

  • It ended in the wilderness near Beyt-Aven town.

and came out at the wilderness of Beyt-Aven: Beyt-Aven was a town in the mountains. It was mentioned in Joshua 7:2.

wilderness: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as wilderness indicates an uninhabited place. The area around “Beyt-Aven” was a wilderness, but it was not a desert with large areas of sand.

Beyt-Aven: Here are some ways that the English versions spell the name of Beyt-Aven town.

Beyt-Aven (BSB, RSV, ESV, NLT, NABRE, NASB, KJV)

Beth Aven (NET, NIV, GW)

Beyt-Aven (Beth-aven) (CEV)

Bethaven (GNT)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

until it reached the wilderness near Beyt-Aven

as far as the wasteland near Beyt-Aven town

title: Joshua 18:13
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:13a

From there the border crossed over to the southern slope of Luz

  • From there the border passed along the mountain slope south of Luz,

  • Then the boundary went along the mountain ridge south of the town of Luz.

From there the border crossed over to the southern slope of Luz: The Hebrew clause behind this verse is more literally “the boundary passed to Luz, to the shoulder of Luz, to the south.”

There is an interpretation issue in this verse. It concerns the placement of the Hebrew word translated as to the southern slope.

  1. The Hebrew word translated as to the southern slope modifies the mountain ridge. It means that the mountain ridge is south of Luz. For example:

    From there it crossed to the south slope of Luz (NIV) (BSB, NIV, NJB, NABRE, NET, GW, NLT, GNT, CEV)

  2. The Hebrew word that means “to the south” modifies the boundary line. It means that the boundary line went south to Luz town. For example:

    From there the boundary passes along southward in the direction of Luz, to the shoulder of Luz (ESV) (ESV, RSV, NJPS)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) along with many English versions and commentaries.Woudstra p 276.

the southern slope of Luz: The southern slope of Luz refers to a mountain ridge that was south of the town of Luz. Compare this with “the northern slope of Yeriho (Jericho)” in 18:12b.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

Then border then went along the mountain ridge that was south of Luz town

From there it went to Luz…The border ran along the ridge south of Luz (CEV)

Luz: The town of Luz was mentioned in Joshua 16:2.

18:13b

(that is, Beyt-El (Bethel))

  • which is now called Beyt-El.

  • Luz is also named Beyt-El.

that is, Beyt-El: The phrase that is, Beyt-El indicates that the town of Luz was named Beyt-El at the time that the book of Yehoshua (Joshua) was written.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It is now called Beyt-El

Luz is also called Beyt-El

18:13c

and went down to Atrot-Adar (Ataroth-addar)

  • Then the border went down to the town of Atrot-Adar

  • The boundary continued down to Atrot-Adar town.

and went down to Atrot-Adar: The town of Atrot-Adar was lower in elevation than the town of Beyt-El (Bethel). It was mentioned in Joshua 16:5.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border went down to the town of Atrot-Adar

Then the border continued down to Atrot-Adar

18:13d

on the hill south of Lower Beyt-Horon (Lower Beth-horon).

  • which is on the mountain to the south of Lower Beyt-Horon town.

  • It is on the hill south of the town of Lower Beyt-Horon.

on the hill south of Lower Beyt-Horon: The town of Lower Beyt-Horon is mentioned in verse 16:3b in connection with the border of Efrayim (Ephraim).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

which is on the hill to the south of Lower Beyt-Horon

Atrot-Adar (Ataroth-addar) is on the hill south of the town of Lower Beyt-Horon

General Comment on 18:12–13

Verses 12–13 describe the northern border of the clan of Benyamin (Benjamin). This border is the same as the southern border of the clan of Efrayim which was described in chapter 16:1–2. It is recommended that you compare these two passages as you translate them.

title: Joshua 18:14
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:14a

On the west side the border curved southward

  • The border then changed direction. The western border went south,

  • Then the boundary turned to the south on its western side.

On the west side the border curved southward: Verses 12–13 described the north side of Benyamin’s (Benjamin’s) land. Verse 14 describes the west side of their land. On the west side the boundary turns toward the south.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The boundary then changed direction. On the west side the boundary went southward

At that point it turned south and became the western border (CEV)

18:14b

from the hill facing Beyt-Horon (Beth-horon) on the south

  • starting at the mountain that was south and across from the town of Beyt-Horon.

  • It began by the mountain which was opposite the town of Beyt-Horon to its south.

from the hill facing Beyt-Horon on the south: The hill facing Beyt-Horon on the south marks the beginning of the western border. The town of Beyt-Horon was on a mountain. Across the valley to the south was another mountain that marked the border. It is the same mountain as was mentioned in verse 13 (that the BSB translates as "hill”).

Note that Joshua 16:5 mentioned the town of Upper Beyt-Horon (Upper Beth-horon). Joshua 18:13 mentioned Lower Beyt-Horon (Lower Beth-horon). In this verse Upper Beyt-Horon and Lower Beyt-Horon are spoken of as one place.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The western boundary started at the mountain that was across from the town of Beyt-Horon

It began at the mountain which was opposite the town of Beyt-Horon, to the south

18:14c

and came out at Kiryat-Ba’al (Kiriath-baal) (that is, Kiryat-Yearim (Kiriath-jearim)),

  • The western border ended at the town of Kiryat-Ba’al. That town was also called Kiryat-Yearim.

  • That side of the boundary ended by the town of Kiryat-Ba’al, which was also named Kiryat-Yearim.

and came out at Kiryat-Ba’al (that is, Kiryat-Yearim): The names Kiryat-Ba’al and Kiryat-Yearim are two names for the same town.

Here are some ways that English versions spell these names:

Kiryat-Ba’al, Kiryat-Yearim (BSB, RSV, ESV, NABRE, NASB, NLT, KJV)

Kiryat (Kiriath) Ba’al (Baal), Kiryat Jearim (NET, NIV, GW, GNT)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The western border ended at the town of Kiryat-Ba’al (Kiriath-baal). That town is also called Kiryat-Yearim (Kiriath-jearim)

That side of the border ended by the town of Kiryat-Ba’al, which was also named Kiryat-Yearim

18:14d

a city of the sons of Yehudah (Judah).

  • It was in land that belonged to the Yehudah clan.

  • People of the clan of Yehudah lived in the town of Kiryat-Ba’al.

a city of the sons of Yehudah: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

That town was in land that belonged to the Yehudah clan

People of the clan of Yehudah lived in the town of Kiryat-Ba’al (Kiriath-baal)

18:14e

This was the western side.

  • This was the western border of the land of Benyamin (Benjamin).

  • That described the western boundary of Benyamin’s land.

This was the western side: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This was the western boundary of the clan of Benyamin

That described the western border

title: Joshua 18:15
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:15a

On the south side the border began at the outskirts of Kiryat-Yearim (Kiriath-jearim)

  • The southern border began at the edge of the town of Kiryat-Yearim,

  • The boundary on the south started at the limits of Kiryat-Yearim.

On the south side the border began at the outskirts of Kiryat-Yearim: Joshua 18:15–19 describes the south border of Benyamin’s (Benjamin’s) land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The south border began at the edge of Kiryat-Yearim

The boundary of Benyamin’s land on the south started at the limits of the town of Kiryat-Yearim

18:15b

and extended westward to the spring at the Waters of Neftoah (Nephtoah).

  • and went to the spring of Neftoah.

  • Then the boundary continued to the spring of water called Neftoah.

and extended westward: The Hebrew text is difficult. The Hebrew text reads “and the boundary goes westward.” However, that contradicts verse 14. In verse 14 the western boundary came to an end. The description of the southern boundary begins here and is described from west to east. The English versions have handled this difficulty in several ways:

  1. Some versions omit the word westward. For example:

    and projected… (NABRE) (NABRE, GNT)

  2. Some versions follow the Hebrew text. For example:

    and extended westward (NET) (BSB, NET, GW, NASB, NJPS)

  3. Some versions change the text to follow Joshua 15:9, which describes the same border, going from east to west. For example:

    and the boundary goes from there to Efron (Ephron) (RSV) (RSV, ESV)

  4. Some versions move the word “west” to a different place in the sentence. For example:

    The southern side began at the outskirts of Kiryat (Kiriath) Jearim on the west (NIV) (NIV)

It is recommended that you follow option (1). This makes the least change to the text, while still making sense. If you do this, it is recommended that you add a footnote to explain the Hebrew text. For example:

FOOTNOTE: The Hebrew text says: “and the boundary goes westward.”

to the spring at the Waters of Neftoah (Nephtoah): This is the spring mentioned in Joshua 15:9b. You should translate this phrase as you did there.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border went on to the spring of Neftoah

Then the border continued to the spring of water called Neftoah

title: Joshua 18:16
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:16a

Then it went down to the foot of the hill

  • Then it descended to the base of the mountain

  • The boundary went down to the foot of the mountain

Then it went down to the foot of the hill: This indicates that the border descended to the foot of the mountain.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border descends to the foot of the mountain (GW)

The boundary went down to the foot of the hill (NIV)

18:16b

that faces the Valley of Hinom (Hinnom)

  • that faced the valley of the son of Hinom.

  • that was opposite the valley of the son of Hinom.

that faces the Valley of Hinom: This valley was mentioned in Joshua 15:8. You should translate it the same way that you did there.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

facing the Valley of Ben Hinom (NIV)

that overlooks the Valley of the Son of Hinom (ESV)

18:16c

at the northern end of the Valley of Refaim (Rephaim)

  • That mountain is on the north side of the valley of Refaim.

  • It is on the northern edge of Refaim Valley (Rephaim Valley).

at the northern end of the Valley of Refaim: This valley was mentioned in Joshua 15:8e. It is recommended that you translate this part of the verse in the same way as you did there.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

That mountain is on the northern side of the Valley of Refaim

It is on the northern edge of Refaim Valley

18:16d

and ran down the Valley of Hinom (Hinnom)

  • Then the border went along the valley of Hinom.

  • The boundary line passed through the Hinom Valley (Hinnom Valley),

and ran down the Valley of Hinom: This indicates that the boundary line of Benyamin’s (Benjamin’s) land continued through the Valley of Hinom.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border went along the Valley of Hinom

The boundary line passed through the Hinom Valley

18:16e

toward the southern slope of the Yevusim (Jebusites) and downward to Eyn-Rogel (En-rogel).

  • It continued to the mountain ridge that was south of Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and then descended to the spring of Eyn-Rogel.

  • and went past the hill that was south of Yerushalem and down to Eyn-Rogel Spring.

toward the southern slope of the Yevusim: The phrase the southern slope of the Yevusim refers to a mountain ridge that was south of Yerushalem.

Yevusim: The Yevusim were people who lived in Yerushalem. Yevus (Jebus) was the name of the town of Yerushalem before David conquered it.

and downward to Eyn-Rogel: The name Eyn-Rogel refers to a spring in the Kidron valley east of Yerushalem.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It continued to the mountain ridge that was south of Yerushalem and then descended to the spring of Eyn-Rogel

and went on past the hill that was south of the town of Yerushalem and down to Eyn-Rogel (En-rogel) Spring

title: Joshua 18:17
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:17a

From there it curved northward and proceeded to Eyn-Shemesh (En-shemesh)

  • Then the border turned to the north and continued to the spring of Eyn-Shemesh.

  • The boundary line then curved northward to Eyn-Shemesh Spring.

From there it curved northward: This indicates that the southern border made a turn to the north at this point.

and proceeded to Eyn-Shemesh: Eyn-Shemesh is the name of a spring of water that was near Yerushalem (Jerusalem). This spring was mentioned in Joshua 15:7. It is recommended that you translate it the same way as you did there.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border turned to the north and continued to the spring of Eyn-Shemesh

The boundary line then curved northward to Eyn-Shemesh Spring

18:17b

and on to Gelilot (Geliloth) facing the Ascent of Adumim (Adummim),

  • From there it went to Gelilot, which faced the Pass of Adumim.

  • Then it continued to the circle of stones which was across from the road going up Adumim Mountain.

and on to Gelilot: The term Gelilot means “circle of stones” in Hebrew. It is not known where Gelilot was. It is uncertain whether or not Gelilot was a town.

Here are some other ways to translate this term:

Gelilot

the circle of stones

facing the Ascent of Adumim (Adummim): The Ascent of Adumim is a road that went up Adumim Mountain. This clause is the same as the one found in Joshua 15:7b. It is recommended that you translate it in the same way.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From there it went on to the circle of stones across from the Pass of Adumim

Then it continued to Gelilot (Geliloth), which was across from the road that went up Adumim Mountain

18:17c

and continued down to the Stone of Bohan son of Re’uven (Reuben).

  • Then the border descended to the stone of Bohan, the son of Re’uven.

  • The boundary continued to go down eastward to the large stone of Bohan, who was the son of Re’uven.

and continued down to the Stone of Bohan son of Re’uven: The Stone of Bohan was mentioned in Joshua 15:6c. It is recommended that you translate it the same way as you did there.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border descended to the large stone of Bohan, the son of Re’uven

The boundary continued to go east downhill to the stone of Bohan. Bohan was the son of Re’uven.

title: Joshua 18:18
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:18a

Then it went on to the northern slope of Beyt-Ha’aravah (Beth-arabah)

  • It went along the north side of the slope overlooking the Yarden (Jordan) River valley.

  • From there it passed north of the ridge that faced the valley of the Yarden River

Then it went on to the northern slope of Beyt-Ha’aravah: There is a textual issue about the Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Beyt-Ha’aravah.

  1. The Hebrew text reads “in front of the Aravah (Arabah).” For example:

    It crossed to the slope in front of the Aravah to the north (NET) (NET, NASB, NABRE, NJPS, GW, GNT, NLT, KJV)

  2. The Septuagint reads “Beyt-Ha’aravah.” For example:

    It continued to the northern slope of Beth Aravah (NIV) (BSB, NIV, RSV, NRSV, NJB, ESV)

It is recommended that you follow option (1). This is the reading of the Hebrew text, and is followed by many English versions and Bible commentaries.Woudstra p. 277.

Some versions follow the Septuagint because they compare this verse with Joshua 15:6. The Hebrew text of Joshua 15:5 reads “It passed along to Beyt-Ha’aravah (Beth-arabah) to the north.” Joshua 15:6 and 18:18 describe the same boundary, although they trace it in different directions.

Beyt-Ha’aravah: The word “arabah” is a Hebrew word that refers to the valley of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Based on option (1) of the previous note, here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From there it passed along the north side of the slope overlooking the Yarden Valley (NLT)

and passed north of the ridge overlooking the Yarden Valley (GNT)

18:18b

and went down into the valley.

  • Then the border descended into the Yarden River valley.

  • and went down into the valley of the Yarden River.

and went down into the valley: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

then the border descended into the Yarden (Jordan) River Valley

then it went down into the valley of the Yarden River

title: Joshua 18:19
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:19a

The border continued to the northern slope of Beyt-Hoglah (Beth-hoglah)

  • From there the border continued east and passed the northern slope of Beyt-Hoglah.

  • Then the boundary went north of the mountain ridge of Beyt-Hoglah town.

The border continued to the northern slope of Beyt-Hoglah: The town of Beyt-Hoglah was mentioned in verse 15:6a. It was to the southeast of the town of Yeriho (Jericho).Rasmussen p. 229.

northern slope of Beyt-Hoglah: The northern slope of Beyt-Hoglah refers to a mountain ridge that was near the town of Beyt-Hoglah.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

passing north of the ridge of Beth Hoglah (GNT)

Then the border went along north of the ridge of Beyt-Hoglah town

18:19b

and came out at the northern bay of the Salt Sea,

  • And the border ended at the bay at the north end of the Salt Sea,

  • It ended at the northern point of the Dead Sea

and came out at the northern bay of the Salt Sea: The northern bay of the Salt Sea is the northernmost part of the Salt Sea.

Salt Sea: In English the Salt Sea is usually referred to as the Dead Sea. You should use the same term as you did in Joshua 15:5a.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The boundary ended at the north end of the Dead Sea

Benyamin’s (Benjamin’s) border ended at the northern end of the Salt Sea

18:19c

at the mouth of the Yarden (Jordan).

  • which is at the south end of the Yarden River.

  • where the Yarden River flowed into it.

at the mouth of the Yarden: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

which was at the south end of the Yarden River

where the Yarden River flowed into it

18:19d

This was the southern border.

  • That was the south border of Benyamin’s (Benjamin’s) land.

  • This describes the southern boundary of the clan of Benyamin.

This was the southern border: This clause is a conclusion to Joshua 18:15–19, which described the southern border.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This described the southern boundary line for the clan of Benyamin

That was the south border of Benyamin’s land

title: Joshua 18:20
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:20a

On the east side the border was the Yarden (Jordan).

  • The Yarden River formed the eastern border.

  • The boundary on the east side of their land was the Yarden River.

On the east side the border was the Yarden: The eastern border is easy to describe. The full description is in this one phrase.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The Yarden River formed the eastern boundary line

The border on the east side of Benyamin’s (Benjamin’s) land was the Yarden River

18:20b

These were the borders around the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Benyamin.

  • This was the land that the clan of Benyamin received as their inheritance. These borders marked the four sides of the land that they received according to their families.

  • That describes the land that the Benyamin clan received. Each family received land within these boundaries.

These were the borders around the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Benyamin: The clause These were the borders around the inheritance is a conclusion to Joshua 18:12–20. We have now made a circle around all four of the boundary lines of the land that Benyamin received.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This was the land that the clan of Benyamin received as their inheritance

That described the land that the Benyamin (Benjamin) clan received as its permanent possession
