These were the borders around the inheritance: The phrase the borders around refers to the boundary lines on all sides: north, south, east and west.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

These boundaries marked out the land that they received according to their family groups

Each clan received land within these boundaries

In some languages it may be more natural to combine the phrase the borders around with the information in 18:20b. For example:

These were the borders of the land which the clan of Benyamin received as their inheritance

Those boundaries described the land that the Benyamin (Benjamin) clan received

the clans: The phrase the clans actually refers to the families within the clan of Benyamin.

title: Joshua 18:21
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:21a

These were the cities of the clans of the tribe of Benyamin:

  • ¶ The following towns belonged to the families of the clan of Benyamin:

  • ¶ The families of the Benyamin (Benjamin) clan received these towns:

These were the cities of the clans of the tribe of Benyamin: This introduces a list of the towns that were within Benyamin’s land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The following towns belonged to the families of the clan of Benyamin

The families of the Benyamin clan received these towns. In the eastern part of their territory there were:

18:21b

Yeriho (Jericho), Beyt-Hoglah (Beth-hoglah), Emek-Ketsits (Emek-keziz),

  • Yeriho and Beyt-Hoglah and Emek-Ketsits,

Yeriho, Beyt-Hoglah, Emek-Ketsits: The towns listed in verses 21–24 were in the eastern part of Benyamin’s (Benjamin’s) territory. The town of Beyt-Hoglah was mentioned in Joshua 18:19a. The town of Emek-Ketsits is mentioned only here in the Bible, and its location is unknown.

content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

18:24a

Kefar-Ha’amoni (Chephar-ammoni), Ofni (Ophni), and Geva (Geba)—

  • and Chepharammoni and Ofni and Geva.

Kefar-Ha’amoni, Ofni, and Geva:

twelve cities, along with their villages.

  • In all there were twelve towns, and there were villages that surrounded them.

  • The number of these was twelve towns, and there were villages that were near them.

twelve cities, along with their villages: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

a total of twelve towns, with the villages that were near them

title: Joshua 18:25
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

18:25

Giveon (Gibeon), Ramah, Be’erot (Beeroth),

  • They also received Giveon and Ramah and Be-eroth

Giveon, Ramah, Be’erot: The towns listed in verses 25–28 were in the western part of Benyamin’s (Benjamin’s) territory. Here is another way to translate these words:

In the western part of their territory there were the towns of Giveon, Ramah, Be-eroth,

content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

title: Joshua 18:28
content:
Section 18:11–28 The clan of Benyamin (Benjamin) received their land

This section describes the boundaries of the land of Benyamin and the towns within it.

Here are some other possible section headings:

The land of the clan of Benyamin

Benyamin’s land

18:28a

Zelah, Ha’elef (Haeleph), Yevus (Jebus) (that is, Yerushalem (Jerusalem)),

  • and Tsela (Zela) and Ha-eleph and Yevus which is now called Yerushalem,

  • and Tsela and Ha-eleph and the town of the Yevus people. That town is now named Yerushalem.

Zelah, Ha’elef, Yevus (that is, Yerushalem): The term Yevus is an older name for the town of Yerushalem.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yevus, which is now called Yerushalem

The town of the Yevus people. That town is now named Yerushalem.

18:28b

Giveah (Gibeah), and Kiryat-Yearim (Kiriath-jearim)—fourteen cities, along with their villages.

  • and Gibe-ah and Kiryat-Yearim. In all there were fourteen towns, and there were villages that surrounded them.

  • There were also Gibe-ah and Kiryat-Yearim. The number of these was fourteen towns, and there were villages near them.

Giveah, and Kiryat-Yearim—fourteen cities, along with their villages: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

there were fourteen towns in this area, and there were villages that surrounded them

a total of fourteen towns, with the villages that were near them

18:28c

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Benyamin (Benjamin).

  • This was the land that the families of the clan of Benyamin received as their inheritance.

  • That describes the land that the families of the Benyamin clan received.

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Benyamin: This verse repeats information from verse 18:20. You should translate it in the same way as you did there.

title: Joshua 19:1
content:
Section 19:1–9: The clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received their land

19:1a

The second lot came out

  • ¶ The second lot belonged to (NET)

  • ¶ Yehoshua (Joshua) threw the lot a second time

The second lot came out: The clause The second lot refers to the second time that Yehoshua threw the lot. This time the lot showed that the clan of Shim’on should receive their land. This verse is similar to verse 15:1 and 18:11. In each case the Hebrew verb is slightly different, but the meaning is the same.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The second lot belonged (NET)

Yehoshua threw the lot a second time

19:1b

for the clans of the tribe of Shim’on (Simeon):

  • the clan of Shim’on. They received land according to their families.

  • and each family of the clan of Shim’on received some land.

for the clans of the tribe of Shim’on: The phrase the clans refers to the families among Shim’on’s descendants. Shim’on was one of the twelve sons of Ya’akov (Jacob) who had many descendants.

the tribe of Shim’on: The phrase the tribe of Shim’on refers to all the clans of Shim’on.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Each of the families of the Shim’on clan received some land

Yehoshua (Joshua) threw the lot again. This second lot showed that the clans of Shim’on was the next to receive land. There was some land for each family in the Shim’on clans.

19:1c

Their inheritance lay within the territory of Yehudah (Judah)

  • Their land was within the land that belonged to the clan of Yehudah.

  • Their land was inside the land that the clan of Yehudah had received.

Their inheritance lay within the territory of Yehudah: The sentence Their inheritance lay within the territory of Yehudah indicates that the land that the clans of Shim’on (Simeon) received was inside the boundaries of the land that the clans of Yehudah had received.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

their land was within the boundaries of the land that belonged to the clans of Yehudah

their land was inside the land that the clans of Yehudah had received

title: Joshua 19:2
content:
Section 19:1–9: The clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received their land

19:2

and included Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba) (or Sheva (Sheba)), Moladah,

  • They received these towns as their permanent possession: Beer-sheba, which is also called Sheva, and Moladah.

  • The land that was assigned to them included the following towns: Beer-sheba or Sheva town, and Moladah town,

and included Be’er-Sheva (or Sheva), Moladah: The towns listed in verses 2–6 were in the south part of the land that belonged to the clan of Yehudah (Judah).

Be’er-Sheva: There is also an interpretation issue with the word Be’er-Sheva.

  1. Sheva is another name for the town of Be’er-Sheva. For example:

    Be’er-Sheva (or Sheva), Moladah (NIV) (BSB, NIV, NET, NJPS, NASB, GW, REB, KJV)

  2. Sheva (Sheba) is a different town. It is not the same town as Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba). For example:

    Be’er-Sheva, Sheva, Moladah (ESV) (ESV, RSV, NRSV, NLT, GNT)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) along with many English versions. There is a similar list of the towns that belonged to the clan of Shim’on (Simeon) in 1 Chronicles 4:28. That list does not include the town of Sheva. Moreover, if Sheva is counted as an independent town in this list, the total number of towns would come to fourteen, rather than thirteen, as stated in verse 6. Because of this, many Bible scholars consider the term Sheva to be an alternative name for the town of Be’er-Sheva.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They received the following towns as its permanent possession: Be’er-Sheva, which is also called Sheva, and Moladah

The land that was assigned to them included the following towns: Be’er-Sheva, or Sheva, and Moladah

Sheva: There is a textual issue with the word Sheva.

  1. The text should say Sheva (Sheba). This follows the Masoretic Text. (BSB, NIV, NET, RSV, ESV, NJPS, NASB, GW, GNT, KJV)

  2. The text should say Shema. This follows the Septuagint, and it also agrees with Joshua 15:26. (NABRE, NJB, CEV)

It is recommended that you follow option (1). This is the reading of most English versions, and is supported by many commentaries.

title: Joshua 19:3
content:
Section 19:1–9: The clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received their land

19:3

Hatsar-Shual (Hazar-shual), Balah, Etsem (Ezem),

  • They also received the towns of Hatsar-Shual, Balah and Etsem,

  • and Hatsar-Shual town and Balah town and Etsem town,

Hatsar-Shual, Balah, Etsem: Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

They also received the towns of Hatsar-Shual and Balah and Etsem

Hatsar-Shual and Balah and Etsem

title: Joshua 19:4
content:
Section 19:1–9: The clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received their land

19:4

Eltolad, Betul (Bethul), Hormah,

  • the towns of Eltolad, Betul and Hormah,

  • and Eltolad town and Betul town and Hormah town,

Eltolad, Betul, Hormah: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the town of Eltolad, the town of Betuel (Bethuel), the town of Hormah

Eltolad town and Betul town and Hormah town

title: Joshua 19:5
content:
Section 19:1–9: The clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received their land

19:5

Tsiklag (Ziklag), Beyt-Hamarkavot (Beth-marcaboth), Hatsar-Susah (Hazar-susah),

  • the towns of Tsiklag, Beyt-Hamarkavot and Hatsar-Susah,

  • and Tsiklag town and Beyt-Hamarkavot town and Hatsar-Susah town

Tsiklag, Beyt-Hamarkavot, Hatsar-Susah: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the town of Tsiklag, the town of Beyt-Hamarkavot, the town of Hatsar-Susah

Tsiklag town and Beyt-Hamarkavot town and Hatsar-Susah town

title: Joshua 19:6
content:
Section 19:1–9: The clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received their land

19:6

Beyt-Leva’ot (Beth-lebaoth), and Sharuhen—thirteen cities, along with their villages.

  • and the towns of Beyt-Leva’ot and Sharuhen. In all there were thirteen towns and the villages that surrounded them.

  • and Beyt-Leva’ot town and Sharuhen town. The number of these towns was thirteen (13), and there were villages that were near them.

Beyt-Leva’ot, and Sharuhen—thirteen cities, along with their villages: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the town of Beyt-Leva’ot and the town of Sharuhen. In all there were thirteen towns and the villages that surrounded them.

and Beyt-Leva’ot and Sharuhen. The number of all these towns was thirteen, and there were villages that were near them.

title: Joshua 19:7
content:
Section 19:1–9: The clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received their land

19:7

Ayin (Ain), Rimon (Rimmon), Ether, and Ashan—four cities, along with their villages,

  • They also received the towns of Ayin, Rimon, Ether and Ashan. There were four towns with the villages that surrounded them.

  • Their land also included the towns of Ayin, Rimon, Ether, and Ashan. The number of these towns was four towns with the villages that were near them.

Ayin, Rimon, Ether, and Ashan—four cities, along with their villages: There is a textual issue in the first part of the word Rimon (some versions have “Eyn-Rimon (En-rimmon)”):

  1. Eyn-Rimon is two towns: Ayin and Rimon. This is the way the vowels are written in the Masoretic text. (BSB, NRSV, NIV, ESV, NJB, NABRE, NJPS, NET, NASB, REB, GNT, KJV)

  2. Eyn-Rimon is one town. This is the reading of the Septuagint. (RSV, CEV)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) along with the majority of English versions. This also agrees with the list of the same towns in Joshua 15:32.

The towns of Ayin (Ain) and Rimon (Rimmon) were in the southern part of Yehudah’s (Judah’s) land. The towns of Ether and Ashan were farther north, in the Shefelah (Shephelah) district.Woudstra p. 281.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also received the towns of Ayin, Rimon, Ether, and Ashan. There were four towns with the villages that surrounded them.

Their land also included the towns of Ayin, Rimon, Ether and Ashan. The number of these towns was four towns with the villages that were near them.

title: Joshua 19:8
content:
Section 19:1–9: The clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received their land

19:8a

and all the villages surrounding these cities as far as Ba’alat-Be’er (Baalath-beer)

  • They received all the villages that were near these towns, as far to the south as the town of Ba’alat-Be’er.

  • Shim’on’s land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Ba’alat-Be’er, (CEV)

and all the villages surrounding these cities as far as Ba’alat-Be’er: Ba’alat-Be’er was a town in the southern part of Yehudah’s (Judah’s) territory.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also received all the villages that were near these towns, as far to the south as the town of Ba’alat-Be’er

Shim’on’s (Simeon’s) land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Ba’alat-Be’er (CEV)

19:8b

(Ramah of the Negev).

  • This town also had the name Ramah of the Negev (Negeb).

  • which is also called Ramah of the South. (CEV)

Ramah of the Negev: The phrase Ramah of the Negev is another name for the town of Ba’alat-Be’er (Baalath-beer). The term Negev means “south” in Hebrew.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This town also had the name Ramah of the South

which is also called Ramah of the South (CEV)

19:8c

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Shim’on (Simeon).

  • This was the land that the families of the clan of Shim’on received as their inheritance.

  • That describes the land that the Shim’on clan received as its permanent possession. Each family received some land.

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Shim’on: This is similar to verse 18:20b.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This was the land which the family groups of the clan of Shim’on received as their inheritance

That described the land that the Shim’on clan received as its permanent possession. Each family received some land.

title: Joshua 19:9
content:
Section 19:1–9: The clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received their land

19:9a

The inheritance of the Simeonites was taken from the territory of Yehudah (Judah),

  • Their clan received land within the boundaries of the clan of Yehudah,

  • That land was inside the land of the Yehudah clan.

The inheritance of the Simeonites was taken from the territory of Yehudah: The information in verse 9a was already stated in verse 1c.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The people of the Shim’on clan received land within the boundaries of the clan of Yehudah

The land that the clan of Shim’on (Simeon) received as their permanent possession was inside the land of the clan of Yehudah

19:9b

because the share for Yehudah’s (Judah’s) descendants was too large for them.

  • because the clan of Yehudah did not need all the land that it had received.

  • The clan of Yehudah had received too much land for the number of people in its clan,

because the share for Yehudah’s descendants was too large for them: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

because the clan of Yehudah did not need all the land that it had received

Yehudah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe (CEV)

19:9c

So the Simeonites received an inheritance within Yehudah’s (Judah’s) portion.

  • Therefore, the inheritance of the clan of Shim’on (Simeon) was within the boundaries of the inheritance of the clan of Yehudah.

  • so part of Yehudah’s land was given to Shim’on. (CEV)

So the Simeonites received an inheritance within Yehudah’s portion: This restates information from verse 9a. The repetition emphasizes that the clan of Shim’on did not receive their own separate land. This repetition may not be natural in some languages. A way to avoid this repetition is suggested below.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So the inheritance of the clan of Shim’on was within the boundaries of the inheritance of the clan of Yehudah

Therefore the clan of Shim’on received their share of land inside the land that belonged to the clan of Yehudah

General Comment on verse 19:9

In some languages it may be more natural to combine the information in this verse so that there is less repetition. For example:

Shim’on (Simeon)'s tribal land was actually inside Yehudah (Judah)'s territory. Yehudah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Yehudah's land was given to Shim’on. (CEV)

title: Joshua 19:10
content:
Section 19:10–16: The clan of Zevulun (Zebulun) received their land

19:10a

The third lot came up for the clans of the tribe of Zevulun:

  • ¶ The third lot belonged to the tribe of Zevulun, by its clans. (NET)

  • ¶ Yehoshua (Joshua) threw the lot a third time and the clan of Zevulun received land, according to its family groups.

The third lot came up for the clans of the tribe of Zevulun: This is similar to 19:1a–b.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The third lot belonged to the tribe of Zevulun, by its clans (NET)

Yehoshua threw the lot a third time and the clans of Zevulun (Zebulun) received land, according to its family groups

19:10b

The border of their inheritance stretched as far as Sarid.

  • Their land reached as far as the town of Sarid in the southeast.

  • Their southern border began at the town of Sarid in the east.

The border of their inheritance stretched as far as Sarid: The land that the clan of Zevulun received was in northern Palestine.

Sarid: Sarid is a town that was southeast of the town of Nazaret (Nazareth) in northern Palestine. This town was in the southeastern most part of Zevulun’s land.Woudstra p. 283.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Their land reached as far as the town of Sarid in the southeast

Their southern border began at the town of Sarid in the east

title: Joshua 19:11
content:
Section 19:10–16: The clan of Zevulun (Zebulun) received their land

19:11a

It went up westward to Maralah,

  • The border went west to the town of Maralah.

  • From there the boundary went west to the town of Maralah,

It went up westward to Maralah: The clause went up westward to Maralah indicates that the boundary line continued westward from Sarid town. The southern boundary line of Zevulun’s land followed the course of the Kishon River.Aharoni p. 257. The Kishon River flows from east to northwest through the Valley of Yizre’el (Jezreel) and enters the Mediterranean Sea at the port of Haifa.

Maralah: It is not certain where this town was located.

There is an interpretation issue with the term Maralah. Bible scholars divide the Hebrew words in two different ways.

  1. The name of the town is Maralah. (BSB, NRSV, NIV, NASB, NJPS, NET, NLT, GW, REB, NJB, CEV, KJV)

  2. The name of the town is Maralah (Mareal). The Hebrew word “Maralah” should be separated into “Maralah” and “-ah.” The last syllable -ah is a Hebrew directional. (RSV, ESV, NABRE, GNT)

It is recommended that you follow option (1). Most English versions and most Bible atlasesRasmussen p.244; Aharoni p, 257. refer to the name of this town as Maralah.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border went west to the town of Maralah

From there the boundary ran on to the town of Maralah

19:11b

reached Dabeshet (Dabbesheth),

  • Then it went on to the town of Dabeshet.

  • and continued to the town of Dabeshet.

reached Dabeshet: The clause reached Dabeshet indicates that the southern border continued to the town of Dabeshet.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

then it went on to the town of Dabeshet

and continued to the town of Dabeshet

19:11c

and met the brook east of Yakeneam (Jokneam).

  • The border then went on to the stream near the town of Jokne-am.

  • Then it went on to the river valley near the town of Jokne-am.

met the brook east of Yakeneam: The phrase the brook east of Yakeneam refers to a streambed that flowed with water in certain seasons. It was near the town of Yakeneam.

east: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as east is more literally “on the face of.” There are two ways to interpret this word.

  1. It means “near” or “opposite.” For example:

    the ravine near Yakeneam (NIV) (NIV, NET, NASB, GW, NJPS, NJB, NABRE, CEV, KJV)

  2. It means “east.” For example:

    the stream east of Yakeneam (Jokneam) (GNT) (BSB, GNT, RSV, ESV, REB, NLT)

It is recommended that you follow interpretation (1). We do not know for certain where the brook was in relation to Yakeneam town. It is best to translate it using a word that means “near” or “close to.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border then went on to the streambed near the town of Jokne-am

It reached the wadi near the town of Jokne-am

title: Joshua 19:12
content:
Section 19:10–16: The clan of Zevulun (Zebulun) received their land

19:12a

From Sarid it turned eastward

  • From the other side of the town of Sarid the border went east toward the sunrise

  • Beginning again at Sarid town the border went east

From Sarid it turned eastward: The description of the border returns to the starting point at the town of Sarid. The southern border is described as it went northeast along the foothills near Nazaret (Nazareth).Aharoni p. 257.

it turned eastward: Although the Hebrew phrase is literally “eastward toward the sunrise,” in some languages it may be redundant to include both the term eastward and the phrase “toward the sunrise.” One of these terms may be left as implicit information. For example:

From Sarid it turned eastward to the territory of Kisloth Tavor (Tabor) (NET)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From the other side of the town of Sarid it turned east toward the sunrise

Beginning again at Sarid town the border went toward the sunrise

19:12b

along the border of Kislot-Tavor (Chisloth-tabor)

  • up to the border of Kislot-Tavor town.

  • to the boundary of the town of Kislot-Tavor.

along the border of Kislot-Tavor: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as border also has the meaning of “territory.” Some English versions translate this term as “territory.” It is recommended that you translate this term as “boundary” or border.

Kislot-Tavor: The term Kislot-Tavor refers to a town. It was southeast of the town of Nazaret (Nazareth).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

up to the border of Kislot-Tavor

and reached the boundary of the town of Kislot-Tavor

19:12c

and went on to Davrat (Daberath) and up to Yafia (Japhia).

  • From there it went to Davrat town and then uphill to Yafia town.

  • The boundary line continued to the town of Davrat and up to the town of Yafia.

and went on to Davrat and up to Yafia: The town of Davrat is northeast of Kislot-Tavor (Chisloth-tabor). The town of Yafia is southeast of the town of Nazaret (Nazareth).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From there the border went on to Davrat town and then on to Yafia town

Then the boundary line continued to the town of Davrat and up to the town of Yafia

title: Joshua 19:13
content:
Section 19:10–16: The clan of Zevulun (Zebulun) received their land

19:13a

From there it crossed eastward to Gat-Hahefer (Gath-hepher)

  • From there the border went east toward the sunrise to the town of Gat-Hahefer,

  • It then continued east to the town of Gat-Hahefer.

From there it crossed eastward to Gat-Hahefer: This verse describes the eastern border. The town of Gat-Hahefer was north of the towns of Davrat (Daberath) and Yafia (Japhia).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From there the eastern border went toward the sunrise to the town of Gat-Hahefer

It then continued on the east side to the town of Gat-Hahefer

19:13b

and to Et-Katsin (Eth-kazin); it extended to Rimon (Rimmon) and curved around toward Ne’ah (Neah).

  • and on to the towns of Et-Katsin and Rimon, turning toward Ne’ah.

  • It continued on to Et-Katsin town and Rimon town, and curved toward Ne’ah town.

and to Et-Katsin: The location of the town of Et-Katsin is unknown.

it extended to Rimon: Rimon was a town six miles northeast of Nazaret (Nazareth).

and curved around toward Ne’ah: The exact location of the town of Ne’ah is unknown. It was on the northern border of Zevulun’s (Zebulun’s) land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It went on to the towns of Et-Katsin and Rimon, turning towards Ne’ah

Then the border continued to Et-Katsin (Eth-kazin) town and Rimon (Rimmon), and curved towards Ne’ah (Neah)

title: Joshua 19:14
content:
Section 19:10–16: The clan of Zevulun (Zebulun) received their land

19:14a

Then the border circled around the north side of Ne’ah (Neah) to Hanaton (Hannathon)

  • Then the border turned north of the town of Hanaton.

  • On the north the border turned toward Hanaton. (GNT)

Then the border circled around the north side of Ne’ah to Hanaton: This verse describes the northern boundary. The border ran to the north of the town of Hanaton. Hanaton was on the northwestern boundary of Zevulun’s land.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

On the north the border turned toward Hanaton (GNT)

The border turned north of the town of Hanaton

19:14b

and ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el.

  • Zevulun’s (Zebulun’s) boundary line ended at the valley of Iphtah-el.

  • The border ended at Iphtah-el Valley on the west.

and ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el: The Valley of Iphtah-el was on the western boundary of Zevulun. This boundary touched Asher’s land. This valley is also mentioned in verse 19:27.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Zevulun’s boundary line ended at the valley of Iphtah-el

The border ended at Iphtah-el valley on the west

title: Joshua 19:15
content:
Section 19:10–16: The clan of Zevulun (Zebulun) received their land

19:15a

It also included Katat (Kattath), Nahalal, Shimron, Yid’alah (Idalah), and Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem).

  • The clan of Zevulun received the towns of Katat, Nahalal, Shimron, Yid’alah and Beyt-Lehem.

  • Zevulun’s land included the towns of Katat, Nahalal, Shimron, Yid’alah and Beyt-Lehem.

It also included Katat, Nahalal, Shimron, Yid’alah, and Beyt-Lehem: It is not certain where the towns of Katat, Nahalal, and Yid’alah were. The town of Shimron was west of Nazaret (Nazareth). The town of Beyt-Lehem which is mentioned here was northwest of Nazaret. It is not the same town as the town of Beyt-Lehem which was in the land of Yehudah (Judah).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The clans of Zevulun received the towns of Katat, Nahalal, Shimron, Yid’alah and Beyt-Lehem

Zevulun’s (Zebulun’s) land included the towns of Katat, Nahalal, Shimron, Yid’alah and Beyt-Lehem

19:15b

There were twelve cities, along with their villages.

  • In all they had twelve towns with their surrounding villages.

  • Altogether there were twelve towns with the villages that were near them.

There were twelve cities, along with their villages: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Altogether there were twelve towns with the villages that surrounded them

These were included in their twelve towns and the villages that were near them

General Comment on verse 19:15

It may be more natural in some languages to reverse the order of the parts of this verse. For example:

Zevulun (Zebulun) had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Katta, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem) (CEV)

title: Joshua 19:16
content:
Section 19:10–16: The clan of Zevulun (Zebulun) received their land

19:16a

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Zevulun,

  • This was the land that the clan of Zevulun received as their inheritance, according to their families.

  • The clan of Zevulun received that land as their permanent possession. Each family received some land.

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Zevulun: This is similar to verse 19:8c.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This was the land that the clan of Zevulun received as their inheritance, according to its families

The clan of Zevulun (Zebulun) received this land as their permanent possession. Each family received some land

19:16b

including these cities and their villages.

  • They received these towns with the villages that were around them.

  • They received those towns with the villages that were near them.

including these cities and their villages: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and they received those towns with the villages that were around them

They received these towns with the villages nearby them

title: Joshua 19:17
content:
Section 19:17–23: The clan of Yisakar (Issachar) received their land

19:17

The fourth lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Yisakar:

  • ¶ The fourth lot belonged to the tribe of Yisakar, by its clans. (NET)

  • ¶ Yehoshua (Joshua) threw the lot a fourth time and the clan of Yisakar received land. Each family of the clan of Yisakar received land.

The fourth lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Yisakar: The first part of the verse is similar to verse 19:1a.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The fourth lot belonged to the tribe of Yisakar (NET)

Yehoshua threw the lot the fourth time and the clan of Yisakar (Issachar) received land

the clans of the tribe of Yisakar: This part is similar to verse 19:1b.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

by its clans (NET)

The clan of Yisakar received land according to their families

Each family of the clan of Yisakar received some land

title: Joshua 19:18
content:
Section 19:17–23: The clan of Yisakar (Issachar) received their land

19:18

Their territory included Yizre’el (Jezreel), Kesulot (Chesulloth), Shunem,

  • Their land included the cities of Yizre’el, Kesulot, Shunem, (T4T)

  • They received the towns of Yizre’el and Kesulot and Shunem

Their territory included Yizre’el, Kesulot, Shunem: The terms Yizre’el, Kesulot, Shunem refer to towns. These towns were in the plain of Yizre’el.Woudstra p, 285.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Their land included the cities of Yizre’el, Kesulot, Shunem (T4T)

They received Yizre’el and Kesulot and Shunem

title: Joshua 19:19
content:
Section 19:17–23: The clan of Yisakar (Issachar) received their land

19:19

Hafarayim (Hapharaim), Shi’on (Shion), Anaharat (Anaharath),

  • and Haphara-im town and Shi’on town and Anaharat town

Hafarayim, Shi’on, Anaharat: The location of these three towns is not certain.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

and Hafarayim town and Shi’on town and Anaharat town

title: Joshua 19:20
content:
Section 19:17–23: The clan of Yisakar (Issachar) received their land

19:20

Rabit (Rabbith), Kishyon (Kishion), Evets (Ebez),

  • and Rabit town and Kishyon town and Evets town

Rabit, Kishyon, Evets: The exact location of these towns is not certain.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

Rabit town and Kishyon town and Evets town

title: Joshua 19:21
content:
Section 19:17–23: The clan of Yisakar (Issachar) received their land

19:21

Remet (Remeth), Eyn-Ganim (En-gannim), Eyn-Hadah (En-haddah), and Beyt-Patsets (Beth-pazzez).

  • and Remet town and Eyn-Ganim town and Eyn-Hadah town and Beyt-Patsets town.

Remet, Eyn-Ganim, Eyn-Hadah, and Beyt-Patsets: The town of Eyn-Ganim was west of Beyt-Shean (Beth-shean) in the southern part of the plain of Yizre’el (Jezreel).Woudstra p. 287. The location of the other towns in this verse is not known.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

and Remet town and Eyn-Ganim town and Eyn-Hadah town and Beyt-Patsets town

title: Joshua 19:22
content:
Section 19:17–23: The clan of Yisakar (Issachar) received their land

19:22a

The border reached Tavor (Tabor), Shahatsimah (Shahazumah), and Beyt-Shemesh (Beth-shemesh),

  • Their boundary line went up to the towns of Tavor and Shahatsimah and Beyt-Shemesh.

  • The border was close to Tavor town, Shahatsimah town and Beyt-Shemesh town.

The border reached Tavor: 1 Chronicles 6:77 mentions a town of Tavor. It is listed as a town that belonged to the clan of Zevulun (Zebulun). It was probably near Mount Tavor, which is in the northeastern part of the plain of Yizre’el (Jezreel).Boling and Wright p. 450. The verb reached indicates that the town of Tavor was beyond the northern boundary of Yisakar’s land. The clan of Yisakar’s land was southeast of Zevulun’s land.

Shahatsimah: the location of the town of Shahatsimah in not known.

and Beyt-Shemesh: This is not the same town as was mentioned in verse 15:10. The location of the town of Beyt-Shemesh in Yisakar’s land is uncertain.Boling and Wright p. 450.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Their boundary line went up northward to the towns of Tavor and the towns of Shahatsimah and Beyt-Shemesh

The border of Yisakar’s (Issachar’s) land was close to Tavor (Tabor), Shahatsimah (Shahazumah) and Beyt-Shemesh (Beth-shemesh)

19:22b

and ended at the Yarden (Jordan). There were sixteen cities, along with their villages.

  • The boundary line ended at the Yarden River. In all, Yisakar received sixteen towns and the villages that surrounded them.

  • The border went on to the east as far as the Yarden River. Yisakar’s land included sixteen towns and the villages that were near them.

and ended at the Yarden. There were sixteen cities, along with their villages: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The boundary line of Yisakar’s land ended at the Yarden River. In all Yisakar received sixteen towns and the villages that surrounded them

The border went on to the east as far as the Yarden River. Yisakar’s (Issachar’s) land included sixteen towns and the villages that were near them

title: Joshua 19:23
content:
Section 19:17–23: The clan of Yisakar (Issachar) received their land

19:23a

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Yisakar,

  • This was the land that the clan of Yisakar received as their inheritance, according to its families.

  • The clan of Yisakar got this land as their permanent possession. Each family received some land.

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Yisakar: This part of the verse is similar to verse 19:16a.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

This was the land that the clan of Yisakar received as their inheritance, according to its families

The clan of Yisakar (Issachar) received this land as their permanent possession. Each family received some land

19:23b

including these cities and their villages.

  • They received these towns with the villages that were around them.

  • They received those towns with the villages that were near them.

including these cities and their villages: This part of the verse is the same as verse 19:16b.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and they received these towns with the villages that were around them

They received these towns with the villages nearby them

title: Joshua 19:24
content:
Section 19:24–31: The clan of Asher received their land

19:24

The fifth lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Asher:

  • ¶ The fifth lot belonged to the tribe of Asher, by its clans. (NET)

  • ¶ Yehoshua (Joshua) threw the lot a fifth time. Each family of the clan of Asher received land.

The fifth lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Asher: This verse is similar to 19:1. It is recommended that you translate it in the same way as you did that verse.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The fifth lot belonged to the tribe of Asher, by its clans (NET)

Yehoshua threw the lot the fifth time. Each of family of the clan of Asher received land

title: Joshua 19:25
content:
Section 19:24–31: The clan of Asher received their land

19:25

Their territory included Helkat (Helkath), Hali, Beten, Akshaf (Achshaph),

  • Their land included the towns of Helkat, Hali, Beten, Akshaf,

  • Their area had Helkat town and Hali town and Beten town and Akshaf town

Their territory included Helkat, Hali, Beten, Akshaf: The clan of Asher received land in the northwest area of Yisrael (Israel). These towns were in the southwest part of Asher’s land.Rasmussen p. 99. The town of Akshaf was mentioned in chapter 11:1. It was at the south edge of the plain of Ako (Acco), near the foot of Mount Karmel (Carmel).Coleson p. 149.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Their land included the towns of Helkat, Hali, Beten, Akshaf

Their area included Helkat and Hali and Beten and Akshaf

title: Joshua 19:26
content:
Section 19:24–31: The clan of Asher received their land

19:26a

Alamelek (Allammelech), Am’ad (Amad), and Mish’al (Mishal).

  • and the towns of Alamelek, Am’ad, and Mish’al.

  • and Alamelek town and Am’ad town and Mish’al town.

Alamelek, Am’ad, and Mish’al: The location of these towns is not certain.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Alamelek town and Am’ad town and Mish’al town

and the towns of Alamelek, Am’ad, and Mish’al

19:26b

On the west the border touched Karmel (Carmel) and Shihor-Livnat (Shihor-libnath),

  • The border began in the southwest at Mount Karmel and Shihor-Livnat.

  • Their western border started from the south at Karmel Mountain and Shihor-Livnat.

On the west the border touched Karmel: The clause On the west the border touched Karmel indicates that the clan of Asher’s land extended to the Mount Karmel Range in the southwest. The Mount Karmel range extends to the Mediterranean Sea south of the land that the clan of Asher received. The western border of Asher’s land ran along the Mediterranean Sea. However, the text does not describe all the western border. Here it mentions the southern point of the western border. In the next verse it describes the border as it ran southeast to the land that belonged to the clan of Zevulun (Zebulun).

and Shihor-Livnat: The location of Shihor-Livnat is unknown. It is not certain whether this name refers to a wadi or a town.Rasmussen p. 251. If the grammar of your language demands a label then it is recommended that you call it a town.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

In the south west the border extended to Mount Karmel and Shihor-Livnat town

The western border started in the south at Karmel Mountain and Shihor-Livnat (T4T)

title: Joshua 19:27
content:
Section 19:24–31: The clan of Asher received their land

19:27a

then turned eastward toward Beyt-Dagon (Beth-dagon),

  • From there it extended southeast to Beyt-Dagon town. (T4T)

  • Then the border went eastward to Beyt-Dagon town.

then turned eastward: This part of the verse describes the southeastern border of Asher’s land.

toward Beyt-Dagon: The location of the town of Beyt-Dagon is unknown.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From there it extended southeast to Beyt-Dagon town (T4T)

From there the border turned eastward to Beyt-Dagon town

19:27b

touched Zevulun (Zebulun) and the Valley of Iphtah-el,

  • It touched the land that belonged to the clan of Zevulun, in the Valley of Iphtahel.

  • The border went on up to Zevulun’s land and the Valley of Iphtahel.

touched Zevulun: The clause touched Zevulun indicates that Asher’s land reached to the clan of Zevulun’s land in the southeast.

and the Valley of Iphtah-el: The Valley of Iphtah-el was mentioned in 19:14b. Its exact location is not known but it formed part of the boundary between the land of Asher’s clan and Zevulun’s clan.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and extended to the land of the clan of Zevulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el

It went up to the border of Zevulun’s land and the Valley of Iphtah-el

19:27c

and went north to Beyt-Ha’emek (Beth-emek) and Neiel,

  • The eastern border went northward to the towns of Beyt-Ha’emek and Neiel

  • Then it went north to the towns of Beyt-Ha’emek and Neiel.

and went north to Beyt-Ha’emek and Neiel: This verse describes the eastern border. These towns were in the north of Asher’s land, along the eastern border.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border continued northward to the towns of Beyt-Ha’emek and Neiel

Then it went north to the towns of Beyt-Ha’emek and Neiel

19:27d

passing Kavul (Cabul) on the left.

  • and on northward to the town of Kavul.

  • It continued on to Kavul in the north.

passing Kavul on the left: The town of Kavul was in the plain of Ako (Acco).Rasmussen p. 230.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and went on northward to the town of Kavul

It continued to Kavul in the north

title: Joshua 19:28
content:
Section 19:24–31: The clan of Asher received their land

19:28

It went on to Evron (Ebron), Rehov (Rehob), Hamon (Hammon), and Kanah, as far as Greater Tsidon (Sidon).

  • Their land included the towns of Evron, Rehov, Hamon and Kanah. The border reached as far north as the great town of Tsidon.

  • The clan of Asher also received the towns of Evron and Rehov and Hamon and Kanah. Their land extended in the north to the important town of Tsidon.

It went on to Evron, Rehov, Hamon, and Kanah, as far as Greater Tsidon: The term Evron is spelled “Avdon (Abdon)” in some Hebrew manuscripts and also in Joshua 21:30 and 1 Chronicles 6:59. For this reason some English versions translate this term as “Avdon” here. It is recommended that you follow the major language version in your area when deciding which spelling to follow here.

Greater Tsidon: The towns listed here were further north than those listed in the previous verse.Woudstra p. 289. The town of Greater Tsidon was an important Phoenician town which was on the Mediterranean Sea. The town of Tsidon marked the northern limit of the land assigned to the clan of Asher.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Their land included the towns of Evron, Rehov, Hamon and Kanah. The border reached as far north as the great town of Tsidon.

The clan of Asher also received the towns of Evron and Rehov and Hamon and Kanah. Their land extended in the north to the important town of Tsidon.

title: Joshua 19:29
content:
Section 19:24–31: The clan of Asher received their land

19:29a

The border then turned back toward Ramah as far as the fortified city of Tsor (Tyre),

  • Then the border turned southward toward Ramah town and continued to the walled town of Tsor.

  • The boundary turned south to Ramah town and went as far as Tsor, a town with high walls.

The border then turned back toward Ramah: The clause The border then turned back toward Ramah indicates that the border turned in another direction, south toward the town of Ramah. The location of this town is not certain. It was somewhere between Tsidon (Sidon) and Tsor.

as far as the fortified city of Tsor: The phrase the fortified city of Tsor indicates a town with strong walls to protect it from enemies. The town of Tsor was on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, south of Tsidon.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border turned southward towards Ramah town and continued to the walled town of Tsor

The boundary turned back south to Ramah town and went as far as Tsor, a town with high walls

19:29b

turned toward Hosah, and came out at the Sea in the region of Akziv (Achzib),

  • Then the border turned to Hosah town and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. It included the towns of Mahalav (Mahalab) and Akziv.

  • The boundary turned west to the town of Hosah and went on to the Mediterranean Sea, to Mahalav town and Akziv town,

turned toward Hosah: The location of the town of Hosah is not known.

and came out at the Sea: After reaching the town of Hosah, the border went west and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

in the region of Akziv: There is an interpretation issue with these two Hebrew words as they are not easy to understand. There are four ways to understand them.

  1. It is two towns called “Mahalav” and Akziv. This is based on the Septuagint and also the parallel passage in Judges 1:31. (RSV, ESV, GW, REB, NJPS, NJB, NABRE, NLT, GNT)

  2. It is two towns called “Hebel” and Akziv. (NET)

  3. The words mean “near Akziv (Achzib).” For example:

    in the region of Akziv (NIV) (BSB, NIV, NASB)

  4. The words mean “from the coast to Akziv.” For example:

    from the coast to Akziv (KJV) (KJV)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) and translate it as “Mahalav (Mahalab), Akziv” the names of two towns. This is supported by many English versions, and by Bible commentaries.Woudstra p. 290.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the border turned west to Hosah town and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. Their land included the towns of Mahalav and Akziv.

The boundary turned to the town of Hosah and went on to the Mediterranean Sea, to Mahalav and Akziv (Achzib).

title: Joshua 19:30
content:
Section 19:24–31: The clan of Asher received their land

19:30

Umah (Ummah), Afek (Aphek), and Rehov (Rehob). There were twenty-two cities, along with their villages.

  • They also received Umah town, Afek town and Rehov town. Their total number of towns was twenty-two, and there were villages that surrounded them.

  • to Umah town, to Afek town and to Rehov town. The total number of towns and nearby villages was twenty-two.

Umah, Afek, and Rehov. There were twenty-two cities, along with their villages: The towns of Umah, Afek, and Rehov were in the plain of Ako (Acco).

There were twenty-two cities, along with their villages: The list of towns given for the clan of Asher totals twenty-four towns. Some Bible scholars suggest that Mahalav (Mahalab) and Akziv (Achzib) is a parenthesis and should not be counted in the total. Others scholars suggest that Tsor (Tyre) and Tsidon (Sidon) should not be included in the list.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also received Umah, Afek, and Rehov. Their total number of towns was twenty-two, including the villages that were near them

to Umah, Afek, and Rehov. The total number of towns and nearby villages was twenty-two

title: Joshua 19:31
content:
Section 19:24–31: The clan of Asher received their land

19:31a

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Asher,

  • This was the land that the clan of Asher received as their inheritance, according to its families.

  • The clan of Asher got this land as their permanent possession. Each family received some land.

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Asher: This is like verse 23a, except that it refers to the clan of Asher instead of Yisakar (Issachar). It is recommended that you translate it in a similar way.

19:31b

including these cities and their villages.

  • They received these towns with the villages that were around them.

  • They received those towns with the villages that were near them.

including these cities and their villages: This part of the verse is like verse 23b. It is recommended that you translate this part of the verse in the same way as you did verse 23b.

title: Joshua 19:32
content:
Section 19:32–39: The clan of Naftali (Naphtali) received their land

19:32

The sixth lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Naftali:

  • ¶ The sixth lot belonged to the tribe of Naftali. (NET) The clan of Naftali received land according to their families.

  • ¶ Yehoshua (Joshua) threw the lot a sixth time and the clan of Naftali received land. Each family of the clan of Naftali received some land.

The sixth lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Naftali: This verse is similar to verse 19:17. It is recommended that you translate it in a similar way.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

The sixth lot belonged to the tribe of Naftali (NET)

Yehoshua threw the lot a sixth time and the clan of Naftali (Naphtali) received land

the clans of the tribe of Naftali: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The clan of Naftali received land according to their family groups

Each of the clans of Naftali received some land

title: Joshua 19:33
content:
Section 19:32–39: The clan of Naftali (Naphtali) received their land

19:33a

Their border started at Helef (Heleph) and the great tree of Tsa’ananim (Zaanannim),

  • Their border began in the southwest at Helef town, near the oak tree at Za-anannim town.

  • The southern border of Naftali’s land began at the town of Helef near the large tree in Za-anannim town.

Their border started at Helef: The town of Helef was at the southwest corner of the land that belonged to the clan of Naftali.Rasmussen p. 238.

and the great tree of Tsa’ananim: The phrase the great tree of Tsa’ananim is mentioned in Judges 4:11.

Tsa’ananim: Judges 4:11 says that Tsa’ananim was near Kedesh. Its exact location is not certain.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Their border began in the south at Helef town, near the tall tree at Tsa’ananim

The southern border of Naftali’s (Naphtali’s) land began at the town of Helef (Heleph) near the large tree in Tsa’ananim (Zaanannim)

19:33b

passing Adami-Nekev (Adami-nekeb) and Yavne’el (Jabneel) as far as Lakum (Lakkum) and ending at the Yarden (Jordan).

  • The border continued east to Adami-Nekev town and Yavne’el town and on to Lakum town. The border ended at the Yarden River.

  • The border passed Adami-Nekev town and Yavne’el town and went on eastward to Lakum town. The Yarden River was the east end of the southern border.

passing Adami-Nekev and Yavne’el as far as Lakum and ending at the Yarden: The towns of Adami-Nekev and Yavne’el were southwest of the Sea of Galil (Galilee).

Lakum: The town of Lakum was near the southern end of the Sea of Galil.

and ending at the Yarden: The south border is described from west to east. The eastern end of the south border was the Yarden River.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The border continued eastward to Adaminekeb, and Yavne’el and on to Lakum. The border ended at the Yarden River

The border passed Adaminekeb and Yavne’el (Jabneel) and went on eastward to Lakum (Lakkum). The Yarden (Jordan) River was the east end of their southern border

title: Joshua 19:34
content:
Section 19:32–39: The clan of Naftali (Naphtali) received their land

19:34a

Then the border turned westward to Aznot-Tavor (Aznoth-tabor)

  • The western boundary extended through Aznot-Tavor town,

  • To the west the border turned to Aznot-Tavor town,

Then the border turned westward to Aznot-Tavor: This verse describes the west border of Naftali’s land. The town of Aznot-Tavor was at the foot of Mount Tavor (Tabor).Aharoni p.259.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The western boundary extended through Aznot-Tavor (T4T)

To the west the border turned to Aznot-Tavor

19:34b

and ran from there to Hukok (Hukkok), touching Zevulun (Zebulun) on the south side,

  • as far as Hukok city. It extended to the borders of the tribe of Zevulun at the south, (T4T)

  • and went northward to Hukok town. The border touched the clan of Zevulun’s land in the south.

and ran from there to Hukok: The town of Hukok was somewhere on the western border of Naftali’s (Naphtali’s) land.

touching Zevulun on the south side: The phrase touching Zevulun on the south side indicates that the southwestern border of Naftali’s land was next to the clan of Zevulun’s land. The southeast border of Naftali’s land was next to the land of the clan of Yisakar (Issachar).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

as far as Hukok. It extended to the borders of the tribe of Zevulun at the south (T4T)

and went on northward to the town of Hukok. The border touched the clan of Zevulun’s land in the south

19:34c

Asher on the west, and Yehudah (Judah) at the Yarden (Jordan) on the east.

  • to the border of the tribe of Asher on the west, and the Yarden River at the east. (T4T)

  • The border touched the clan of Asher’s land on the west side and the Yarden River on the east side.

Asher on the west: The phrase Asher on the west indicates that the west border touched the border of the clan of Asher’s land.

and Yehudah at the Yarden on the east: There is a textual issue in this part of the verse. The word Yehudah is in the Hebrew text but is not in the Septuagint.

  1. The text is Yarden on the east. (NIV, NET, NJB, NABRE, REB, NLT, GNT)

  2. The text includes the word Yehudah. For example:

    and Asher on the west, and Yehudah on the east at the Yarden (RSV) (BSB, RSV, NASB, ESV, GW, NJPS, KJV)

It is recommended that you follow option (1) along with many English versions. The border of the clan of Yehudah (Judah) did not touch the border of the clan of Naftali (Naphtali).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

to the border of the tribe of Asher on the west, and the Yarden (Jordan) River at the east (T4T)

The border touched the clan of Asher’s land on the west and the Yarden River on the east

title: Joshua 19:35
content:
Section 19:32–39: The clan of Naftali (Naphtali) received their land

19:35

The fortified cities were Tsidim (Ziddim), Tser (Zer), Hamat (Hammath), Rakat (Rakkath), Kineret (Chinnereth),

  • Within their land were several cities with strong walls around them. They were Tsidim, Tser, Hamat, Rakat, Kineret. (T4T)

  • The towns with strong walls that belonged to the clan of Naftali were Tsidim and Tser and Hamat and Rakat and Kineret

The fortified cities: The term fortified cities indicates towns that have strong walls around them. This term occurred in verse 19:29.

were Tsidim, Tser, Hamat, Rakat, Kineret: The location of the towns of Tsidim and Tser is not known. The towns of Hamat and Rakat were on the western shore of the Sea of Galil (Galilee). The town of Kineret was northwest of the Sea of Galil. It is called Gennaisaret (Gennesaret) in the New Testament.Rasmussen p. 242.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Within their land were several cities with strong walls around them. They were Tsidim, Tser, Hamat, Rakat, Kineret (T4T)

The towns with strong walls that belonged to the clan of Naftali (Naphtali) were Tsidim, and Tser and Hamat and Rakat and Kineret

title: Joshua 19:36
content:
Section 19:32–39: The clan of Naftali (Naphtali) received their land

19:36

Adamah, Ramah, Hatsor (Hazor),

  • There were also the towns of Adamah, Ramah, Hatsor,

  • and Adamah town and Ramah town and Hatsor town

Adamah, Ramah, Hatsor: The town of Adamah was probably to the west of the sea of Galil (Galilee). The towns of Ramah and Hatsor were in upper Galil. The town of Hatsor was mentioned in 11:1.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

There were also Adamah town, Ramah town, Hatsor town

Adamah town and Ramah town and Hatsor town

title: Joshua 19:37
content:
Section 19:32–39: The clan of Naftali (Naphtali) received their land

19:37

Kedesh, Edre’i (Edrei), Eyn-Hatsor (En-hazor),

  • Kedesh town, Edre-i town, Eyn-Hatsor town,

  • and Kedesh town and Edre-i town and Eyn-Hatsor town.

Kedesh, Edre’i, Eyn-Hatsor: The town of Kedesh was northwest of the Sea of Galil (Galilee), in the hill country of Galil. The locations of the towns of Edre’i and Eyn-Hatsor are not known.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Kedesh town, Edre’i town, Eyn-Hatsor town

and Kedesh town and Edre’i town and Eyn-Hatsor town

title: Joshua 19:38
content:
Section 19:32–39: The clan of Naftali (Naphtali) received their land

19:38a

Iron, Migdal-El (Migdal-el), Horem, Beyt-Anat (Beth-anath), and Beyt-Shemesh (Beth-shemesh).

  • and Yir’on (Yiron) and Migdal-El and Horem and Beyt-Anat and Beyt-Shemesh.

  • They also had Yir’on town, Migdal-El town, Horem town, Beyt-Anat town, and Beyt-Shemesh town.

Iron: This town was in upper Galil (Galilee). It was on the modern border between Levanon (Lebanon) and Yisrael (Israel).Woudstra p. 292.

Migdal-El, Horem, Beyt-Anat: The location of these three towns is not known.

and Beyt-Shemesh: This town is not the same as the town mentioned on Yehudah’s (Judah’s) northern border in 15:10. This town and the others listed above were most likely in Upper Galil.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also had Iron town, Migdal-El town, Horem town, Beyt-Anat town, and Beyt-Shemesh town

and Iron and Migdal-El (Migdal-el) and Horem and Beyt-Anat (Beth-anath) and Beyt-Shemesh (Beth-shemesh)

19:38b

There were nineteen cities, along with their villages.

  • In all there were nineteen towns with the villages that surrounded them.

  • There were nineteen towns with their nearby villages.

There were nineteen cities, along with their villages: The total number of towns listed in verses 35–38 is sixteen towns. The names of the three other towns that are counted here are not known.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

In all there was a total of nineteen towns with the villages that surrounded them

There were nineteen towns with their nearby villages

title: Joshua 19:39
content:
Section 19:32–39: The clan of Naftali (Naphtali) received their land

19:39a

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Naftali,

  • This was the land that the clan of Naftali received as their inheritance, according to its families.

  • The clan of Naftali got this land as their permanent possession. Each family received some land.

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Naftali: This verse is like verse 19:23a, except that here it refers to the clan of Naftali. It is recommended that you translate this verse in a similar way to that verse.

19:39b

including these cities and their villages.

  • They received these towns with the villages that were around them.

  • They received those towns with the villages that were near them.

including these cities and their villages: This part of the verse is the same as verse 19:23b. It recommended that you translate this part of the verse as you did that verse.

title: Joshua 19:40
content:
Section 19:40–48: The clan of Dan received their land

19:40

The seventh lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Dan:

  • ¶ The seventh lot belonged to the tribe of Dan, by its clans. (NET)

  • ¶ Yehoshua (Joshua) threw the lot a seventh time. Each family of the clan of Dan received land.

The seventh lot came out for the clans of the tribe of Dan: This verse is similar to verse 19:24. It is recommended that you translate it in a similar way to that verse.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The seventh lot belonged to the tribe of Dan, by its clans (NET)

Yehoshua threw the lot a seventh time. Each of the families of the clan of Dan received land

title: Joshua 19:41
content:
Section 19:40–48: The clan of Dan received their land

19:41

The territory of their inheritance included Tsor’ah (Zorah), Eshtaol, Ir-Shemesh (Ir-shemesh),

  • Their land included the towns of Tsor’ah, Eshta-ol, Ir-Shemesh,

  • The land that they received had the following towns: Tsor’ah town and Eshta-ol town and Ir-Shemesh town,

The territory of their inheritance included Tsor’ah, Eshtaol, Ir-Shemesh: The clan of Dan received the towns of Tsor’ah and Eshtaol from the clan of Yehudah (Judah). These towns are mentioned in chapter 15:33. The town of Ir-Shemesh was also called Beyt-Shemesh (Beth-shemesh) and was listed as a border town of the clan of Yehudah in chapter 15:10.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Their land included the towns of Tsor’ah, Eshtaol, Ir-Shemesh

The land that they received had the following towns: Tsor’ah and Eshtaol and Ir-Shemesh

title: Joshua 19:42
content:
Section 19:40–48: The clan of Dan received their land

19:42

Sha’alvim (Shaalabbin), Ayalon (Aijalon), Yitlah (Ithlah),

  • Sha-alabbin, Ayalon, Yitlah,

  • and Sha-alabbin town and Ayalon town and Yitlah town,

Sha’alvim: The town of Sha’alvim was on the north side of the valley of Ayalon, north of Beyt-Shemesh (Beth-shemesh).Boling and Wright p. 464.

Ayalon: The town of Ayalon was northwest of Yerushalem (Jerusalem) in the valley of Ayalon.

Yitlah: The location of the town of Yitlah is uncertain.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

Sha’alvim town and Ayalon town and Yitlah town

title: Joshua 19:43
content:
Section 19:40–48: The clan of Dan received their land

19:43

Eylon (Elon), Timnah, Ekron,

  • Eylon, Timnah, Ekron,

  • and Eylon town and Timnah town and Ekron town,

Eylon: The town of Eylon was probably on the south side of the Ayalon (Aijalon) valley.Boling and Wright p. 465.

Timnah, Ekron: The towns of Timnah and Ekron were on the boundary between the lands of the clan of Dan and the clan of Yehudah (Judah).

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

Eylon town and Timnah town and Ekron town

title: Joshua 19:44
content:
Section 19:40–48: The clan of Dan received their land

19:44

Elteke (Eltekeh), Gibton (Gibbethon), Ba’alat (Baalath),

  • Elteke, Gibton, Ba’alat,

  • and Elteke town and Gibton town and Ba’alat city

Elteke, Gibton: These two towns were southeast of the town of Yafo (Joppa).

Ba’alat: The location of this town is uncertain.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

Elteke town and Gibton town and Ba’alat town

title: Joshua 19:45
content:
Section 19:40–48: The clan of Dan received their land

19:45

Yehud (Jehud), Beney-Berak (Bene-berak), Gat-Rimon (Gath-rimmon),

  • Yehud, Beney-Berak, Gat-Rimon,

  • and Yehud town and Beney-Berak town and Gat-Rimon town,

Yehud, Beney-Berak, Gat-Rimon: The town of Yehud was east of the town of Yafo (Joppa) in the coastal plain. The town of Beney-Berak was southeast of Yafo. The town of Gat-Rimon was northeast of Yafo.19:45 Dallaire, p. 1011.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

Yehud town and Beney-Berak town and Gat-Rimon town

title: Joshua 19:46
content:
Section 19:40–48: The clan of Dan received their land

19:46

Mey-Hayarkon (Me-jarkon), and Rakon (Rakkon), including the territory across from Yafo (Joppa).

  • Mey-Hayarkon and Rakon, with the area facing Yafo town.

  • Mey-Hayarkon town and Rakon town. Their territory also included land that was near Yafo town.

Mey-Hayarkon: The Hebrew words that the BSB translates as Mey-Hayarkon can also be translated as “the waters of Yarkon.” The Yarkon River flows into the Mediterranean Sea north of Yafo town. Some scholars consider Mey-Hayarkon to refer to the river, not to a town. However, it is recommended that you translate it as a town name as in the majority of English versions.

and Rakon: The location of this place is uncertain.

including the territory across from Yafo: The phrase territory across from Yafo indicates that the clan of Dan received land that was near the town of Yafo as part of their tribal inheritance.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Mey-Hayarkon and Rakon, with the area facing Yafo (NIV)

Mey-Hayarkon (Me-jarkon) and Rakon (Rakkon). Their territory also included land that was near Yafo (Joppa) town

title: Joshua 19:47
content:
Section 19:40–48: The clan of Dan received their land

19:47a

(Later, when the territory of the Danim (Danites) was lost to them,

  • But the people of the Dan clan failed to conquer the land that was assigned to them.

  • But the clan of Dan did not succeed in taking all their land.

Later, when the territory of the Danim was lost to them: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as the territory of the Danim was lost to them is more literally “the territory of the people of Dan went out from them.” The clan of Dan was not able to take over all the land that was given to them by lot. Judges 1:34 says that the Amorim (Amorites) fought against the people of Dan and so they could not take over the land that was on the plain near the sea.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But the people of the Dan clan failed to conquer all the land they had received

But the tribe of Dan had trouble taking possession of their land (NLT)

19:47b

they went up and fought against Leshem,

  • So they went northeast to Leshem town and attacked it.

  • Because of that, they went up to Leshem town and fought against it.

they went up and fought against Leshem: The town of Leshem was an ancient town that was at the source of the Yarden (Jordan) River. It was northeast of the other towns given to the people of Dan. In Judges 18:7 this town is called Layish (Laish). The clause they went up and fought against Leshem indicates that the members of the Dan clan attacked the town of Leshem.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So the clan of Dan went northeast to the town of Leshem and attacked it

Because of that, the people of the Dan clan went up to Leshem and fought against it

19:47c

captured it, and put it to the sword.

  • They conquered the town and killed the people with the sword.

  • They defeated and killed the people in the town.

captured it, and put it to the sword: The clause that the BSB translates as captured it, and put it to the sword indicates that the Dan people defeated and killed the people of Leshem town.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They conquered the town and killed the people with the sword

They defeated and killed the people in the town

19:47d

So they took possession of Leshem, settled there,

  • Then they moved into the town and lived in it.

  • Then they began to live in Leshem,

So they took possession of Lethem, settled there: The clause they took possession of Lethem, settled there indicates that the people of the Dan clan moved into the town and began to live there.

19:47e

and renamed it after their father Dan.)

  • They gave the town a new name, Dan, according to the name of their ancestor.

  • and changed the name of the city to Dan, the man from whom their tribe descended. (T4T)

and renamed it: The phrase renamed it indicates that the Dan clan renamed the town of Leshem. They named it “Dan.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then they moved into that town and lived in it. They gave the town a new name, Dan.

Then they began to live in Leshem, and changed the name of the town to Dan (T4T)

after their father Dan: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

according to the name of their ancestor Dan

the man from whom their tribe descended (T4T)

title: Joshua 19:48
content:
Section 19:40–48: The clan of Dan received their land

19:48a

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Dan,

  • This was the land that the clan of Dan received as their inheritance, according to its families.

  • The clan of Dan received this land as their permanent possession. Each family received some land.

This was the inheritance of the clans of the tribe of Dan: This part of the verse is similar to 19:16a. It is recommended that you translate in a similar way here.

19:48b

including these cities and their villages.

  • They received those towns with the villages that were around them.

  • They received these towns with the villages nearby them.

including these cities and their villages: This part of the verse is the same as in 19:16b. It is recommended that you translate it the same way as you did there.

title: Joshua 19:49
content:
Section 19:49–51: Yehoshua (Joshua) received land

19:49a

When they had finished distributing the land into its territories,

  • ¶ When they had finished distributing the land

  • ¶ After the people of Yisrael (Israel) had finished dividing the land among the clans,

When they had finished distributing the land into its territories: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

When they had finished distributing the land

After the people of Yisrael had finished dividing the land among all the clans

19:49b

the Israelis (Israelites) gave Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun an inheritance among them,

  • they also gave some land to Yehoshua son of Nun as his inheritance.

  • they also gave a portion of land to Yehoshua the son of Nun.

the Israelis gave Yehoshua son of Nun an inheritance among them: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the people of Yisrael (Israel) also gave some land to Yehoshua son of Nun as his inheritance

they also gave a portion of land to Yehoshua son of Nun

title: Joshua 19:50
content:
Section 19:49–51: Yehoshua (Joshua) received land

19:50a

as Yahweh had commanded. They gave him the city of Timnat-Serah (Timnath-serah) in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim), as he requested.

  • Yahweh had said that Yehoshua could have whatever town he wanted. So they gave him the town that he chose, which was Timnat-Serah in the mountain country that belonged to the clan of Efrayim.

  • Yahweh had commanded them to give Yehoshua whatever town he chose. He chose the town of Timnat-Serah, in the hill country that belonged to the Efrayim tribe.

as Yahweh had commanded. They gave him the city of Timnat-Serah in the hill country of Efrayim, as he requested: The command that is referred to here is not recorded anywhere in the book of Yehoshua.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yahweh had said that Yehoshua could have whatever town he wanted. So, they gave him the town that he chose

Yahweh had commanded them to give Yehoshua (Joshua) whatever town he chose

the city of Timnat-Serah (Timnath-serah) in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim): The town of Timnat-Serah was southwest of the town of Shekem (Shechem).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

which was Timnat-Serah in the mountain country that belonged to the clan of Efrayim

He chose the town of Timnat-Serah which was in the hill country that belonged to the clan of Efrayim

19:50b

He rebuilt the city and settled in it.

  • Yehoshua rebuilt that town and lived in it.

  • After Yehoshua (Joshua) conquered it he rebuilt the town and lived there.

He rebuilt the city and settled in it: Archaeology shows that the town of Timnat-Serah (Timnath-serah) was abandoned at the time that Yehoshua settled there. That is why he rebuilt the town.19:50 Coleson, p. 152.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yehoshua rebuilt that town and lived in it

He built up the town and lived there

title: Joshua 19:51
content:
Section 19:49–51: Yehoshua (Joshua) received land

19:51a

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Yehoshua son of Nun,

  • This is the land that Eleazar the priest and Yehoshua son of Nun assigned as an inheritance

  • Eleazar the priest and Yehoshua son of Nun divided this land

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Yehoshua son of Nun: This verse is similar to chapter 14:1. You should compare how you translated similar words and phrases in that verse and translate in a similar way here.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

These are the pieces of land that Eleazar the priest and Yehoshua the son of Nun assigned as an inheritance

Eleazar the priest and Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun divided out all of this land

19:51b

and the heads of the families distributed by lot to the tribes of Yisrael (Israel)

  • together with the leaders of the families of the clans of Yisrael.

  • along with the leaders of the clans of Yisrael.

and the heads of the families: This phrase refers to the leaders of the Israeli (Israelite) clans. In Numbers 34:16–29 Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) to appoint one leader from each of the clans of Yisrael to help assign the land along with Yehoshua and Eleazar the priest. Mosheh decided who each of these leaders would be.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and the leaders of the families of the Israeli tribes (GNT)

along with the leaders of all the tribes of Yisrael (NCV)

distributed by lot: The phrase distributed by lot indicates that Eleazar and the tribal leaders cast a lot to decide which pieces of land each clan should receive.

19:51c

at Shiloh before Yahweh

  • They used lots to divide the land in the presence of Yahweh at Shiloh,

  • They threw the lot to assign this land in the presence of Yahweh at Shiloh.

at Shiloh: The term Shiloh was first used in chapter 18:1a. Shiloh was twelve miles south of Shekem (Shechem) and was in the tribal territory of Efrayim (Ephraim). It was in the center of the Israeli (Israelite) land west of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

before Yahweh: The phrase that the BSB translates as before Yahweh indicates the presence of Yahweh. Yahweh was present in the tent of meeting, which is mentioned in the next part of the verse.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They used the lot to divide the land in the presence of Yahweh at Shiloh

They threw the lot to assign these inheritance lands in the presence of Yahweh at Shiloh

19:51d

at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

  • at the entrance of the Meeting Tent.

  • They stood at the door of the Holy Tent.

at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting: The term Tent of Meeting is first used in chapter 18:1b. You should translate the term here in the same way as you did in Chapter 18.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

at the entrance of the Meeting Tent

They stood at the door of the Holy Tent

19:51e

So they finished dividing up the land.

  • And so they finished giving out the land.

  • In that way they completed dividing up the land. (T4T)

So they finished dividing up the land: This sentence is the conclusion to chapters 14–19.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They finished giving out all the land to the clans

In that way they completed dividing up the land (T4T)

title: Joshua 20:1
content:
Section: 20:1–9 Yehoshua (Joshua) set apart towns of refuge so that people could run to them and be safe

20:1

Then Yahweh said to Yehoshua,

  • ¶ After this, Yahweh said to Yehoshua:

  • ¶ Yahweh told Yehoshua

Then Yahweh said to Yehoshua: The Hebrew sentence that the BSB translates as Then Yahweh said to Yehoshua is more literally “and Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua, saying…” This sentence begins a new topic. Use a word or a phrase that marks a new topic in your language.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

After this, Yahweh said to Yehoshua

Then Yahweh spoke to Yehoshua (Joshua). He said

Yahweh told Yehoshua

title: Joshua 20:2
content:
Section: 20:1–9 Yehoshua (Joshua) set apart towns of refuge so that people could run to them and be safe

20:2a

“Tell the Israelis (Israelites)

  • “Tell the Israelis,

  • to say to the people of Yisrael (Israel)

Tell the Israelis: The phrase Tell the Israelis is a command from Yahweh to Yehoshua. This command is in direct speech. In some languages it may be more natural to report this command in indirect speech. For example,

Then Yahweh told Yehoshua to say to the people of Yisrael

20:2b

to designate the cities of refuge,

  • ‘Choose the towns to which people can run and be safe

  • “Designate towns where people can escape and be safe.

to designate the cities of refuge: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as designate is more literally “give to yourselves” or “set for yourselves.” In this context it indicates that the Israelis (Israelites) must choose some towns.

cities of refuge: A refuge is a place where someone can be safe. The cities of refuge were towns to which people who were in trouble could run and be safe.

Here are some other ways to translate this phrase:

safe towns

towns to be safe

towns of safety

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Choose for yourselves towns where people can run and be safe

that they should select safe towns

20:2c

as I instructed you through Mosheh (Moses),

  • that I had Mosheh speak to you about.

  • In the past I told Mosheh to speak to you about these towns.

as I instructed you through Mosheh: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as as I instructed you through Mosheh is more literally “which I spoke to you by the hand of Mosheh.” Yahweh had spoken to Mosheh and told him to tell the Israelis (Israelites) to select these towns after they had crossed the Yarden (Jordan) River. This is reported in Numbers 35:9–29 and in Deuteronomy 19:1–13.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

I commanded Mosheh to speak to you about them.

long ago I told Mosheh to speak to you about these towns

title: Joshua 20:3
content:
Section: 20:1–9 Yehoshua (Joshua) set apart towns of refuge so that people could run to them and be safe

20:3a

so that anyone who kills another unintentionally or accidentally may flee there.

  • Any person who kills someone by mistake, who did not intend to do that, can escape there.

  • These will be towns of safety. Perhaps somebody will kill a person by accident. He did not plan to kill them. He can go to one of these towns and be safe there.

so that: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as so that indicates purpose. This verse explains the purpose of the towns of refuge.

Here are some other ways to translate this word:

that

in order that

anyone who kills another unintentionally or accidentally: The Hebrew phrase which the BSB translates as unintentionally can also be translated “by mistake” or “in error.” It means that the killer did not plan to kill the person.

accidentally: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as accidentally is more literally “without knowledge.” This is a synonym of the word “unintentionally.” It means that the killer did not plan to kill the person. Some languages may not have two words for this concept. In that case you may need to use only one word. For example:

If any of you accidentally kills someone (GNT)

may flee there: The verb flee can also be translated “escape” or “run away.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

These will be towns of safety. Anybody who kills a person by accident, without planning to kill him, may go there.
