Any person who kills someone by accident and did not intend to kill him may run away to that place so that he can be safe.

Anyone who kills a person by mistake, who did not intend to kill, can escape there.

20:3b

These will be your refuge from the avenger of blood.

  • These cities will be a safe place for any of you from the relative of the dead person who wants to kill you.

  • They will be a place of safety from any relative who wants to get revenge for the death.

These will be your refuge from the avenger of blood: A refuge is a place where somebody can be safe.

avenger of blood: An avenger of blood is a person who wants to get revenge. Usually this was a relative of the person who died. He would seek to get revenge for his relative by finding the killer and killing him.Woudstra, p, 299.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

These towns will be a safe place to protect you from the relative of the dead man who wants to kill you

They will be a place of refuge from any relative who can avenge the death. (GW)

they will be places of refuge from relatives seeking revenge for the person who was killed (NLT)

title: Joshua 20:4
content:
Section: 20:1–9 Yehoshua (Joshua) set apart towns of refuge so that people could run to them and be safe

20:4a

When someone flees to one of these cities,

  • Any person who has killed someone should run to one of these towns.

  • Anyone who kills someone accidentally can escape to one of these towns.

When someone flees to one of these cities: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The person who has killed someone should run to one of these towns.

Anyone who kills someone accidentally can escape to one of these towns.

20:4b

stands at the entrance of the city gate,

  • He should stand at the entrance to the town gate where the elders judge cases.

  • He will stand at the entrance to the town where the leaders make decisions.

stands at the entrance of the city gate: The entrance of the city gate was an open area near the town entrance. The town leaders gathered there to decide about cases between people that needed to be settled. It may be helpful to include this implicit information when translating this part of the verse. For example,

He should stand at the entrance to the town gate where the elders judge cases.

There he will stand at the entrance to the town where the leaders hold court.

20:4c

and states his case before its elders,

  • He should state his case to the elders of that town.

  • He must tell the town leaders what he did.

and states his case before its elders: The clause that the BSB translates as states his case before its elders is more literally in Hebrew “he will speak his words in the ears of the elders of that town.” The term elders refers to the leaders of the town.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

He should state his case to the elders of that town.

He must tell the town leaders what he did.

20:4d

they are to bring him into the city and give him a place

  • Then the elders will allow him to come into the town and give him a place to live,

  • The town leaders will bring him into the town and give him a place to stay,

they are to bring him into the city: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as they are to bring him into the city is more literally “and they will gather him to the town, to themselves.” It means that the elders will allow him to enter the town.

and give him a place: The clause give him a place indicates that the elders would find a place where he could live.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the elders will allow him to come into the town, and they will give him a place to live there.

The town leaders will bring him into the town and give him a place to stay.

20:4e

to live among them.

  • and he will stay there with them.

  • and he will live among them.

to live among them: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and he will stay in that town with them

and he will live among them

title: Joshua 20:5
content:
Section: 20:1–9 Yehoshua (Joshua) set apart towns of refuge so that people could run to them and be safe

20:5a

Now if the avenger of blood pursues him,

  • If the relative who wants to kill him chases after him

  • And if the relative who wants to get revenge follows after the killer,

Now: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as Now can also be translated “but” to indicate contrast. It is not a time word. Choose the word that is most natural in this context. Some English versions do not translate this word.

if: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as if can also be translated as “when.” Choose the conjunction that is most natural in your language.

the avenger of blood: The term avenger of blood was first mentioned in 20:3b. You should translate it the same way here.

pursues him: The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as pursues can also be translated as “chases” or “follows.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But if the relative of the person who died chases after the person who killed him

But if the relative of the dead person follows after the killer

20:5b

they must not surrender the manslayer into his hand,

  • the elders must not hand him over to that relative.

  • the town leaders must not give him up.

they: The pronoun they refers to the elders of the town.

must not surrender the manslayer into his hand: The clause must not surrender the manslayer into his hand means that the elders must protect the manslayer (the person who killed someone) from the person who is trying to get revenge. They must not hand him over to that person.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the elders must not hand over the killer to the person trying to avenge the dead man

the town leaders must not give up the person who killed to the relative

20:5c

because that man killed his neighbor accidentally

  • They must protect him because he has killed his neighbor without intending it.

  • They must do this because he killed the other person without planning to do it,

because that man killed his neighbor accidentally: The clause that man killed his neighbor accidentally indicates the reason why the person who killed should be protected from his pursuer.

his neighbor: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as neighbor can also be translated “friend,” “companion” or “other one.” In this context it refers to a fellow human being.

accidentally: The word accidentally means that the killer did not plan to kill. This is the same Hebrew word as in verse 20:3.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They must protect him because he has killed his fellow man without intending it.

They must do this because he killed the other person without planning to do it.

20:5d

without prior malice.

  • He had not hated him in the past.

  • and not because he was angry with him in past times.

without prior malice: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as without prior malice is more literally “and not hating him from yesterday three days ago.” The phrase “from yesterday three days ago” is a Hebrew idiom that means “in the past.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

He had not hated him in the past.

and not because he was angry with him in the past

General Comment on verse 20:5

In the Hebrew and in the BSB verse 5 is a long sentence. It may be more natural in some languages to divide it into more than one sentence. For example:

But if the one who is chasing him follows him to that town, the leaders of the city must not hand over the killer. It was an accident. He did not hate him beforehand or kill him on purpose. (NCV)

title: Joshua 20:6
content:
Section: 20:1–9 Yehoshua (Joshua) set apart towns of refuge so that people could run to them and be safe

20:6a

He is to stay in that city until he stands trial before the assembly

  • But he must live in that town until his trial before the assembly.

  • He should stay in that town until the congregation has judged his case.

The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB leaves untranslated but some English versions translate as “and” can also be translated as “but.” Choose the connecting words that are most natural in your language. Some English versions do not translation this conjunction.

He is to stay in that city: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as He is to stay in that city can also be translated “he must live in that town.”

until he stands trial before the assembly: The clause until he stands trial before the assembly indicates that there will be a trial for the person who was accused of killing someone. The trial will be conducted by the assembly which was composed of all the adult males of the town.Boling and Wright p. 474.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But he must live in that town until his trial before the assembly.

He should stay in that town until the people gather and judge his case.

20:6b

and until the death of the high priest serving at that time.

  • If he is innocent he must continue to stay there until the high priest of that time has died.

  • If they decide that he is not guilty, he should live there until the chief priest in those days has died.

until the death of the high priest serving at that time: There is implicit information in this part of the verse. First the congregation must decide that the person who killed someone was innocent of murder. If they decided he was innocent he could stay in the town of refuge until the high priest died. It may be clearer in some languages to include this implicit information.

high priest: The high priest was the leader of all the priests. The priests offered sacrifices on behalf of the people, but the high priest offered certain sacrifices that no other priest could offer. He represented the Israeli (Israelite) people to God.

If you have translated the gospels you should translate high priest the same way you did there. See for example John 18:19.

Here are some other ways to translate the term high priest:

the chief/leader of all the priests

the main/principal priest

the highest/leading priest

at that time: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as at that time is more literally “in those days.” The high priest continued his duties until he died or could not carry them out. Then a new person was chosen.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

If he is innocent he must continue to stay there until the high priest of that time has died.

After he is judged to be not guilty he should live there until the chief priest in those days has died.

20:6c

Then the manslayer may return to his own home in the city from which he fled.”

  • Then he may return to his own house in the town that he escaped from.’ ”

  • After that, the person may go back to his home in the town that he ran away from.”

Then the manslayer may return to his own home: This clause indicates that the person who killed unintentionally could then return to his home.

in the city from which he fled: the city from which he fled is the same town as is indicated in the phrase “to his own home.” In some languages it may be clearer to combine these two phrases. For example:

to his own home in the town from which he fled

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the person who killed unintentionally may return to his own house in his town.

After that the person may go back to his home in the town that he ran away from.

title: Joshua 20:7
content:
Section: 20:1–9 Yehoshua (Joshua) set apart towns of refuge so that people could run to them and be safe

20:7a

So they set apart Kedesh in Galil (Galilee) in the hill country of Naftali (Naphtali),

  • ¶ So the people of Yisrael (Israel) chose Kedesh town. It was in the region of Galil in the mountain country that belonged to the Naftali people.

  • ¶ Then the Israelis (Israelites) designated Kedesh town in Galil in the hill country where the Naftali clan lived.

So: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as So indicates the next event in the storyline. Choose a connecting word that is natural in your language.

they set apart: The pronoun they refers to the people of Yisrael. The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as set apart means to choose something for a special use.

Here are some other ways to translate this verb:

the people chose

they designated

Kedesh in Galil (Galilee) in the hill country of Naftali (Naphtali): The town of Kedesh was northwest of the Sea of Galil. It is mentioned in 19:37.

Galil: Galil is the name of a region in northern Yisrael (Israel). It was a part of the land assigned to the clan of Naftali.

the hill country of Naftali: The term hill country of Naftali refers to the mountainous region that belonged to the clan of Naftali.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The people of Yisrael chose the town of Kedesh. It was in the region of Galil in the hill country that belonged to Naftali.

Then they designated the town of Kedesh in Galil in the mountainous region that belonged to the clan of Naftali.

20:7b

Shekem (Shechem) in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim),

  • They also chose the town of Shekem. It was in the mountain country that belonged to the Efrayim people.

  • They also designated the town of Shekem. It was in the hill country where the Efrayim clan lived.

Shekem in the hill country of Efrayim: The town of Shekem was on the boundary of the clan of Efrayim and Menasheh (Manasseh). This town was in the middle region of the country of Yisrael (Israel). It is mentioned in 17:7.

hill country of Efrayim: The term hill country of Efrayim refers to the mountainous region that belonged to the clan of Efrayim.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also chose the town of Shekem. It was in the mountain country of the clan of Efrayim.

They also designated the town of Shekem. It was in the hill country of the clan of Efrayim.

20:7c

and Kiryat-Arba (Kiriath-arba) (that is, Hevron (Hebron)) in the hill country of Yehudah (Judah).

  • They also chose the town of Kiryat-Arba in the mountain country that belonged to the Yehudah people. The name of that town is now Hevron.

  • They also designated the town of Kiryat-Arba which was in the hill country where the Yehudah clan lived. That town is now called Hevron.

and Kiryat-Arba (that is, Hevron): The town of Kiryat-Arba was mentioned in 15:13 and 14:15. Its name was later changed to Hevron. It was in the southern area of Yisrael (Israel), fifteen miles southwest of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).Rasmussen p. 238.

in the hill country of Yehudah: The term hill country of Yehudah refers to the mountainous region which belonged to the clan of Yehudah.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also chose the town of Kiryat-Arba in the mountain country of the clan of Yehudah. The name of that town is now Hevron.

They also appointed the town of Kiryat-Arba which was in the hill country of the clan of Yehudah. That town is now called Hevron.

title: Joshua 20:8
content:
Section: 20:1–9 Yehoshua (Joshua) set apart towns of refuge so that people could run to them and be safe

20:8a

And beyond the Yarden (Jordan), east of Yeriho (Jericho),

  • On the east side of the Yarden River, across from Yeriho town,

  • Across the Yarden River, to the east of the town of Yeriho,

And: The Hebrew conjunction And makes this sentence a continuous sentence with the previous verse. In some languages it may be more natural to begin a new sentence here.

beyond the Yarden: The phrase beyond the Yarden indicates that the next towns were on the east side of the Yarden River.

east of Yeriho: The phrase east of Yeriho indicates that the next towns in the list were east of the town of Yeriho.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

On the east side of the Yarden River, across from Yeriho town

Across the Yarden (Jordan) River, to the east of the town of Yeriho (Jericho)

20:8b

they designated Betser (Bezer) on the wilderness plateau from the tribe of Re’uven (Reuben),

  • they chose the town of Betser. It was in the wilderness on the plain that belonged to the Re’uven people.

  • the Israelis (Israelites) designated Betser town. It was on the wilderness plateau where the Re’uven clan lived.

they designated Betser: The town of Betser was in the south part of Yisrael (Israel) and east of the Yarden River.

on the wilderness plateau: The phrase the wilderness plateau indicates that Betser was in a flat, uncultivated area. The term plateau refers to a flat plain.

from the tribe of Re’uven: The phrase from the tribe of Re’uven indicates that the town of Betser was in the area that belonged to the clan of Re’uven. The land that Mosheh (Moses) assigned to the clan of Re’uven is described in 13:15–23.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the people of Yisrael chose the town of Betser. It was in the wilderness on the plain that belonged to the clan of Re’uven.

They also designated Betser (Bezer) town, on the wilderness plateau that belonged to the Re’uven (Reuben) clan.

20:8c

Ramot (Ramoth) in Gilead from the tribe of Gad,

  • They also chose Ramot town in the region of Gilead that belonged to the Gad people,

  • They also designated Ramot town in Gilead region where the Gad clan lived,

Ramot in Gilead: The town of Ramot was north of the modern town of Amman in Yarden (Jordan).Rasmussen p. 249. It was in the middle region of Yisrael’s (Israel’s) land on the east side of the Yarden River. Gilead was a mountainous area north of the Dead Sea and east of the Yarden River. This area is now in the country of Yarden.

from the tribe of Gad: The phrase the tribe of Gad indicates that Mosheh (Moses) had assigned the town of Ramot in the region of Gilead to the clans of Gad.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also chose Ramot town in the region of Gilead, which belonged to the people of Gad.

They also designated the town of Ramot in Gilead region, where the Gad clans lived.

20:8d

and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh).

  • and Golan town in the Bashan region that belonged to the Menasheh people.

  • and Golan town in the Bashan region, where the Menasheh clan lived.

and Golan in Bashan: The town of Golan was in the region of Bashan, which is a high plateau in the northeast part of the land of Yisrael (Israel).

from the tribe of Menasheh: The phrase the tribe of Menasheh indicates that the town of Golan was in land that belonged to the clans of Menasheh.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and Golan town in the Bashan region, which belonged to the people of Menasheh

They also designated the town of Golan in the Bashan region, where the Menasheh people lived.

title: Joshua 20:9
content:
Section: 20:1–9 Yehoshua (Joshua) set apart towns of refuge so that people could run to them and be safe

20:9a

These are the cities appointed for all the Israelis (Israelites)

  • These towns of refuge were chosen for all the people of Yisrael (Israel)

  • These were the towns that they designated to benefit all the Yisrael people

These are the cities appointed for all the Israelis: The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as appointed can also be translated “designated” or “agreed upon.” It may be clearer to add the implicit information “towns of refuge.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

These towns of refuge were appointed for all the people of Yisrael.

These were the safe towns that were selected for all the Yisrael people.

20:9b

and foreigners among them,

  • and also for the foreigners who lived among them.

  • and anyone who lived with them.

and foreigners among them: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as foreigners among them is more literally “the sojourner who sojourns among them.” This refers to foreigners who were living among the people of Yisrael (Israel).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

a foreigner who lived among them

anyone who lived among them

20:9c

so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there

  • Anyone who killed a person accidentally could run to them.

  • Anyone who killed a person by mistake could escape there.

so that: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as so that indicates purpose. It can also be translated as “that.”

anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there: This clause is like the clause in verse 20:3a.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

so that anyone who killed a person accidentally could run there

anybody who killed a person by mistake could escape there

20:9d

and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood

  • Then the relative who wanted to kill him would not be able to kill him

  • He would not die from the relative who wanted to get revenge

and not die: The phrase and not die indicates the purpose of running away to the town of safety. The person who had killed by accident could escape to a safe town and be safe from the person who wanted to kill him.

by the hand of the avenger of blood: The phrase by the hand of the avenger of blood indicates how the one who had killed might die. The avenger of blood would find him and kill him. You should translate the term avenger of blood the same way as you did in verse 20:3b.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the relative of the person who died would not kill him

so that he will be safe from the relative who wanted to kill him

20:9e

prior to standing trial before the assembly.

  • until his trial before the assembly of the people.

  • before the congregation had judged his case.

prior to standing trial before the assembly: This part of the verse is like verse 20:6a. It may be clearer to include here the information “for judgment” which is found in that verse in Hebrew.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse.

until he comes before the assembly and they judge him

until the congregation has judged his case

title: Joshua 21:1
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:1a

Now the family heads of the Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun,

  • ¶ Then the family heads of the clan of Levi came to Eleazar the priest, and Yehoshua the son of Nun,

  • ¶ After that, the leaders of the families of the Levi people had a request. They went to Eleazar the priest, and to Yehoshua whose father was Nun,

Now: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as Now indicates the next event in the story. This begins a new section. Use a connecting word that is appropriate in your language to begin a new section.

the family heads of the Levites: The phrase the family heads of the Levites refers to the leaders of the Levite clan. This same phrase was used in 14:1. Translate it in a similar way to how you did in that verse.

approached Eleazar the priest, Yehoshua son of Nun: Yahweh had told Mosheh (Moses) in Numbers 34:16–17 that Eleazar and Yehoshua would assign land to all the clans of Yisrael (Israel). Yahweh had also told Mosheh in Numbers 35:1–8 to give the Levites towns to live in and pasturelands around the towns.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then the heads of the families in the clan of Levi came to Eleazar the priest and to Yehoshua the son of Nun

After that, the leaders of the families of the Levi clan went to Eleazar the priest and to Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun

21:1b

and the heads of the other tribes of Yisrael

  • and to the heads of the clans of Yisrael

  • and to the leaders of the other clans of Yisrael.

and the heads of the other tribes of Yisrael (Israel): In verse 21:1a the leaders were those of the Levi clan. They approached the leaders from all the other clans of Yisrael.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and to the heads of the other Yisrael clans

and to the leaders of all the other clans of Yisrael

title: Joshua 21:2
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:2a

at Shiloh in the land of Kena’an (Canaan) and said to them,

  • at Shiloh in the land of Kena’an. They said to them,

  • They were still at Shiloh town in the land of Kena’an. They said to them,

There is a Hebrew conjunction at the beginning of this verse that is often translated as “and.” It introduces the next event in the story. The BSB leaves this conjunction untranslated.

at Shiloh in the land of Kena’an and said to them: in 18:1 the Israelis (Israelites) had set up the tent of meeting at Shiloh. Shiloh was a town twelve miles south of Shekem (Shechem) and was in the tribal territory of Efrayim (Ephraim). It was in the center of the Israeli (Israelite) land west of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

While they were still at Shiloh town in the land of Kena’an, they said

21:2b

“Yahweh commanded through Mosheh (Moses) that we be given cities in which to live,

  • “Yahweh told Mosheh that you must give us towns to live in,

  • “Yahweh said to Mosheh: ‘Command the Israelis to give the descendants of Levi towns to live in,

Yahweh commanded through Mosheh: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as Yahweh commanded through Mosheh is more literally “Yahweh commanded by the hand of Mosheh.” Yahweh had told Mosheh to give the following command to the Israelis.

that we be given cities in which to live: In Numbers 35:1 Yahweh had told Mosheh to command the Israelis (Israelites) to give the Levites towns to live in. These towns belonged to the various clans but the Levites lived in them.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Yahweh told Mosheh to command you(plur) to give us towns to live in.

Yahweh said to Mosheh, “Command the Israelis to give the Levi people towns to live in.”

21:2c

together with pasturelands for our livestock.”

  • and the pasture lands around them for our cattle to graze on.”

  • and the grasslands near them for their livestock to eat.’”

together with pasturelands for our livestock: The phrase together with pasturelands for our livestock indicates that the Levites should receive the lands around the towns where their livestock could eat grass.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and the pasturelands around them for our cattle to graze there

and the grasslands near them to provide grass for our livestock

General Comment on verses 1–2

In some languages it may be more natural to combine verses 1 and 2 and reorder them. For example:

2aWhile the Israelis (Israelites) were still at Shiloh in the land of Kena’an (Canaan), 1athe heads of the Levi clan went to Eleazar the priest, to Yehoshua (Joshua) the son of Nun, 1band to the other heads of the clans of Yisrael (Israel). They said to them, 2b“Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) to command you to give us towns to live in 2cand grasslands for our cattle.”

title: Joshua 21:3
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:3a

So by the command of Yahweh,

  • So the Yisrael (Israel) people obeyed Yahweh’s command.

  • So as Yahweh had told them to do,

So: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as So indicates the next event in the narrative. Translate this connecting word in a way that is natural in your language.

by the command of Yahweh: The Hebrew phrase that the BSB translates as by the command of Yahweh is more literally, “by the mouth of Yahweh.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Just as Yahweh had commanded

According to what Yahweh had said

21:3b

the Israelis (Israelites) gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands out of their own inheritance:

  • They gave the following towns and the grasslands around them to the clan of Levi. They gave them from the land that they had been given.

  • the people of Yisrael (Israel) gave some of the towns and pasturelands that they had received to the Levi people. This is a list of those towns.

the Israelis gave the Levites these cities and their pasturelands out of their own inheritance: The phrase their own inheritance refers to the towns and lands that the people of Yisrael received when Yehoshua (Joshua) and Eleazar the priest threw lots for them.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The Yisrael people gave these towns and the lands around them to the clan of Levi from the land that they had been given

The people of Yisrael gave to the Levi people some of the towns and pasturelands that they had received

title: Joshua 21:4
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:4a

The first lot came out for the Kohatite (Kohathite) clans.

  • ¶ The first lot was for the descendants of Kohat (Kohath).

  • ¶ The families who descended from Kohat received their towns by lot first.

The first lot came out: The clause The first lot came out is the same Hebrew expression as in 16:1 where it BSB translates it as “The allotment for.” It means that Eleazar the priest threw the lot to show which clan would receive their towns first.

for the Kohatite clans: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as clans refers to groups of families or sub-clans. This word was used in 15:1b.

Kohatite: The term Kohatite refers to the descendants of Kohat. Kohat was one of Levi’s three sons. (See Genesis 46:11.)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The first lot was for the descendants of Kohat.

The families of the descendants of Kohat received their towns first by lot.

21:4b

The Levites who were descendants of Aharon (Aaron) the priest

  • The Levi people who were descended from Aharon the priest

  • The men of the Levi clan who were descendants of Aharon the chief priest

There is a Hebrew conjunction here, which the BSB leaves untranslated, that indicates the next event in the narrative. Translate this conjunction in a way that is natural in your language.

The Levites who were descendants of Aharon the priest: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as Levites who were descendants of Aharon the priest is more literally “the sons of Aharon the priest from the Levites.” This refers to the male descendants of Aharon.

Aharon the priest: Aharon was a grandson of Kohat (Kohath), one of the three sons of Levi. Aharon was the first chief priest of Yisrael (Israel). The male descendants of Aharon had the responsibility to serve Yahweh as priests (Exodus 29).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The Levi people who were descended from Aharon the first chief priest

The male descendants of Aharon (Aaron) the priest, who was of the clan of Levi

21:4c

received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Yehudah (Judah), Shim’on (Simeon), and Benyamin (Benjamin).

  • received thirteen towns when the lot was thrown. These towns were from the descendants of Yehudah, Shim’on and Benyamin.

  • were given thirteen towns by lot. The towns they received came from the clan of Yehudah, the clan of Shim’on, and the clan of Benyamin.

received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Yehudah, Shim’on, and Benyamin: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

received thirteen towns when the lot was thrown. These towns belonged to the clans of Yehudah, Shim’on, and Benyamin.

were given thirteen towns by lot. The towns they received came from the clan of Yehudah, the clan of Shim’on, and the clan of Benyamin.

title: Joshua 21:5
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:5a

The remaining descendants of Kohat (Kohath) received ten cities by lot from the tribes of Efrayim (Ephraim),

  • The remaining people who were descended from Kohat received their towns from the families of the clan of Efrayim,

  • The other Kohat people were given towns by lot from the descendants of Efrayim,

The remaining descendants of Kohat: The phrase remaining descendants of Kohat refers to the clans of Kohat who were not descended from Aharon (Aaron).

received ten cities by lot from the tribes of Efrayim: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The other families who were descended from Kohat received their towns from the families of the clan of Efrayim

The other families of Kohat were given towns by lot from the clan of Efrayim

21:5b

Dan, and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh).

  • the clan of Dan, and from half of the clan of Menasheh. They received by lot ten towns in all.

  • and from the descendants of Dan, and from the half of the descendants of Menasheh who live west of the Yarden (Jordan) River. They received ten towns by lot.

Dan, and the half-tribe of Menasheh: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

from the clan of Dan, and from half of the clan of Menasheh. They received ten towns in all by lot.

from the clan of Dan, and from the half of the Menasheh clan that lived west of the Yarden River. They received ten towns.

General Comment on verse 21:5

In some languages it may be more natural to reorder the parts of this verse. For example:

The other families who were descendants of Kohat (Kohath) received ten towns by lot. These towns came from the clan of Efrayim (Ephraim), from the clan of Dan, and from half the clan of Menasheh (Manasseh).

title: Joshua 21:6
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:6a

The descendants of Gereshon (Gershon) received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Yisakar (Issachar),

  • The descendants of Gereshon received towns by lot from the families of the clan of Yisakar,

  • When the lot was thrown, the people who were descended from Gereshon received towns from the descendants of Yisakar,

The descendants of Gereshon: Gereshon was one of Levi’s three sons.

received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Yisakar: This clause is like the clause in verse 21:5a.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The descendants of Gereshon received towns by lot from the families of the clan of Yisakar,

When the lot was thrown, the people who were descended from Gereshon received towns from the clan of Yisakar,

21:6b

Asher, Naftali (Naphtali), and the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) in Bashan.

  • the clan of Asher, the clan of Naftali, and from the part of the clan of Menasheh who live in Bashan east of the Yarden (Jordan) River. They received thirteen towns.

  • and from the descendants of Asher, and from the descendants of Naftali, and from the half of the descendants of Menasheh who live in Bashan east of the Yarden. They received thirteen towns.

Asher, Naftali, and the half-tribe of Menasheh in Bashan: This part of the verse is like verse 21:5b. The phrase the half-tribe of Menasheh in Bashan refers to the part of the Menasheh clan that lived on the east side of the Yarden River. Bashan was an area northeast of the Sea of Galil (Galilee).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

from the clan of Asher, from the clan of Naftali, and from the part of the clan of Menasheh who live in Bashan, east of the Yarden River. They received thirteen towns.

and from the clan of Asher, and the clan of Naftali, and from the half of the clan of Menasheh who live in Bashan, east of the Yarden. They received thirteen towns.

General Comment on 21:6

It may be more natural in some languages to rearrange the parts of this verse. For example:

The descendants of Gereshon (Gershon) received thirteen towns by lot. These towns came from the families of the clan of Yisakar (Issachar), the clan of Naftali (Naphtali), and half of the clan of Menasheh (Manasseh).

title: Joshua 21:7
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:7a

And the descendants of Merari

  • The descendants of Merari by their families

  • The families that were descended from Merari

And the descendants of Merari: Merari was one of the three sons of Levi.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The descendants of Merari, by their families

The families that were descended from Merari

21:7b

received twelve cities from the tribes of Re’uven (Reuben), Gad, and Zevulun (Zebulun).

  • received twelve towns from the clans of Re’uven, Gad, and Zevulun.

  • were given twelve towns from the descendants of Re’uven, and the descendants of Gad, and the descendants of Zevulun.

received twelve cities from the tribes of Re’uven, Gad, and Zevulun: This verse is similar to 21:4c although it does not have the phrase “by lot.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

received twelve towns from the clans of Re’uven, Gad, and Zevulun

were given twelve towns in all from the clan of Re’uven, the clan of Gad, and the clan of Zevulun

title: Joshua 21:8
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:8a

So the Israelis (Israelites) allotted to the Levites these cities, together with their pasturelands,

  • ¶ The people of Yisrael (Israel) gave these towns and the grasslands around them to the clan of Levi by throwing lots,

  • ¶ The Yisrael people gave the towns listed here and the lands around them for grazing livestock to the Levi people by throwing lots.

So the Israelis allotted to the Levites these cities, together with their pasturelands: Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

the Israelis gave these towns and their grasslands to the clan of Levi by throwing lots

21:8b

as Yahweh had commanded through Mosheh (Moses).

  • just as Yahweh had commanded Mosheh to tell them to do.

  • Yahweh had told Mosheh that they must do this.

as Yahweh had commanded through Mosheh: This part of the verse is similar to verse 21:2b.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

just as Yahweh had commanded Mosheh to tell them to do

Yahweh had told Mosheh that they must do this

General Comment on 21:8

Verse 8 is a summary statement of verses 4–7. It restates the information that was first said in verse 3.

title: Joshua 21:9
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:9a

From the tribes of Yehudah (Judah) and Shim’on (Simeon),

  • ¶ From the clans of Yehudah and Shim’on,

  • ¶ From the land that belonged to the descendants of Yehudah and to the descendants of Shim’on

From the tribes of Yehudah and Shim’on: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From the clans of Yehudah and Shim’on

From the land that belonged to the clan of Yehudah, and the clan of Shim’on

21:9b

they designated these cities by name

  • the Israelis (Israelites) gave these towns which they called by name.

  • the people of Yisrael (Israel) named the following towns.

they designated these cities by name: The Hebrew sentence that the BSB translates as they designated these cities by name is more literally “they gave them these towns which they called them by name.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the Israelis gave these cites which they called by name

the Israelis named the following towns

General Comment on 21:9

It may be more natural to reorder the parts of this verse. For example,

The Israelis (Israelites) gave these towns from the clans of Yehudah (Judah) and Shim’on (Simeon) and told their names.

title: Joshua 21:10
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:10a

to the descendants of Aharon (Aaron) from the Kohatite (Kohathite) clans of the Levites,

  • They gave these towns to the descendants of Aharon, who belonged to the Kohat (Kohath) family in the clan of Levi,

  • They gave these towns to the descendants of Aharon. The descendants of Aharon were one of the families of the Kohat people, from the clan of Levi.

to the descendants of Aharon from the Kohatite clans of the Levites: The Hebrew text begins a new sentence here.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

These towns belonged to the descendants of Aharon, who were one of the families of the Kohat people, from the clan of Levi.

These towns were given to the descendants of Aharon, who belonged to the Kohat family in the clan of Levi.

21:10b

because the first lot fell to them:

  • because they received the first lot.

  • They got their land first because the first lot pointed to them.

because the first lot fell to them: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

because the first lot pointed to them

because they received the first lot

title: Joshua 21:11
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:11a

They gave them Kiryat-Arba (Kiriath-arba) (that is, Hevron (Hebron)),

  • The people of Yisrael (Israel) gave to them the town of Kiryat-Arba, which is now called Hevron.

  • The Israelis (Israelites) gave them the town of Kiryat-Arba. That town has another name, which is Hevron.

They gave them Kiryat-Arba (that is, Hevron): The town of Kiryat-Arba is mentioned in 14:15. The word “Kiryat (Kiriath)” means “town” in Hebrew. Arba was the name of one of the Anak people.

21:11b

with its surrounding pasturelands, in the hill country of Yehudah (Judah). (Arba was the father of Anak.)

  • Kiryat-Arba is in the mountain region that belonged to the clan of Yehudah. They also gave them the grasslands around it. Arba was the father of Anak.

  • They also gave them land around the town for their animals. Kiryat-Arba is in the mountain country of the descendants of Yehudah. Arba was the father of Anak.

with its surrounding pasturelands, in the hill country of Yehudah: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It was in the mountain region that belonged to the clan of Yehudah. They also gave them the grasslands around it.

They gave them lands around the town for their animals. Hevron (Hebron) was in the mountains of the clan of Yehudah.

Arba was the father of Anak: The clause that the BSB translates as Arba was the father of Anak is background information. In some languages it may be more natural to place this background information at some other point in the verse.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse

The Israelis (Israelites) gave them the town of Kiryat-Arba (Kiriath-arba), which is now called Hevron. Arba was the father of Anak.

The people of Yisrael (Israel) gave them Kiryat-Arba town. Arba was the father of Anak. That town had another name, Hevron.

General Comment on verse 21:11

In some languages it may be more natural to reorder the parts of this verse. For example:

The Israelis gave them Kiryat-Arba, together with the grasslands around it, in the hill country of Yehudah (Judah). That town was named after Arba, who was the father of Anak. It is also called Hevron.

title: Joshua 21:12
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:12

But they had given the fields and villages around the city to Kalev (Caleb) son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh) as his possession.

  • But the fields and villages that were around the town had already been given to Kalev the son of Yefuneh as his own property.

  • However, Kalev the son of Yefuneh had already received the fields and villages that surrounded the town as his own.

But: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as But indicates a contrast.

they had given the fields and villages around the city to Kalev son of Yefuneh as his possession: The Hebrew sentence places the object first to emphasize it. Use the order that is natural in your language.

the fields: The phrase the fields refers to the land around the town that was good for growing crops.

villages around the city: The phrase villages around the city refers to small settlements near the town that did not have a wall around them.

had given…to Kalev: The story of how Kalev received the town of Hevron (Hebron) was told in 14:6–15.

as his possession: The phrase as his possession can also be translated “as his property.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

But the fields and villages that were around the town had already been given to Kalev (Caleb), the son of Yefuneh (Jephunneh), as his own property.

However, Kalev the son of Yefuneh had already received the fields and villages that surrounded the town as his own.

title: Joshua 21:13
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:13a

So to the descendants of Aharon (Aaron) the priest they gave these cities, together with their pasturelands: Hevron (Hebron), a city of refuge for the manslayer,

  • The Yisrael (Israel) people gave the descendants of Aharon the priest the town of Hevron and its grazing lands. It was a town where people could run to escape when they had killed someone by accident.

  • The people of Yisrael gave Hevron town with its pasturelands to the descendants of Aharon the priest. Hevron was a town of safety for those who had killed by mistake.

So: This verse repeats information which was stated in verse 21:10–11. Some English versions translate this Hebrew conjunction as So, as “thus” or “and.” Use the connecting word that is natural in your language.

to the descendants of Aharon the priest they gave these cities, together with their pasturelands: Hevron, a city of refuge for the manslayer: In this verse Aharon is given the title of Aharon the priest, which is slightly different from verse 21:10. The Hebrew sentence puts the object of the sentence first to emphasize it. Use the sentence order that is natural in your language.

together with their pasturelands: The phrase together with their pasturelands refers to the land around Hevron where livestock could eat grass.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

So the people of Yisrael gave Hevron town with its pasturelands to the descendants of Aharon the priest. Hevron was a town of safety for those who had killed someone by mistake.

a city of refuge for the manslayer: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as manslayer is the same Hebrew word that occurred in 20:3. In that verse the BSB translated it as “anyone who kills another.” It is recommended that you translate this term the same way as you did in verse 20:3.

21:13b

Livnah (Libnah),

  • They also gave them Livnah town and the grazing lands around it,

  • They also gave them Livnah town and its grasslands,

Livnah: The town of Livnah was southwest of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).Rasmussen p.243.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also gave them Livnah and the grazing lands around it,

Livnah town and the grasslands around it,

title: Joshua 21:14
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:14

Yatir (Jattir), Eshtemoa,

  • Yatir town and the grazing lands around it, Eshtemoa town and the grazing lands around it,

  • and Yatir town with its grasslands, and Eshtemoa town with its grasslands,

Yatir: The town of Yatir was mentioned in 15:48. It was southwest of Hevron (Hebron), in the hill country of Yehudah (Judah).Rasmussen p. 240.

Eshtemoa: The town of Eshtemoa was mentioned in 15:50. It was also southwest of Hevron in the hill country of Yehudah.Rasmussen p. 2234.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

Yatir town and the grazing lands around it and Eshtemoa town with the grazing lands around it

and Yatir town with its grasslands and Eshtemoa town with its grasslands

title: Joshua 21:15
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:15

Holon, Devir (Debir),

  • Holon town and the grazing lands around it, Devir town with the grazing lands around it,

  • and Holon town with its grasslands, and Devir town with its grasslands,

Holon: The town of Holon was mentioned in 15:51. It was in the south hill country of the clan of Yehudah (Judah).

Devir: The town of Devir was mentioned in 15:15. It was southwest of Hevron (Hebron).Rasmussen p. 232.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

Holon and the grazing lands around it and Devir with the grazing lands around it.

and the town of Holon with its grasslands and the town of Devir with its grasslands

title: Joshua 21:16
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:16

Ayin (Ain), Yutah (Juttah), and Beyt-Shemesh (Beth-shemesh)—nine cities from these two tribes, together with their pasturelands.

  • Ayin town and the grazing lands around it, Yutah town and the grazing lands around it, and Beyt-Shemesh town with the grazing lands around it. Nine towns in all were given from these two clans.

  • and Ayin town with its grasslands, and Yutah town with its grasslands, and Beyt-Shemesh town with its grasslands. The descendants of Yehudah (Judah) and Shim’on (Simeon) gave nine towns to the descendants of Aharon (Aaron).

Ayin: The town of Ayin was mentioned in 15:32. It was allotted to both the clan of Yehudah and the clan of Shim’on. It was in the south part of the land that was given to these clans.

Yutah: The town of Yutah was mentioned in 15:55. It was south of Hevron (Hebron).Rasmussen p. 241.

Beyt-Shemesh: The town of Beyt-Shemesh was mentioned in chapter 15:10. It was on the north boundary of the land that belonged to the clan of Yehudah, to the west of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).Rasmussen p. 230.

nine cities from these two tribes: The phrase nine cities from these two tribes indicates that the descendants of Aharon were given a total of nine towns from the clans of Yehudah and Shim’on.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

Ayin and the grazing lands around it, Yutah and the grazing lands around it, and Beyt-Shemesh with the grazing lands around it. Nine towns in all were given from these two clans.

and the town of Ayin (Ain) with its grasslands, the town of Yutah (Juttah) with its grasslands, and the town of Beyt-Shemesh (Beth-shemesh) with its grasslands. The clans of Yehudah and Shim’on gave nine towns to the descendants of Aharon.

title: Joshua 21:17
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:17

And from the tribe of Benyamin (Benjamin) they gave them Giveon (Gibeon), Geva (Geba),

  • The clan of Benyamin gave them these towns: Giveon town and the grazing lands around it, Geva town and the grazing lands around it,

  • The following towns were given by the descendants of Benyamin: Giveon town and its grasslands, and Geva town and its grasslands,

And from the tribe of Benyamin: This indicates that the clan of Benyamin gave the Levi people towns from their land for them to live in.

they gave them Giveon: The town of Giveon was mentioned in 18:25. It was northwest of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).Rasmussen p. 236.

Geva: The town of Geva was mentioned in chapter 18:24. It was northeast of Yerushalem.Rasmussen p. 235.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

The clan of Benyamin gave these towns: Giveon and the grazing lands around it, Geva and the grazing lands around it,

The following towns were given from the clan of Benyamin (Benjamin): the town of Giveon (Gibeon) and its grasslands, the town of Geva (Geba) and its grasslands,

title: Joshua 21:18
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:18

Anatot (Anathoth), and Almon—four cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • Anatot town and the grazing lands around it, and Almon town and the grazing lands around it. These four towns were given by the clan of Benyamin (Benjamin).

  • and Anatot town and its grasslands, and Almon town and its grasslands. The descendants of Benyamin gave them these four towns.

Anatot: The town of Anatot has not been mentioned previously. It was northeast of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).Rasmussen p. 226.

and Almon: The town of Almon has not been mentioned previously. It was northeast of Anatot.Woudstra p. 309.

four cities: The phrase four cities indicates that there were four towns in all that were given to the descendants of Aharon (Aaron) from the clan of Benyamin.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

Anatot and the grazing lands around it, and Almon and the grazing lands around it. These four towns were given from the clan of Benyamin.

Anatot (Anathoth) and its grasslands, and Almon and its grasslands. The clan of Benyamin gave four towns to the descendants of Aharon.

title: Joshua 21:19
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:19

In all, thirteen cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the priests, the descendants of Aharon (Aaron).

  • A total of thirteen towns and the grazing lands around them were given to the priests, the descendants of Aharon.

  • The priests were all descendants of Aharon. They received thirteen towns in all and the grasslands that surrounded them.

In all, thirteen cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the priests, the descendants of Aharon: This verse is a concluding statement of the paragraph.

In all, thirteen cities, together with their pasturelands: The total number of towns that the descendants of Aharon received was thirteen towns and the lands around them for their livestock to graze.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

These thirteen towns and the grazing lands around them were given to the priests, the descendants of Aharon.

The priests, who were all descended from Aharon, received thirteen towns in all and the grasslands that surrounded them.

the priests, the descendants of Aharon (Aaron): In Joshua 21:13 it referred to Aharon the priest. This verse refers to the priests, who were all the descendants of Aharon.

title: Joshua 21:20
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:20a

The remaining Kohatite (Kohathite) clans of the Levites

  • ¶ The remaining Levi people who belonged to the Kohat (Kohath) families of the Levi clan

  • ¶ The descendants of Levi who belonged to the families of Kohat

The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB leaves untranslated can also be translated “and.” Many English versions leave this conjunction untranslated. Use the form that is natural in your language.

remaining Kohatite clans of the Levites: Exodus 6:16 says that Kohat had four sons. The eldest son was Amram who was the father of Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron). The three other sons had sons who became the families that are spoken of here.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The remaining Levi people who belonged to the Kohat families of the Levi clan

The Levi people who belonged to the other families of Kohat

21:20b

were allotted these cities: From the tribe of Efrayim (Ephraim)

  • received their towns by lot from the clan of Efrayim.

  • were given towns from the descendants of Efrayim, by lot.

were allotted these cities: From the tribe of Efrayim: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

received their towns by lot from the clan of Efrayim

were given towns from the clan of Efrayim by lot

title: Joshua 21:21
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:21a

they were given Shekem (Shechem) in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim)

  • The people of Yisrael (Israel) gave them the town of Shekem. Shekem and the grazing lands around it were in the mountain country of the clan of Efrayim.

  • They received Shekem town. Shekem and the grasslands around it were in the mountains of Efrayim.

they were given Shekem: The Hebrew clause that the BSB translates as they were given Shekem is more literally “they gave them Shekem.”

in the hill country of Efrayim: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

in the mountain country of the clan of Efrayim

in the mountains of Efrayim

21:21b

(a city of refuge for the manslayer),

  • It was a town where people could run to escape when they had killed someone by accident.

  • It was a town of safety for those who had killed by mistake.

a city of refuge for the manslayer: This phrase is the same Hebrew phrase as was found in verse 21:13. You should translate this phrase in the same way as you did in that verse.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It was a town where people could run to escape if they had killed someone by accident.

which was a town of safety for anyone who had killed somebody by mistake

21:21c

Gezer,

  • They also received Gezer town and the grazing lands around it,

  • They also received the town of Gezer and the grasslands around it,

Gezer: The town of Gezer was mentioned in Joshua 10:33. It was southeast of Yafo (Joppa).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also received Gezer and the grazing lands around it

They received the town of Gezer and the grasslands around it

General Comment on verse 21:21

In some languages it may be more natural to reorder the parts of this verse. For example:

They received the town of Shekem (Shechem) and the pasturelands around it, in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim). It was a town of safety where anyone who killed somebody accidentally could escape. They also received the town of Gezer and the pasturelands around it.

title: Joshua 21:22
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:22

Kivtsayim (Kibzaim), and Beyt-Horon (Beth-horon)—four cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • Kibza-im town with the grazing lands around it, and Beyt-Horon town with the grazing lands around it. They received four towns from the clan of Efrayim (Ephraim).

  • and Kibza-im town with its grasslands, and Beyt-Horon town with its grasslands. In all there were four towns.

Kivtsayim: The town of Kivtsayim has not been mentioned previously. The location of this town is uncertain.

Beyt-Horon: The town of Beyt-Horon was mentioned in Joshua 10:10–11. It was northwest of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).

four cities: The phrase four cities refers to the four towns that the Kohat (Kohath) families received from the clan of Efrayim.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Kibza-im town with the grazing lands around it, and Beyt-Horon town with the grazing lands around it. They received four towns from the clan of Efrayim.

and the town of Kibza-im with its grasslands and the town of Beyt-Horon (Beth-horon) with its grasslands. In all there were four towns.

title: Joshua 21:23
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:23

From the tribe of Dan they were given Elteke, Gibton (Gibbethon),

  • From the clan of Dan they received the town of Elteke with the grazing lands around it, the town of Gibton with the grazing lands around it,

  • They received these towns from the descendants of Dan: Elteke and its grasslands, and Gibton and its grasslands,

The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB leaves untranslated is often translated as “and.” It indicates the next event in the story. It may be more natural in some languages to begin a new sentence and to omit this conjunction.

From the tribe of Dan they were given: The phrase that the BSB translates as From the tribe of Dan can also be translated as “from the clan of Dan.”

Elteke: The town of Elteke was mentioned in 19:44. Its location is uncertain.

Gibton: The town of Gibton was also mentioned in Joshua 19:44. It was south of Yafo (Joppa) and west of Gezer.Rasmussen p. 236.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

From the clan of Dan they received the town of Elteke with the grazing lands around it, and the town of Gibton with the grazing lands around it.

They received these towns from the clan of Dan: Elteke and its grasslands, Gibton (Gibbethon) and its grasslands,

title: Joshua 21:24
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:24

Ayalon (Aijalon), and Gat-Rimon (Gath-rimmon)—four cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • Ayalon town with the grazing lands around it, and Gat-Rimon town and the grazing lands around it. The descendants of Dan gave them four towns.

  • and Ayalon town and its grasslands, and Gat-Rimon town and its grasslands. In all there were four towns.

Ayalon: The town of Ayalon was mentioned in 19:42. It was northwest of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).Rasmussen p.225.

Gat-Rimon: The town of Gat-Rimon was mentioned in 19:45. It was probably northeast of Yafo (Joppa).Rasmussen p. 235.

four cities, together with their pasturelands: The phrase four cities refers to the four towns that the Kohat (Kohath) families received from the clan of Dan.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

They also received the town of Ayalon and the grazing lands around it, and the town of Gat-Rimon and the grazing lands around it.

Ayalon (Aijalon) and its grasslands, Gat-Rimon (Gath-rimmon) and its grasslands.

title: Joshua 21:25
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:25

And from the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) they were given Ta’anak (Taanach) and Gat-Rimon (Gath-rimmon)—two cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • From the half of the clan of Menasheh who live west of the Yarden (Jordan) River they received Ta’anak town and the grazing lands around it, and Jibleam town and the grazing lands around it. The total was two towns.

  • The part of the Menasheh people who live west of the Yarden River gave them Ta’anak town and its grasslands, and Jibleam town and its grasslands. They received two towns from the Menasheh people.

And: The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB translates as And indicates the next event in the story. It may be more natural in some languages to omit this conjunction.

from the half-tribe of Menasheh: The half-tribe of Menasheh refers to the part of the clan of Menasheh that lived west of the Yarden River.

Ta’anak: The town of Ta’anak was mentioned in 12:21. It was on the border of the lands that belonged to the clans of Yisakar (Issachar) and Menasheh.Rasmussen p.252.

Gat-Rimon: There is a textual issue with the name of this town:

  1. The name of the town is Jibleam. NJB, CEV

  2. The name of the town is Gat-Rimon (Gath-rimmon). BSB, RSV, ESV, NIV, NET, NASB, GW, REB, NJPS, NABRE, GNT, NLT, KJV

It is recommended that you follow option (1). This is not the word in the Hebrew text, but it is supported by one ancient Greek manuscript and by the parallel passage in I Chronicles 6:70. This is the recommendation of most commentariesSee, for example, Butler p. 222, Boling and Wright p. 490, Dallaire p. 1019, and Hess p 311. and also of the Hebrew Old Testament Text Project (HOTTP). These commentaries think we should not translate it as “Gat-Rimon,” because the town of Gat-Rimon was assigned to the clan of Dan in verse 21:24.

two cities: The phrase two cities refers to the towns that the half-clan of Menasheh (Manasseh) gave to the Kohat (Kohath) families.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From the half of the clan of Menasheh that lived west of the Yarden (Jordan) River they received Ta’anak (Taanach) and the grazing lands around it, and Jibleam and the grazing lands around it. The total was two towns.

The part of the Menasheh clan that lived west of the Yarden River gave them Ta’anak town and its grasslands and Jibleam town and its grasslands. They received two towns from that clan.

title: Joshua 21:26
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:26

In all, ten cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the rest of the Kohatite (Kohathite) clans.

  • The remaining families of Kohat (Kohath) received ten towns in all with the grazing lands that were around them.

  • The other families that were descended from Kohat were given ten towns and their grasslands.

In all, ten cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the rest of the Kohatite clans: This verse is like verse 21:19. It is a concluding statement for the paragraph about the towns that the other Kohat families received.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

The rest of the families of Kohat received ten towns in all with the grazing lands that were around them.

The other families that were descended from Kohat were given ten towns and their grasslands.

title: Joshua 21:27
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:27a

This is what the Levite clans of the Gershonim (Gershonites) were given:

  • ¶ The families that descended from Gereshon (Gershon), who was one of the sons of Levi,

  • ¶ The families that descended from Gereshon also belonged to the clan of Levi.

The Hebrew conjunction that the BSB leaves untranslated indicates the next event in the story. It may be more natural in some languages to begin a new sentence and to omit this conjunction.

the Levite clans of the Gershonim: The Hebrew phrase which the BSB translates as Gershonim is more literally “the descendants of Gereshon.” Gereshon was one of the three sons of Levi, and the Gershonim were his descendants.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The families that descended from Gereshon, who was one of the sons of Levi

The family groups that descended from Gereshon also belonged to the clan of Levi

21:27b

From the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh) they were given Golan in Bashan, a city of refuge for the manslayer,

  • received the town of Golan in Bashan with its grazing lands from the half clan of Menasheh who live east of the Yarden (Jordan) River. It was a town where anyone could run to escape when they had killed someone by accident.

  • They were given Golan town in Bashan region and the grasslands around it. The half of the Menasheh people who live east of the Yarden River gave it to them. It was a town of safety for those who had killed by mistake.

From the half-tribe of Menasheh they were given: The phrase the half-tribe of Menasheh refers to the part of the Menasheh clan that lived on the east side of the Yarden River.

Golan in Bashan: The town of Golan was mentioned in 20:8. It was east of the Sea of Galil (Galilee), in the region of Bashan.Rasmussen p. 237.

a city of refuge for the manslayer: This is the same Hebrew phrase as in verse 21:13 and 21. You should translate it as you did in those verses.

Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

received the town of Golan in Bashan with its grazing lands from the half-clan of Menasheh that lived east of the Yarden River. It was a town where anyone who had killed someone by mistake could run and escape.

21:27cRasmussen p. 232.

and Be’eshterah (Beeshterah)—two cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • They also received the town of Be-eshterah with its grazing lands. They received two towns in all.

  • They were also given Be-eshterah town and the grasslands around it. In total there were two towns.

and Be’eshterah—two cities, together with their pasturelands: The town of Be’eshterah is called Ashtarot (Ashtaroth) in I Chronicles 6:71. It was in the region of Bashan, east of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also received the town of Be’eshterah with its grazing lands. They received two towns from this clan.

They were also given Be’eshterah and the grasslands around it. The total was two towns.

title: Joshua 21:28
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:28

From the tribe of Yisakar (Issachar) they were given Kishyon (Kishion), Davrat (Daberath),

  • From the clan of Yisakar the Kohat (Kohath) families received the town of Kishyon and the grazing lands around it, the town of Davrat and the grazing lands around it,

  • The descendants of Yisakar gave them Kishyon town with its grasslands, and Davrat town with its grasslands,

From the tribe of Yisakar they were given Kishyon: The town of Kishyon was mentioned in 19:20. It was the southeast of Nazaret (Nazareth).Rasmussen p. 242.

Davrat: The town of Davrat was mentioned in 19:12. It was east of Nazaret

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From the clan of Yisakar the Kohat families received the town of Kishyon and the grazing lands around it and the town of Davrat with the grazing lands around it.

The clan of Yisakar gave them the town of Kishyon with the grasslands around it and the town of Davrat with the grasslands around it.

title: Joshua 21:29
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:29

Yarmut (Jarmuth), and Eyn-Ganim (En-gannim)—four cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • the town of Yarmut with the grazing lands around it, and the town of Eyn-Ganim with the grazing lands around it.

  • and Yarmut town with its grasslands, and Eyn-Ganim town with its grasslands.

Yarmut: The town of Yarmut was south of Kishyon (Kishion).Rasmussen p. 102.

and Eyn-Ganim: The town of Eyn-Ganim was mentioned in 19:21. It was southwest of the Sea of Galil (Galilee).

four cities: The clan of Yisakar (Issachar) gave four cities in all to the Kohat (Kohath) families of the Levi people.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the town of Yarmut with the grazing lands around it and the town of Eyn-Ganim with the grazing lands around it. They gave four towns in all.

Yarmut (Jarmuth) town with its grasslands and Eyn-Ganim (En-gannim) town with its grasslands. The total was four towns.

title: Joshua 21:30
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:30

From the tribe of Asher they were given Mish’al (Mishal), Avdon (Abdon),

  • From the clan of Asher, they received the town of Mish’al with the grazing lands around it, the town of Avdon with the grazing lands around it,

  • The descendants of Asher gave the Kohat (Kohath) people Mish’al town with its grasslands, and Avdon town with its grasslands,

From the tribe of Asher they were given Mish’al: The town of Mish’al was mentioned in 19:26. Its location is uncertain.

Avdon: The town of Avdon was mentioned in 1 Chronicles 6:74.It was northeast of Ako (Acco).Rasmussen p. 224.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From the clan of Asher they received the town of Mish’al with the grazing lands around it and the town of Avdon with the grazing lands around it,

The clan of Asher gave the Kohat families Mish’al town with its grasslands and Avdon town with its grasslands,

title: Joshua 21:31
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:31

Helkat (Helkath), and Rehov (Rehob)—four cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • the town of Helkat and the grazing lands around it, and the town of Rehov and the grazing lands around it. They gave four towns in all.

  • and Helkat town and its grasslands, and Rehov town and it grasslands. The descendants of Asher gave a total of four towns.

Helkat: The town of Helkat was mentioned in 19:25. Its location is uncertain.

and Rehov: The town of Rehov was mentioned in 19:28. It location is uncertain.Rasmussen p. 249.

four cities: The total number of towns that the clan of Asher gave to the Kohat (Kohath) clans was four cities.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

the town of Helkat and the grazing lands around it and the town of Rehov and the grazing lands around it. They gave four towns in all.

Helkat (Helkath) town and its grasslands, and Rehov (Rehob) town and its grasslands. The total was four towns.

title: Joshua 21:32
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:32a

And from the tribe of Naftali (Naphtali) they were given Kedesh in Galil (Galilee) (a city of refuge for the manslayer),

  • From the clan of Naftali they received the town of Kedesh in the region of Galil with its grasslands. It was a town where anyone could run to escape when they had killed someone by accident.

  • The descendants of Naftali gave them Kedesh town in Galil region and the grasslands around it. It was a town of safety for those who had killed by mistake.

And from the tribe of Naftali: The phrase from the tribe of Naftali can also be translated “from the clan of Naftali.”

they were given Kedesh in Galil: The town of Kedesh in Galil was mentioned in 12:22. It was northwest of the Sea of Galil.Rasmussen p. 241.

a city of refuge for the manslayer: This is the same Hebrew phrase as in verse 21:13, 21:21, and 21:27. You should translate it as you did in those verses.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

From the clan of Naftali they received the town of Kedesh in the region of Galil, with its grasslands. It was a town where anyone who had killed someone by mistake could run and escape.

The clan of Naftali (Naphtali) gave them Kedesh in Galil (Galilee) region and the grazing lands around it. It was a town of safety for anyone who had killed someone accidentally.

21:32b

Hamot-Dor (Hammoth-dor), and Kartan—three cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • They also received the town of Hamot-Dor and the grazing lands around it, and the town of Kartan and the grazing lands around it. They received three towns in all.

  • They also gave the Gereshon (Gershon) families the town of Hamot-Dor with its grasslands, and the town of Kartan with its grasslands. The total was three towns.

Hamot-Dor: The town of Hamot-Dor is called “Hamat (Hammath)” in Joshua 19:35.Woudstra p. 313.

and Kartan: The location of the town of Kartan is uncertain.

three cities, together with their pasturelands: The phrase three cities indicates that the clan of Naftali gave a total of three towns to the Gereshon families.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They also received Hamot-Dor and the grazing lands around it and Kartan and the grazing lands around it. They received three towns in all.

They also gave the Gereshon clans the town of Hamot-Dor (Hammoth-dor) with its grasslands and the town of Kartan with its grasslands. The total was three towns.

title: Joshua 21:33
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:33

In all, thirteen cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the Gershoni (Gershonite) clans.

  • The Gereshon (Gershon) families received a total of thirteen towns and the grazing lands around them.

  • The families of the Gereshon people were given thirteen towns and their grasslands.

In all, thirteen cities, together with their pasturelands, were given to the Gershoni clans: This verse is like verses 21:19 and 21:26. It is a concluding statement for this paragraph.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

The Gereshon families received a total of thirteen towns and the grazing lands around them.

The family groups of the Gereshon people were given thirteen towns and their grasslands.

title: Joshua 21:34
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:34a

This is what the Merari (Merarite) clan (the rest of the Levites) were given:

  • ¶ The remaining Levi people belonged to the families descended from Merari.

  • ¶ The other Levi people were families who descended from Merari.

the Merari clan: The phrase the Merari clan refers to the families who were descended from Merari. All the Levites who were not yet named were from the Merari families.

the rest of the Levites: The phrase the rest of the Levites refers to all the descendants of Levi who had not been named previously.

21:34b

From the tribe of Zevulun (Zebulun) they were given Yakeneam (Jokneam), Kartah,

  • From the clan of Zevulun they were given the town of Jokne-am with the grazing lands around it, the town of Kartah with the grazing lands around it,

  • The descendants of Zevulun gave them Jokne-am town with its grasslands, and Kartah town with its grasslands,

From the tribe of Zevulun they were given: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The Levites that remained belonged to the families descended from Merari. From the clan of Zevulun they were given…

The other Levi people were descended from Merari. The clan of Zevulun gave them…

Yakeneam: The town of Yakeneam is mentioned in 12:22. It was northwest of Meggido at the foot of Mount Karmel (Carmel).Rasmussen p. 241.

Kartah: The location of the town of Kartah is unknown.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The town of Jokne-am with the grazing lands around it, the town of Kartah with the grazing lands around it,

Jokne-am town with its grasslands, Kartah town with its grasslands

title: Joshua 21:35
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:35

Dimnah, and Nahalal—four cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • the town of Dimnah with the grazing lands around it, and the town of Nahalal with the grazing lands around it. The total number was four towns.

  • and Dimnah town with its grasslands, and Nahalal town with its grasslands. They received four towns from the descendants of Zevulun (Zebulun).

Dimnah: The town of Dimnah was probably the same town as was called “Rimon (Rimmon)” in 19:13.Butler p. 233.

and Nahalal: The town of Nahalal was mentioned in 19:15. Its location is unknown.

four cities: The phrase four cities indicates that the families of Merari received four towns in all from the clan of Zevulun.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

the town of Dimnah with the grazing lands around it and the town of Nahalal with the grazing lands around it. The families of Merari received four towns from the clan of Zevulun.

Dimnah with its grasslands and Nahalal with its grasslands. In all they received four towns.

title: Joshua 21:36
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:36

From the tribe of Re’uven (Reuben) they were given Betser (Bezer), Yahats (Jahaz),

  • From the clan of Re’uven, they received the town of Betser with the grazing lands around it, the town of Yahats with the grazing lands around it,

  • The descendants of Re’uven gave the Merari families the town of Betser and its grasslands, and the town of Yahats and its grasslands,

From the tribe of Re’uven they were given Betser: The town of Betser was mentioned in 20:8. It was east of the Yarden (Jordan) River.

Yahats: The town of Yahats was mentioned in 13:18. It was probably east of the Dead Sea, southeast of Meydeva (Medeba).Rasmussen p. 240.

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

From the clan of Re’uven, they received the town of Betser with its grazing lands and the town of Yahats with its grazing lands,

The clan of Re’uven gave from their lands the Merari families the town of Betser and the grasslands around it and the town of Yahats and the grasslands around it,

title: Joshua 21:37
content:
Section 21:1–45 The clan of Levi received towns to live in

21:37

Kedemot (Kedemoth), and Mofa’at (Mephaath)—four cities, together with their pasturelands.

  • the town of Kedemot with the grazing lands around it, and the town of Mepha-ath with the grazing lands around it. The total was four towns.

  • and the town of Kedemot with its grasslands, and the town of Mepha-ath with its grasslands. The clan of Re’uven (Reuben) gave the families of Merari four towns in all.

Kedemot: The town of Kedemot was mentioned in 13:18. It was possibly east of the Dead Sea and north of the Arnon River.Rasmussen p. 241.

and Mofa’at: The town of Mofa’at was mentioned in 13:18. Possibly it was south of the town of Amman in what is now the country of Yarden (Jordan).Rasmussen p. 244.
