  • and he set up laws and commands for them to follow at Shekem town.

  • At the town of Shekem he established laws and regulations for them.

and there at Shekem he established for them a statute and ordinance: The words statute and ordinance refer to all the laws that Yahweh specified should be part of the covenant. Some languages may not have two terms that refer to laws. In this case, only one term may be used.

Shekem: The town of Shekem was mentioned in verse 24:1.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

At Shekem, he set up rules and commands for them to follow

He established laws and regulations for them at the town of Shekem

at Shekem (Shechem)…Yehoshua (Joshua) made laws for Yisrael (Israel) (CEV)

title: Joshua 24:26
content:
Section 24:1–33: Yisrael (Israel) renewed their covenant with Yahweh

In this section Yehoshua (Joshua) called the people of Yisrael together to affirm that they would worship and obey only Yahweh. He warned them that Yahweh would bring disaster on them if they worshiped other gods. Then Yehoshua died and was buried.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Renewing the covenant at Shekem (Shechem)

The Israelis (Israelites) promise to worship only Yahweh

24:26a

Yehoshua recorded these things in the Book of the Law of God.

  • Then Yehoshua wrote down these words in the book that contained God’s laws.

  • Then Yehoshua wrote these things in the book of God’s teachings for them.

Yehoshua (Joshua) recorded these things: The phrase these things refers to the statues and ordinances that are mentioned in the previous verse.

in the Book of the Law of God: The Book of the Law of God refers to the book, or scroll, in which Yehoshua wrote down the laws that he received from God for them.Woudstra p. 357–358. The people of that time wrote things on scrolls rather than in books. Some English versions use the word scroll. For example:

Yehoshua wrote these words in the Law Scroll of God (NET)

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Then Yehoshua wrote down all these words in the book that contained God’s laws.

Then Yehoshua wrote these things in the book of God’s teachings for them.

24:26b

Then he took a large stone and set it up there under the oak that was near the sanctuary of Yahweh.

  • He took a large stone and set it up under the oak tree near the holy place of Yahweh.

  • He set a large stone on its end under the oak tree near the place that was set apart to worship Yahweh.

Then he took a large stone and set it up there under the oak: In many languages it may be more natural to begin a new sentence here. The clause set it up indicates that Yehoshua (Joshua) stood the large stone up on its end.

He erected a big stone

He stood a big stone on its end

Then: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Then introduces the next event in the storyline. Introduce the next event in a natural way in your language.

oak: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as oak is found only in this verse. It refers to a kind of tree, but scholars do not agree on what kind of tree it was. Some English versions translate this word as “terebinth,” which is a tree in the cashew family.

Here are some ways to translate this word:

oak (BSB, RSV, NET, NASB, NIV, GW, NJPS, GNT, CEV, NCV, NJB, KJV)

terebinth (ESV, NABRE, NLT, REB)

near the sanctuary of Yahweh: This sanctuary was a place where Yahweh was worshiped. The tree was probably close to this place.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

He took a large stone and set it up under the oak tree near the holy place of Yahweh.

He set a large stone on its end under the oak tree, near the place that was set apart to worship Yahweh.

title: Joshua 24:27
content:
Section 24:1–33: Yisrael (Israel) renewed their covenant with Yahweh

In this section Yehoshua (Joshua) called the people of Yisrael together to affirm that they would worship and obey only Yahweh. He warned them that Yahweh would bring disaster on them if they worshiped other gods. Then Yehoshua died and was buried.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Renewing the covenant at Shekem (Shechem)

The Israelis (Israelites) promise to worship only Yahweh

24:27a

And Yehoshua said to all the people,

  • ¶ Then Yehoshua said to all the people,

  • ¶ Yehoshua told all the Israelis,

And: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as And introduces the next event in the storyline. Introduce the next event in a way that is natural in your language.

24:27b

“You see this stone. It will be a witness against us,

  • “Look. This stone will be a witness against us(incl),

  • “Look at this stone. If it could speak it would give evidence against us.

You see: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as You see calls attention to the next statement. Some languages may have grammatical markers that fulfill this function.

Here are some other ways to translate this word:

Look

Look at this stone

this stone. It will be a witness against us: In verse 24:22 Yehoshua (Joshua) told the Israelis (Israelites) that they would be witnesses against themselves in the future. In this verse he told them that the stone he had set up would also be a witness. He said it was a witness against us because he was including himself with the other Israelis.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Look. This stone will be a witness against us(incl)

Look at this stone. It will give evidence against us.

Look at this stone. If it could speak it would testify against us.

24:27c

for it has heard all the words Yahweh has spoken to us,

  • because it has heard all the words that Yahweh spoke to us.

  • It is as though it has heard all the words that Yahweh has spoken to us.

for it has heard all the words Yahweh has spoken to us: Yahweh had spoken to the people of Yisrael (Israel) through Yehoshua (Joshua), and the stone had been a witness to all the words he said.

This does not mean that the stone had magical powers, or that there were spirits who lived in the stone. If it sounds strange in your language to have a stone be able to hear, you could use a simile.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

because it has heard all the words that Yahweh spoke to us

It is as though it has heard all the words that Yahweh has spoken to us.

24:27d

and it will be a witness against you if you ever deny your God.”

  • It will be a witness against you(plur) if you are not faithful to your God.”

  • So, it could give evidence against you if you betray God.”

and: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as and connects sentences. Many English versions do not translate this word here. Use a connecting word if there is a natural one in your language.

it will be a witness against you: This sentence uses almost the same words as in part b of this verse. Yehoshua (Joshua) repeated his statement to emphasize it. However, in this part of the verse he used the pronoun you instead of “us.”

if you ever deny your God: The Hebrew verb that the BSB translates as deny can also be translated “betray” or “be unfaithful.”

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

So it will be a witness against you(plur), if you are not faithful to your God.

It could give evidence against you if you betray God.

title: Joshua 24:28
content:
Section 24:1–33: Yisrael (Israel) renewed their covenant with Yahweh

In this section Yehoshua (Joshua) called the people of Yisrael together to affirm that they would worship and obey only Yahweh. He warned them that Yahweh would bring disaster on them if they worshiped other gods. Then Yehoshua died and was buried.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Renewing the covenant at Shekem (Shechem)

The Israelis (Israelites) promise to worship only Yahweh

24:28

Then Yehoshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance.

  • Then Yehoshua told all the people to leave and return to their own property.

  • Then Yehoshua told all the people to go to their homes.

Then: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Then introduces the next event in the storyline. Introduce the next event in a natural way in your language.

Yehoshua (Joshua) sent the people away, each to his own inheritance: The phrase each to his own inheritance indicates that each person returned to the land that Yehoshua gave him when land was divided among the clans of Yisrael (Israel).

Here are some other ways to translate this verse:

Then Yehoshua told all the people to leave and return to their own property.

Then Yehoshua told all the people to go to their homes.

title: Joshua 24:29
content:
Section 24:1–33: Yisrael (Israel) renewed their covenant with Yahweh

In this section Yehoshua (Joshua) called the people of Yisrael together to affirm that they would worship and obey only Yahweh. He warned them that Yahweh would bring disaster on them if they worshiped other gods. Then Yehoshua died and was buried.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Renewing the covenant at Shekem (Shechem)

The Israelis (Israelites) promise to worship only Yahweh

24:29a

Some time later, Yehoshua son of Nun, the servant of Yahweh, died

  • ¶ After these events had happened, Yehoshua the son of Nun, the servant of Yahweh, died

  • ¶ Sometime after that, Yehoshua died. He was the son of Nun, and he was Yahweh’s servant.

Some time later, Yehoshua (Joshua) son of Nun, the servant of Yahweh, died: The phrase Some time later refers to an indefinite period of time. It does not mean that Yehoshua died right after the ceremony of Shekem.

servant of Yahweh: The phrase servant of Yahweh is the same title that Mosheh (Moses) received. Translate this title in the same way as you did in Joshua 1:1.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

After these events had happened, Yehoshua the son of Nun, the servant of Yahweh, died.

Sometime after that, Yehoshua died. He was the son of Nun and he was Yahweh’s servant.

24:29b

at the age of 110.

  • at the age of one hundred and ten.

  • He was one hundred and ten years old when he died.

at the age of 110: Here is another way to translate this part of the verse:

He was one hundred and ten years old when he died.

title: Joshua 24:30
content:
Section 24:1–33: Yisrael (Israel) renewed their covenant with Yahweh

In this section Yehoshua (Joshua) called the people of Yisrael together to affirm that they would worship and obey only Yahweh. He warned them that Yahweh would bring disaster on them if they worshiped other gods. Then Yehoshua died and was buried.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Renewing the covenant at Shekem (Shechem)

The Israelis (Israelites) promise to worship only Yahweh

24:30a

And they buried him in the land of his inheritance, at Timnat-Serah (Timnath-serah)

  • They buried him on his own land in the town of Timnat-Serah,

  • The Israelis buried him in the land that he had received, which was the town of Timnat-Serah.

And: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as And introduces the next event in the story line.

they buried him in the land of his inheritance: The Israelis buried Yehoshua (Joshua) in the land that they had given him. The story of how they gave him this land is in Joshua 19:49.

at Timnat-Serah: The town of Timnat-Serah was southwest of the town of Shekem (Shechem). It is mentioned in Joshua 19:50.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

They buried him in the land that he had received, which was the town of Timnat-Serah.

The Israelis (Israelites) buried him in his own land at the town of Timnat-Serah (Timnath-serah).

24:30b

in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim), north of Mount Ga’ash (Gaash).

  • which was north of Ga’ash Mountain in the hilly region of the clan of Efrayim.

  • It was in the mountain region of the clan of Efrayim, north of the mountain of Ga’ash.

in the hill country of Efrayim, north of Mount Ga’ash: Mount Ga’ash is not mentioned anywhere else in the Bible.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

It was in the mountain region of the clan of Efrayim, north of the mountain of Ga’ash.

which was north of Ga’ash Mountain in the hilly region of the clan of Efrayim

title: Joshua 24:31
content:
Section 24:1–33: Yisrael (Israel) renewed their covenant with Yahweh

In this section Yehoshua (Joshua) called the people of Yisrael together to affirm that they would worship and obey only Yahweh. He warned them that Yahweh would bring disaster on them if they worshiped other gods. Then Yehoshua died and was buried.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Renewing the covenant at Shekem (Shechem)

The Israelis (Israelites) promise to worship only Yahweh

24:31a

Yisrael had served Yahweh throughout the days of Yehoshua

  • The people of Yisrael served Yahweh during Yehoshua’s lifetime,

  • As long as Yehoshua lived, the people of Yisrael (Israel) worshiped Yahweh.

The Hebrew word that the BSB leaves untranslated but some English versions translate as “and” introduces the next event in the storyline.

Yisrael served Yahweh throughout the days of Yehoshua (Joshua): The phrase throughout the days of Yehoshua indicates all the time that Yehoshua lived.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The people of Yisrael served Yahweh during Yehoshua’s lifetime.

As long as Yehoshua lived, the people of Yisrael worshiped Yahweh.

24:31b

and of the elders who outlived him

  • and during the lifetimes of the elders who lived longer than Yehoshua did.

  • They continued to worship Yahweh during the lifetimes of the leaders who still lived after Yehoshua had died.

and of the elders who outlived him: The term elders also occurs in Joshua 24:1. You should translate it the same way in both places.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

and during the lifetimes of the elders who lived longer than Yehoshua (Joshua) did

They continued to worship Yahweh during the lifetimes of the leaders who still lived after Yehoshua had died.

24:31c

and who had experienced all the works that Yahweh had done for Yisrael (Israel).

  • Those elders had seen all the mighty acts that Yahweh had done for the people of Yisrael.

  • The leaders had experienced all the things that Yahweh had done to help the Israelis (Israelites).

and who had experienced all the works that Yahweh had done for Yisrael: The elders had seen how Yahweh helped Yisrael to leave Mitsrayim (Egypt) and conquer the land of Kena’an (Canaan).

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Those elders had seen all the mighty acts that Yahweh had done for the people of Yisrael.

The leaders had experienced all the things that Yahweh had done to help the Israelis.

title: Joshua 24:32
content:
Section 24:1–33: Yisrael (Israel) renewed their covenant with Yahweh

In this section Yehoshua (Joshua) called the people of Yisrael together to affirm that they would worship and obey only Yahweh. He warned them that Yahweh would bring disaster on them if they worshiped other gods. Then Yehoshua died and was buried.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Renewing the covenant at Shekem (Shechem)

The Israelis (Israelites) promise to worship only Yahweh

24:32a

And the bones of Yosef (Joseph), which the Israelis had brought up out of Mitsrayim (Egypt), were buried at Shekem

  • The people of Yisrael had brought Yosef’s bones with them when they left Mitsrayim. They buried them at Shekem.

  • The Israelis buried Yosef’s bones at Shekem town. They had brought the bones with them when they came out of Mitsrayim.

And the bones of Yosef, which the Israelis had brought up out of Mitsrayim, were buried at Shekem: In Genesis 50:25 Yosef had made the Israelis promise to bring his bones with them when they left Mitsrayim.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The people of Yisrael (Israel) had brought Yosef’s bones with them when they left Mitsrayim. They buried them at the town of Shekem (Shechem).

The Israelis (Israelites) buried Yosef’s bones at Shekem town. They had brought the bones with them when they came out of Mitsrayim.

24:32b

in the plot of land that Ya’akov (Jacob) had purchased from the sons of Hamor, Shekem’s father, for a hundred pieces of silver.

  • Ya’akov had bought a plot of land there from the sons of Hamor, who was Shekem’s father. He had paid one hundred pieces of money for it.

  • They buried them in the plot of land that Ya’akov had bought for one hundred silver pieces from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shekem.

in the plot of land that Ya’akov had purchased from the sons of Hamor, Shekem’s father, for a hundred pieces of silver: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as pieces of silver is found in only two other places in the Old Testament: Genesis 33:19 and Job 42:11. It was an ancient weight, but it is not certain how heavy it was.

Avoid using the word “coins.” Coins had not been invented at this time. They used pieces of silver in a wedge shape with a standard weight.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Ya’akov had bought a plot of land there from the sons of Hamor, who was Shekem’s (Shechem’s) father. Ya’akov had paid one hundred pieces of silver for it.

They buried them in the plot of land that Ya’akov had bought for one hundred silver pieces from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shekem.

24:32c

So it became an inheritance for Yosef’s (Joseph’s) descendants.

  • That land was in the area that belonged to the descendants of Yosef.

  • Yosef’s descendants now owned that land.

So it became an inheritance for Yosef’s descendants: Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

That land was in the area that belonged to the descendants of Yosef.

Yosef’s descendants now own that land.

General Comment on verse 24:32

In some languages it may be more natural to reorder the parts of this verse so that they are in chronological order. For example:

Many years ago Ya’akov (Jacob) had bought a piece of land from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shekem (Shechem) for one hundred pieces of silver. When the Israelis (Israelites) left Mitsrayim (Egypt) they carried Yosef’s (Joseph’s) bones with them. Now, years later, they buried his bones in that piece of land that Ya’akov had bought in Shekem.

title: Joshua 24:33
content:
Section 24:1–33: Yisrael (Israel) renewed their covenant with Yahweh

In this section Yehoshua (Joshua) called the people of Yisrael together to affirm that they would worship and obey only Yahweh. He warned them that Yahweh would bring disaster on them if they worshiped other gods. Then Yehoshua died and was buried.

Here are some other possible section headings:

Renewing the covenant at Shekem (Shechem)

The Israelis (Israelites) promise to worship only Yahweh

24:33a

Eleazar son of Aharon (Aaron) also died,

  • Later, Eleazar the priest, the son of Aharon, died.

  • Some time after that, Eleazar died. He was the son of Aharon.

The Hebrew word that the BSB leaves untranslated but some English versions translate as “and” introduces the next event in the storyline. Introduce the next event in a way that is natural in your language.

Eleazar son of Aharon also died: Eleazar was a priest. He was last mentioned in Joshua 21:1.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

Later, Eleazar the priest the son of Aharon died.

Some time later, Eleazar died. He was a son of Aharon.

24:33b

and they buried him at Giveah (Gibeah),

  • The Israelis (Israelites) buried him at Gibe-ah, which belonged to his son Pinhas (Phinehas).

  • The people of Yisrael (Israel) buried Eleazar in the town of Gibe-ah. That town had been given to his son Pinhas

and: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as and introduces the next event in the storyline.

they buried him at Giveah: The Hebrew word that the BSB translates as Giveah is the name of a town, and is also a noun meaning “hill.” The English versions do not agree on how to translate it in this context.

  1. It is the name of a town. For example:

    and they buried him at Giveah, the town of Pinhas his son (ESV) (BSB, ESV, RSV, NET, NASB, NIV, GNT, NLT, NCV, NJB)

  2. It is a noun that means “hill.” For example:

    and they buried him on the hill of his son Pinhas (Phinehas) (NJPS) (NJPS, NABRE, GW, REB, CEV, KJV)

It is recommended that you choose interpretation (1). This is the interpretation taken by many English versions.

The location of Giveah (Gibeah) is uncertain, except that it was in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim). It belonged to Pinhas.

Here are some other ways to translate this part of the verse:

The Israelis (Israelites) buried him at Giveah, which belonged to his son Pinhas.

The people of Yisrael (Israel) buried Eleazar in the town of Giveah. That town had been given to his son Pinhas.

24:33c

which had been given to his son Pinhas (Phinehas) in the hill country of Efrayim.
